# sliver_tree fix plan

Companion to `sliver_tree_review_2026_08_22.md`, which holds the evidence for
each finding. This document holds the **solutions**: one implementation-ready
block per item, ordered by severity. Nothing here is code; each block names the
files, functions and fields to change so the work can start without
rediscovering the problem.

Scope: `lib/sliver_tree` at commit `4d15c0c` (0.0.34).

committed (H6, M14, M22, M23, M3), and they moved code in seven files.

So 257 of 294 body citations into those seven files point at the wrong code
in a working-tree checkout, while remaining correct against `4d15c0c`. No
other file in the document is affected; the rest are untouched.

The blocks were NOT rewritten, deliberately. Re-anchoring 256 citations by
hand invites exactly the transcription errors this document exists to avoid,
and the next landed item would stale them again. Instead:

- Before implementing a block, re-derive its anchors by grepping for the
  named symbol rather than trusting the number. Every citation names the
  construct as well as the line.
- Treat `git show 4d15c0c:<path>` as the authority for what a citation MEANT.
- Committing the four landed items and regenerating anchors is the permanent
  fix. That is a maintainer decision, not something an implementer should do
  in the middle of a block.

The Status paragraphs of LANDED items are exempt: they describe the current
working tree, and their citations are kept correct against it.

## Readiness rubric

Every audit pass judges each item against exactly this bar. An item is
**ready-to-implement** when all ten hold:

1. **Finding verified.** The status (confirmed by test, confirmed by reading,
   plausible) is stated, and every `file:line` citation resolves to code that
   says what the block claims.
2. **Root cause named.** The block points at the specific code that produces
   the behavior, not at the symptom.
3. **Solution concrete.** Files, functions and fields are named; every decision
   rule, predicate or formula the implementer needs is written down. No
   "consider", no "investigate", no open questions.
4. **Alternatives resolved.** At least one alternative is recorded with the
   architecture or performance reason it lost, or the block states that the fix
   is forced.
5. **Architecture fit.** The owning layer is named and the change reuses an
   existing mechanism rather than adding a parallel one. It does not violate a
   convention in `CLAUDE.md` (nid storage, live-space indices, the two
   notification channels and the `affectedKeys` contract, the animation-family
   boundary rule, the coordinate spaces, the FLIP-only carve-outs, the
   `PointerSpace`-owns-the-scrollable rule).
6. **Performance stated.** Complexity before and after, and for anything on a
   hot path (`performLayout`, `paint`, `hitTest`, per-pointer-event, per-tick)
   the added per-frame cost and allocation count.
7. **No regression of a documented behavior.** If the fix changes something the
   package documents on purpose, the block says so and states the doc change.
8. **Risk named.** The other readers of the touched path are listed, and the
   existing tests that will need updating are named by file.
9. **Test specified.** A regression test that fails before and passes after,
   described precisely enough to write, or an explicit "none" with a reason.
10. **Sequencing consistent.** If the item interacts with another item, the
    dependency is recorded in both blocks and in the sequencing section.

An item that fails any of the ten is **not-ready**, and the audit says which
number failed and why.

## Conventions used in the blocks

- Severity and IDs match the review document. `H*` items are user-visible with
  common inputs; `M*` need a specific sequence; `L*` are cleanup.
- Effort is S (under a day), M (a day or two), L (more, or needs a design
  decision from the maintainer).
- "Hot path" means `performLayout`, `paint`, `hitTestChildren`, an animation
  tick, or a per-pointer-event drag path.
- **Never cite this document by line number.** Cite SOURCE as `file:line`, but
  refer to another item by its ID and the name of the section inside it, for
  example "M8's Doc changes item 2". This document is reassembled from per-slice
  sources on every edit, so every line number in it moves whenever any earlier
  block grows, and a self-citation is stale before the next merge finishes. The
  same applies to quoting another block's text: name the block and the section,
  and quote the words, not a line.
- A bare line citation such as `:2861` refers to the file most recently named
  in the same block. Every citation in this document resolves to a real file
  and an in-range line, re-checked mechanically after every edit; no count is
  written here because the document grows and any figure would be stale by the
  next merge; the bare form is
  the only one that depends on reading order, so if a block's prose leaves it
  genuinely unclear which file a bare reference means, that is a rubric item 1
  failure and the reference must be qualified.

## Sequencing

Items that interact. Landing them out of this order either wastes work or
lands a fix the next change immediately rewrites. Each dependency is repeated
in the affected blocks.

**Chain 1, bulk extents and admission (M6, then M7, then M8, with H2).**
`M6` and `M7` sit in the same method and are two sides of one staleness
problem: `M7`'s symptom appears only on frames that stay on the fast path,
which is rare today precisely because `M6` makes the path fall off almost
every frame. Fixing `M6` first makes `M7` fire every frame, so they land as
ONE commit with two tests. `M8` rewrites the same admission loop, so it lands
after `M6` rather than being rewritten by it. `H2`'s accumulator seed belongs
wherever admission ends up: decide `M8`'s shape (unify into
`LayoutAdmissionPolicy`, or patch the bulk loop in place) BEFORE writing `H2`,
or `H2` has to be applied twice.

`M6` also interacts with `H2` directly, which an earlier draft of `M6` denied.
They share the loop body at `render_sliver_tree.dart:453-463` (`M6` rewrites
the extent write at `:457`; `H2` part (c) replaces the break at `:458-459`,
and its floor predicate reads what `:457` produces), the same new required
`BulkAnimationData<TKey> bulkData` on the signature at `:446-450`, and the
sole call site at `:2768-2772`, which both must widen. Land `M6` first, as
`H2` already says. Two consequences worth carrying: after both land,
`bulkData.containsMemberNid(nid)` is called twice per row and should be
hoisted to one local; and `M6` deliberately KEEPS the `offset` local at `:455`
that its own rewrite would otherwise drop, so `H2`'s snippet pastes unchanged.
`M8` then supersedes the shape again, so if `M8` lands last its widened
`onCacheRegionAdmit(nid, visibleIndex)` carries `M6`'s arithmetic forward
rather than discarding it.

**Chain 2, sibling refresh (M9 before M21).** `M21` adds two
`_siblingRefreshSet` call sites, which are exactly the sites `M9` is making
cheap. Writing `M21` first means rewriting it; write it against `M9`'s
resulting API.

**Chain 3, exit-ghost pipeline (M10, then L6, L7 and L24).** All four decide
which delta a ghost pass reads and who paints the anchor. `M10` establishes the
FLIP-only rule for `_ExitGhost` records, the
`getSlideDeltaNid == getFlipSlideDeltaNid + getHeldPreviewDeltaNid` identity,
and the read-site inventory in `CLAUDE.md`, which is the premise the other
three build on. `L6` additionally CREATES a new read location, the
`applyPaintTransform` branch for anchor-based ghosts, and therefore owns
raising the inventory count when it lands.

**Chain 4, the drag proxy and the hidden row (H5 with M19).** `H5` decides
whether the row's captured widget instance may be mounted twice; `M19` decides
how the in-place row is hidden. If `H5` takes the placeholder approach, most
of `M19`'s wrapper question is answered by it. Decide them together.

**Chain 5, scroll targeting (H1, then H3, then M20).** `H1` changes what a
scroll offset means for never-measured rows, `H3` changes when the orchestrator
may read the position, and `M20` adds a sticky inset to the computed target.
Each later item's test would be unstable on top of an unfixed earlier one.

**Chain 6, drag row lookup (M11 before L21).** Both change what
`findRowAtPaintedY` answers during a drag: `M11` adds the lifted-range skip,
`L21` is about the same function not knowing pinned bands.

**Chain 7, the sync diff (M12 and M13 are one change).** The root-removal
deferral in `syncRoots` is deliberate and documented: removing a root first
marks its subtree pending-deletion and wrecks the FLIP slide of a child
reparenting out of it. So the fix is not "remove first like the children path";
it is to give `syncRoots` the same mover-ancestor precision rule
`syncMultipleChildren` already has, which fixes both items with one shared
helper.

**Chain 8, the THREE blocks that rewrite `_cancelDeletion` (M1, then M2, then
M5).** M1 changes which branch the ROOT key of a cancelled deletion takes
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:408-413`), M2 rewrites the DESCENDANT half
(`:414-425`), and M5 annotates every `_startStandalone*` install site with its
animation family, one of which M1 deletes. All three edit one method body.
Land M1, then M2, then M5, and rebase M5's call-site table on the result.

**Chain 12, blocks that change the `_startStandalone*` install-site set (M5
with H4 and L27).** M5's whole design is an enumerated table of the install
sites, each given a required family parameter. TWO other blocks change that
set, not one. H4 ADDS four new install sites inside `expandAll`/`collapseAll`
and extracts two existing ones into a helper. L27's edit 2 replaces
`tree_controller.dart:4223-4227`, today `_addBulkMember(key)`, with
`_startStandaloneEnterAnimation(key)`, which is a new install site in the
bulk-reverse branch. Under M5's design none of those calls compiles without
the family parameter, and any count of sites written in the block stops being
true. Whichever lands last re-derives M5's table from the tree rather than
from a number written anywhere, per M5's own rule. All three blocks record
this pairing.

A fourth block also changes that set, by SUBTRACTION rather than addition:
`M1` deletes the `_startStandaloneEnterAnimation` call at
`_tree_controller_animation.dart:410`. That pairing is carried by chain 8
instead, because M1 and M5 collide on the same method BODY and not merely on
the site inventory, and chain 8 already fixes their order. It is named here so
that a reader checking "which blocks change the install-site set" against this
chain does not conclude M1 was missed. Measured this session over the plan:
the blocks that mention `_startStandalone` at all are exactly M1, M5, H4 and
L27, and the only one adding a bare call in its replacement code is L27.

**Chain 18, the carve-out inventory (H1 with M10), no fixed order.** `H1`
step 6 adds a `hasActiveFlipSlides` read in the `correctionsAllowed` gate,
which is a FOURTH block editing the FLIP-only carve-out inventory that `M10`
owns the recipe for. Unlike the other chains here this one fixes no landing
order: `M10` rewrites the inventory into four categories and `H1` contributes
plus one read in a new category, SCROLL-CORRECTION RE-ENTRANCY, whose LETTER
is all that depends on order, (e) after `M10` and (c) if `H1` lands first,
because chains 3 and 5 have no fixed order relative to each other. Whoever
lands second re-runs `M10`'s grep recipe and writes what it returns, per
`M10`'s rule that no block writes an absolute total. `M10`'s counting rule
names the blocks that change the inventory and must name all four.

**Chain 16, the sticky force-create loop (M7, then H1).** Both rewrite
`render_sliver_tree.dart:2961-2969`. M7 part 2 prints a full replacement body,
changing `priorExtent` at `:2963` from `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` to
`controller.getCurrentExtentNid(nid)`; H1 step 3 adds an `aboveAnchorDelta`
accumulation inside the `extent != priorExtent` branch at `:2967`. The two are
compatible in substance, so the combined body is printed ONCE, in H1 step 3,
and M7's block says its own body is the pre-H1 shape and points there. Land M7
first. The reverse order fails QUIETLY, which is why it is worth a chain:
applying M7's literal body on top of H1 compiles clean and simply drops the
accumulation, leaving `aboveAnchorDelta` declared and still emitted, so the
correction silently under-reports instead of erroring.

**Chain 17, the measurement loop (M8, then H1).** H1 step 2 writes its
accumulator into the extent-changed branch at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2819-2824`
under the condition `i < anchorIndex`, and M8's Step 4/5 rewrites that loop to
iterate `_writtenCacheRegionNids`, which has no per-row `i`. Land M8 first, and
H1's condition becomes `_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] + estimatedExtent <= scrollOffset`.
That is not an approximation of `i < anchorIndex`, it is the same predicate:
`_findFirstVisibleIndex`'s non-bulk arm is literally that compare on those two
arrays (`:3310-3313`), and both operands are already in the loop (`:2818`,
`:2828`, with `scrollOffset` at `:2521`). Because the offset form does not
depend on the iteration shape, H1 becomes a two-line insert into M8's
`if (actual != estimated)` branch. Two alternatives were rejected on M8's own
grounds: a per-changed-row `visibleIndexOfNid` reintroduces exactly the lookup
M8 Step 5 exists to remove, and a parallel index track beside
`_writtenCacheRegionNids` is the third bookkeeping notion M8 Step 4's
alternative (i) already rejects, needing two writers kept in lockstep
(`:461`, `:491-498`). H1's step 1 `anchorIndex` capture is withdrawn as a dead
local under this form, so H1 also stops paying a binary search.

**Chain 15, the op-group reversal bodies (H4 with L27), ONE commit.** Both
rewrite `tree_controller.dart:4189-4203` and `:4395-4412`, and H4 also
rewrites `:4208-4231` inside which L27's edit 2 replaces `:4223-4227`. They
are not alternatives: both changes are wanted, and there is exactly one
correct order INSIDE each merged body: partition, `continue` where H4's rule
says so, DISPLACE via `_startStandalone*`, then `pendingRemoval.clear()` on
the expand side or the re-pend on the collapse side, then L27's Path-1 rebase
over the SURVIVORS only, then L27's `runWithGroupDetached` reset, then
`forward()` / `reverse()`. No intermediate state is shippable, so the two
op-group halves land as one commit. Three failures if the order is broken:
applying L27's edit 1 literally on top of H4 deletes the partition and the
zombie rows return (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:266-282` removes nothing
from `_order`); applying H4's original `targetExtent = _fullExtentOf(...) ??
_unknownExtent` on top of L27 leaves the sentinel in a member whose controller
is then reset, so the row paints at zero for a frame (`types.dart:252-254`
with `curves.dart:92-97`); and rebasing before displacing mis-seeds the
displaced row through `_animation_coordinator.dart:577`. L27's edit 2 is the
one separable piece, and only in one direction: it may land alone BEFORE H4,
whose `_routeShownNodesToStandaloneEnters` extraction then absorbs it.

**Chain 14, the resolve guard and the plain-path session (H3 with L13).**
Both restructure `ScrollOrchestrator.animateScrollToKey`. H3's (a0) hoists a
resolve check above both routing decisions; L13 installs a plain-path session
in `_activeScroll` early in the same method. Order is not free: with the
install above the guard, an unresolvable key registers a session, cancels an
in-flight animated scroll through the single-flight slot
(`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:397-401`), and only then returns false, which is
the exact defect (a0) prevents. Whichever lands second, the resolve guard must
precede the session install. This pair is deliberately kept out of chain 5,
whose other two members L13 does not interact with.

**Chain 13, the relocation helper and its notification (M4 with M21).** M4
folds the two byte-identical relocation blocks in `insertRoot` and `insert`
into one helper, and that helper contains the exact
`_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: {node.key})` line M21 exists to replace.
Landing M4 after M21 silently reinstates M21's defect; landing M4 first makes
M21 inexpressible unless the helper takes a `TKey? parentKey` so it can call
`_siblingRefreshSet`. The helper takes that parameter, and M21 becomes a
one-line change inside it.

**Chain 9, the sync diff's `remaining` list (M12 with L2).** L2 deletes the
`remaining` list in both sync methods on the grounds that nothing reads it
after the seeding loop. That is true of the code as it stands, but M12
reintroduces `remaining` as a live read in `syncRoots` step 3 to convert
survivor space into live space. Land M12 first and narrow L2's deletion to the
`syncChildren` copy only, or land L2 first and have M12 reintroduce the list
deliberately.

**Chain 10, comment fixes that depend on their code change (L26 with H6 and
M14).** Two of L26's documentation repairs describe behavior that only becomes
true once H6 and M14 land. They must not go in ahead of them.

**Chain 11, admission sub-items (L25.4 and L25.6 with M8).** TWO of `L25`'s
sub-items sit on M8's path. 25.4 edits the same admission loop M8
restructures. 25.6's first slice targets `render_sliver_tree.dart:2798` and
`:2817`, which M8's Step 4 deletes outright via the sparse track plus
`keyOfNid`. Both land with M8 or after it, never before: landing either
first is discarded work. L25's block and M8's block both record this.

## Textual adjacency without an ordering constraint

Four pairs edit the same method or file at disjoint statements. Each was
checked against source: either landing order compiles and behaves identically,
so none is a chain. They are listed because the independence note below would
otherwise read as a promise that they cannot collide in review, and because
one of them moves the other's anchors.

- **M3 with M23**, `expand` Path 2. M3 replaces the mixed body at
  `tree_controller.dart:3865-3897`; M23 wraps the `forward()` two lines later
  at `:3899-3900`. Membership is identical under either body (both skip
  `_isPendingDeletion` before joining the group), so M23's emptiness guard
  reads the same answer. But M3 shrinks the preceding body from about 33 lines
  to about 13, so if M3 lands first, M23's line anchors move and must be
  re-derived. M23's block already warns that its anchors are fragile; this is
  the specific reason.
- **M9 with M16**, `moveNode`'s single `affected` block. M16 rewrites the
  depth branch at `tree_controller.dart:3627-3633`; M9 renames the two
  `_siblingRefreshSet` calls at `:3636-3637`. Semantically independent: M16
  changes which keys the depth branch contributes, M9 changes when the sibling
  set is materialized. Adjacent lines, so expect a merge conflict, not a bug.
- **M17 with M25**, `PointerSpace.sample` (`_drag_session.dart:79-97`). M25
  inserts a `syncScrollSubscription()` call at the prologue and deletes
  `DragSession.subscribeScroll` (`:299-320`); M17 replaces the `sliverX`
  expression at `:89`. Disjoint statements, neither reads state the other
  establishes.
- **H5 with L26**, `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart`. L26's ASCII pass rewrites
  comment bytes across the file and one string literal at `:735`; H5 rewrites
  `:1031-1033` and two dartdoc paragraphs. Disjoint, but a whole-file byte
  pass over a file another item is editing is worth knowing about.

Independent of everything else: M3, M14, M16, M17, M22, M23, M25, and the Low
list except L2, L6, L7, L13, L21, L24, L26, L27 (chain 15), and L25
(whose sub-items 25.4 and 25.6 are in chain 11).

**Suggested landing order.** M14, M22 first: each is small, isolated, and
independently testable. H6 landed on 2026-08-22 and is done.

An earlier draft of this sentence also listed H4 as small and isolated. That was wrong, and it is corrected here rather than left to mislead a scheduler: H4 is rated M, not S, and it is coupled twice over. Chain 15 pairs it with L27 as a ONE COMMIT (no shippable intermediate), and chain 12 pairs it with M5. It sits in the H4 / L27 / M1 / M2 / M5 cluster and cannot be taken as a standalone first item. Then chain 1 as one render-layer sitting, which
must come BEFORE H1: chain 16 requires M7 to land first and chain 17 requires
M8 to land first, because each shares a loop body with an H1 step, and taking
H1 first puts both in the silent-failure order those chains describe. Then
chain 5, whose H1 is the largest single piece of work in the plan. Then chain 4 and
the remaining drag items. The Low list batches at the end, except `L25`'s
sub-items, which are cheapest to land alongside whichever render-layer change
is already open.

**Note carried from the M6-M10 drafting pass.** M6 then M7 (M7's symptom only appears on frames that stay on the fast path, which M6 makes the norm; `render_sliver_tree.dart:2818-2823` and `:3035-3051` are in the same method and should land as one commit with two tests). M8 is independent of both in behaviour but shares `_admitBulkFastPath`, so it should land after M6 to avoid rewriting the same loop twice. M9 and M10 are independent of the render-performance three and of each other.

## Documentation impact

The blocks named below change documentation as part of their fix. They are
collected here because an implementer landing items piecemeal will otherwise
miss them, and because several are the ONLY record that a documented behavior
changed.

No absolute count is written here, for the reason M10 gives about the
carve-out inventory: a total stated in a section that several blocks edit goes
stale the moment one of them lands, and a stale count reads exactly like a
measured one. The authoritative set is the blocks named in the bullets below,
minus any named only as a prerequisite or as contributing nothing. Each block
also states its own documentation impact under its Risk section, which is what
an implementer landing that one item actually reads.

**`CLAUDE.md` (and its `AGENTS.md` twin, which repeats several of the same
paragraphs).**

- `M10`, `L6`, `L7` and `H1` all edit the FLIP-only carve-out inventory.
  `M10` rewrites it into four categories with a canonical grep recipe, and
  within chain 3 it lands before `L6` and `L7`; `H1` is in chain 18, which
  fixes no order relative to `M10`. `L7` contributes a delta of plus one to
  category (a) (edge-ghost lifecycle). `L6` contributes plus TWO to category
  (c) (exit-ghost lifecycle), because its gate reads both the ghost and the
  anchor. `H1` contributes plus one `hasActiveFlipSlides` read in a NEW
  category, SCROLL-CORRECTION RE-ENTRANCY: the `correctionsAllowed` gate in
  `RenderSliverTree.performLayout`. That category's letter depends on landing
  order, (e) after `M10` and (c) if `H1` lands first, because chains 3 and 5
  have no fixed order relative to each other. `H1`'s read is deliberate and
  not reducible to the composed predicate: the gate protects re-entrancy of
  the once-per-frame pre-Pass-1 pipeline, not displacement, and composed
  `hasActiveSlides` would refuse corrections for the whole length of a drag,
  which is when they are both needed and survivable. `L24` contributes ZERO
  and writes no count: it passes the composed `controller.hasActiveSlides` at
  both call sites and paints through the composed `_paintRow`. No block writes
  an absolute total except `M10` for its own landing, because four blocks
  changing one number in a partly unfixed order is how that number goes stale.
  Whoever lands a block re-runs the recipe and writes what it returns.

- The recipe itself needs care, and `M10` owns stating it correctly. Today's
  `CLAUDE.md` says "nine read locations (grep minus the two declarations)",
  but the grep returns 14 lines: 2 declarations (`tree_controller.dart:1061`,
  `:1332`) and 3 doc-comment mentions (`:1321`, `_ghost_registry.dart:136`,
  `:173`) sit above the 9 real reads. The number nine is right; subtracting
  only the declarations yields 12.
- `M5` corrects the animation-family boundary rule's own example list once
  standalone installs carry a family.
- `M9` and `M11` touch the `affectedKeys` contract paragraph and the drag
  session's `PointerSpace` rule respectively.

## High

### H1. Scroll position is never corrected for estimate vs measured row height

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24. `audit_repro_h1_test.dart` red on unfixed code exactly as the block derives: case 1 anchor painted at +304 (off by the 312 px band residual) with `pixels` still 8000, case 2 landing +312 below the target. Part (a) landed as printed: the offset-form anchor test in the sparse measurement loop, the sticky mirror through the structural authority, the budgeted emit with the self-resetting per-frame counter and follow-up scheduler, epsilon 0.01, and the FLIP-only re-entrancy gate. Part (b) landed with one addition the block does not print: a fourth repro case pins the settle snap through an ANIMATED scroll (absolute ticks overwrite mid-flight corrections; red with the snap disabled), because nothing else discriminated part (b). One probe recorded: removing the `!isAnimatingNid` filter leaves case 3 green in its own scenario, because Pass 1's per-frame walk keeps animating rows' slots current and the measurement loop then sees no residual for them; the filter stays as specified, and case 3's red direction is demonstrated by an unconditional-emit correction storm instead (the budget caps it at 3 layouts per pump and the assert catches the growth). Nine demo states shown red individually. Inventory: category (e) SCROLL-CORRECTION RE-ENTRANCY added; recipe re-run at landing returns 24 non-comment lines minus 3 declarations = twenty-one reads, eighteen FLIP-only. The widget suite's three pixel pins pass via the snap exactly as the block traces; the full suite shifted nothing (1138 passed, 4 skipped); analyze at the 48-issue baseline.

**Finding.** `RenderSliverTree.performLayout` never produces a
`SliverGeometry.scrollOffsetCorrection` (`grep -rn "scrollOffsetCorrection" lib`
returns 0 lines, run this session). Pass 2 measures every admitted row,
including rows in the LEADING cache band above `constraints.scrollOffset`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2812-2829`), and on any difference rewrites every
later offset (`:2819-2824`, `:2853` `_recomputeOffsetsFrom`), while
`constraints.scrollOffset` stays put. The unmeasured fallback is
`TreeController.defaultExtent = 48.0` (`tree_controller.dart:831`,
`:981-985 getEstimatedExtentNid`), so any row taller than 48 px shifts content
on first measurement. `RenderSliverList` emits a correction whenever the
leading child's placement moves
(`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/sliver_list.dart:148,158,191`),
and the viewport reruns layout in the same frame
(`rendering/viewport.dart:846-848` returns the correction,
`:1721-1740` applies `offset.correctBy` and retries, capped at
`_maxLayoutCyclesPerChild * childCount` = `:1685,1719`).

**Root cause.** Offsets are a GLOBAL prefix sum over the whole visible order
(Pass 1, `render_sliver_tree.dart:2636-2642`), not a per-child linked walk, so
a measurement anywhere above the viewport changes the ABSOLUTE offset of
everything below it. `_recomputeOffsetsFrom` (`:2358-2371`) keeps
`offset[fromIndex]` fixed and pushes the delta forward; nothing tells the
viewport that the anchor moved, so `pixels` and the offset array drift apart
by the accumulated measurement error. The doc at
`tree_controller.dart:1982-1985` ("the render pass that includes the target
will snap to the exact offset on the next frame") describes a snap that does
not exist in `_scroll_orchestrator.dart`.

**Solution.** Two changes, in two layers.

*(a) Render layer: anchor-preserving `scrollOffsetCorrection`.*
In `render_sliver_tree.dart` `performLayout`:

1. The anchor needs no capture and no binary search. It is `scrollOffset`
   itself, already a local at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2521`. The ANCHOR ROW
   is the row CONTAINING the viewport top under the offsets Pass 1 and
   admission just wrote (`_admitBulkFastPath` writes `_nodeOffsetsByNid` for
   every index it walks, `:455-457`), which is the row
   `_findFirstVisibleIndex(scrollOffset)` names. Rows strictly before it lie
   entirely above `scrollOffset`; the anchor row itself straddles the top and
   must grow DOWNWARD, so it contributes nothing. Step 2 tests that membership
   DIRECTLY, on offsets, rather than by comparing indices, which is what lets
   the accumulation survive M8's rewrite of the measurement loop (Chain 17
   below). `anchorIndex` stays this block's PROSE name for the anchor row's
   index, used by the test case's arithmetic below; after this change no such
   local exists in the code, and the earlier draft that captured one is
   withdrawn.

2. Add a frame-local accumulator (`double aboveAnchorDelta = 0.0;`, declared
   beside `extentsChanged` at `:2809-2810`), written only inside the existing
   extent-changed branch of the measurement loop (`:2819-2824`), so the
   steady-state path pays nothing:
   ```
   if (_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] + estimatedExtent <= scrollOffset &&
       !controller.isAnimatingNid(nid)) {
     aboveAnchorDelta += actualAnimatedExtent - estimatedExtent;
   }
   ```
   The first clause IS "this row lies entirely above the anchor", not an
   approximation of it. `_findFirstVisibleIndex` is a binary search for the
   first index whose END offset exceeds its argument, and its non-bulk arm is
   that comparison written on exactly these two arrays
   (`offset + extent <= scrollOffset` at `:3313`, over `_nodeOffsetsByNid` and
   `_nodeExtentsByNid` read at `:3310-3311`), so `i < anchorIndex` and the
   clause above are one predicate evaluated on one set of numbers. Both
   operands are already in hand and both are still PRE-measurement, which is
   the geometry the anchor is defined on: `estimatedExtent` is read at `:2818`,
   before the branch overwrites the slot at `:2820`, and
   `_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid]` is the value the loop's own parentData write reads
   two lines later (`:2828`), the loop writing no offsets at all. Freshness of
   that offset slot is not a new obligation: on a bulk frame
   `_admitBulkFastPath` writes it for every index it iterates before its break
   (`:455-457` precede `:459`), and after M8 this loop visits only admitted
   nids, which is the same set.

   `isAnimatingNid` is the O(1) nid mirror (`tree_controller.dart:866`,
   `_animation_coordinator.dart:904-909`). Excluding animating rows is the
   containment rule: a row whose extent is being driven by an expand/collapse
   is SUPPOSED to push content, and Pass 1 already accounts for that
   movement, so only the measurement residual is a correction.

   One caveat, recorded because it is real and because it is bounded. The
   bulk arm of the search compares `_offsetAtVisibleIndex(mid + 1)`
   (`:3274-3277`), while the clause compares the slot pair `:455-457` stores,
   i.e. `_offsetAtVisibleIndex(i)` plus
   `_offsetAtVisibleIndex(i + 1) - _offsetAtVisibleIndex(i)`. Those are equal
   algebraically and may differ by one ULP in Float64, so the two forms can
   disagree only for a row whose bottom lands within one ULP of the viewport
   top, and only by that row's measurement residual, inside a correction the
   next layout re-derives from scratch against the epsilon in step 5.

3. Mirror the same accumulation in the sticky force-create block
   (`:2961-2969`): `extent != priorExtent` there is the same class of
   measurement residual, and the loop is bounded by `newStickyNodes.length`
   (at most `maxStickyDepth` rows). This block lands AFTER M7, which supplies
   a full replacement body for the same nine lines (M7 Solution part 2,
   changing `priorExtent` at `:2963` from `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` to
   `controller.getCurrentExtentNid(nid)`, the forwarder at
   `tree_controller.dart:1026`), so the COMBINED body is stated once, here,
   and supersedes the body printed in M7:
   ```
   for (final nodeId in newStickyNodes) {
     final nid = _controller.nidOf(nodeId);
     // M7's comment block on the next line is unchanged, not repeated here.
     final priorExtent = controller.getCurrentExtentNid(nid);
     final extent = _layoutNodeChild(nodeId, crossAxisExtent);
     if (extent != null) {
       _nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = extent;
       if (extent != priorExtent) {
         stickyExtentsChanged = true;
         final visIdx = _controller.visibleIndexOfNid(nid);
         if (visIdx >= 0 &&
             _structuralOffsetAt(visIdx, nid) + priorExtent <= scrollOffset &&
             !controller.isAnimatingNid(nid)) {
           aboveAnchorDelta += extent - priorExtent;
         }
       }
     }
   }
   ```
   Three notes on that body. (i) The single-statement `if` at `:2967` becomes
   a braced block, per the house rule; M7's decision is otherwise untouched
   and its comment on the `priorExtent` line travels with it verbatim.
   (ii) The position test is step 2's geometric one, and it reads
   `_structuralOffsetAt(visIdx, nid)` (`:352-356`) rather than the raw offset
   slot, because these nids are outside the cache region by construction
   (`:2931`) and their raw slots are stale on a bulk frame, which is exactly
   the rule M7's Solution part 3 states for this block.
   `visibleIndexOfNid` is an O(1) `Int32List` read
   (`tree_controller.dart:969-972`), the same pair M7 part 3 item 1 already
   computes for the layoutOffset write at `:3000-3006`, and it runs only for a
   candidate whose extent actually changed. (iii) The test is a guard, not a
   formality, and an earlier draft of this step argued it away ("a
   force-created pinned header lives above the viewport by construction, so
   `visibleIndexOfNid(nid) < anchorIndex`"). Checked: the candidate walk gates
   a candidate's TOP against the band top (`naturalY > stackTop` breaks,
   `_sticky_header_computer.dart:383-384`) and retires it on
   `pinnedY + extent <= stackTop` (`:446`); neither gate asserts that the
   candidate's BOTTOM is above `scrollOffset`. The claim holds for every
   ordinary pinned header, and a header straddling the viewport top is
   normally admitted and so never reaches this loop, but the compare costs one
   add and does not depend on the argument being airtight.

4. Emit the correction ONCE, after the sticky block and before the
   paint-extent loop (insert at `:3029`, above `:3030`), so a single aborted
   cycle covers both measurement sources. The emit is BUDGETED PER FRAME (see
   step 4b, which is what keeps this inside the viewport's cycle cap):
   ```
   final bool wantsCorrection = correctionsAllowed &&
       aboveAnchorDelta.abs() > _kScrollCorrectionEpsilon;
   if (wantsCorrection && _correctionsThisFrame >= _kMaxCorrectionsPerFrame) {
     // Budget spent for this frame. Consume the rest next frame instead of
     // dropping it (see step 4b), then fall through and finish the layout.
     _scheduleCorrectionFollowUp();
   } else if (wantsCorrection) {
     _correctionsThisFrame++;
     _lastVisibleNodeCount = visibleNodes.length;
     _lastTotalScrollExtent = totalScrollExtent;
     _animationsWereActive = hasAnimations;
     geometry = SliverGeometry(scrollOffsetCorrection: aboveAnchorDelta);
     childManager?.didFinishLayout();
     return;
   }
   ```
   The three field writes replicate `:3253-3255` so the same-frame re-run
   starts from a consistent checkpoint: without them `:2516` would see
   `visibleNodes.length != _lastVisibleNodeCount` and force a redundant full
   Pass 1 walk, and the "pure scrolling" branch (`:2645-2648`) would reuse a
   stale `_lastTotalScrollExtent`. `didFinishLayout` is safe to call twice in
   one frame: it only flips `_inLayout` and calls `_scheduleStaleEviction`,
   which dedupes on `_staleEvictionScheduled` and defers the walk to a
   post-frame callback (`sliver_tree_element.dart:406-414`, `:461-470`).

4b. **Per-frame correction budget, and why the scheme terminates.** One new
   private field on `RenderSliverTree`, one constant, and one helper:
   ```
   int _correctionsThisFrame = 0;
   static const int _kMaxCorrectionsPerFrame = 2;

   /// Ask for one more layout so a correction the per-frame budget refused
   /// is applied on the next frame instead of being dropped.
   void _scheduleCorrectionFollowUp() {
     SchedulerBinding.instance.ensureVisualUpdate();
     SchedulerBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback((_) {
       if (attached) {
         markNeedsLayout();
       }
     });
   }
   ```
   `_correctionsThisFrame` needs NO frame identity and deliberately does not
   use one. It is reset at the single point in `performLayout` that is reached
   only by a layout which did NOT emit a correction, immediately before
   `geometry` is assigned for real (alongside the existing `_lastVisibleNodeCount`
   / `_lastTotalScrollExtent` writes at `render_sliver_tree.dart:3253-3255`):
   ```
   _correctionsThisFrame = 0;
   ```
   That is exactly the "this frame's layout settled" point, because the
   viewport re-runs `performLayout` after a correction and only stops when one
   returns without one (`viewport.dart:1721-1740`). Two mechanisms that look
   simpler were rejected: `SchedulerBinding.instance.currentFrameTimeStamp`
   does NOT advance across `tester.pump()` with no duration, so consecutive
   pumps would share a stamp and the budget would never reset under test; and
   `SchedulerBinding` exposes no public per-frame counter (`_debugFrameNumber`
   at `scheduler/binding.dart:1155` is private and debug-only).
   This is load-bearing, not defensive. `RenderViewport` re-runs
   `_attemptLayout` after every correction and throws once the loop exceeds
   `_maxLayoutCyclesPerChild * childCount` (`viewport.dart:1685`, `:1719`,
   `:1740-1742`), where `childCount` counts the viewport's SLIVER children:
   a single-sliver `CustomScrollView` gets exactly TEN cycles per frame.

   Without a budget the scheme can exceed that. The divergent case is rows
   SHORTER than `TreeController.defaultExtent` (48). Measuring a leading band
   of short rows produces a NEGATIVE correction, which moves the cache window
   UP in scroll space and exposes a fresh band of never-measured rows above
   the anchor; measuring those produces another negative correction, and with
   an 8 px row height each cycle exposes more rows than the last, so the loop
   grows rather than shrinks and blows the ten-cycle cap.

   The budget converts that into convergence over FRAMES instead of cycles:
   - At most two corrections per frame come from this sliver, so a
     single-sliver viewport uses at most two of its ten cycles and never
     throws. A viewport with other correcting slivers still has eight left.
   - Any residual is carried to the next frame BY AN EXPLICIT REQUEST, not by
     hope: the branch that refuses a correction calls
     `_scheduleCorrectionFollowUp`, which marks this sliver dirty in a
     post-frame callback. Nothing else guarantees another layout, since a
     viewport whose dimensions did not change schedules none
     (`IdleScrollActivity.applyNewDimensions`, `scroll_activity.dart:186-188`),
     so without this the third and later residuals of the short-row case would
     simply be dropped. On the next frame `aboveAnchorDelta` is recomputed
     from whatever is now measured and corrected again.
   - The process terminates because each correction consumes real
     over-estimate: a row's measured extent is stored once
     (`controller.setFullExtent`, `render_sliver_tree.dart:2400`) and a
     measured row never re-enters the unmeasured set except through a purge,
     so the total remaining residual, the sum of `|measured - estimate|` over
     rows above the anchor, strictly decreases and is finite. The visible
     result of a far jump into a region of very short rows is that the
     content settles over a few frames rather than one; the alternative
     today is a permanent mismatch, and the alternative without the budget is
     a thrown assertion.
   - Frame identity is deliberately NOT derived from
     `SchedulerBinding.instance.currentFrameTimeStamp`. That was the earlier
     design here and it is withdrawn: the stamp does not advance across a
     `tester.pump()` with no duration, so every such pump in a widget test
     would read as the same frame and the budget would refuse corrections
     that a real frame is entitled to. The self-resetting counter above
     needs no stamp, which is why it replaced it.

5. `_kScrollCorrectionEpsilon = 0.01` (new private const in
   `render_sliver_tree.dart`), NOT `precisionErrorTolerance` (1e-10,
   `foundation/constants.dart:71`): the offsets are a Float64 prefix sum over
   up to 10^5 rows, and a 1e-10 gate would let float drift emit corrections
   forever against the viewport's cycle cap.

6. `correctionsAllowed` = `!controller.hasActiveFlipSlides && !_composer.hasGhosts`
   (`tree_controller.dart:1332`, `_slide_composer.dart:90`). This is a
   RE-ENTRANCY gate, not a displacement gate, and that distinction is what
   picks the predicate.

   *It is not a displacement gate.* `aboveAnchorDelta` is accumulated
   exclusively from `_nodeOffsetsByNid` and `constraints.scrollOffset`, and
   `_nodeOffsetsByNid` is STRUCTURAL: every write to it is a prefix sum or a
   measured extent (`render_sliver_tree.dart:456`, `:2347`, `:2367`, `:2638`,
   `:2671`, `:2698`; `grep -n "_nodeOffsetsByNid\[" lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart`
   returns those six writes and nothing else). FLIP deltas and preview offsets
   are added at READ time instead, which is why painted position is spelled
   `_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] + controller.getSlideDeltaNid(nid)` at the two
   painted-position sites (`:2096`, `:2117`) and why the two terms are summed
   inside `getSlideDeltaNid` (`tree_controller.dart:1032-1041`). So a
   correction emitted while rows are displaced is NOT computed from displaced
   positions, by either engine, and "would the correction read a displaced
   position" cannot decide this predicate.

   *What it is a gate for.* The emit in step 4 ABORTS the method and the
   viewport re-runs it at a different `constraints.scrollOffset`
   (`viewport.dart:1721-1740`). Two things in the pre-Pass-1 slide pipeline
   are once-per-frame and would be wrong or lost on the second run:
   - `_composer.ghosts.normalizeForViewport` at `:2558-2563`, which fires on
     `scrollChanged` and would run a second time in the same frame at a
     different scroll value. Covered by `!_composer.hasGhosts`.
   - `_consumeSlideBaselineIfAny` at `:2564`, whose slot is CONSUME-ONCE
     (`:901` `_composer.baselineSlot.consume()`, `:902` returns on null) and
     which binds the slides it installs to THIS frame's viewport: it rewrites
     each ghost entry's base through
     `_composer.baseFor(ghostKey, currentViewport)` (`:958`) and states at
     `:972-975` that new edge anchors created in the consume use
     `currentViewport`. The re-run gets `null` from the slot and can redo none
     of it. This is NOT covered by the ghost term, because a baseline consume
     can install slides on a frame with no ghosts at all; it IS covered by
     `!controller.hasActiveFlipSlides`, because a consume on this run leaves
     `_slide.hasActive` true by the time control reaches the emit site at
     `:3029`. The FLIP term is therefore load-bearing on its own and is not a
     restatement of the ghost term.

   *Why FLIP-only and not the composed `hasActiveSlides`.* This is a
   correctness choice, not a documentation convenience. `hasActiveSlides` is
   `_slide.hasActive || _preview.hasActive` (`tree_controller.dart:1315`) and
   a preview offset is HELD, so the composed read is true from a drag's first
   resolve to its release. Gating on it would refuse every correction for the
   whole of a drag, and a drag is both the period when the correction matters
   most and the period when it survives:
   - It survives. `AutoScroller._onTick` integrates RELATIVELY off the current
     position, `newPixels = position.pixels + velocity * dt` then
     `position.jumpTo(newPixels)`
     (`_drag_session_behaviors.dart:135-141`, class at `:31`), so a
     `correctBy` applied since the previous tick is carried forward. That is
     the opposite of `DrivenScrollActivity._tick`, which calls
     `applyMoveTo(_controller.value)` with an ABSOLUTE value
     (`widgets/scroll_activity.dart:750-754`) and overwrites it, which is the
     case part (b) exists to clean up after.
   - It matters most. `PointerSpace.sample` maps the pointer through
     `position.pixels + local.dy - precedingScrollExtent`
     (`_drag_session.dart:90-93`). An autoscroll that measures a leading band
     of never-measured rows moves every row offset while `pixels` stays put,
     so WITHOUT a correction the resolved drop target jumps by exactly the
     residual the correction absorbs. Refusing corrections during a drag does
     not make the drag safer; it reintroduces the bug into the one interaction
     that reads the offset array against `pixels` on every pointer event.
   - The preview is not disturbed by a correction. Its targets are relative
     shifts built from `lift`, never absolute offsets
     (`tree_controller.dart:1762-1777`), so moving `pixels` and the offset
     array together leaves every shift target valid.

   The gate is also what keeps the exact-layout-count perf pins intact (see
   Risk). This read is a NEW member of the FLIP-only carve-out family and is
   recorded as one: see "Carve-out inventory" under Risk, and the M10
   sequencing note below for how the delta is written.

*(b) Controller layer: post-frame settle snap for `animateScrollToKey`.*
The correction keeps `pixels` and the offset array in one coordinate system,
which alone fixes the "lands 312 px off" symptom when the caller supplies no
`extentEstimator` (both `scrollOffsetOf` via `fullOffsetAt`/
`getEstimatedExtentNid` and render Pass 1 via `getCurrentExtentNid` fall back
to the same `defaultExtent`). It does NOT fix the case where the caller
passes an `extentEstimator` that disagrees with `defaultExtent`
(`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:134-156` takes the slow path and uses the
estimator; the render layer never sees it), and it cannot fix
`position.animateTo`, whose `DrivenScrollActivity._tick` calls
`applyMoveTo(_controller.value)` with an ABSOLUTE pixel value every tick
(`widgets/scroll_activity.dart:750-754`) and therefore overwrites any
correction applied since the previous tick.

Add to `ScrollOrchestrator` (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart`) a single-shot
post-frame snap, scheduled (not awaited) from both terminal branches of
`animateScrollToKey` (`:270-274`):

```
void _scheduleSettleSnap({key, scrollController, alignment, sliverBaseOffset, extentEstimator})
```
- One pending slot (`bool _snapScheduled` plus the captured request), newest
  wins; cleared in `dispose` (`:480-490`).
- Registers `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback` once. In the
  callback: bail on `_disposed`, on `!scrollController.hasClients`, on
  `_activeScroll != null` (the follower owns the position), and on
  `position.userScrollDirection != ScrollDirection.idle` (a user drag or
  fling took over). `ScrollDirection` needs an explicit
  `import 'package:flutter/rendering.dart' show ScrollDirection;` because
  `widgets.dart` re-exports `rendering.dart` only `show TextSelectionHandleType`
  (`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/widgets.dart:19`). Verified: `jumpTo` does
  leave `userScrollDirection` idle, because it calls `goIdle()` and
  `beginActivity` publishes the new activity's direction, which for
  `IdleScrollActivity` is `ScrollDirection.idle`
  (`scroll_position_with_single_context.dart:123-125`, `:197-207`). So the
  guard rejects exactly a user drag or fling, which is what it is for.
- Recompute `sliverOffset = scrollOffsetOf(key, extentEstimator: ...)`,
  `rowExtent = extentOf(...)`, `target = sliverBaseOffset + sliverOffset -
  (viewportDimension - rowExtent) * alignment`, clamp, and
  `position.jumpTo(clamped)` only when
  `(clamped - position.pixels).abs() > 0.5`.
- Exactly one iteration, never rescheduled from inside itself. With (a) in
  place this converges: with no estimator the first re-derive already equals
  `pixels`; with an estimator it removes the whole
  `sum over measured rows of (measured - defaultExtent)` residual and leaves
  only `(estimator - defaultExtent) * (unmeasured rows before the target)`,
  which no amount of iteration can remove without measuring those rows.

The returned Future is unchanged in timing: it still resolves right after
`jumpTo` (duration zero) or after `animateTo` completes. The snap lands on
the next frame, which is precisely what `tree_controller.dart:1982-1985`
already documents.

**Sequencing dependency (Chain 16, M7 then H1).** M7 and this block both
rewrite the sticky force-create loop at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2961-2969`.

**Alternatives considered.**
- *Diff the anchor's stored offset before/after Pass 2 instead of an explicit
  accumulator.* Rejected: it cannot distinguish an animation-driven shift
  from a measurement residual (both land in `_nodeOffsetsByNid` via
  `_recomputeOffsetsFrom`), so every expand above the viewport would be
  "corrected" and fight its own animation. The explicit accumulator is also
  cheaper (no second `_findFirstVisibleIndex`-class read after the recompute).
- *Route every non-zero-duration scroll through `_animatedConcurrentScroll`
  so the target is re-derived per tick.* Rejected on behavior, not cost: that
  follower drives the position with `jumpTo` every tick (`:386-388`), which
  replaces `animateTo`'s real `ScrollActivity` (user-interruptible, ballistic
  handoff) with a forced-pixels loop for ALL scrolls. Reserved for H3's
  narrow case.
- *Estimate-free layout (measure every row).* Rejected: O(N) per frame,
  destroys the whole nid/prefix-sum design.

**Architecture fit.** (a) belongs to `RenderSliverTree`: the sliver protocol
makes `scrollOffsetCorrection` the render object's obligation, and the
anchor/correction arithmetic is pure sliver-scroll-space work, the space
`SliverTreeParentData.layoutOffset` and `_nodeOffsetsByNid` already speak. It
adds no new coordinate space and no new notification channel. (b) belongs to
`ScrollOrchestrator`, which already owns the frame-wait pattern
(`:246-251`), the single-flight session slot, and the final-snap idiom
(`:452-468`); the snap reuses `scrollOffsetOf`/`extentOf`/`fullOffsetAt`
rather than adding a second offset source. `isAnimatingNid` /
`hasActiveFlipSlides` / `_composer.hasGhosts` are all existing predicates
read at their existing meanings; no new flag is introduced and no code
outside the boundary re-derives whether a row is animating. The one thing
this block does add to a shared surface is a read location in the FLIP-only
carve-out family, asking a question none of its existing categories asks;
that is a documentation obligation, discharged under Risk and against M10's
counting rule, not a new mechanism.

**Performance.** Steady state (no measurement residual): NO extra binary
search. The anchor test is an offset compare on two values the measurement
loop already holds (`:2818`, `:2828`) against a constraint local (`:2521`), so
the added steady-state cost is one `double` compare at `:3029` and nothing per
row until an extent actually changes. (An earlier draft captured `anchorIndex`
with a third `_findFirstVisibleIndex` per layout and priced it against the two
at `:2736` and `:3035`; step 2's offset form removes that search, and M7
removes the `:3035` one outright.) Zero allocations. Inside the measurement
loop the added work is one double add and one compare for the anchor test,
plus one `isAnimatingNid` (a `Uint8List` read behind `ensureAnimatingKeys()`,
already called elsewhere in the same frame) and one double add for the
accumulation itself, and only in the branch that already fired
because an extent changed, so the cache-hit path is unchanged. When a
correction IS emitted the
frame runs `performLayout` at most three times (up to
`_kMaxCorrectionsPerFrame` = 2 aborted runs plus the settled one): each later run takes Pass 1's
"pure scrolling" or "transitional" branch, re-admits, and re-measures against
`RenderBox.layout`'s constraint-unchanged short-circuit, so the dominant
cost is one extra admission walk plus one `ViewportSnapshot` allocation
(`:1393-1400`). Corrections fire only while rows above the anchor are being
measured for the first time, i.e. once per newly-entered leading band, not
per frame; the converged state emits none. `_scheduleSettleSnap` is one
post-frame callback, one `fullOffsetAt` (O(1) amortized off the prefix cache,
`:94-119`) and at most one `jumpTo` per `animateScrollToKey` call.

**Risk.** Reads of this path: `_findFirstVisibleIndex` also serves
`findRowAtPaintedY` (`ReorderRenderPort`) and the sticky probe, both of which
read the SAME arrays the correction keeps consistent with `pixels`, so they
gain rather than lose. Mid-drag: `offset.correctBy` mutates `_pixels` without
notifying (`widgets/scroll_position.dart:458-465`), and `PointerSpace.sample`
computes `sliverY = position.pixels + local.dy - precedingScrollExtent`
(`_drag_session.dart:88-96`); the correction moves `pixels` and every row
offset by the same amount, so the pointer-to-row mapping is invariant and the
autoscroller's viewport-local `local.dy` is untouched. Mid-animation: the
`!isAnimatingNid` filter means an expand/collapse emits no correction of its
own, and that includes a first-frame enter: an entering row IS animating, so
the filter excludes it while it animates, and its measured extent is folded in
by the ordinary path on the first settled layout after the animation ends,
where the filter no longer excludes it. (An earlier draft of this sentence
claimed such a row "emits exactly one" correction, which contradicts the
filter it sits next to.) Mid `animateTo`: the correction is applied
and then overwritten by the next `DrivenScrollActivity` tick, so the net
visual result is no worse than today plus one extra layout cycle per frame of
that scroll; the settle snap fixes the landing.

### H2. Admission starves the viewport below a row taller than the cache extent

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, chain 1 commit, landed last as specified. Part (d) landed first (the repro reads the pin); `audit_repro_h2_test.dart` pre-fix reds: case 1 at r11, scroll 600 (the first refused intersecting row), case 2 at f9, matching the block's f9..f17 against the post-M8 admission (f0..f8 admitted). Parts (a) and (b) landed in `LayoutAdmissionPolicy.admit`: the seed (its first term on the bulk arm from the view, as the Sequencing paragraph requires, shared with `postOffsetOrigin`), the hoisted animation reads, the guarded floor on both the two-view stop and M8's bulk live-cut break, and the widened admit decision; the collapse phase's threshold folds to `budgetCap - seed`. Part (c) withdrawn exactly as written (M8's Step 2a deleted its target). The two direct unit cases Risk requires were added to `layout_admission_policy_test.dart` and each shown red under targeted disablement (seed zeroed: end 7 not 8; floor forced false: end 1 not 7); the three existing call sites gained the new arguments with unchanged expectations. Doc items landed per the ownership split. Full suite green.

**Finding.** `LayoutAdmissionPolicy.admit` seeds both accumulators at 0 at
`cacheStartIndex` (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:67-68`) and charges a
non-animating row its whole extent (`:119-121`), while `budgetCap` is
`remainingCacheExtent + slideOverreach * 2.0` (`:78`), i.e. the width of the
window `[effectiveCacheStart, effectiveCacheEnd)` computed at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:2594-2595`. `cacheStartIndex` is the row CONTAINING
`effectiveCacheStart` (`:2736`, `_findFirstVisibleIndex` at `:3264-3320`
returns the first index whose `offset + extent > x`), so the part of the
leading row lying ABOVE the window is charged against the window's budget.
The bulk path repeats the flaw: `fullCacheEnd` is anchored at the leading
row's full-space TOP (`:2745-2749`).

**Root cause.** The accumulators measure the span from the LEADING ROW'S TOP
(`:67-68` seeds both at 0 at `cacheStartIndex`) and are compared against a cap
that measures a WINDOW (`:78`: `remainingCacheExtent + slideOverreach * 2.0`,
the width of `[effectiveCacheStart, effectiveCacheEnd)`). The two agree only
when the leading row's top coincides with the window's start. The overcharge
equals `effectiveCacheStart - nodeOffsetsByNid[first]`, which is bounded by
the leading row's extent, so it is invisible for 48 px rows and becomes a
viewport-sized hole once a row approaches the cache extent (the review
measured 415 blank px for a 700 px row).

The comment at `:109-111` is part of the defect, not evidence about it, and
this block rewrites it. Read together with `:74-77`, the file says in one
place that the budget is "measured over every row the loop has considered"
and in another that the cap "must cover the full widened interval", and
nowhere that those are two different quantities; a reader checking the
comparison at `:85-88` against them concludes it is sound. Part (a) then makes
`:109-111` flatly false as well, because the accumulators stop starting at
zero. Both comments, and every other comment these three changes falsify or
leave silent on a new term, are rewritten in the same commit under Doc changes
below.

**Solution.** Three independent changes in the admission path, plus one debug
surface the test needs.

*(a) Seed the accumulators with the leading row's out-of-window part.*
`_layout_admission_policy.dart`: add a required `double effectiveCacheStart`
parameter to `admit` and replace `:67-68` with
```
final double seed = cacheStartIndex < visibleNodes.length
    ? nodeOffsetsByNid[orderNids[cacheStartIndex]] - effectiveCacheStart
    : 0.0;
double liveAccum = seed;
double postAccum = seed;
```
(`orderNids` is already fetched at `:69`; the same
`cacheStartIndex < visibleNodes.length` guard already exists at `:70-72` for
`postOffsetOrigin`.) `seed` is <= 0 in the scrolled case, so the leading row
stops eating budget it never occupies, and is > 0 when the window starts
before the content (scroll offset 0 with a non-zero `slideOverreach`, where
`effectiveCacheStart` is negative), which correctly cancels the unusable half
of `slideOverreach * 2.0`. Caller: `render_sliver_tree.dart:2774-2784` passes
`effectiveCacheStart: effectiveCacheStart` (already in scope from `:2594`).

This does NOT weaken the mass-mount cap. The cap comes from `:114-117`
charging an ANIMATING row its `getEstimatedExtentNid` (full) extent while its
live offset reflects the shrunken animated position; the seed is a one-time
constant bounded by one row's height and leaves that asymmetry untouched.

*(b) A geometric floor: never refuse a non-animating row that intersects the
paint region.* Add required `double paintRegionStart` and
`double paintRegionEnd` to `admit` (caller passes `scrollOffset` and
`scrollOffset + remainingPaintExtent`, both already local at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:2521-2522`). Inside the loop:
The animation reads MOVE ABOVE the break (they sit at `:100-101` today, below
it), because the floor must carry the same `!isAnimating` guard in BOTH the
break and the admit decision:
```
final bool isAnimating = _controller.isAnimatingNid(nid);
final bool isExit = isAnimating && _controller.isExitingNid(nid);
final double liveExtent = nodeExtentsByNid[nid];
final bool paintFloor = !isAnimating &&
    liveOffset < paintRegionEnd &&
    liveOffset + liveExtent > paintRegionStart;
```
- `:92-94` becomes `if (!liveBudgetOk && !postBudgetOk && !paintFloor) break;`
- `:102` becomes
  `final bool admit = liveBudgetOk || (!isExit && postBudgetOk) || paintFloor;`

Guarding the BREAK, not only the admit clause, is the whole point. An
unguarded floor term (`intersectsPaint` without `!isAnimating`) would leave
admissions correct but destroy the loop bound: on frame 1 of an animated
`expand` of a large subtree the entering rows sit at sub-pixel live extents
packed inside the paint region, so the floor term stays true across the entire
entering subtree, the break never fires, and a loop that stops after roughly
23 rows today would walk thousands, paying `isAnimatingNid` and
`getEstimatedExtentNid` per row on every frame of the animation. With the
guard, animating rows contribute nothing to either decision and the loop
stops where it does today.

Termination is preserved: `liveOffset` is monotonically non-decreasing across
the loop, so once `liveOffset >= paintRegionEnd` the floor is false for every
later row, animating or not, and the original break condition applies. The
extra iterations the floor can add are bounded by the count of NON-ANIMATING
rows inside the paint region, which is exactly the set that must be built for
the viewport not to be blank.

Cost of the move: the two `isAnimatingNid` / `isExitingNid` reads (both
`Uint8List` reads behind the coordinator's union mirror) now also run for the
single row that triggers the break, and no longer run at all for rows past it,
since the loop exits before them. Net per-layout change is one extra pair of
array reads.

*(c) Bulk path.* In `render_sliver_tree.dart`, replace the `fullCacheEnd`
computation at `:2744-2752` with a full-space anchor at the window start
rather than the row top:
```
final double liveTop = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(cacheStartIndex);
final double liveBottom = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(cacheStartIndex + 1);
final double fullTop = _stableCumulative[cacheStartIndex] +
    _bulkFullCumulative[cacheStartIndex];
final double fullBottom = _stableCumulative[cacheStartIndex + 1] +
    _bulkFullCumulative[cacheStartIndex + 1];
final double liveSpan = liveBottom - liveTop;
final double f = liveSpan <= 0.0
    ? 0.0
    : ((effectiveCacheStart - liveTop) / liveSpan).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
fullCacheEnd = fullTop + f * (fullBottom - fullTop) +
    remainingCacheExtent + slideOverreach * 2.0;
```
`f` is the fraction of the leading row that lies above the window, measured
in live space; scaling the row's FULL span by it maps that overhang into full
space, which is exact whenever the leading row is not a bulk member (live
extent equals full extent) and monotone otherwise. Then give
`_admitBulkFastPath` (`:446-465`) the same paint-region floor: pass the
already-fetched `BulkAnimationData<TKey> bulkData` (`:2605`) plus
`paintRegionStart`/`paintRegionEnd`, and change `:459` to
```
final bool intersectsPaint = offset < paintRegionEnd &&
    offset + _nodeExtentsByNid[nid] > paintRegionStart;
if (fullOffset >= fullCacheEnd &&
    !(intersectsPaint && !bulkData.containsMemberNid(nid))) {
  break;
}
```
`containsMemberNid` is an O(1) `Uint8List` read (`types.dart:479-484`).
Both the extent and the offset on that line are already computed at
`:455-457`.

```dart
  /// "where the row is now" and "where it will end up" disagree:
```

   with:

```dart
  /// Two accumulators run in parallel, because an extent animation makes
  /// "where the row is now" and "where it will end up" disagree:
  ///
  /// - liveAccum tracks the current layout, charging animating rows their
  ///   FULL extent. That fills the budget faster during an enter, which
  ///   is what holds admission near the pre-animation row count instead
  ///   of mass-mounting the entering subtree on frame 1 of an expand.
  /// - postAccum tracks the post-animation layout, charging each row its
  ///   target extent: full for enters, 0 for exits, live otherwise.
  ///
  /// Both are spent against `budgetCap`, which is the width of the WINDOW
  /// `[effectiveCacheStart, effectiveCacheEnd)`, so both have to measure
  /// that same window. The walk starts at the row CONTAINING
  /// [effectiveCacheStart], not at a row whose top coincides with it, so
  /// both start at the seed `nodeOffsetsByNid[first] - effectiveCacheStart`,
  /// the signed distance from the window's start to the leading row's top
  /// (0 when the walk starts past the end of the visible order). The seed is
  /// negative in the scrolled case, handing back the part of the leading row
  /// that lies ABOVE the window and that the window's budget must not be
  /// charged for; it is positive when the window starts before the content
  /// (scroll offset 0 with a non-zero [slideOverreach], where
  /// [effectiveCacheStart] is negative), which cancels the leading half of
  /// `slideOverreach * 2.0` that no row can occupy.
  ///
  /// Admission is then a THREE-WAY decision:
  ///
  /// - either budget view has room, except that an exit can only be
  ///   admitted through the live view, having no post-animation position
  ///   worth pre-mounting for;
  /// - or the PAINT FLOOR holds: the row is NOT animating and its live span
  ///   intersects `[paintRegionStart, paintRegionEnd)`, the region the
  ///   caller passes as `scrollOffset` and
  ///   `scrollOffset + remainingPaintExtent`.
  ///
  /// The floor is geometric, not budgeted, and it exists because the budget
  /// views can be exhausted while later rows are still on screen: one row
  /// taller than the cache extent does it on its own, and a row the viewport
  /// paints but nobody built is a blank band. Animating rows are excluded
  /// from the floor, so an enter's sub-pixel rows cannot reach it and the
  /// mass-mount cap the two views impose is untouched.
  ///
  /// The loop stops once both views agree no later row could be admitted
  /// AND the floor does not hold for the current row. That still terminates:
  /// live offsets are monotonically non-decreasing, so once a row's
  /// `liveOffset` reaches [paintRegionEnd] the floor is false for every
  /// later row, animating or not, and the two-view stop condition applies
  /// unchanged.
  ///
  /// The stop is CONSERVATIVE where both views are exhausted at an
  /// ANIMATING row whose live offset is still inside the paint region: the
  /// walk ends at that row, so the floor reaches no further. It still
  /// admits no fewer rows than it did before the floor existed, both the
  /// stop and the admission only gained a disjunct, but it does mean the
  /// floor does not repair a blank band that begins below such a row.
```

2. `_layout_admission_policy.dart:74-77`, above `budgetCap`. Not false today,
   and left standing it is one half of the mismatch the Root cause describes:
   it is where the file says what the cap measures, and after (a) it must also
   say what makes the accumulators measure the same thing. Replace:

```dart
    // The admission walk starts at `cacheStart - slideOverreach` and may
    // continue through `cacheEnd + slideOverreach`. Rows from both widened
    // sides consume accumulator budget, so the cap must cover the full
    // widened interval, not just one extra side.
```

   with:

```dart
    // The admission walk starts at the row CONTAINING
    // `cacheStart - slideOverreach` and may continue through
    // `cacheEnd + slideOverreach`. Rows from both widened sides consume
    // accumulator budget, so the cap must cover the full widened interval,
    // not just one extra side. The cap therefore measures an INTERVAL, and
    // the seed above is what makes the accumulators measure the same one:
    // without it the leading row is charged in full while occupying only
    // the part of itself that falls inside that interval.
```

   with:

```dart
      // [isAnimatingNid] and [isExitingNid] are O(1) (nid-keyed mirror).
      // Read BEFORE the break, not after it: the floor below is guarded on
      // `!isAnimating` and the break consults that same floor, so both
      // decisions need this row's animation state.
      final bool isAnimating = _controller.isAnimatingNid(nid);
      final bool isExit = isAnimating && _controller.isExitingNid(nid);
      final double liveExtent = nodeExtentsByNid[nid];

      // The paint floor: a NON-ANIMATING row whose live span intersects the
      // paint region is admitted whatever the two budget views say, because
      // the viewport paints it and a row nobody built paints as a blank
      // band. A single row taller than the cache extent exhausts both views
      // on its own, which is how rows still on screen below it came to be
      // refused. Animating rows are excluded deliberately: on frame 1 of an
      // expand the entering subtree sits at sub-pixel extents packed inside
      // the paint region, so an unguarded floor would hold this loop open
      // across the whole subtree and destroy its bound.
      final bool paintFloor = !isAnimating &&
          liveOffset < paintRegionEnd &&
          liveOffset + liveExtent > paintRegionStart;

      // Stop at the first row that fails BOTH views and the floor. That
      // terminates: `liveOffset` and both accumulators only grow, so a view
      // that has failed stays failed for every later row, and the floor can
      // hold only while `liveOffset < paintRegionEnd`, which is a prefix of
      // the walk. Past the point where both views fail, the loop therefore
      // runs only through rows the floor admits, at most one paint region's
      // worth of them.
      //
      // The stop is CONSERVATIVE, and that is the whole of what the guarded
      // floor gives up. The floor is guarded on `!isAnimating`, so if both
      // views are exhausted at an ANIMATING row whose live offset is still
      // inside the paint region (the accumulator update below charges an
      // animating row its FULL extent while its live offset reflects the
      // shrunken animated position, which is what caps mass-mounting on
      // frame 1 of an expand), the walk ends at that row even though a
      // later NON-animating row at the same live offset would have
      // satisfied the floor. Ending there admits no fewer rows than this
      // loop admitted before the floor existed, since both the stop and the
      // admission below only gained a disjunct; it bounds how far the floor
      // reaches, it does not change what an expand mounts. Breaking on
      // `liveOffset >= paintRegionEnd` instead would reach those rows and

      // exactly what the guard exists to prevent. A row below the stop that
      // was mounted on an earlier frame still paints in the right place:
      // the post-sticky parentData refresh rewrites `layoutOffset` for
      // mounted off-cache rows.
      if (!liveBudgetOk && !postBudgetOk && !paintFloor) {
        break;

      // Exits admit through the LIVE view only; they have no post-animation
      // position and should not be pre-mounted just because the post view
      // has budget. The floor cannot admit one either, being guarded on
      // `!isAnimating`.
      final bool admit =
          liveBudgetOk || (!isExit && postBudgetOk) || paintFloor;
```

```dart
/// Cache-region admission policy. Decides which visible-order positions
/// should be admitted into the cache region during Pass 2 of the layout.
///
/// BOTH arms of Pass 2 decide here, under one copy of the rule. The
/// NON-BULK arm reads each row's position and extent from the render
/// object's per-nid slots, and weighs where the row is now against where
/// it ends up, because an extent animation makes the two disagree. The
/// BULK arm passes a [BulkAdmissionView] instead, and the same two views
/// take closed forms on it: the live position is
/// `stableCumulative[i] + value * fullCumulative[i]`, and the post view
/// charges 0 for a member of a COLLAPSING group. That post view is the one
/// the render object's old inline bulk loop never grew, which is why rows
/// after a collapsing subtree were never pre-mounted however far the
/// subtree had shrunk.
///
/// A collapse resolves that post view WITHOUT a walk: every member charges
/// 0, so its admissible set is a prefix found by binary search on
/// `stableCumulative`, and the survivors inside it are reached by
/// survivor-to-survivor hops. A 200k-row `collapseAll` therefore does not
/// pay O(N) per frame, which is the whole reason the bulk fast path exists.
///
/// A row taller than the cache extent can exhaust both weighings while
/// later rows are still on screen, which is what the paint-region floor
/// exists to prevent.
///
/// This class writes exactly one piece of render state, the
/// `inCacheRegionByNid` flag whose meaning it owns. The per-nid offset and
/// extent slots stay the render object's: on the bulk arm its
/// [onCacheRegionAdmit] callback writes them for each admitted row.
```

```dart
  /// Admits cache-region members under the bulk-only fast path.
  ///
  /// Invoked from Pass 2 when [_bulkCumulativesValid] is true. A row's
  /// OFFSET comes from the precomputed cumulatives, through
  /// [_offsetAtVisibleIndex]; its EXTENT does not, it is
  /// [TreeController.getEstimatedExtentNid] times the cached group value
  /// for a bulk member and that estimate unscaled for a non-member, which
  /// is bitwise what the Pass 2 measurement computes, so the exact `!=`
  /// there fires only on a real height change. Both are synced into the
  /// per-nid slots so downstream code (Pass 2 measurement, paint,
  /// hit-test) reads correct values without a branch per access. Anchors
  /// the admission band to full-space (`fullCacheEnd`) so a low bulk
  /// progress value doesn't admit thousands of sub-pixel rows on frame 1
  /// of `expandAll`. The caller anchors that band at the full-space IMAGE
  /// of the window start, not at the leading row's full-space top, so a
  /// leading row straddling the window start cannot shorten the band by
  /// its own overhang.
  ///
  /// One exception to the band, mirroring the paint floor in
  /// [LayoutAdmissionPolicy.admit]: a row that is NOT a member of the
  /// running bulk group and whose live span intersects
  /// `[paintRegionStart, paintRegionEnd)` is admitted even past
  /// `fullCacheEnd`, because the viewport paints it. Members are excluded
  /// through [BulkAnimationData.containsMemberNid], an O(1) nid-indexed
  /// read (`types.dart:479-484`), which is what stops a low progress value
  /// from admitting the entering subtree through the exception. The
  /// exception is conservative in the same way its non-bulk twin is: the
  /// break still fires at the first MEMBER past `fullCacheEnd`, so it
  /// reaches no further than that row even if later non-members paint.
  ///
  /// The caller owns the outer-loop dispatch; this method performs the
  /// per-row writes and sparse-track buffer maintenance for the admitted
  /// range.
```

true, and the reason is the one M8's own Repository-level docs note gives,
not this block's earlier one. An earlier draft justified it with "the policy
still owns the non-bulk cache-region decision, the floor lives inside it, and
the bulk half stays inline on the render object"; the last clause is false
after M8's Step 3a, which deletes the inline bulk loop. The verdict survives
the correction: after M8 the policy owns BOTH arms, so "cache-region admission
via `LayoutAdmissionPolicy`" gets truer rather than falser, the floor lives
inside it either way, and "bulk-only cumulative fast path" still names what

binary searches and its admit callback both read. Neither
file states the accumulator rule, the cap, or the paint region
(`grep -ni "accumulator\|budget\|paint region\|admit\|admission" CLAUDE.md
AGENTS.md`, run this session: the only other hit is `CLAUDE.md:76`'s "layout
ADMITS preview-shifted rows (`RenderSliverTree.admittedSlideBound`)", which
this block does not touch). No `CHANGELOG.md` entry either: this is a
rendering-correctness repair with no API change and no change to documented
public behavior.

**Alternatives considered.**
- *Offset-only admission (drop the accumulators, admit purely on
  `liveOffset < effectiveCacheEnd`).* Rejected: the accumulators exist
  precisely because an animating row's live offset is not where it will be,
  and dropping them reinstates the mass-mount spike that
  `sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:787-884` pins ("2.5k rebuilds for 2.7k
  children").
- *Start the walk at `cacheStartIndex + 1` when the leading row is mostly
  above the window.* Rejected: the leading row still has to be BUILT (it
  paints), so skipping it trades a blank band at the bottom for a blank band
  at the top.
- *Widen `budgetCap` by a fudge factor proportional to the tallest measured
  row.* Rejected: it is a magic number that scales the overbuild for every
  tree, whereas the seed is the exact quantity being double-counted.

**Sequencing dependency.** Chain 1 in the plan's Sequencing section is M6, then
M7, then M8, then H2. All four edit the same bulk admission and measurement
path, and this block is written to land last.

inline in `render_sliver_tree.dart` or moves behind `LayoutAdmissionPolicy`.
That question is SETTLED in favour of unifying, and M8's Step 2a settles the
consequence for this block: part (c) has no target, because Step 2a deletes
the `fullCacheEnd` computation part (c) rewrites. Both halves of part (c) are
carried instead by parts (a) and (b) applied to the unified policy, the
re-anchor by part (a)'s seed and the member-excluded paint floor by part (b)'s
floor over M8's `BulkAdmissionView`, and Doc changes item 7 is withdrawn for

draft of this paragraph said. Part (a)'s seed reads
`nodeOffsetsByNid[orderNids[cacheStartIndex]]`, a slot M8's Step 3a writes only
for ADMITTED rows, so on the bulk arm the seed's first term must instead be
`bulkView.stableCumulative[cs] + bulkView.value * bulkView.fullCumulative[cs]`,
the same substitution Step 3a already forces on part (b)'s
`nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` read. With that substitution the seed also closes a
corner M8's Step 2a records and accepts: on the bulk arm the unified predicate
gains a live-position conjunct `liveOffset(i) < effectiveCacheEnd` that today's
bulk break does not have, it can refuse a row only where the seed is positive,
and the seed cancels exactly that.

Parts (a) and (b) are otherwise independent of M8. Part (d) is NOT, and an

parameter and caches nothing between calls, holding only a re-bindable
back-pointer to its `TreeController`
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:1-9`, `:22-35`), so `effectiveCacheStart` /
`paintRegionStart` / `paintRegionEnd` join `effectiveCacheEnd` /
`slideOverreach` / `remainingCacheExtent` (`:62-64`, inside the signature at
`:55-65`) as three more frame inputs; nothing new is stored.
