**Performance.** (a) is one subtraction and two assignments per layout, O(1),
zero allocations; it strictly REDUCES the admitted set at the top of the list
(seed > 0) and increases it by at most one leading row's worth elsewhere.
(b) adds two double compares and one already-loaded array read per iteration
of a loop bounded by the cache region (about one viewport of rows), and
changes the loop's worst-case bound from "budget exhausted" to
"`liveOffset >= paintRegionEnd`", which is a bound the paint loop
(`:3037-3055`) and hit-test already walk every frame anyway. (c) is 6 typed
reads, one divide and one clamp per layout on bulk frames only, plus one
`Uint8List` read per bulk-path iteration. No allocations anywhere. Net
per-frame mount count is unchanged for uniform short-row trees and grows by
exactly the rows that were being skipped while visible.

**Risk.** Callers of `admit`: one production site
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2774`) and three in
`test/sliver_tree/layout_admission_policy_test.dart:61,85,104`
(`grep -rn "\.admit(" lib test` this session). The three test calls must gain
the new required arguments; traced by hand, their expectations do not change:
at `:61` `effectiveCacheStart: 0.0` gives `seed == 0`, at `:85`
`effectiveCacheStart: 250.0` equals `nodeOffsetsByNid[first]` so `seed == 0`
again, and passing `paintRegionStart: 0.0, paintRegionEnd: 0.0` makes the
floor inert, so `end` stays 4 and 7. New cases should then be added there for
the tall-leading-row seed and the floor.

`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:787-884` (collapse must not mass-mount 200
children, rows 48 px, all exits animating so the floor excludes them),

      contract, every row intersecting the viewport is built on that
      frame, not one of the two mechanisms behind it.

      Separating them at the unit level IS reachable after chain 1, and an
      earlier draft of this note concluded the opposite: "separating them
      would need a unit hook into `_admitBulkFastPath`, which is private

      `:2768-2772`) and routes both arms through

      DECISION: add the direct cases, and KEEP this widget case too.

      The direct cases are already committed to: Risk requires those same
      three call sites to gain part (a)'s and part (b)'s new required
      arguments, and states that new cases "should then be added there for
      the tall-leading-row seed and the floor". Those two are exactly what
      this note wants, and each isolates one mechanism using the arguments
      Risk already traces: a seed case with the floor made inert
      (`paintRegionStart: 0.0, paintRegionEnd: 0.0`) and a leading row
      whose top is above `effectiveCacheStart`, which pins part (a) alone;
      and a floor case with both budgets exhausted by one tall row, which
      pins part (b) alone. Whether the BULK arm can additionally be driven
      that way depends on how M8 shapes `BulkAdmissionView` and is M8's to

      those three call sites already use is enough to separate them.

      (`debugLastLayoutUsedBulkAdmission`, part (d)) with the real
      cumulatives behind it, at a real mid-flight bulk value, with a real
      leading row straddling the window start, and that the rows the
      decision admits are the rows the viewport paints. A policy unit test

      can prove the rule is right and never that the render object feeds
      it correctly. Two levels, not a choice between them.
Both must be accompanied by an unchanged run of
`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:787-884` to prove the cap survived.

**Effort.** M.

### H3. `animateScrollToKey` after a mutation clamps to the pre-layout `maxScrollExtent`

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24. `audit_repro_h3_test.dart` red on unfixed code at the JOURNEY, not the landing: with H1's settle snap already landed, the zero-duration landing self-heals a frame later, so both cases discriminate mid-flight (case 1 riding to the stale 400 clamp, 200.0 against the greater-than-500 pin; case 2 pinned at 0.0). Case 1 starts from a NONZERO stale max, because a clamp equal to the current pixels completes instantly, goes idle, and lets the snap mask the defect. (a0), (a) with `waitForQuiescence`, and (b) landed as printed; the animated-ancestor call site passes false and its token-based exit is unchanged; the controller doc gained the two clauses. One harness finding recorded: a Ticker's epoch is its FIRST tick, so a ride started between frames (which (b)'s wait forces) banks no time by the next pump; both cases give it an epoch-setting tick before sampling. Case 2's mid-flight literal is 50, the tracked value depending on the clamp against the mid-expansion max (measured 95.1 at the sample). Case 3 is the (a0) guard, red with the guard removed (the routed call cancels the in-flight scroll, whose future then resolves false). Six demo states shown red individually. Risk suites 42 green; full suite 1142 passed, 4 skipped; analyze at the 48-issue baseline.

**Finding.** `_scroll_orchestrator.dart:236-253` waits one frame ONLY when
the orchestrator itself expanded ancestors
(`collapsedAncestors.isNotEmpty && expandedCount > 0`). The target is then
clamped against `position.maxScrollExtent` at `:265-268` with no other guard,
and `jumpTo`/`animateTo` runs at `:270-274`. `TreeController.expand` sets the
expanded flag before any group is created (`tree_controller.dart:3713` and
`:3718`, both ahead of the animated branch below `:3745`), so a caller-side
`expand` leaves `collapsedAncestors` empty at `:204-211` and the wait is
skipped entirely.

**Root cause.** The wait is keyed on "did I expand something" rather than on
"is the position's geometry stale relative to the tree I am about to measure
against". Any caller-side mutation (`insertRoot`, `expand`, `setChildren`)
that has not been laid out yet leaves `position.maxScrollExtent` describing
the pre-mutation content, and the clamp at `:265-268` silently truncates the
target to it while `:275` still returns `true`.

**Solution.** Three additions to `animateScrollToKey`
(`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:186-276`), all placed after the existing
ancestor-expansion block at `:236-253` and before the target computation at
`:255`, in the order given: the resolve guard FIRST, then the two routing
decisions.

*(a0) Hoist the resolve check above both routing decisions.* Today the only
key-validity test is `sliverOffset == null` at `:256`, which sits BELOW where
(a) and (b) go. Routing an unresolvable key into `_animatedConcurrentScroll`
would be wrong twice over: that method has no key-validity early-out of its
own (its follower simply returns when `getVisibleIndex(key) < 0` at `:355`,
and the final snap returns `true` at `:455`), so the call would resolve
`true`, contradicting the documented "Returns true if a scroll was issued,
false if [key] could not be resolved" (`tree_controller.dart:1996-1998`); and
installing the session would cancel any in-flight animated scroll through the
single-flight slot at `:397-401`, so an unresolvable key would silently kill a
legitimate scroll. Insert immediately after the expansion block:
```
// The key must resolve BEFORE either routing decision below: routing an
// unresolvable key would both report success and cancel an in-flight
// animated scroll through the single-flight slot.
if (_controller.getVisibleIndex(key) < 0) {
  return false;
}
```
`getVisibleIndex(key) < 0` is exactly the condition under which
`scrollOffsetOf` returns null (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:127-129`), so this
hoists the existing test rather than inventing a new one, and the `:256` null
check stays as written (now unreachable for a visible key, and still correct
if a future estimator path can fail). The documented contract is therefore
PRESERVED, not changed: no doc edit is required.

*(a) Route to the existing follower when the content is still moving.*
```
if (duration != Duration.zero && _controller.hasActiveAnimations) {
  return _animatedConcurrentScroll(
    key: key,
    ancestors: const <TKey>[],
    scrollController: scrollController,
    duration: duration,
    curve: curve,
    alignment: alignment,
    extentEstimator: extentEstimator,
    sliverBaseOffset: sliverBaseOffset,
    waitForQuiescence: true,
  );
}
```
`_animatedConcurrentScroll` already handles an empty ancestor list: the
expand loop at `:313-315` and the token capture at `:322-326` both no-op, so
`startedTokens` is empty and `expansionDone` is trivially true. Its follower
(`:330-389`) re-derives the target every tick off `fullOffsetAt(targetIdx)`
plus a per-animating-key correction, which is exactly the "the target is
moving" problem. It keeps ticking after the tree's own animations settle
because `scrollProgress.addListener(_controller.notifyAnimationListenersForScroll)`
(`:310`) dispatches through `AnimationCoordinator.notifyListeners`
unconditionally (`_animation_coordinator.dart:298-313`).

Add ONE new parameter, `required bool waitForQuiescence`, and change the
loop's exit at `:437` to
```
if (scrollDone && expansionDone && (!waitForQuiescence || !_controller.hasActiveAnimations)) break;
```
The existing `AncestorExpansionMode.animated` call site at `:219-228` passes
`waitForQuiescence: false`, so its semantics (token-based, pinned by
`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:1516-1603`) are bit-for-bit unchanged. The
final precise snap at `:452-468` then lands on settled geometry.

*(b) A precise one-frame stale-geometry wait for the non-animating case.*
After (a0) has passed and (a) has declined, before `:255`:
```
final position = scrollController.position;
if (position.hasViewportDimension && position.hasContentDimensions) {
  final double treeTotal = fullOffsetAt(_controller.visibleNodeCount);
  final double requiredMax =
      sliverBaseOffset + treeTotal - position.viewportDimension;
  if (requiredMax > position.maxScrollExtent + 0.5) {
    final scheduler = SchedulerBinding.instance;
    if (!scheduler.hasScheduledFrame) {
      scheduler.scheduleFrame();
    }
    await scheduler.endOfFrame;
    if (_disposed || !scrollController.hasClients) return false;
  }
}
```
The decision rule is one-sided and therefore safe: the scrollable's content
is at least `sliverBaseOffset + treeTotal`, so once the tree has been laid
out `maxScrollExtent >= sliverBaseOffset + treeTotal - viewportDimension`
must hold (slivers after the tree only make it larger). Observing a
materially SMALLER max proves a layout is pending. `fullOffsetAt` is the
prefix cache already used by `scrollOffsetOf` (`:116-119`, `:94-111`), so the
predicate costs one O(1) amortized read. Exactly one wait, never a loop: one
frame is sufficient when no animation is in flight, and the animated case was
routed away by (a).

Also update the doc block at `tree_controller.dart:1957-1999` to say that (i)
a non-zero-duration call issued while tree animations are in flight follows
the moving target and therefore participates in the single-flight slot
documented at `:1992-1994`, and (ii) `duration: Duration.zero` issued during
an in-flight animation lands on the current animated geometry (plus H1's
post-frame snap), not the settled one.

Returned-Future meaning per branch:
- `duration == Duration.zero`, no animations: unchanged, resolves `true`
  synchronously after `jumpTo` (or after one extra frame when the
  stale-geometry predicate fired). H1's snap corrects the landing next frame.
- `duration > 0`, no animations: unchanged, resolves when `animateTo`
  completes.
- `duration > 0`, animations in flight: resolves when the scroll curve has
  finished AND `hasActiveAnimations` is false AND the final snap at `:463`
  has run; resolves `false` if superseded by another animated scroll or if
  the controller was disposed. Known imprecision: M23 (empty operation-group
  shells hold `hasActiveAnimations` true for a full duration) can delay this
  resolution by up to one `expandCollapse.duration`; the position is already
  correct by then, only the Future is late.

**Alternatives considered.**
- *Unconditionally `await endOfFrame` whenever `SchedulerBinding.hasScheduledFrame`
  is true (the review's suggestion).* Rejected on test/API blast radius: a
  frame is scheduled for any reason at all (a ticking animation elsewhere,
  a pending rebuild), so it would make `animateScrollToKey` require a pumped
  frame in cases that resolve synchronously today.
  `sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:1353-1380` awaits the Future with no pump
  between; that call would deadlock. The content-dimension predicate fires
  only when the clamp is actually going to truncate a reachable target, and
  by hand it does NOT fire for that test (10 rows x 50 px, `treeTotal` 500,
  viewport 400, `requiredMax` 100, observed max 100).
- *A post-layout snap instead of the follower for the animating case.* It
  fixes the landing but not the journey: the scroll would run to a stale
  target and then jump the residual (the review measured 3588 px). The
  follower already solves this and is the house mechanism.
- *Poll `maxScrollExtent` in a loop until it stops growing.* Rejected:
  unbounded latency and no clear Future semantics; the follower is the
  bounded, single-flight version of the same idea.

**Sequencing dependency.** Chain 5 in the Sequencing section: H1 changes what
a scroll offset means for never-measured rows and M20 adds a sticky inset to
the same three target computations this block touches
(`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:261-264`, `:377-380`, `:459-462`). Land H1 first,
this item second, M20 third; landing M20 before this item would put the inset
arithmetic in a method whose routing is about to move. The same dependency is
recorded in M20's block.

**Sequencing dependency (L13).** L13 restructures the SAME method, installing
a plain-path session in `_activeScroll` so a later animated scroll cannot
silently kill it. The two interact and the order is not free: L13's install
sits early in the method, while the (a0) resolve guard added by this block
sits after the ancestor-expansion block. If L13 lands with its install ABOVE
that guard, an unresolvable key registers a session, cancels an in-flight
animated scroll through the single-flight slot at
`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:397-401`, and only then returns false, which is
precisely the defect (a0) exists to prevent. Rule: whichever lands second, the
resolve guard must precede the session install. L13's block records the
matching note.

**Architecture fit.** Both changes live entirely in `ScrollOrchestrator`,
which already owns `animateScrollToKey`, the prefix cache, the one-frame wait
idiom (`:246-251`), the `_ActiveScroll` single-flight slot (`:41-54`) and the
final-snap idiom (`:452-468`). (a) reuses `_animatedConcurrentScroll` rather
than adding a second follower, which is the stated preference; the one new
parameter is a per-call mode flag on a private method, not a public API
addition, and the existing call site keeps its exact behavior. (b) reuses
`fullOffsetAt` as the single source of tree geometry, so there is no second
offset model to keep in sync. `TreeController.animateScrollToKey`
(`:2000-2016`) is a pure delegator and needs no change beyond its doc.

**Performance.** (b) is one `fullOffsetAt` (O(1) amortized; O(N) only when
the caller's own mutation already invalidated the prefix, which the immediate
`scrollOffsetOf` at `:255` would have paid anyway) plus three
`ScrollPosition` field reads, and zero extra frames in the common case. (a)
adds one `AnimationController` and one animation-listener registration for
the duration of the scroll, identical to the cost the animated-ancestor mode
already pays; the follower's per-tick cost is one `fullOffsetAt`, a loop over
`currentlyAnimatingKeys` (empty when the tree is idle) and one `jumpTo`. No
per-frame cost is added to layout, paint or hit-test. Zero steady-state
allocations.

**Risk.** Readers of this path:
`test/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:1282-1690` (nine cases),
`audit_repro_f24_test.dart`, `scroll_orchestrator_dispose_test.dart`,
`scroll_orchestrator_position_swap_test.dart`,
`synced_on_controller_created_test.dart`
(`grep -rln "animateScrollToKey" test/`, 5 files). All nine
`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart` cases that use `_ScrollToKeyHarness` build the
controller with `TreeAnimationStyle.disabled` (`:1936-1939`), so
`hasActiveAnimations` is false and branch (a) never fires for them; the two
`_DeepCollapsedTreeHarness` cases (`:1516`, `:1605`) use
`AncestorExpansionMode.animated` and hit the existing call site with
`waitForQuiescence: false`, so their exit condition is unchanged. The case
most worth re-reading after the change is `:1353` ("clamps target into scroll
bounds at the tail"), because it is the one that deliberately exercises the
clamp; the predicate must not fire there. `scroll_orchestrator_dispose_test.dart`
exercises teardown while a session is live and now has a second entry path
into `_activeScroll`; re-run it and add a case for the new route.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_h3_test.dart`, two cases,
matching the review's repros:
1. *Synchronous mutation, no animations.* `TreeAnimationStyle.disabled`,
   10 roots x 50 px in a 600 px viewport (so `maxScrollExtent == 0`; assert
   that as setup sanity). `controller.insertRoot` 35 more roots, then

2. *Caller-side animated expand.* 300 ms `expandCollapse`, 10 roots x 50 px,

   `position.pixels > 1000`. Fails today (`animateTo(0)`, pixels stay 0
   while `maxScrollExtent` grows to 1356).

**Effort.** M.

### H4. Depth-limited `expandAll` / `collapseAll` ignore post-flip visibility

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, landed with L27 as chain 15 requires, in
ONE commit; five audit passes over the pair, 4 and 5 consecutively clean
(pass 1 recorded the now-stale synchronous-trigger rationale on
`_opGroupSnapshot`'s field doc, pass 2 caught a non-ASCII separator in a new
test comment, pass 3 tightened an over-broad reachability claim in a new
code comment). All three edits landed as prescribed, merged with L27's
recipe in this block's stated per-branch order (partition, continue,
displace, clear or re-pend, rebase the survivors, detached reset,
forward or reverse). Anchors re-derived against the landed tree: the
harvest gate (`tree_controller.dart:4382`) and its debug assert (`:4437`),
`_partitionByPostFlipVisibility` (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:505`)
with the two scratch lists (`tree_controller.dart:642-643`), the four
rewritten reversal branches, `_routeShownNodesToStandaloneEnters` (`:4274`,
called unconditionally in the bulk-reverse branch and from the continuation
branch), and the collapseAll harvest filter (`:4696`). Chain 12's
re-derivation rule was followed: the install-site grep returns 17 call
sites post-merge (14 before this pair; the four new displacements plus the
helper's two, minus the three absorbed loops), every one carrying M5's
required family parameter, the new ones all `expandCollapse`.

`test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_h4_test.dart` carries this block's five
cases. Pre-fix reds matched the predictions exactly: cases 1 through 3
settled to the zombie orders ([a, b, c] twice, [r, a, b, c]), case 4's
sampled extent decreased mid-flight, and case 5 emptied the order to [a].
Every sanity and settled-state assertion across the pair's two new test
files was individually shown red by a test-side construction (24
constructions, one run), and the primaries by the pre-fix run. The block's
Risk suites pass; `expand_collapse_staging_gate_test` and the fuzz suites
are green in the full run (1116 passed, 4 skipped, the 1104 post-M5
baseline plus these twelve; analyze at the 48-issue baseline). The
specified-but-unexercised op-group displacement in expandAll (visible and
hidden non-empty in the SAME group) remains defensive, exactly as this
block records; its bulk mirror is exercised by case 2.

**Finding.** Two mirrored defects, both rooted in a depth-blind harvest.

`expandAll` harvests exiting children "regardless of depth" (`tree_controller.dart:4128-4147`), then un-pends EVERY op group with a non-empty `pendingRemoval` (`:4191-4192`, `group.pendingRemoval.clear()`) and EVERY bulk pending member (`:4212`, `_clearBulkPending()`), with no check that the member's post-flip ancestor chain is expanded. The op-group `completed` handler removes nothing from `_order` (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:266-282`) and `_onBulkAnimationComplete` removes only on `dismissed` (`:216`), so a member whose chain stayed collapsed grows back to full extent and stays in the visible order forever.

`collapseAll` has the mirror: `nodesToHide` is filled by `_getVisibleDescendants` with no depth filter (`tree_controller.dart:4318-4323`), and the branches below act on it regardless of whether `_collapseAllInRegistry(maxDepth)` actually hid anything. The animated branch drags still-visible rows to zero and pops them back (`:4417-4438`); the non-animated branch is worse, `:4498-4505` unconditionally `_removeFromVisibleOrder`s them. `collapseAll(maxDepth: 0, animate: false)` on a fully expanded `a > b > c` therefore empties the order down to `["a"]` while `isExpanded("a")` is still true, because `_collapseAllInRegistry(0)` flips nothing (`_node_store.dart:459`, `_depthByNid[nid] < maxDepth` is never true for `maxDepth == 0`).

**Root cause.** Both directions use "is this group collapsing / expanding?" as the predicate instead of "will this member be visible after the flips this call just applied?". The correct predicate already exists and is already the one the terminal handlers use: `_ancestorsExpandedFast` (`tree_controller.dart:321` forwarding `_node_store.dart:361-365`, a single dense `Uint8List` read, O(1)), read at `_tree_controller_animation.dart:309` and `:223`. At `tree_controller.dart:4180` the cache is already post-flip, because `_setExpandedKey` ran at `:4161-4164` and `_rebuildAllAncestorsExpanded()` at `:4165`; on the collapse side `_collapseAllInRegistry` rebuilds it itself (`_node_store.dart:465`).

**Solution.** Three coordinated edits, all in `tree_controller.dart` plus one shared helper in `_tree_controller_animation.dart`.

1. Gate the harvest (`tree_controller.dart:4128-4147`). Compute once per visited node, next to `withinDepthLimit` at `:4097`:
   `final postFlipExpanded = withinDepthLimit || _isExpandedKey(key);`
   and wrap the whole child loop at `:4129-4147` in `if (postFlipExpanded) { ... }`. This is exact, not conservative: the DFS pushes children only when the parent is `withinDepthLimit` (`:4150-4154`), and such a parent is either already expanded or joins `nodesToExpand` (`:4099-4100`), so by induction from the roots (roots always carry the ancestors-expanded bit, `_node_store.dart:86-87`) every visited node is itself post-flip visible; therefore "parent post-flip expanded" is equivalent to "these children are post-flip visible". Pending-deletion nodes never enter the induction, the DFS skips them before pushing children (`:4088-4090`). Add, immediately after `_ensureVisibleOrder()` at `:4178`, a debug assert pinning that contract:
   `assert(nodesToReverseExit.every(_ancestorsExpandedFast));`

2. Add the shared partition helper to the `_TreeControllerAnimationOps` extension in `_tree_controller_animation.dart` (the part file that already owns cross-source expand/collapse routing):

   ```
   void _partitionByPostFlipVisibility(
     Iterable<TKey> members,
     List<TKey> visibleOut,
     List<TKey> hiddenOut,
   )
   ```

   It CLEARS both out-lists itself (so no caller can forget), then appends each member to `visibleOut` when `_ancestorsExpandedFast(m)` and to `hiddenOut` otherwise. Callers must have applied their expansion flips and rebuilt the ancestors-expanded cache first. It only READS `members`, which is why passing the live `group.members.keys` / `_activeBulkGroup!.pendingRemoval` view is safe: every subsequent mutation runs over the scratch copies. Add two reusable scratch lists beside `_opGroupSnapshot` (`tree_controller.dart:583-584`), same rationale block:
   `final List<TKey> _partitionVisibleScratch = <TKey>[];`
   `final List<TKey> _partitionHiddenScratch = <TKey>[];`
   Both are fully consumed before the group's `forward()`/`reverse()` runs, so nothing in them has to survive a call that can fire a synchronous terminal handler.

   TWO out-lists, not one plus a count. The expandAll direction displaces the HIDDEN members and the collapseAll direction displaces the VISIBLE ones, and in both cases the displacement call detaches the member from the group it is iterating (`_startStandaloneExitAnimation` / `_startStandaloneEnterAnimation` both begin with `_captureAndRemoveFromGroups`, `_tree_controller_animation.dart:504` and `:368-369`), which mutates `group.members` / `_activeBulkGroup!.members` mid-iteration. Rejected alternatives: (a) one out-list plus `group.members.keys.toList()` at the collapseAll displacement site, which allocates a full member-list copy per group per call on a path that already owns a reusable-scratch convention (`tree_controller.dart:573-584`) and still needs the other list to decide the skip; (b) returning a bitmask or index set, which does not apply here, group membership is keyed (`OperationGroup.members` is a `Map<TKey, NodeGroupExtent>`, `AnimationGroup.members` / `pendingRemoval` are `Set<TKey>`, `types.dart`), so a dense index space would need an extra key-to-nid pass, strictly more work than two list appends.

3. Rewrite the four reversal branches to partition instead of acting wholesale. Both directions obey ONE rule, stated so it needs no further thought:

   > Partition the group's relevant member set. If the set that would be DISPLACED is empty and the group's direction is already correct for the post-flip state, leave the group completely untouched. Otherwise: re-target the survivors, displace the others to standalone animations iterating the SCRATCH list, then run the group's controller call.

   Concretely, per branch:

   `expandAll` op groups (`tree_controller.dart:4189-4203`), inside the existing `_opGroupSnapshot` loop, per group:
   - partition `group.members.keys`;
   - if `_partitionVisibleScratch` is empty, `continue`: leave the group pended and reversing. The `dismissed` handler then removes the members correctly via `_ancestorsExpandedFast` at `_tree_controller_animation.dart:307-312`;
   - otherwise, in this order: (0) capture `preReversalCurvedValue = group.curvedValue` BEFORE any write, exactly as `expand` Path 1 does at `tree_controller.dart:3769`; (i) for each key in `_partitionHiddenScratch` call `_startStandaloneExitAnimation(key)`, which captures the member's current mid-collapse extent AND detaches it from the group (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:504` into `_animation_coordinator.dart:568-587`); (ii) `group.pendingRemoval.clear()`; (iii) rebase the SURVIVING `group.members.entries` with L27's Path-1 recipe, which REPLACES the bare `targetExtent = _fullExtentOf(member.key) ?? _unknownExtent` at `:4198-4199`: per member `final full = _fullExtentOf(member.key) ?? defaultExtent;`, `member.value.startExtent = member.value.computeExtent(preReversalCurvedValue, full);`, `member.value.targetExtent = full;`, and `member.value.targetIsCaptured = false;` when `_fullExtentOf` returned null; (iv) `_anim.opGroups.runWithGroupDetached(entry.key, (g) { g.controller.value = 0.0; })`, the reset that makes (iii) exact and whose synchronous status event the detach drops (`_operation_group_registry.dart:207-218`); (v) `group.controller.forward()`. The displacement must precede (iii) AND (iv): the extent `captureAndRemoveFromGroups` computes from the member's own record (`_animation_coordinator.dart:577`) reads both the endpoints (iii) overwrites and the `group.curvedValue` (iv) moves, and a displacement inside (iv)'s detached window loses the capture entirely. Full analysis in the Sequencing dependency (Chain 15) below;
   - `disposeIfEmpty` (`_operation_group_registry.dart:187-196`) cannot fire mid-branch: it requires BOTH `members` and `pendingRemoval` empty (`:190-192`), and during step (i) `pendingRemoval` is still full.

   `expandAll` bulk (`tree_controller.dart:4208-4231`): replace `_clearBulkPending()` at `:4212` with a partition of `_activeBulkGroup!.pendingRemoval`. Displace `_partitionHiddenScratch` with `_startStandaloneExitAnimation` (the bulk branch of `captureAndRemoveFromGroups`, `_animation_coordinator.dart:589-597`, captures `full * bulk.value` and removes from both sets). Un-pend `_partitionVisibleScratch` with `_removeBulkPending(key)` (`tree_controller.dart:517`). If the visible list is empty, do NOT call `forward()` at `:4230`; route `nodesToReverseExit` and `nodesToShow` through standalone ENTERS instead, which is exactly the body of the continuation branch at `:4244-4259`. Extract that body once as `void _routeShownNodesToStandaloneEnters(List<TKey> reverseExit, List<TKey> show)` and call it from both places. `BulkAnimator.removeMember` (`_bulk_animator.dart:164-178`) does not dispose an emptied group, so `_activeBulkGroup` stays non-null for that call. L27's edit 2 lands INSIDE this rewritten region: it replaces the joiner loop at `:4223-4227`, whose `_addBulkMember` pops a genuinely new row from 0 to `full * bulk.value` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:867-869`), with the continuation branch's standalone-enter policy. Merged, that makes the joiner policy identical in both sub-cases, so `_routeShownNodesToStandaloneEnters(nodesToReverseExit, nodesToShow)` is called UNCONDITIONALLY in this branch and the only thing the partition still decides is whether `forward()` at `:4230` runs. The extraction is exact: `:4215-4219` is already byte-identical to the continuation branch's `:4244-4248` (`diff` run this session), and with L27's edit 2 applied `:4223-4227` carries the same predicate as `:4249-4259`.

   `collapseAll` op groups (`tree_controller.dart:4395-4412`), per group with empty `pendingRemoval` (an EXPANDING group):
   - partition `group.members.keys`;
   - if `_partitionHiddenScratch` is empty, `continue`: no re-pend, no `startExtent` normalization, no `reverse()`. THIS RULE WINS over "displace the visible members". When nothing under a group becomes invisible the group is already animating in the right direction and the collapse call has nothing to say about it; tearing it apart into per-member standalone enters would dispose a live group, restart every member from its current extent on a different family (`effectiveEnterExit` rather than `expandCollapse`, `tree_controller.dart:419-420`), and produce a visible timing discontinuity for a call that flipped nothing. Skipping is a true no-op. This is the `collapseAll(maxDepth: 0)` case and the "group rooted beyond the depth limit" case;
   - otherwise, in this order: (0) capture `preReversalCurvedValue = group.curvedValue` BEFORE any write, as `collapse` Path 1 does at `tree_controller.dart:3985`; (i) `group.pendingRemoval.add(nodeId)` for each key in `_partitionHiddenScratch` that is not `_isPendingDeletion` (preserving the existing guard at `:4400`); (ii) `_startStandaloneEnterAnimation(key)` for each key in `_partitionVisibleScratch`, so those rows finish growing on their own timeline instead of being dragged to zero by the group's `reverse()`; (iii) rebase the SURVIVING `group.members.entries` with L27's mirror recipe, which SUBSUMES the `startExtent = 0.0` normalization at `:4407-4408` rather than replacing it: per member `final full = _fullExtentOf(member.key) ?? defaultExtent;`, `member.value.targetExtent = member.value.computeExtent(preReversalCurvedValue, full);`, `member.value.startExtent = 0.0;`, and no `targetIsCaptured` write, because on this side `targetExtent` IS a genuine capture; (iv) `_anim.opGroups.runWithGroupDetached(entry.key, (g) { g.controller.value = 1.0; })` (`_operation_group_registry.dart:207-218`); (v) `group.controller.reverse()`. Re-pending first is what makes `pendingRemoval` non-empty before any detach, which hard-blocks `disposeIfEmpty` at `_operation_group_registry.dart:190-192`. The displacement at (ii) must precede (iii) and (iv) for the same reason as the `expandAll` mirror: `_startStandaloneEnterAnimation` opens with `_captureAndRemoveFromGroups` (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:370`), whose op-group arm reads the record and the curved value both (iii) and (iv) move (`_animation_coordinator.dart:577`). A group this rule `continue`s past gets NO rebase and NO reset: it stays pended and reversing, and resetting a group that is not reversing direction would be a pure regression.

   `collapseAll` bulk (`tree_controller.dart:4417-4438`): partition `_activeBulkGroup!.members`. If `_partitionHiddenScratch` is empty, leave the group untouched (no `_addBulkPending` loop at `:4421-4425`, no `reverse()` at `:4437`). Otherwise `_addBulkPending` the hidden ones and `_startStandaloneEnterAnimation` the visible ones off the scratch list, then `reverse()`. The `nodesToHide` loop at `:4428-4434` runs unconditionally in both cases: it serves nodes that are NOT bulk members and is a no-op once `nodesToHide` has been filtered (below).

   `collapseAll` depth-independent harvest. Add, immediately after `_recordExpansionChanges(_collapseAllInRegistry(maxDepth), ...)` at `:4381-4384` (the call itself is at `:4382`; post-flip, so the cache `_node_store.dart:465` rebuilt is fresh) and before `_structureGeneration++` at `:4385`:
   `nodesToHide.retainWhere((k) => !_ancestorsExpandedFast(k));`
   `nodesToHideSet` is dead after `:4366` (its only reads are `:4332`, `:4346`, `:4359`), so it needs no update. Every branch from `:4386` onward iterates `nodesToHide` and is a no-op when it empties, including the non-animated removal at `:4498-4505`, which is what fixes the synchronous `collapseAll(maxDepth: 0, animate: false)` defect in the Finding.

   Family, per the boundary rule: `expandAll` / `collapseAll` declare `expandCollapse` once at `:4060-4062` and `:4305-4307`. Displaced members ride `_startStandaloneExitAnimation` / `_startStandaloneEnterAnimation`, which the `StandaloneAnimator` times with `effectiveEnterExit` (`tree_controller.dart:419-420`). That is the existing, already-taken route for every displaced member in these two methods (`:4217`, `:4246`, `:4257`, `:4273`, `:4432`, `:4461`, `:4481`), so this change introduces no new TIMING: each displaced member lands on the spec its siblings in the same branch already use. No new `Duration?` parameter, no new public flag.

   It does add CALL SITES, and M5 counts those. Four are new: the exit displacement in the `expandAll` op-group branch, the exit displacement in the `expandAll` bulk branch, the enter displacement in the `collapseAll` op-group branch, and the enter displacement in the `collapseAll` bulk branch. Two more MOVE rather than appear, `:4246` and `:4257`, both into `_routeShownNodesToStandaloneEnters`. M5 turns exactly these calls into family-declaration sites carrying a required family parameter, so an earlier draft's claim that this block "adds no NEW family site and inherits M5's fix for free" was wrong twice over: under M5's own design the four new calls do not COMPILE without that parameter, and M5's enumerated table of fifteen sites becomes nineteen (`grep -rn "_startStandaloneEnterAnimation\|_startStandaloneExitAnimation" lib` this session: thirteen in `tree_controller.dart`, two in `_tree_controller_animation.dart` at `:410` and `:482`, excluding the two declarations at `:368` and `:497`). Each new site passes the family M5 assigns its sibling in the same branch, which is the assignment that reproduces today's `effectiveEnterExit` timing.

**Sequencing dependency (Chain 15).** Chain 15 in the plan's Sequencing section pairs this block with L27 (`sol_H.md`), and it REPLACES the Sequencing section's current entry listing L27 as independent of everything else. That entry is false: the two blocks rewrite the SAME two method bodies with competing ordered scripts. Shared statements, all opened this session: `tree_controller.dart:4192` (`group.pendingRemoval.clear()`), `:4197-4199` (the target-extent restore, replaced by this block's step (iii) and by L27's edit 1), `:4201` (`group.controller.forward()`), the `collapseAll` mirror at `:4405-4408` (`startExtent = 0.0`) and `:4410` (`reverse()`), and `:4223-4227`, which L27's edit 2 replaces and which sits inside the `:4208-4231` region this block rewrites. Required order INSIDE each merged branch, and it is one order, not two: partition, then `continue` where the displaced-set rule says to, then DISPLACE, then `pendingRemoval.clear()` (expand) or the re-pend (collapse), then L27's rebase over the SURVIVORS only, then L27's `runWithGroupDetached` reset, then `forward()` / `reverse()`. Three things break the other way. (a) L27's edit-1 code block replaces `:4191-4201` wholesale, with an unconditional `pendingRemoval.clear()` and a loop over ALL `group.members.entries`; applied literally on top of this block it deletes the partition, the `continue` and the displacement, and since the op-group `completed` handler removes nothing from `_order` (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:266-282`) every zombie row in the Finding above comes straight back. (b) This block's ORIGINAL step (iii), the bare `targetExtent = _fullExtentOf(member.key) ?? _unknownExtent`, applied literally on top of L27 puts the sentinel back into a member whose controller L27 then resets: `computeExtent` ignores both endpoints under `targetExtent == -1.0` and returns `fullExtent * curvedValue` (`types.dart:251-257`, branch at `:252-254`), and `Curve.transform` returns `t` unchanged at `t == 0.0` (`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/animation/curves.dart:92-97`), so a surviving row paints at zero for a frame. That is strictly worse than today, and it is why step (iii) is now written as the rebase. (c) Displacement after the rebase but before the reset seeds the standalone animation from `member.computeExtent(group.curvedValue, full)` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:577`) read off the REBASED record at the still-unmoved curved value: `lerp(currentExtent, full, cv)` instead of `currentExtent`, too tall by `(full - currentExtent) * cv`, and the `collapseAll` mirror returns `currentExtent * cv`, too short by `currentExtent * (1 - cv)`. Displacement inside the `runWithGroupDetached` window is worse still: the group is removed from `_groups` for the duration (`_operation_group_registry.dart:211`), so `opGroups.groupAt` returns null (`_animation_coordinator.dart:572-573`), the key falls through to `clearMembership` at `:586`, and `_startStandaloneExitAnimation` seeds from `_fullExtentOf(key) ?? defaultExtent` instead (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:504-506`), a jump to full height. One more merge constraint worth stating because L27's block does not: keeping the displacement ABOVE `pendingRemoval.clear()` is what leaves `disposeIfEmpty` blocked by its non-empty-`pendingRemoval` clause (`_operation_group_registry.dart:190-192`, reached from `_animation_coordinator.dart:582`) rather than by the `continue` alone. **Land the two op-group halves as ONE commit.** There is no shippable intermediate: each merged branch is a single rewritten body, and this block's steps (iii)/(iv) above already ARE L27's recipe. Only `:4223-4227` is separable, and in one direction only: L27's edit 2 may land alone BEFORE this block, after which the `_routeShownNodesToStandaloneEnters` extraction absorbs it.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Make the op-group `completed` handler (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:266-282`) also remove members whose chain is collapsed. Rejected: it treats the symptom at the wrong end. The rows would still have GROWN back to full extent over the whole animation and then vanished in one frame, and it would push "collapse semantics" into the handler whose entire contract is "expansion done, nothing structural happened" (`:267-272`).
- Push the predicate into `OperationGroupRegistry` / `BulkAnimator`. Rejected on layering: both are constructed with a `NodeIdRegistry` only (`_animation_coordinator.dart:149-169`, `_bulk_animator.dart:25-37`), and `AnimationCoordinator` itself holds `_nids`, not the `NodeStore` (`:106-107`). The expansion bits live in `NodeStore` (`_node_store.dart:82` for the own-expanded flags, `:91` for the ancestors-expanded cache), so either class would need a new structural dependency to answer a question the controller answers in O(1) today.
- Short-circuit the partition when `maxDepth == null`. Rejected as a false economy: the partition is O(M) `Uint8List` reads once per call over in-flight group members only, and the short-circuit would silently skip the pending-deletion-ancestor case, which is reachable with `maxDepth == null` precisely because the DFS refuses to flip a pending-deletion node (`:4088-4090`), so its descendants can stay hidden through a full `expandAll()`.

**Sequencing dependency (Chain 12).** Chain 12 in the plan's Sequencing section pairs this block with M5. The two work the same call sites from opposite ends: this block adds four and relocates two, M5 gives every one of them a required family parameter and pins the set in an enumerated table. Whichever lands SECOND must RE-DERIVE that table from the tree (`grep -rn "_startStandaloneEnterAnimation\|_startStandaloneExitAnimation" lib`, minus the two declarations in `_tree_controller_animation.dart`) instead of trusting the count the first one wrote, because a table carried over unchecked is precisely how a site keeps its old implicit family while every other site declares one. M5's block records the matching note.

**Architecture fit.** Controller layer. Reuses the existing `_ancestorsExpandedFast` O(1) cache (already the predicate both terminal handlers use, `_tree_controller_animation.dart:223` and `:309`), the existing cross-source detach path (`captureAndRemoveFromGroups`, reached only through the controller forwarder at `tree_controller.dart:546-547` as the part-file doc at `_tree_controller_animation.dart:34-42` requires), the existing `_opGroupSnapshot` scratch convention (`tree_controller.dart:573-584`), and the existing "displace to standalone" policy the continuation branches already apply (`:4240-4243`).

**Performance.** Before: `expandAll` reversal is O(G + B) where G is total op-group members and B is bulk pending. After: same order, plus one `_ancestorsExpandedFast` per member, which is one `Map<TKey,int>` lookup plus one `Uint8List` index (`_node_store.dart:362-364`). Zero per-frame cost, zero paint cost. Allocations: two reusable `List<TKey>` fields, cleared per use, matching `_opGroupSnapshot`. The harvest gate at `:4129` is a net SAVING: a boundary node that stays collapsed now skips two per-child probes (`_standaloneAt` and `_operationGroupOf` plus a map lookup). `collapseAll` gains one `retainWhere` over `nodesToHide`, O(|nodesToHide|) with the same O(1) predicate, and SAVES work whenever it filters, every filtered key is a standalone exit or bulk pending entry not installed. For `expandAll()` / `collapseAll()` with `maxDepth == null` and no pending-deletion ancestors the partition finds zero displaced members, so both paths are behaviourally and cost-identical to today.

**Risk.** The reversal branches are read by every mid-flight expand/collapse crossover. Existing suites to re-run and check: `test/sliver_tree/op_group_iteration_snapshot_test.dart` (its `expandAll` and `collapseAll` cases pass no `maxDepth`, so all members survive the partition and it must stay green, including the synchronous-terminal-status re-entrancy it pins at `:24-71` and `:73-111`, and the multi-group case at `:113-160`), `test/sliver_tree/animation_transitions_test.dart:533-615` (the two bulk-reversal cases in the "expandAll / collapseAll reversal" group, no `maxDepth`, all members survive), `test/sliver_tree/bulk_reentry_continuation_test.dart` (touches the continuation branch whose body is being extracted; both its cases also pass no `maxDepth`), `test/sliver_tree/expand_all_interior_expanded_test.dart:79-121` (the only existing `maxDepth` test; no exiting animations, so `nodesToReverseExit` is empty and the gate is inert, and the gate does not touch `nodesToExpand` / `nodesToShow`, which is what that test pins), `test/sliver_tree/expand_collapse_all_stale_order_test.dart`, `test/sliver_tree/collapsed_interior_fallback_test.dart`, `test/sliver_tree/tree_expansion_listener_test.dart` (reads `_collapseAllInRegistry`'s flipped list).

Known remaining gap, deliberately out of scope: the DFS descends only when `withinDepthLimit` (`:4150`), so exiting nodes below an ALREADY-expanded node at the depth boundary are still never harvested. Widening the descent to `withinDepthLimit || _isExpandedKey(key)` preserves the induction above, but it is a separate behaviour change and I have not tested it.

Also unverified: `expandAll(animate: false)` (`:4289-4293`) touches only `nodesToReverseExit` and leaves in-flight groups running, which lets a mid-collapse row shrink to zero and pop back; a pop, not a zombie, and not addressed here.

One branch is specified but NOT exercised by the tests below, and I am marking it rather than inventing a test that cannot fail: the op-group displacement in `expandAll` (visible non-empty AND hidden non-empty in the SAME op group). I could not construct that state through the public mutators. An op group's members come from one collapse walk whose descent is gated on each node's expansion flag (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:251-253`), so a member at depth d+1 implies its parent was expanded, and `expandAll` never collapses anything; and every route that does collapse an interior member first detaches its descendants from the group (`tree_controller.dart:4026` `_captureAndRemoveFromGroups` on the fresh-collapse path, `:3954` `_removeAnimation` on the non-animated path). The branch stays because its bulk mirror IS reachable (test case 2) and one rule across both directions is worth more than a special case, but it is defensive.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_h4_test.dart`, five cases with a 300ms `expandCollapse` spec. There is no public op-group-membership getter (`isBulkMember` at `tree_controller.dart:1417` is bulk-only), so the setup sanity assertions use `isExiting` (`:1504`), which probes bulk pending, op-group pending and standalone exits alike (`_animation_coordinator.dart:658-670`).

1. op-group early-return variant. `a > b > c`, expand all three without animation, `collapse(key: "b")`, pump 100ms, sanity-assert `controller.isExiting("c")` is true and `controller.isExpanded("b")` is false, then `expandAll(maxDepth: 1)`, `pumpAndSettle()`. Expect `visibleNodes == ["a", "b"]` and `isExpanded("b") == false`. Fails today with `["a", "b", "c"]`: `nodesToExpand` is empty (a is already expanded) but the depth-blind harvest puts c in `nodesToReverseExit`, so `:4156` does not early-return and group "b" is un-pended. With edit 1 the harvest is gated at b (`withinDepthLimit` false, `_isExpandedKey("b")` false) and `:4156` early-returns.

2. bulk mixed partition. `a > b > c` all expanded, `collapseAll()`, pump 100ms, sanity-assert `controller.isBulkMember("b")` and `isBulkMember("c")`, then `expandAll(maxDepth: 1)`, `pumpAndSettle()`. Expect `visibleNodes == ["a", "b"]`, `isExpanded("a") == true`, `isExpanded("b") == false`. This is the genuinely MIXED case: `collapseAll()` clears every expansion flag (`_node_store.dart:453`), `expandAll(maxDepth: 1)` re-expands only depth 0, so bulk pending splits into b (post-flip visible) and c (post-flip hidden). Fails today with `["a", "b", "c"]`.

3. op-group skip-and-survive, two groups in one call. `r > a > b > c`. Expand r, a, b without animation, then `collapse(key: "a")` and `collapse(key: "r")`, both animated, pump 100ms. That yields exactly two op groups: "a" with members {b, c} and "r" with member {a}. c does not migrate into group "r", because `collapse("r")`'s descendant walk stops at the already-collapsed a (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:251-253`). Sanity-assert `isExiting("a")`, `isExiting("b")`, `isExiting("c")` all true and `isExpanded("b")` still true. Then `expandAll(maxDepth: 1)`, `pumpAndSettle()`. Expect `visibleNodes == ["r", "a"]`, `isExpanded("r") == true`, `isExpanded("a") == false`. Fails today with `["r", "a", "b", "c"]`: both groups are un-pended and forwarded, so b and c grow to full extent under a collapsed a and never leave `_order`. After the fix group "r" partitions to visible = [a] and takes the un-pend path unchanged, while group "a" partitions to visible = [] and takes the `continue`, letting its `dismissed` handler remove b and c through `_ancestorsExpandedFast` (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:307-312`).

4. `collapseAll` animated mirror. `a > b > c` all collapsed, `expandAll()` animated, pump 100ms, sanity-assert `isBulkMember("b")` and that `getCurrentExtent("b")` is strictly between 0 and `getEstimatedExtent("b")`. Record `getCurrentExtent("b")`, call `collapseAll(maxDepth: 0)`, then pump in 16ms steps to settle asserting the sampled extent is monotonically non-decreasing at every step. Expect `visibleNodes == ["a", "b", "c"]` after settle. Fails today: `maxDepth: 0` flips nothing, yet every bulk member is re-pended and the group reverses, so the sampled extent drops toward zero before the disposal pops it back.

5. `collapseAll` synchronous mirror. `a > b > c` all expanded (no animation), `collapseAll(maxDepth: 0, animate: false)`. Expect `visibleNodes == ["a", "b", "c"]` and `isExpanded("a") == true` immediately, no pump needed. Fails today with `["a"]`: `nodesToHide` is depth-blind and the non-animated branch removes both rows from the visible order even though nothing was collapsed.

**Effort.** M.

### H5. A `GlobalKey` inside a row breaks dragging

**Finding.** `_startDrag` hands the exact instance the `nodeBuilder` returned to the owner (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:1381`, `_onDragStartCallback(widget.nodeKey, widget.child)`, received at `:670`), and `_DragProxy.build` mounts that same instance in the root overlay (`:1550`, `:1559-1560`) while the in-place copy stays mounted, wrapped only in `IgnorePointer` + `Opacity(0)` (`:1127-1130`). The descendant clone stack has the same shape: `:1584` calls `nodeBuilder(context, row.key, row.depth)` for each frozen descendant while those descendants' in-place rows also stay mounted.

**Root cause.** Two live inflations of one widget subtree, and the second one happens during LAYOUT. `Element.inflateWidget` routes a `GlobalKey` through `_retakeInactiveElement` (`C:\flutter_sdk\flutter\packages\flutter\lib\src\widgets\framework.dart:4572`, body at `:4481-4534`), which yanks the element out of its current parent with `parent.forgetChild(element); parent.deactivateChild(element);` (`:4528-4529`).

The lift frame produces exactly that. `_onDragStart` inserts the overlay entry and then calls `setState` (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:685-686`), so on the next frame the build phase inflates the proxy (a legal build-phase retake from the still-live row), and the same `setState` rebuilds `SliverTree`, which makes `SliverTreeElement.update` queue every mounted key (`sliver_tree_element.dart:190-191`). Those keys are consumed in `createChild` during layout (`:517-549`), where `widget.nodeBuilder(this, nodeId, depth)` at `:538` produces a FRESH row widget, so the row's `widget.child` is a new instance, `Element.updateChild` does not short-circuit (`framework.dart:4014`), and the row re-inflates the `GlobalKey` subtree from inside `owner!.buildScope` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:532`) inside `RenderSliverTree.performLayout`. The retake now deactivates a render object in the OVERLAY subtree, whose layout root is unrelated to the sliver: `_debugCanPerformMutations` walks to `activeLayoutRoot == null` (`C:\flutter_sdk\flutter\packages\flutter\lib\src\rendering\object.dart:2332-2354`) and throws exactly the reported message (`:2363-2379`).

That chain has a precondition the heading hides, and it decides how the repro must be written: the retake fires only when the SAME `GlobalKey` INSTANCE is reachable from both mounts. `_retakeInactiveElement` returns null the moment `key._currentElement` is null (`framework.dart:4488-4491`), so an inline `GlobalKey()` that every `nodeBuilder` invocation rebuilds fresh never collides with the instance the overlay captured at lift; its layout-phase inflation is then a plain `createElement` inside the sliver's OWN layout callback, which `object.dart:2342` permits (`doingLayoutWithCallback` is true for the sliver being laid out). The key that crashes is an app-owned one that is stable across builds, and test case 1 below is written accordingly.

Which element loses the key: the OVERLAY's. The build phase hands it from the row to the overlay and that direction is legal; the layout phase takes it BACK for the row, so the `parent.deactivateChild(element)` at `framework.dart:4529` is applied to the overlay's copy and the render object whose mutation is refused sits in the overlay subtree, which is why the reported message names a `RenderPointerListener` from the proxy's stack rather than a row from the list. I did not re-run the review's repro, and under the citation above its inline `GlobalKey()` should not have reproduced anything; the fix does not turn on resolving that, because it removes the second inflation outright.

**Sequencing dependency.** Chain 4: decide H5 together with M19. H5 decides whether the row's captured widget may be mounted twice at all; M19 decides how the in-place row is hidden. They are the same wrapper. If H5 takes the placeholder approach below, most of M19's wrapper question is already answered by it: the payload of the unconditional `IgnorePointer` + `Opacity` pair (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:1127-1130`) becomes a `SizedBox` for the dragged subtree, and the `Opacity(0)` M19 is weighing becomes redundant over that payload while still being the thing that keeps the row's widget SHAPE stable (`:1158-1165`). Landing M19 first would mean re-deciding it after H5 changes what it wraps.

**Solution.** Adopt the reference contract: while the drag proxy owns the subtree, the in-place copies are sized placeholders, so the row content is inflated exactly once. All edits in `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart`.

In `_ReorderableRowState.build`, replace `:1031-1033` (the snippet re-declares `scope` and `hidden` verbatim from `:1031-1032`, so the replaced range is all three lines, not the `content` line alone):

```
final scope = _ReorderableScope.maybeOf<TKey>(context);
final hidden = _inDraggedSubtree(scope?.draggedKey);
// Placeholder only when the proxy is the subtree's mount. With
// showDragProxy false nothing else inflates the row, so the live copy
// stays and the app's State survives.
final placeholder = hidden && (scope?.dragProxyEnabled ?? false);
Widget content = placeholder
    ? SizedBox(
        height: _reorder.treeController.getEstimatedExtent(widget.nodeKey),
      )
    : widget.child;
```

`getEstimatedExtent` is public (`tree_controller.dart:1506-1510`) and returns the cached measured extent, falling back to `defaultExtent`. Sizing the placeholder to it is self-consistent, because it is the same number every other consumer of the row's extent already reads: the make-room gap lift re-derives itself LIVE on every re-target by summing `getCurrentExtentNid` over the dragged subtree (`tree_controller.dart:1713-1716`), which at rest is the cached full extent; and the proxy's frozen stack captured the same values at lift through the same accessor (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:410-449`, extents read at `:438`, pinned into the band at `:1580-1581`). The row re-measures to exactly the value already cached, so `_fullExtentByNid`, the gap lift and the pinned proxy geometry all stay on one number. The row's own slot must keep its extent: the slot closes through the preview's held offsets, not by the row measuring zero.

That last sentence holds only for a row that HAS been measured, and the exception is worth stating rather than leaving as a caveat, because it is reachable: a descendant of the dragged subtree that was never laid out before the lift. `getEstimatedExtent` falls back to `defaultExtent` for it (`tree_controller.dart:1509-1510`), so its placeholder is 48 px, and `_layoutNodeChild` writes that back as a MEASURED extent the first time the row is admitted mid-drag (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2400`, `controller.setFullExtent(nodeId, child.size.height)`). Verified consequences, and the decision is to ACCEPT them:

- The live gap lift stops moving. `setReorderPreviewAtIndex` re-sums `getCurrentExtentNid` over the dragged subtree on every re-target (`tree_controller.dart:1713-1716`), and the frozen proxy stack summed the same accessor at lift (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:438`), where a never-measured row also contributed `defaultExtent`. The placeholder keeps those two sums equal for the whole session.
- Today they diverge, visibly. The first real measurement grows the structural offsets of every following row immediately, while the preview's HELD offset only catches up when the next re-target re-sums the lift, so rows below the gap displace by the difference in between, and stay displaced if the user holds still. The placeholder removes that displacement rather than causing one.
- What genuinely changes is the STORED value: `getMeasuredExtent` returns `defaultExtent` instead of null for such a row until the drop (`tree_controller.dart:1007`), which for the length of the drag suppresses a caller-supplied `extentEstimator` for exactly that key (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:149-154`, `:162-165`), and the row's true height is folded in one frame later, at the drop, when real content replaces the placeholder and `:2400` re-measures. Test case 5 pins both halves.

Everything below `:1033` stays byte-identical: `TreeRowDragScope` at `:1082-1086`, `IgnorePointer` + `Opacity` at `:1127-1130`, `Semantics` at `:1166`. Only the payload changes, so the row's own widget SHAPE is unchanged and `_ReorderableRowState` itself is never re-inflated, which is the invariant `:1158-1165` protects. The `Opacity(0)` is now redundant over a `SizedBox` but stays for exactly that reason.

The proxy side is untouched: `:1550`, `:1559-1560` and `:1579-1586` keep mounting live subtrees, so the `dragProxyBuilder` contract at `:212-255` (real `rowChild`, mounted for the whole session, self-driving animations, `ListenableBuilder` reactivity) is preserved verbatim. That contract is the reason the proxy, not the in-place copy, is the side that keeps the mount.

What happens to State. The app's `State` under `nodeBuilder`'s output is created fresh in the overlay at lift and again in place at drop, unless the app puts its own `GlobalKey` on the row content, in which case the SAME element migrates in place, then to the proxy, then back, and State is preserved end to end. Today that GlobalKey is precisely what crashes, so the change strictly widens what apps can do: the default becomes `ReorderableListView`'s behaviour (`reorderable_list.dart:1293-1296` returns `SizedBox.fromSize` for the dragging item), and State preservation becomes opt-in and working.

Frame ordering makes the migration legal in both directions, and both directions are same-frame by construction. At LIFT, `_ensureProxy(context)` and `setState` run in one gesture callback (`:685-686`); the root overlay (`:641`, `rootOverlay: true`) is shallower than the rows and `BuildOwner._flushDirtyElements` sorts by ascending depth (`framework.dart:2800` using `Element._sort` at `:3616-3621`), so the overlay inflates first, in the BUILD phase, which is the "forward-looking" retake `framework.dart:4482-4487` documents; the row then rebuilds to a placeholder and never re-inflates the key during layout, which is the crash the fix removes. At DROP, `_onDragEnd` calls `setState` and `_removeProxy()` in one callback (`:707-708`), so the overlay entry is deactivated in the same build phase; the row's layout-phase `createChild` then finds `key._currentElement._parent == null`, skips the whole `if (parent != null)` block (`framework.dart:4504-4530`) and therefore performs NO render-tree mutation, takes the element out of `_inactiveElements` (`:4532`) and reactivates it (`:4582`). The element is still there to take, because `WidgetsBinding.drawFrame` runs `buildOwner!.finalizeTree()` only AFTER `super.drawFrame()` has flushed layout (`C:\flutter_sdk\flutter\packages\flutter\lib\src\widgets\binding.dart:1571-1578`). The drop-side reactivation is reasoned from those sources, not yet run; test case 2 below is what pins it.

Subtree stack clones (`:1584`). Their in-place counterparts are covered by the same `hidden` predicate (`:1032`, `_inDraggedSubtree` at `:1011-1027`), so each descendant is also inflated exactly once. This closes a hazard the review's control table did not cover: the clone path re-invokes `nodeBuilder`, so an app-owned STABLE `GlobalKey` (a key stored per node id, the ordinary pattern for `Form` / menu anchors) duplicates on descendants too. I have not reproduced that case; an inline `GlobalKey()` cannot produce it, and cannot produce the main-path crash either, because a fresh instance per build never satisfies the `key._currentElement != null` precondition (`framework.dart:4488-4491`). Stable per-node-id keys are what test cases 1 and 2 supply.

Documentation to update in the same change: `showDragProxy` (`:169-210`) and `dragProxyBuilder` (`:212-255`) gain a paragraph stating that the dragged subtree's in-place rows are replaced by sized placeholders for the session, that row `State` is therefore recreated unless the caller supplies a `GlobalKey`, and that a `GlobalKey` on row content is now supported. Plus a CHANGELOG entry under "Unreleased" flagging the behaviour change.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Keep the in-place mount and give the proxy a non-mounting representation (a `toImageSync` raster in a `RawImage`). Rejected on contract and architecture: `dragProxyBuilder` receives `rowChild` as "exactly what `nodeBuilder` returned" (`:212-214`) and the docs at `:237-250` promise the returned subtree stays mounted so `TweenAnimationBuilder` / `ListenableBuilder` content works. A raster is a frozen widget the builder cannot meaningfully wrap, it requires `addRepaintBoundaries: true` (`:276-278`), and it costs a GPU texture per dragged row. It guts the documented contract to fix a framework-uniqueness problem.
- Debug assert plus documentation only (tell keyed rows to supply a `dragProxyBuilder` that does not mount `rowChild`). Rejected on correctness: it is not a fix. A `dragProxyBuilder` styles only the dragged row's portion (`:230-235`) and cannot suppress the descendant clones at `:1584`, so dragging an expanded parent still has no escape hatch; and a top-level `widget.child.key is GlobalKey` check misses the nested case the repro used, so the assert would need a full element walk to be useful and would still not stop the exception in release.
- Rebuild the proxy content from `nodeBuilder` instead of mounting the captured instance. Rejected as ineffective: `:1584` already does exactly that for descendants, and a fresh build re-uses the same app-owned `GlobalKey` instances, so nothing is de-duplicated.

**Architecture fit.** Widget layer only, inside `_ReorderableRowState.build`, the one site that already owns the drag-hide decision (`:1030-1033`, `_inDraggedSubtree` at `:1011-1027`). Reuses the existing inherited `dragProxyEnabled` flag (`:298`, `:324`, already in `updateShouldNotify` at `:363`) and the existing public extent query (`tree_controller.dart:1509-1510`). No render-layer, controller or `ReorderRenderPort` change. It aligns the package with `reorderable_list.dart:1293-1296` while keeping the package's own proxy design, which is the part the docs actually commit to.

**Performance.** Per drag lift and drop: one extra widget swap per row of the dragged subtree, which those rows already pay (the `hidden` flip already rebuilds them). Net saving for the session: the dragged subtree's content is inflated once instead of twice, so element count, layout and paint for the subtree drop by roughly half for the length of the drag; each hidden row's paint becomes a zero-child `RenderConstrainedBox` instead of a full row under `Opacity(0)` (`RenderOpacity.paint` already returns early at alpha 0, `C:\flutter_sdk\flutter\packages\flutter\lib\src\rendering\proxy_box.dart:949-951`, so the paint saving is smaller than the layout and build saving). One extra `getEstimatedExtent` call per hidden-row build: one map lookup plus one `Float64List` read. No per-frame cost; nothing rebuilds per pointer move (`:237-241`).

**Risk.** Everything that asserts on the in-place copy while a drag is live. Verified by reading: `test/sliver_tree/drag_subtree_hide_test.dart:99-108` (`_inPlaceOpacityOf` scopes `find.byKey(ValueKey("row-$k"))` under the `CustomScrollView`; that key no longer exists in place, so `:141`, `:147` and `:176` fail) and `test/sliver_tree/drag_handle_hidden_test.dart:82-90`, `:101`, `:122`, `:130` (`_effectiveOpacity` is unscoped and returns the MINIMUM opacity on the ancestor path, so with the in-place copy gone it would resolve the proxy's copy at 0.9).

Candidates measured with two greps over `test/sliver_tree`: `grep -rl "Opacity"` returns 11 files and `grep -rln "findsNWidgets"` returns 11 files, overlapping in 4 (`drag_handle_audit_test.dart`, `reorder_controller_disposed_swap_test.dart`, `reorder_controller_swap_mid_drag_test.dart`, `sliver_reorderable_tree_widget_test.dart`), so the union is 18 files. Two of them are the verified failures above; the other 16 each need re-checking: `can_reorder_flip_mid_drag_test.dart:30-34`, `external_cancel_drag_test.dart:26-29`, `reorder_controller_disposed_swap_test.dart:63-68`, `:103`, `reorder_controller_swap_mid_drag_test.dart:95-100`, `:133`, `drag_backstop_deactivate_test.dart:192`, `drag_handle_audit_test.dart:901`, `drag_proxy_indent_tracking_test.dart:160`, `drag_proxy_move_rebuild_test.dart:130`, `drag_proxy_test.dart:334`, `drag_subtree_proxy_test.dart:160`, `:198`, `sliver_reorderable_tree_widget_test.dart:292`, `hidden_row_hit_test.dart` (its premise, that hidden row CONTENT is unreachable, becomes trivially true; the semantics half at `:233-240` reasons about `Opacity` / `Semantics` nesting and needs re-verification because the row's own content semantics disappear), `caller_placed_handle_test.dart`, `caller_placed_handle_modes_test.dart`, `reorder_enabled_toggle_test.dart`, `synced_reorder_test.dart`.

The one consumer that does depend on the hidden row's render box measuring from real content is the extent cache itself, and it is no longer an open question: `render_sliver_tree.dart:2400` stores the placeholder's `defaultExtent` as a measured extent for a descendant first admitted mid-drag. Traced in the Solution above, accepted there with its three consequences, and pinned by test case 5.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_h5_test.dart`, default configuration (`showDragProxy: true`, `addRepaintBoundaries: true`):
1. Row content contains a nested `SizedBox` carrying a `GlobalKey` HOISTED out of the builder: one instance per node id, held in a map on the test's `State` and returned by `nodeBuilder` on every invocation, so the row's layout-phase rebuild and the overlay's captured copy name the SAME instance. An inline `GlobalKey()` will not do, and this is the whole reason the case is specified this way: a fresh instance per build makes `_retakeInactiveElement` return null (`framework.dart:4488-4491`), the layout-phase inflation is then a plain `createElement` that `object.dart:2342` permits inside the sliver's own layout callback, and the test would pass on unfixed code. Lift, move, release. Assert `tester.takeException()` is null after each of the lift, move and release pumps. Fails today on the LIFT frame's layout phase: `_onDragStart`'s `setState` (`:686`) queues every mounted key through `SliverTreeElement.update` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:190-191`), `createChild` re-invokes `nodeBuilder` inside the sliver's layout callback (`:532`, `:538`), and the retake pulls the key back out of the OVERLAY, deactivating a render object whose layout root is not the sliver (`object.dart:2363-2379`).
2. Same, with the app holding a STABLE `GlobalKey` per node id and a `StatefulWidget` under it recording `initState` / `dispose`. Drag an EXPANDED parent so the descendant clone path at `:1584` is exercised. Assert no exception and that the `State` instance is identical before and after the drop (the documented opt-in preservation, and the pin for the drop-side reactivation reasoned above).
3. Without any `GlobalKey`, assert the row's `State` is a NEW instance after a drop and that `dispose` fired exactly once at lift, pinning the documented default.
4. Sanity control: `showDragProxy: false` keeps the live in-place mount (assert `find.byKey(rowContentKey)` still resolves inside the `CustomScrollView` mid-drag), pinning the `dragProxyEnabled` gate.
5. A never-measured descendant keeps its lift-time extent and heals at the drop, pinning the accepted consequence from the Solution. Rows 100 px tall (deliberately above `defaultExtent` 48), parent `p` expanded with 40 children in the 600 px viewport, so the lower ones were never laid out. Setup sanity, both halves: assert `controller.getMeasuredExtent("p0") == 100.0` and `controller.getMeasuredExtent("p30") == null`, proving the row under test is genuinely never-measured. Record `lift0`, the sum of `controller.getCurrentExtent(k)` over `p` and its 40 children, which is the quantity `tree_controller.dart:1713-1716` re-derives per re-target. Lift `p`, `scrollController.jumpTo` far enough that `p30` enters the cache region, pump. Assert `controller.getMeasuredExtent("p30") == TreeController.defaultExtent` and that the same sum still equals `lift0`. Release, pump, assert `getMeasuredExtent("p30") == 100.0`. The mid-drag half fails today at 100.0 and `lift0 + 52`: the hidden row still inflates real content, measures its true height, and `render_sliver_tree.dart:2400` stores it, moving the gap lift off the value the proxy's frozen stack captured at `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:438`.

**Effort.** L.
