### H6. Inherited-widget reads in `nodeBuilder` never refresh rows

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-22, landed together with L26 (g)2 as chain 10 requires. `lib/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_element.dart` gains the `didChangeDependencies` override and the corrected `performRebuild` comment, `lib/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_widget.dart` gains the `nodeBuilder` cost note, and `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_h6_test.dart` is the regression test.

Verified by seven independent audit passes, each with no knowledge of the others; passes 6 and 7 were consecutively clean. Three defects were found and fixed along the way: a missing hoist assertion in the test's case 4 (it discriminated only by accident), a false absolute in the (g)2 comment (carried verbatim from this plan, corrected in both), and a false claim that `createChild` rebuilds ONLY what the cache region admits (it also force-creates sticky rows the cache region rejected, `render_sliver_tree.dart:2928-2934`, `:2952`; demonstrated by probe).

One imprecision is KNOWN and deliberately left: the `performRebuild` comment says `didChangeDependencies` has queued every mounted key and called `markNeedsLayout` by the time the build phase arrives, which is not executed on the `_children.isEmpty` early-return path. Three auditors examined it and none scored it, because the conclusion it supports (nothing left to do) holds on that path too, and the sibling producer `_onNodeDataChanged` documents itself the same way. Recorded here so it is not rediscovered as a finding.

**Finding.** Rows are built with the `SliverTreeElement` itself as their `BuildContext` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:538`, `widget.nodeBuilder(this, nodeId, depth)`), so a `Theme.of(context)` inside a `nodeBuilder` registers its dependency on that element. Nothing on the element reacts: `performRebuild` calls only `super` and queues nothing (`:194-201`), and there is no `didChangeDependencies` override in the file.

**Root cause.** `_dirtyKeys` has exactly three producers (documented at `:69-74`): `update` (`:190-191`), `_onStructuralChange` (`:236-249`) and `_onNodeDataChanged` (`:342-343`). The inherited-dependency channel is a fourth cause with no producer. A dependency change calls `Element.didChangeDependencies`, whose default implementation is `markNeedsBuild()` (`C:\flutter_sdk\flutter\packages\flutter\lib\src\widgets\framework.dart:5190-5194`), which lands in `performRebuild`; the override there drops it. The Flutter reference has the identical one-context-for-all-rows shape (`SliverChildDelegate.build` receives the ADAPTOR ELEMENT, `C:\flutter_sdk\flutter\packages\flutter\lib\src\widgets\sliver.dart:1054-1056`) and does the work synchronously instead: `SliverMultiBoxAdaptorElement.performRebuild` (`:963`) re-runs `_build` + `updateChild` for every entry of `_childElements` through `processElement` (`:972-1000`), driven at `:1032`.

**Solution.** Add a `didChangeDependencies` override to `SliverTreeElement` (`sliver_tree_element.dart`, next to `update` at `:146-192`), and leave `performRebuild` (`:194-201`) as it is apart from a corrected comment:

```
@override
void didChangeDependencies() {
  super.didChangeDependencies();
  // Fourth _dirtyKeys producer. Rows build with THIS element as their
  // BuildContext (see createChild), so every inherited read a
  // nodeBuilder performs registers here; a Theme / MediaQuery /
  // DefaultTextStyle change means every mounted row's builder output
  // may differ. Same lazy shape as update: queue, mark layout, let
  // createChild rebuild the cache-region and sticky rows the next
  // layout reaches (see _dirtyKeys). NOT only the cache region:
  // sticky headers the cache region rejected are force-created too
  // (render_sliver_tree.dart:2928-2934, :2952).
  if (_children.isEmpty) {
    return;
  }
  _dirtyKeys.addAll(_children.keys);
  renderObject.markNeedsLayout();
}
```

`didChangeDependencies`, not `performRebuild`, and it is an ADDITION, not a move. Two reasons, both verified against the framework:
- `RenderObjectElement.update` calls the private `_performRebuild()` directly (`framework.dart:6806-6814`, the call at `:6813`), NOT the virtual `performRebuild()` (`:6825-6827`). Moving the queueing out of `update` into `performRebuild`, as the review suggests, would therefore silently break the parent-rebuild refresh path. There is also no double-queueing to avoid: `_performRebuild` clears `_dirty` via `super.performRebuild()` (`:6842`), and `Element.rebuild` early-returns when not dirty (`framework.dart:5505-5507`), so `update` and `performRebuild` never both run for one frame.
- `didChangeDependencies` fires for exactly one cause, which keeps the `_dirtyKeys` doc's "populated by N sources" list honest and cause-named. `performRebuild` would also fire on the reassemble path. When that reassemble makes the ancestor hand down a FRESH `SliverTree`, `update`'s `_didReassemble` branch (`:177-182`) handles it more strongly via `_invalidateAllChildren`. When the ancestor hands down the IDENTICAL instance, `Element.updateChild` short-circuits (`framework.dart:4014`), `update` does not run that frame, and the rows stay stale until some later `update`. Measured during implementation review: 0 rows rebuild on the reassemble frame in that shape. That gap is real, pre-existing and hot-reload-only; it is filed as M26 rather than folded in here.

ALL mounted keys, not a cache-region subset, and the distinction is only apparent. `_dirtyKeys` is a QUEUE, consumed in `createChild` (`:528`, `_dirtyKeys.remove(nodeId)`), which `RenderSliverTree.performLayout` calls only for admitted keys. Off-screen queued entries wait for re-entry or are dropped by stale eviction (`:504`). So queueing all mounted keys already yields cache-region-only rebuilding, which is the exact design `update` uses (`:184-191`) and the `_dirtyKeys` doc describes (`:76-87`). Filtering at queue time would need the admission answer before layout has computed it, and would lose the "refreshed on re-entry" property.

Also update `SliverTree.nodeBuilder`'s doc (`sliver_tree_widget.dart:73-85`): rows share ONE `BuildContext`, so any inherited widget any row reads dirties every mounted row, and a high-frequency inherited value in a row builder costs one queue plus one layout per notification.

**Sequencing dependency (chain 10, L26 with H6 and M14).** Chain 10 in the plan's Sequencing section is "comment fixes that depend on their code change", L26 with H6 and M14. This block owns one of the two comments L26 defers.

L26's sub-item (g)2 rewrites the comment at `sliver_tree_element.dart:197-200`, inside `performRebuild` (`:194-201`), which today claims "the actual reconciliation lands when the next layout fires and iterates cache-region keys". That is this block's Finding restated: `performRebuild` marks nothing dirty, and `createChild` early-returns for an existing, non-dirty key (the `needsRefresh` read at `:528`, the return at `:529-531`), so no reconciliation lands. The comment becomes true only once THIS block's `didChangeDependencies` override queues the keys, which is why the Solution above leaves `performRebuild` alone "apart from a corrected comment". Land (g)2 INSIDE this block's commit. Landing it first turns a comment that is at least honestly wrong into one that reads as a specification the code does not meet; landing it later leaves this block shipping the stale comment it named. L26's block records the same rule.

M14 is chain 10's third member and edits the same file, `forgetChild` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:588-604`), for L26's other deferred comment, (g)3 at `:593-597`. There is no behavioral interaction between M14 and this block: the inherited-dependency channel and the `GlobalKey` retake path share no state, which is why the Sequencing section can list M14 among the items independent of everything else AND as a chain-10 member without contradiction. The constraint runs from L26's comment edits into each of them, never between them, which is also why the suggested landing order is free to put them adjacent. The one mechanical coupling is line numbers: the `didChangeDependencies` override this block inserts next to `update` (`:146-192`) sits ABOVE `performRebuild` at `:194`, so it shifts `forgetChild`'s body and with it both M14's deletion range (`:593-601`) and L26's (g)3 anchor (`:593-597`). Whichever of the two lands second re-derives those ranges from the file rather than reusing the numbers written in its block.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Wrap each row in a `Builder` inside `createChild` so every row gets its own context and its own dependency registration. Rejected on both axes. Performance: the framework would then dirty each row element directly and rebuild it in the build phase, bypassing `_dirtyKeys` and the cache-region deferral entirely, which is the full `SliverMultiBoxAdaptorElement` cost the deferral exists to avoid, plus one extra element and one extra build per row. Architecture: `nodeBuilder`'s `BuildContext` is a public contract, and this silently changes what `context.findRenderObject()` and every ancestor lookup resolve to.
- Queue in `performRebuild` instead. Rejected: it does not fire on the `update` path (see above), so the queueing cannot be moved there. Adding it there in ADDITION to `update` would conflate the dependency cause with reassemble at a shared sink, which is the exact attribution error this item exists to correct. Note the gain is not zero, and an earlier draft of this bullet was wrong to say so: because the element is dirty on the reassemble path too, queueing here would also close the hot-reload staleness measured in M26. M26 closes it at `reassemble` itself, which keeps one cause to one call site.

**Architecture fit.** Element layer, one new override next to the three existing `_dirtyKeys` producers, reusing the exact `queue + markNeedsLayout` pair `_onNodeDataChanged` uses (`:342-343`) and the lazy `createChild` consumption the whole mechanism is built on. No new state, no new field.

**Performance.** Before: 0 work, 0 correctness. After, per dependency notification: `O(|_children|)` set inserts plus one `markNeedsLayout`, then `O(|admitted|)` `nodeBuilder` plus `updateChild` calls during the next layout. `|_children|` is roughly the cache region plus not-yet-evicted stragglers; the figure the module doc records for a steady 2000-row tree is 18 mounted (CLAUDE.md, the eviction note in the `AnimationCoordinator` entry; I did not re-measure it), so a theme toggle costs about 18 hash inserts and at most 18 row rebuilds per notification. Against the reference: `SliverMultiBoxAdaptorElement.performRebuild` does `|_childElements|` full `_build` + `updateChild` calls synchronously per notification (`sliver.dart:1032` driving `processElement` at `:972-1000`, `_build` at `:981`), including keep-alive and off-cache-region children (`:993` shows kept-alive entries living in the same map), so this is a strict subset.

Notification frequency is bounded, not one-shot: `MaterialApp` wraps in `AnimatedTheme` (`C:\flutter_sdk\flutter\packages\flutter\lib\src\material\app.dart:1057-1062`), `_AnimatedThemeState.build` emits a fresh `Theme` per tick (`theme.dart:303-305`) and `_InheritedTheme.updateShouldNotify` compares `theme.data != old.theme.data` (`theme.dart:232`), so dependents ARE notified on every frame of `kThemeAnimationDuration` (200ms, `theme.dart:20`). The review's claim that the theme "animates without rebuilding the subtree" is wrong about the dependents: the subtree is not rebuilt (`_AnimatedThemeState.build` passes the identical `widget.child` through, so `Element.updateChild` short-circuits at `framework.dart:4014`), but the dependency channel fires every tick, and that is exactly why the fix works. Cost of a 200ms toggle is therefore roughly 13 frames of the above, matching what any other `Theme.of` consumer in the app pays. No storm reintroduced: the regression the `_dirtyKeys` doc names (`:83-87`) is `update`-driven by an ancestor `ListenableBuilder` on the controller, pinned by `test/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:685`, and that path is untouched. Allocations: none beyond the set's growth.

**Risk.** Read by the whole refresh path: `createChild` (`:517-549`), stale eviction (`:501-509`), GC (`:385-393`), controller swap (`:161`). Existing suites to re-run: `test/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_widget_test.dart` (the four build-count regressions in the "nodeBuilder invocation during animation" group at `:534`, namely the tests starting at `:535`, `:610`, `:685` and `:787`; none change an inherited widget, so all should stay green, and they are the exact instruments that would catch an over-queue), `test/sliver_tree/tree_node_builder_targeted_rebuild_test.dart`, `test/sliver_tree/parent_data_refresh_iteration_test.dart`, `test/sliver_tree/child_count_invalidation_test.dart`, `test/sliver_tree/data_only_reinsert_notification_test.dart`, `test/sliver_tree/controller_swap_test.dart`. Unverified window, and I am mirroring the existing sites rather than guarding it: `_onStructuralChange` (`:233`) already calls `markNeedsLayout` without an `_inLayout` guard (the field is `:54`), and a nested `owner.buildScope` inside `createChild` (`:532`) could in principle rebuild a dirty ancestor `InheritedElement` mid-layout and route a notification here. No test constructs that window today; adding an asymmetric guard would make this site inconsistent with the three existing producers. A second window was raised during implementation review and is now verified as safe rather than left open: `Element.activate` calls `didChangeDependencies()` whenever the element had dependencies (`framework.dart:4769-4771`), so this override also runs during reactivation and calls `markNeedsLayout` there. That is both safe and wanted. Safe, because `RenderObject.markNeedsLayout` sets its local `_needsLayout` flag first (`object.dart:2666`) and reaches the pipeline owner only through a null-guarded pattern match (`:2667`), so a render object that is not yet re-attached simply carries the flag until it is. Wanted, because an element that was inactive may have missed inherited changes, so queueing its rows on reactivation is the correct response, not a spurious one.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_h6_test.dart`. Cases 2, 3 and 4 share ONE harness, and its defining property is load-bearing: the widget that flips the inherited value must pass the `CustomScrollView` subtree through as a HOISTED `child`, so that flipping the value rebuilds only the inherited widget and not the `SliverTree` instance. Without the hoist the toggle rebuilds `SliverTree` too, `SliverTreeElement.update` queues every mounted key (`sliver_tree_element.dart:190-191`), and the row sees the new value even on unfixed code, so the test would pass today and prove nothing. The hoist is the same mechanism `AnimatedTheme` relies on (`theme.dart:304` passes the identical `widget.child`, and `Element.updateChild` short-circuits on `child.widget == newWidget` at `framework.dart:4014`), which is why case 1 fails today without needing it stated. Shape:

```
class _ValueScope extends InheritedWidget {
  const _ValueScope({required this.value, required super.child});
  final int value;
  static int of(BuildContext context) =>
      context.dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType<_ValueScope>()!.value;
  @override
  bool updateShouldNotify(_ValueScope old) => value != old.value;
}

class _Toggler extends StatefulWidget {
  const _Toggler({required this.child});
  final Widget child;
  ...
}
// _TogglerState.build returns _ValueScope(value: _value, child: widget.child);
// setState only changes _value, so widget.child is the identical instance.
```

Every case using it asserts the hoist held, as a setup sanity check: capture `tester.widget<SliverTree<String, String>>(find.byType(SliverTree<String, String>))` before and after the toggle and assert `identical(before, after)`.

1. `MaterialApp` with a `theme` held in the test's own `StatefulWidget`, `Scaffold > CustomScrollView > SliverTree`, `nodeBuilder` reading `Theme.of(context).brightness` into a per-key log and returning a `SizedBox` painted with a theme colour. Pump, assert the last logged brightness is light. Flip to `ThemeData.dark()`, `pumpAndSettle()` past `kThemeAnimationDuration`, assert the last logged brightness is dark AND the mounted row widget carries the dark colour. The log is empty, so the case dies on `log.last` rather than on a brightness comparison. 2. Non-animated control isolating the mechanism from `AnimatedTheme` timing: the shared harness above with a single `_Toggler` toggle, `_ValueScope.of` read in the `nodeBuilder`. One `pump`, assert the row saw the new value. Fails today.
3. `SliverList` control with the same harness, the same hoist assertion (on the `SliverList` instance) and the same log, asserting it already updates, so the harness itself is proven sound. ### M1. Re-insert of a mid-exit node under a collapsed parent leaves a permanent row

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, three audit passes, 2 and 3 consecutively
clean; pass 1 replaced a false absolute in the new test comment ("keeps the
row visible forever": any later order rebuild drops it, since the completed
enter leaves no standalone for the collapsed-parent branch to retain). Landed
as the Solution prescribes, and this file's anchors were NOT stale: the three
edits went in at the cited symbols with the gate verbatim
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:475-495`, flag default false at `:478`,
gate at `:490-493`), `_cancelDeletion`'s root half routed through the policy
with `explicitTarget: true` (`:410-415`) and the unconditional
`_clearPendingDeletion` moved into the non-animate arm, and the case-1 doc
and `_cancelDeletion` doc updated to the new contract. Descendant behavior is
bit-identical: with the flag at its false default the new gate reduces to the
old three-way conjunction.

The regression test extends `tree_controller_test.dart`'s "honors parentKey
when node is pending deletion under another parent" in place, per this
block's prescription (`:1417-1441` after the edit): the destination-collapsed
sanity plus the settle assertion. Pre-fix red exactly as predicted:
`visibleNodes` settles to [a, b, x]. Both new assertions were shown red
individually: the settle pin by the pre-fix run, the sanity by a test-side
variant that expands the destination first, which itself surfaced a
construction trap worth recording: `expand()` no-ops on a childless node
(`tree_controller.dart:3818-3821`), so the variant only goes red once the
destination is given a child. One measured gap, recorded deliberately: with
`explicitTarget` flipped to false at the root call site, the ENTIRE suite
stays green, so no existing test discriminates the flag; its justification
is this block's Alternatives argument (a group-captured exit would snap
instead of grow), which remains design-level and untested. The block's
suites pass (121 tests), the full suite reads 1098 passed, 4 skipped (count
unchanged: the repro extends an existing test), `flutter analyze` stays at
the 48-issue baseline.

**Finding.** `_cancelDeletion` unconditionally reverses the ROOT key into an
enter (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:408-413`: `_clearPendingDeletion(key)`
then `if (animate) _startStandaloneEnterAnimation(key)`), while every
descendant goes through the case-1/2/3 policy that DOES gate on
`_ancestorsExpandedFast` (`:468-489`, gate at `:478-480`). `moveNode` reaches
the correct behavior only because it routes its root through the same policy
(`_revertSubtreeFromPendingDeletion`, `:437-441`, called from
`tree_controller.dart:3586`).

**Root cause.** The enter installed at `_tree_controller_animation.dart:410`
puts a standalone state on a node whose new parent is collapsed.
`_rebuildVisibleOrderImpl`'s collapsed-parent branch keeps any child that
`_hasStandalone` (`tree_controller.dart:4624-4636`), so the row stays in the
order; when the enter completes, `_finalizeAnimation` falls through the
exiting branch and the pending-deletion safety net and returns `false`
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:668-678`), so
`_onStandaloneTickComplete` never adds it to `_keysToRemoveScratch`
(`tree_controller.dart:466-484`). The row is now permanent.

**Solution.** Single owner: make `_revertSinglePendingDeletion` the only site
that decides an exit reversal, and give it the one exemption the root needs.

1. `_tree_controller_animation.dart:468-471`, add a flag:

```dart
void _revertSinglePendingDeletion(
  TKey nodeId, {
  required bool preserveSubtreeState,
  bool explicitTarget = false,
}) {
```

2. Replace the case-1 gate at `:478-480` with:

```dart
    // `explicitTarget` relaxes ONLY the "was mid-exit" requirement: the
    // caller named this key, so it comes back even if its exit had already
    // been swallowed by a group. The visibility gate is NOT relaxed. A key
    // re-added under a collapsed chain must not enter; entering there
    // parks a permanent row under a collapsed parent (M1).
    final bool reverseIntoEnter =
        (explicitTarget || (preserveSubtreeState && isStandaloneExiting)) &&
        _ancestorsExpandedFast(nodeId);
    if (reverseIntoEnter) {
```

3. `_cancelDeletion` (`:400-426`): drop the unconditional
`_clearPendingDeletion(key)` at `:408` (the policy method early-returns on a
non-pending key at `:472-474`) and route the root:

```dart
    if (animate) {
      _revertSinglePendingDeletion(
        key,
        preserveSubtreeState: true,
        explicitTarget: true,
      );
    } else {
      _clearPendingDeletion(key);
      _removeAnimation(key);
    }
```

**Exact predicate:** `_ancestorsExpandedFast(key)` (`tree_controller.dart:321`),
read AFTER the relocation. Both callers already relocate first
(`insertRoot` at `tree_controller.dart:2418-2445` before the
`_cancelDeletion` at `:2447`; `insert` at `:2889-2923` before `:2925`), which
is exactly the ordering `_revertSubtreeFromPendingDeletion`'s doc demands
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:432-435`). When the predicate is false the
node falls into case 2 (`:483-484`): pending-deletion cleared, exit left
running, so the row shrinks away smoothly and `_finalizeAnimation`'s non-purge
branch (`:655-665`) drops it from the order with its structure intact under
the collapsed parent.

**Sequencing dependency.** M1 and M5 both edit the same body,
`_cancelDeletion` (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:400-426`), and M1 deletes
the install site M5's call-site table annotates: after step 3 above there is no
`_startStandaloneEnterAnimation` at `:410` any more, only the
`_revertSinglePendingDeletion` call, so the family declaration M5 needs on
that path is the one literal inside the policy method at `:482`. M2 edits the
descendant half of the SAME body (`:414-425`). Land them in the order
**M1, then M2, then M5**: M1 rewrites the root half, M2 rewrites the descendant
half against M1's result, and M5 then annotates whatever install sites survive
(the `:482` literal, plus `tree_controller.dart:2580`, `:3074`, `:3117`).
Landing M5 first means re-doing its `:410` annotation and re-checking its
count of 15 install sites; landing M2 before M1 means resolving the same
conflict hunk twice.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Patch the two call sites (`tree_controller.dart:2447`, `:2925`) with their
  own `_ancestorsExpandedFast` check before calling `_cancelDeletion`. Rejected:
  it creates a third copy of the visibility predicate (moveNode already has

- Drop `explicitTarget` and call
  `_revertSinglePendingDeletion(key, preserveSubtreeState: true)`. Rejected:

  of growing from its captured extent, a visual regression on the path
  `_startStandaloneEnterAnimation` explicitly handles via
  `_captureAndRemoveFromGroups` (`:370`).

**Architecture fit.** Controller layer, animation part file.
`_revertSinglePendingDeletion` stays the single owner of the case-1/2/3
policy; `_cancelDeletion` becomes a thin root-plus-descendants driver, which is
the shape `_revertSubtreeFromPendingDeletion` already has (`:437-441`).

**Performance.** Unchanged: one extra bool parameter and one
`_ancestorsExpandedFast` call (O(1), eagerly maintained by the node store per
`tree_controller.dart:4578-4580`) on a path that already runs a full
`_getDescendants` walk (`:414`).

**Risk.** `_cancelDeletion` has exactly two callers
(`tree_controller.dart:2447`, `:2925`); `_revertSinglePendingDeletion` has two
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:421`, `:440`). Existing tests to re-run and

`test/sliver_tree/tree_controller_test.dart:1378-1419` in place (house

### M2. Re-inserting a mid-exit node keeps its old subtree

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, five audit passes, 4 and 5 consecutively
clean; pass 3 caught the M1-era `_cancelDeletion` doc gone stale ("root and
descendants all route through the policy"), now rewritten for the split.
Landed as the Solution prescribes, contract (B): the descendant half routes
default-flag re-adds through the new `_discardPendingSubtree`
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:423-426` branch, helper at `:459-490`,
body verbatim from this block), the preserve loop passes the literal `true`,
and `preservePendingSubtreeState` is documented on both public signatures
(`tree_controller.dart:2546-2553`, `:3018-3025`) with the exit-lands-later
caveat this block requires.

`test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_m2_test.dart` implements steps 1 through 7 as
three tests (repro, A/B convergence control, smoothness control) under
`debugFullConsistencyChecks = true`. Pre-fix red at exactly step 4:
`getLiveChildren("A")` read `["a1"]`; both controls passed pre-fix, as
designed. All 11 assertions were individually shown red: six by test-side
constructions, the step-4 pin by the pre-fix run, the three settled-state
pins under a discard-disabled mutation, and the smoothness pin under a
purge-immediately mutation (dropping the standalone skip moved c by exactly
b1's mid-exit 50 px), with the lib restored diff-verified byte-identical
after each.

One finding against this block's Risk enumeration: FOUR pre-existing tests
pinned the old default-restore contract and were missed by the list, all
four present at 4d15c0c (measured). The two tests in `tree_controller_test.
dart`'s "remove and re-add across intermediate animation states" group, the
depth-cascade test sitting just past the list's cited `:1378-1419` range,
and `skip_repro_test.dart`'s "reinsert then re-expand restores descendants
smoothly" all re-added with default flags and asserted subtree restoration.
Each was adapted to `preservePendingSubtreeState: true` with a comment
naming this contract, which preserves their subjects (extent resume, depth
cascade, restoration smoothness) on the path that now owns restoration; the
adapted extent-resume tests pass through case 1 because the preserve branch
keeps the parent's expansion. Recorded so the next contract-touching item
re-greps for affected tests rather than trusting a block's enumeration.
The block's Risk suites pass, the full suite reads 1101 passed, 4 skipped
(the 1098 post-M1 baseline plus these three), `flutter analyze` stays at
the 48-issue baseline, and the source-encoding guard is green.

**Finding.** With default flags, `_cancelDeletion(preserveSubtreeState: false)`
sends every descendant to `_revertSinglePendingDeletion` with
`preserveSubtreeState: false` (`_tree_controller_animation.dart:421-424`),
where case 1 can never fire, so each mid-exit descendant takes case 2
(`:483-484`): pending-deletion CLEARED, exit left running. The subtree
therefore survives structurally. `remove(animate: false)` instead purges it
outright (`tree_controller.dart:3129` calls `_removeNodesImmediate`,
`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:490-492`), so the observable result depends on
whether an exit happened to be in flight.

**Root cause.** Case 2 clears the pending-deletion marker
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:484`), which is precisely what makes
`_finalizeAnimation` take its non-purge branch (`:655-665`) instead of the
purge branch (`:553-654`). Clearing the marker was the right call for
`preserveSubtreeState: true`; it is applied unconditionally.

**Contract decision.** Two options:

- **(A) Restore the subtree.** Document on `insertRoot`/`insert` that re-adding
  a mid-exit node brings its descendants back.
- **(B) Discard the subtree, keep the motion.** A default re-add restores the
  NODE, not its subtree, exactly as `remove(animate: false)` plus `insert`
  does; descendants stay pending-deletion so the existing purge machinery
  removes them when their exits land.

Pick **(B)**. Three architecture reasons. First, `preservePendingSubtreeState`
exists as the opt-in for (A); if (A) were the default the flag would have no
meaning, and both declarative call sites already pass `true`
(`tree_sync_controller.dart:299`, `:664`), so (B) costs the sync layer
nothing. Second, an observable structural outcome must not depend on animation
timing; today the same two-call sequence settles to `getChildren("A") == [a1]`
or `[]` depending only on whether the style happened to be animating. Third,
(B) keeps the smoothness the descendants were preserved for:
`test/sliver_tree/skip_repro_test.dart:204-277` pins that after a default
re-insert of "b", "c" must not jump by b1's current extent (assertion at
`:268-274`), which requires b1 to stay in the visible order and keep
shrinking. Keeping the pending-deletion marker keeps it in the order and keeps
it animating; only the terminal branch changes.

Which rebuild branch admits b1 there is worth stating exactly, because the
audit challenged it. The re-add is `insertRoot(..., index: 1)` with default
flags, so the arm at `tree_controller.dart:2469-2478` runs and
`_setExpandedKey(node.key, false)` at `:2475` COLLAPSES "b" before the
`_markVisibleOrderDirty()` at `:2476`. At rebuild time "b" is therefore an
expanded=false, non-pending parent, which is the else branch at
`:4624-4636`, admitting b1 via `_hasStandalone`. It is not the expanded branch
at `:4620-4623`: that branch is unreachable for "b" here. The in-repo comment
at `:2469-2474` names the same branch ("continue animating out under the
restored parent via `_rebuildVisibleOrder`'s 'collapsed with active
animations' branch"). The audit's correction on this point does not hold, and
`:4624-4636` stands.

**Solution.** In `_tree_controller_animation.dart`, replace the descendant
loop of `_cancelDeletion` (`:414-425`, the half M1 does not touch) and add one
helper next to it:

```dart
    if (!preserveSubtreeState) {
      _discardPendingSubtree(key, animate: animate);
      return;
    }
    for (final nodeId in _getDescendants(key)) {
      if (!animate) {
        _clearPendingDeletion(nodeId);
        _removeAnimation(nodeId);
        continue;
      }
      _revertSinglePendingDeletion(nodeId, preserveSubtreeState: true);
    }
```

(The descendant loop now only ever runs with `preserveSubtreeState: true`,
which is the only value under which case 1 was reachable in the first place.)

```dart
  /// Discards the in-flight removal subtree under a node whose deletion was
  /// just cancelled WITHOUT `preservePendingSubtreeState`.
  ///
  /// Contract: a default re-add restores the node, not its subtree, matching
  /// `remove(animate: false)` followed by `insert`. Members with a live
  /// standalone exit KEEP their pending-deletion marker, so
  /// [_finalizeAnimation]'s purge branch removes them when the exit lands;
  /// that is what stops the following rows jumping upward by the
  /// descendant's current extent in a single frame (pinned by
  /// `test/sliver_tree/skip_repro_test.dart`). Members with no exit were
  /// never in the visible order, so nothing would ever finalize them; they
  /// and their whole subtree are purged here.
  ///
  /// The walk descends into a member only once it has decided to purge it,
  /// so a purged node never leaves a live child behind and no parent-pointer
  /// severing (the [_finalizeAnimation] ABA guard) is needed: a survivor's
  /// parent is always a survivor, because a node with an exit was in
  /// `_order`, and `_order` is closed under "child present implies parent
  /// present" (`_rebuildVisibleOrderImpl` only pushes children of a key it
  /// has already added, `tree_controller.dart:4601-4638`).
  void _discardPendingSubtree(TKey key, {required bool animate}) {
    final seed = _childListOf(key);
    if (seed == null || seed.isEmpty) {
      return;
    }
    List<TKey>? purgeNow;
    final stack = <(TKey, bool)>[];
    for (final child in seed) {
      stack.add((child, false));
    }
    while (stack.isNotEmpty) {
      final (nodeId, forced) = stack.removeLast();
      if (!forced) {
        if (!_isPendingDeletion(nodeId)) {
          continue;
        }
        if (animate && _hasStandalone(nodeId)) {
          continue;
        }
      }
      (purgeNow ??= <TKey>[]).add(nodeId);
      final children = _childListOf(nodeId);
      if (children != null) {
        for (final grandChild in children) {
          stack.add((grandChild, true));
        }
      }
    }
    if (purgeNow != null) {
      _purgeAndRemoveFromOrder(purgeNow);
    }
  }
```

`_purgeAndRemoveFromOrder` (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:379-486`) already
does the whole protocol: visible-subtree-size decrement, unlink from the
parent child list, `_purgeNodeData` (which clears standalone state, group
membership, pending-deletion and releases the nid, `:312-352`),
`_liveIndexCache.bump()` and order compaction. Parents-before-children is the
same ordering `_removeNodesImmediate` feeds it (`:490-492`).

Also document `preservePendingSubtreeState` on both public signatures
(`tree_controller.dart:2402`, `:2856`): today it carries no dartdoc at all.
The doc must say that a surviving descendant is discarded when its exit
lands, not at the instant of the re-add, since the raw
`getChildren` view (`tree_controller.dart:898-902`) still lists it until then.

**Sequencing dependency.** M2 is not independent. It is the middle of the THREE
blocks that rewrite one method body, `_cancelDeletion`
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:400-426`): M1 rewrites the ROOT half
(`:408-413`, the `_clearPendingDeletion(key)` plus the enter/`_removeAnimation`
branch), M2 rewrites the DESCENDANT half (`:414-425`), and M5 annotates the
install sites in the same body with their animation family. Land **M1, then M2,
then M5**. M1's step 3 replaces only the root branch and leaves the descendant
loop verbatim, so M2's replacement applies on top of it without a conflict;
landing M2 first means resolving the same hunk twice, and landing M5 before
either means re-doing its `:410` annotation and re-checking its install-site
count. Nothing in M2's contract decision or its tests depends on M1 or M5, only
the patch order does.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Contract (A) plus a doc line. Rejected: it makes an idempotent-looking
  re-add resurrect an arbitrary amount of structure, and it leaves the
  animated and non-animated paths permanently divergent, which is the actual
  defect.
- Purge every pending descendant immediately (drop the exits). Rejected: it
  yanks the rows out of the visible order in one frame and breaks
  `test/sliver_tree/skip_repro_test.dart:204-277`, the exact regression that
  test exists to catch.

**Architecture fit.** Controller layer, animation part file, beside the policy
it complements. Reuses `_purgeAndRemoveFromOrder`, the designated general-case
purge (its own doc names the two sites allowed to bypass it,
`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:359-363`), rather than adding a fourth purge
protocol.

**Performance.** Before: O(D) descendant walk plus one policy call per member.
After: same O(D) walk (now iterative with an explicit stack instead of
`_getDescendants`'s allocated list, so one fewer list allocation in the
default path), plus `_purgeAndRemoveFromOrder` over the dormant members only,
which is the same work `remove(animate: false)` already does. No per-frame
cost. Allocations: one `List<(TKey, bool)>` stack and one lazily-created
`purgeNow` list, both on a cold path.

**Risk.** Readers of the default-flag re-add: `insertRoot`
(`tree_controller.dart:2447`), `insert` (`:2925`),
`SectionedListController.addSection` (`lib/sectioned_sliver_list/sectioned_list_controller.dart:314`)
and `addItem` (`:406`), `TreeSyncController` root add
(`tree_sync_controller.dart:317`, the branch taken only when the key is
absent). Both sync re-add branches pass `preservePendingSubtreeState: true`
(`:299`, `:664`) and are unaffected. Existing tests to re-run:
`test/sliver_tree/skip_repro_test.dart` (the `:204-277` default-path case is
the important one and should stay green),
`test/sliver_tree/reparent_during_exit_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/tree_controller_test.dart:1154-1230` and `:1378-1419`,
`test/sectioned_sliver_list/readd_pending_deletion_test.dart` (both sections
are created with `itemsOf: (_) => const []`, `:38`, `:73`, so the discard is a
no-op there), `test/sectioned_sliver_list/imperative_remove_with_mirror_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/purge_cache_audit_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/purge_subtree_visible_size_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/visible_subtree_size_invariant_fuzz_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_m2_test.dart`, with

**Effort.** M.

### M3. `expand(animate: false)` mid-collapse misorders new descendants

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23, five audit passes, 4 and 5 consecutively clean. All three parts landed as prescribed: `VisibleOrderBuffer.insertAllKeysAtGaps` (backward merge, O(suffix + k)), `_spliceIntoVisibleOrderAfter` in `_tree_controller_helpers.dart`, and both `expand` call sites routed through it on `alreadyVisibleCount == 0`. The new primitive follows the buffer's existing mutator protocol exactly: capacity, write, `_len +=`, `_suppress`-guarded `bumpFromSelf`, one `_onMutated()`.

Anchors re-derived rather than trusted: the Solution's `:3726-3746` / `:3738-3742` / `:3740` were stale by +42, and the current sites are named rather than re-cited, because this file moves on every landed item. `_updateIndicesFrom(gaps.first)` is equivalent to the old `minInsertIndex` and never later than it, since gaps are non-decreasing and the first inserted key lands exactly at `gaps.first`.

**Path 2's mixed branch has ZERO test coverage, measured not assumed.** Instrumented all three Path-2 branches and ran the full suite: all-new 107 hits, all-visible 3, mixed 0. Reaching it needs a node that is collapsed, holds no operation group, and whose expansion-gated flatten still names a row already in `_order`; several attempted sequences all collapsed into the all-new branch instead. The rewrite of that branch was kept anyway: the cursor logic it depends on IS pinned by the three non-animated repros driving the same helper, the only untested part is the `onVisit` transcription, and leaving the old copy would preserve exactly the duplicate protocol this item exists to remove. Anyone who reaches that branch with a test should add it.

`test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_m3_test.dart`, five cases. Three are repros (non-animated expand mid-collapse; the same via `animateScrollToKey`'s immediate ancestor expansion; a new child BETWEEN two mid-collapse siblings), all failing pre-fix with `["A", "a3", "a1", "a2"]`. One is a multi-gap oracle: six new children interleaved among four mid-collapse ones, producing `gaps = [1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 5]`, checked against `getLiveChildren` rather than a literal; pre-fix it yields all six new keys at the head. It was added because the other four exercise `k == 1` only, where the merge is indistinguishable from one memmove.

Two test defects were found by audit and fixed. The fifth case was originally labelled a Path-2 mixed-branch guard; it is not, because an animated `expand` whose key already holds an operation group takes Path 1 (`tree_controller.dart:3804-3806`), and an in-flight collapse is exactly such a group. That was caught by neutering the helper's cursor and watching the test stay green, not by reading. Separately, a setup assertion on the old children's relative order was DROPPED for being inert: `insert` never reorders existing children, so it could not fail in the direction it claimed. It was replaced by a span check that the new keys are interleaved rather than contiguous, which does fail when the insert positions are made contiguous.

The plan's request for a direct `insertAllKeysAtGaps` unit test was not met as written: `VisibleOrderBuffer` is not exported, so a direct test would widen the public API, against L11. It is tested through its only caller instead. `gap == 0` and `k == 0` are unreachable that way (the cursor starts at `parentIndex + 1 >= 1`, and the helper returns before calling when there are no gaps), so those two guards are defensive and are labelled as such.

Full suite 1084 passed, 4 skipped; `flutter analyze` unchanged at 48; the Solution's eight Risk suites plus both invariant fuzz suites run green together (146 tests); `test/source_encoding_guard_test.dart` green and all 295 added `lib/` lines pure ASCII.

**Finding.** The non-animated branch collects every member of
`_flattenSubtree(key, includeRoot: false)` that is not already in the order and
splices the whole block at `parentIndex + 1`
(`tree_controller.dart:3726-3746`, block insert at `:3738-3742`), ignoring
where the members already in the order sit. The animated Path-2 mixed branch
solves exactly this with a cursor (`:3865-3897`), and Path 1 uses
`_insertNewNodeAmongSiblings` (`:3799`, declared at
`_tree_controller_animation.dart:686`, doc from `:681`).

**Root cause.** `nodesToShow` is a DFS pre-order flatten (`_flattenSubtree`,
`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:265-307`), so `[a1, a2, a3]`. Mid-collapse,
`a1` and `a2` are still in `_order` (the op-group carve-out at
`tree_controller.dart:4624-4636`), so `nodesToInsert == [a3]` and
`_order.insertAllKeys(parentIndex + 1, [a3])` (`:3740`) places a3 BEFORE them:
`[A, a3, a1, a2]`. `_removeAnimation` (`:3735`) only detaches animation state
(`tree_controller.dart:548` to `_animation_coordinator.dart:613-636`); it never
touches `_order`, so nothing corrects the placement.

**Solution.** One shared mixed-splice helper for both sites, built on ONE new
bulk primitive rather than on repeated single inserts. The existing Path-2
cursor is not extracted as written: `VisibleOrderBuffer.insertNid`
(`_visible_order_buffer.dart:432-441`) `setRange`s the whole suffix on EVERY
call, so k cursor inserts cost O(k * suffix). The batched form computes all k
positions in a non-mutating pass and moves each entry exactly once.

Part 1, `_visible_order_buffer.dart`, beside `insertAllKeys` (`:460-479`),
which is the same protocol for the all-new case:

```dart
  /// Inserts [keys] at the PRE-insert positions [gaps], in one pass.
  ///
  /// `gaps[i]` is the index in the current buffer that `keys[i]` lands in
  /// front of; several entries may share a gap and keep their relative
  /// order. [gaps] must be non-decreasing and in range, which the caller
  /// guarantees by building it with a forward-only cursor.
  ///
  /// The mixed-block counterpart of [insertAllKeys]: k separate [insertNid]
  /// calls each memmove the whole suffix, O(k * suffix), while the backward
  /// merge below moves every entry exactly once, O(suffix + k).
  void insertAllKeysAtGaps(List<int> gaps, List<TKey> keys) {
    final int k = keys.length;
    assert(gaps.length == k);
    assert(() {
      for (int i = 1; i < k; i++) {
        if (gaps[i] < gaps[i - 1]) {
          return false;
        }
      }
      return k == 0 || (gaps.first >= 0 && gaps.last <= _len);
    }(), "insertAllKeysAtGaps needs non-decreasing, in-range gaps.");
    if (k == 0) {
      return;
    }
    _ensureOrderCapacity(_len + k);
    int write = _len + k - 1;
    int read = _len - 1;
    for (int i = k - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      final int gap = gaps[i];
      while (read >= gap) {
        _orderNids[write--] = _orderNids[read--];
      }
      _orderNids[write--] = _nids[keys[i]]!;
    }
    _len += k;
    if (!_suppress) {
      for (int i = 0; i < k; i++) {
        bumpFromSelf(_nids[keys[i]]!, 1);
      }
    }
    _onMutated();
  }
```

Part 2, `_tree_controller_helpers.dart`:

```dart
  /// Splices the DFS pre-order [nodesToShow] into the visible order starting
  /// just after [parentIndex], keeping every NEW key at its structural
  /// position relative to members that are ALREADY in the buffer (rows a
  /// mid-collapse operation group is still animating out). Pending-deletion
  /// members are skipped.
  ///
  /// [onVisit] fires for each surviving member during the placement pass,
  /// with `alreadyVisible` telling the caller which arm it is on, so
  /// per-node bookkeeping (group membership, animation teardown) happens in
  /// the same walk.
  ///
  /// Pass 1 mutates nothing, which is why there is no `insertOffset`
  /// correction: `_order.indexOf` still answers in the one index space
  /// every gap is expressed in. Pass 2 is a single
  /// [VisibleOrderBuffer.insertAllKeysAtGaps] plus one [_updateIndicesFrom].
  /// The cursor only moves forward, so `gaps` is sorted by construction
  /// even if the order it reads is already corrupt, and a new row can never
  /// land ahead of a member visited before it.
  bool _spliceIntoVisibleOrderAfter(
    int parentIndex,
    List<TKey> nodesToShow, {
    void Function(TKey nodeId, bool alreadyVisible)? onVisit,
  }) {
    List<int>? gaps;
    List<TKey>? newKeys;
    int cursor = parentIndex + 1;
    for (final nodeId in nodesToShow) {
      if (_isPendingDeletion(nodeId)) {
        continue;
      }
      final existingIndex = _order.indexOf(nodeId);
      final alreadyVisible = existingIndex != VisibleOrderBuffer.kNotVisible;
      onVisit?.call(nodeId, alreadyVisible);
      if (alreadyVisible) {
        if (existingIndex + 1 > cursor) {
          cursor = existingIndex + 1;
        }
        continue;
      }
      (gaps ??= <int>[]).add(cursor);
      (newKeys ??= <TKey>[]).add(nodeId);
    }
    if (gaps == null) {
      return false;
    }
    _order.insertAllKeysAtGaps(gaps, newKeys!);
    _updateIndicesFrom(gaps.first);
    return true;
  }
```

Deferring the buffer write until after the whole `onVisit` pass is safe: the
only two callees Path 2 passes are `_captureAndRemoveFromGroups`
(`tree_controller.dart:546-547` to `_animation_coordinator.dart:568-607`) and
`_setOperationGroup` (`:507-508`), and neither reads or writes `_order`. A
future callee that did would break the interleaved cursor just as badly, since
that one exposes a half-spliced buffer instead of an untouched one.

Rewrite `tree_controller.dart:3726-3746` as:

```dart
    if (!animate) {
      final nodesToShow = _flattenSubtree(key, includeRoot: false);
      final nodesToInsert = <TKey>[];
      int alreadyVisibleCount = 0;
      for (final nodeId in nodesToShow) {
        if (_isPendingDeletion(nodeId)) continue;
        if (!_order.contains(nodeId)) {
          nodesToInsert.add(nodeId);
        } else {
          alreadyVisibleCount++;
          _removeAnimation(nodeId);
        }
      }
      if (alreadyVisibleCount == 0) {
        // Every member is new: one memmove, the dominant case.
        if (nodesToInsert.isNotEmpty) {
          final insertIndex = parentIndex + 1;
          _order.insertAllKeys(insertIndex, nodesToInsert);
          _updateIndicesFrom(insertIndex);
        }
      } else {
        // Mixed: members of an in-flight collapse still hold their order
        // slots, so a block insert at parentIndex + 1 would place the new
        // rows AHEAD of their own earlier siblings.
        _spliceIntoVisibleOrderAfter(parentIndex, nodesToShow);
      }
      _structureGeneration++;
      _notifyStructural(affectedKeys: <TKey>{key});
      return;
    }
```

`_removeAnimation` in the classification pass is safe ahead of the splice for
the same reason as above: `removeFromAllSources`
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:613-636`) touches animation sources only.

Replace the Path-2 mixed body (`:3865-3897`) with the same helper:

```dart
    } else {
      _spliceIntoVisibleOrderAfter(
        parentIndex,
        nodesToShow,
        onVisit: (nodeId, _) {
          final capturedExtent = _captureAndRemoveFromGroups(nodeId);
          group.members[nodeId] = NodeGroupExtent(
            startExtent: capturedExtent ?? 0.0,
            targetExtent: _fullExtentOf(nodeId) ?? _unknownExtent,
          );
          _setOperationGroup(nodeId, key);
        },
      );
    }
```

The read order is preserved: the original reads `_order.indexOf(nodeId)`
BEFORE `_captureAndRemoveFromGroups` (`:3872-3873`), and the helper calls
`onVisit` after capturing `existingIndex`.

**Rule for the implementer.** A visible-order block insert is chosen by ONE
test, `alreadyVisibleCount == 0`. All members new: `insertAllKeys` at
`parentIndex + 1`. Otherwise: `_spliceIntoVisibleOrderAfter`, which computes
every gap in a non-mutating pass and performs exactly ONE buffer insert. Never
place k rows with k `insertKey`/`insertNid` calls, and never reach for
`_markVisibleOrderDirty()` to correct a placement bug: the splice owns
placement, the rebuild owns bulk restructuring.

Optionally add, under `debugFullConsistencyChecks`, an assertion that `_order`
equals the expansion-gated structural DFS. Today's inline check only compares
the order against the reverse index over the changed span
(`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:61-70`, the `debugAssertSpanIndexed` arm at
`:68`), which is why this corruption is silent.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Extract the existing Path-2 cursor verbatim (k separate `_order.insertKey`
  calls plus the `+ insertOffset` post-insert index correction). Rejected on
  the real number: `insertNid` (`_visible_order_buffer.dart:432-441`) does one
  `setRange` over the whole suffix PER CALL, so the cursor is O(k * suffix),
  not O(k + suffix). At k = 1, which is the repro and the common mixed case,
  it ties the batched merge; but a single already-visible member routes the
  WHOLE expand to the mixed branch (`:3848` takes the block path only when
  every member is new), so a fresh expand of a large child list with one
  sibling still mid-collapse is quadratic today. Extracting that as the shared
  helper would have promoted a live quadratic to the single owner of the
  protocol.
- `_markVisibleOrderDirty()` in the mixed case. Rejected on cost and blast
  radius. Cost: outside a batch it runs `_rebuildVisibleOrderAndBump`
  immediately (`tree_controller.dart:4554-4560`, `:4539-4542`), which is
  `VisibleOrderBuffer.rebuild` (`_visible_order_buffer.dart:372-379`): three
  O(N) passes (clear plus DFS populate, `rebuildIndex`, `_rebuildSubtreeSizes`)
  with a `<TKey>` stack and a hash lookup per node, against O(suffix + k)
  typed-data moves for the merge. The trigger path is
  `ScrollOrchestrator.ensureAncestorsExpanded`
  (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:169-182`), which calls `expand(animate: false)`
  once per collapsed ancestor (`:179`), so a depth-d chain pays d full
  rebuilds per `animateScrollToKey`. Honest note: this cost argument does NOT
  settle the rebuild against the cursor, since O(k * suffix) is worse than
  O(N) for large k; it settles it against the batched merge, which is
  O(suffix + k) in every case. Blast radius: the rebuild re-derives the entire
  order, reverse index and subtree-size cache from a call site whose bug is
  one local misplacement. It also does not agree with the incremental path by
  construction: the splice skips pending-deletion members (`:3731`), while
  `_rebuildVisibleOrderImpl` adds every popped key unconditionally (`:4603`)
  and pushes every child of an expanded, non-pending parent (`:4620-4623`).
  The two can only differ for a pending-deletion member currently OUT of the
  order; I did not find a reachable state that produces one under a
  non-pending parent (`remove` marks and animates or purges as one unit,
  `tree_controller.dart:3108-3135`), so treat that divergence as unverified
  and do not lean on it.
- Always splice, dropping the `insertAllKeys` fast path. Rejected: the all-new
  case is the dominant one, and the fast path keeps it allocation-free (no
  gap/key scratch lists) on a primitive that is already tested. The animated
  Path 2 already keeps exactly this three-way split (`:3836`, `:3848`,
  `:3865`).

**Architecture fit.** Controller layer plus one addition to `VisibleOrderBuffer`,
which is where the module doc puts bulk order protocols ("owned by
intention-revealing methods"). Keeps the "one owner per bulk order protocol"
rule: the mixed-splice protocol becomes one helper over one primitive instead
of one correct-but-quadratic and one incorrect copy.

**Performance.** Common case unchanged (one `insertAllKeys` memmove plus one
`reindexFrom`). Mixed case: O(suffix + k) moves plus O(k * depth)
`bumpFromSelf` (the same per-key bump `insertAllKeys` already does at
`_visible_order_buffer.dart:473-477`) plus one `reindexFrom`. That replaces an
O(k * suffix) sequence of memmoves in Path 2 and a same-cost but wrongly
ordered block insert in the non-animated branch, so Path 2's mixed branch gets
asymptotically faster and the non-animated branch gets correct at unchanged
cost. Allocations on the mixed path only: two lazily-created scratch lists of
length k, plus one closure per `expand` call (not per node) at Path 2. No
per-frame cost.

**Risk.** Readers of the order produced here: everything downstream of

### M4. Comparator re-insert of an existing key moves it one slot right

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23, three audit passes, all three clean
(passes 1 and 2 are the required consecutive pair; pass 3 was an extra
lens over the M21 handoff and the named Risk tests). Landed as the
Solution prescribes, anchors re-derived against the landed tree:
`_sortedIndex` gains `excludeIndex` with the index-shift fast path and the
`reduced` linear arm verbatim from this block (`tree_controller.dart:
2449-2493`), the shared helper `_relocateOrUpdateExistingSibling` sits
beside the live-space boundary helpers (`:2768`, after `_liveCountOf`),
and both re-insert arms are one-call replacements (insertRoot `:2648`,
insert `:3134`). `_sortedIndex` now has 7 call sites plus the declaration
(measured): six keep the default and only the helper passes
`excludeIndex`, which preserves this block's "only the re-insert paths
exclude" rule with the two prescribed sites collapsed into one. For M21:
the two `_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: <TKey>{node.key})` lines this
block cites at `:2536` and `:3010` are now ONE line, `:2805` inside the
helper (the grep returns exactly one occurrence), and that line is what
M21 replaces.

`test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_m4_test.dart` is the regression test: five
tests, 19 assertions. Pre-fix reds matched the traces exactly: both
idempotent re-inserts read [a, c, b], the pending-deletion case reads
[a, d, b] in live space, and a changed payload sorting EARLIER lands at
index 3 ([a, b, d, c, e]). One finding against this block's sketch: its
Zebra changed-payload case passes on UNFIXED code too (traced: the
polluted upper-bound search happens to land a to-end move correctly), so
it is kept as a contract pin and the to-front payload case above was
added as the changed-payload discriminator. All 19 assertions were
individually shown red: seven by test-side constructions (six runs; the
two byte-identical three-root setup sanities share one), four by the
pre-fix run, and eight under four temporary lib mutations (relocation
forced on equality; the node-data fire dropped; forced relocation with an
off-by-one insert position; relocation suppressed), with the lib restored
and diff-verified byte-identical after each. The block's Risk suites pass
together (128 tests), the full suite reads 1093 passed, 4 skipped (the
1088 post-M9 baseline plus these five), `flutter analyze` stays at the
48-issue baseline, and the source-encoding guard is green.

**Finding.** `_sortedIndex` is an upper-bound binary search
(`tree_controller.dart:2320-2346`; `cmp(midNode, node) <= 0` moves `lo` past
the equal slot at `:2328-2329`), and both re-insert paths call it with the
node still in the list (`:2504-2506` for roots, `:2979-2981` for children).
The result is compared against the node's own current index (`:2517`, `:2992`)
and used as the insert position after a `removeAt` (`:2525-2529`,
`:2999-3003`), which is never adjusted for the removal.

**Root cause.** Two compounding errors at `:2504-2529` and its byte-identical
twin at `:2979-3003`. (1) The node's own slot is counted, so `_sortedIndex`
returns `current + 1` for an idempotent re-insert. (2) The comparison happens
against the node's ALREADY-OVERWRITTEN data: `_store.setData(node.key, node)`
runs first (`:2487` for roots, `:2961` for children), so if the payload
changed the list is no longer sorted at the node's own slot and the binary
search precondition is violated outright.

Traced on `[a:Apple, b:Banana, c:Cherry]` with
`insertRoot(TreeNode(key: "b", data: "Banana"))`: `_sortedIndex` returns 2,
`currentRootIndex` is 1, `wantsRelocate` is true, `removeAt(1)` gives
`[a, c]`, `insert(2)` gives `[a, c, b]`. Repeating returns 1 against a current
index of 2 and flips it back to `[a, b, c]`.

**Solution.** Two parts: fix the math in `_sortedIndex` by excluding the node's
own slot, then collapse the two copies into one helper.

Part 1, `tree_controller.dart:2320-2346`:

```dart
  /// Binary-searches [siblings] for the sorted insertion index of [node]
  /// using [comparator]. Skips pending-deletion keys.
  ///
  /// When [excludeIndex] is non-negative, the entry at that position is
  /// treated as absent and the result is a position in the list AFTER
  /// `removeAt(excludeIndex)`. The re-insert paths need this for two
  /// reasons: the upper-bound search would otherwise count the node's own
  /// equal-comparing slot and report `current + 1`, and the caller has
  /// already overwritten that slot's data with [node], so the list is not
  /// sorted there and must not be probed at all.
  int _sortedIndex(
    List<TKey> siblings,
    TreeNode<TKey, TData> node, {
    int excludeIndex = -1,
  }) {
    assert(comparator != null);
    assert(excludeIndex < siblings.length);
    final cmp = comparator!;
    final int n = excludeIndex >= 0 ? siblings.length - 1 : siblings.length;
    if (_anim.pendingDeletionCount == 0) {
      int lo = 0, hi = n;
      while (lo < hi) {
        final mid = (lo + hi) >> 1;
        // Index-shift the excluded slot out of the search space; no list
        // copy, still O(log n).
        final raw = (excludeIndex >= 0 && mid >= excludeIndex) ? mid + 1 : mid;
        final midNode = _dataOf(siblings[raw])!;
        if (cmp(midNode, node) <= 0) {
          lo = mid + 1;
        } else {
          hi = mid;
        }
      }
      return lo;
    }
    // Pending-deletion keys are intermixed; a single linear scan is
    // allocation-free and competitive for typical sibling counts. `reduced`
    // counts positions in the post-removal list, which is the space the
    // caller inserts into.
    int reduced = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < siblings.length; i++) {
      if (i == excludeIndex) {
        continue;
      }
      final k = siblings[i];
      if (!_isPendingDeletion(k)) {
        final other = _dataOf(k)!;
        if (cmp(other, node) > 0) {
          return reduced;
        }
      }
      reduced++;
    }
    return reduced;
  }
```

Only the two re-insert sites pass `excludeIndex`. The other six call sites
search a list the node is NOT in and keep the default: `:2426` and `:2902`
(the pending-deletion relocation, after the unlink), `:2558` and `:3032` (fresh
node), `:3546` and `:3555` (`moveNode`, after
`_childListOf(oldParent)?.remove(key)` / `_roots.remove(key)` at `:3530-3535`).

Part 2, de-duplication. Add one helper beside the other live-space boundary
helpers (`_liveIndexToFullInsertIndex` at `:2617`, `_liveCountOf` at `:2639`):

```dart
  /// The "key is already present under the requested parent" arm shared by
  /// [insertRoot] and [insert]. [parentKey] is null for the roots case and
  /// selects the RAW sibling list the relocation writes to (`_roots`, or the
  /// parent's child list). Relocates when the caller's requested position
  /// differs from the current one and fires the matching notification:
  /// structural on a move (it subsumes the data channel's row refresh),
  /// node-data only on a pure payload update.
  ///
  /// [index] is live-space; the comparator path works in the post-removal
  /// full-space the insert applies to (see [_sortedIndex]'s `excludeIndex`).
  void _relocateOrUpdateExistingSibling(
    TKey? parentKey,
    TreeNode<TKey, TData> node,
    int? index,
  ) {
    final siblings = parentKey == null
        ? _roots
        : _childListOrCreate(parentKey);
    final currentIndex = siblings.indexOf(node.key);
    final int? sortedDesired = index == null && comparator != null
        ? _sortedIndex(siblings, node, excludeIndex: currentIndex)
        : null;
    final bool wantsRelocate;
    if (index != null) {
      final currentLiveIndex = getIndexInParent(node.key);
      final liveCount = _liveCountOf(siblings);
      wantsRelocate =
          index != currentLiveIndex &&
          // Appending is a no-op if already live-last.
          !(currentLiveIndex == liveCount - 1 && index >= liveCount);
    } else if (sortedDesired != null) {
      // Post-removal space: the node's own position is unchanged by its
      // removal, so equality is the exact no-op test. No append guard is
      // needed, `sortedDesired` maxes out at `siblings.length - 1`.
      wantsRelocate = sortedDesired != currentIndex;
    } else {
      wantsRelocate = false;
    }
    if (wantsRelocate) {
      siblings.removeAt(currentIndex);
      final insertAt = index != null
          ? _liveIndexToFullInsertIndex(siblings, index)
          : sortedDesired!.clamp(0, siblings.length);
      siblings.insert(insertAt, node.key);
      // Raw sibling-list writes above; invalidate cached live indices.
      _liveIndexCache.bump();
      _markVisibleOrderDirty();
      _notifyStructural(affectedKeys: <TKey>{node.key});
    } else {
      _notifyNodeDataChanged(node.key);
    }
  }
```

`insertRoot:2501-2544` becomes
`_relocateOrUpdateExistingSibling(null, node, index); return;` and
`insert:2975-3016` becomes
`_relocateOrUpdateExistingSibling(parentKey, node, index); return;` (the
`final siblings = _childListOrCreate(parentKey)` at `:2975` moves inside the
helper; `_childListOrCreate` is `tree_controller.dart:292`, and `insert`'s
`parentKey` is non-nullable, `:2852`). The helper takes the parent key rather
than the list for the reason in the sequencing note below: the list is
derivable from the key, the key is not derivable from the list, and M21 needs
the key. The `_liveIndexCache.bump()` stays AFTER the write cluster, as the
live-space contract requires, and remains inside a single owner, which keeps
`live_index_oracle_fuzz_test.dart`'s script valid without a new entry.

**Sequencing dependency.** M4 is not independent of M21. The helper body above
swallows the two `_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: <TKey>{node.key})` lines at
`tree_controller.dart:2536` and `:3010`, which are exactly the two lines M21
exists to replace with `_siblingRefreshSet`. Landing M4 AFTER M21 would fold
M21's two calls back into one literal one-element set and silently reinstate
the defect, so re-read the helper's notification line against M21 before
merging in that order. Landing M4 FIRST is the intended order: M21 then becomes
one line inside the helper,
`_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: _siblingRefreshSet(parentKey))`, which for the
roots case resolves through `_siblingRefreshSet`'s own null-parent branch to
`_roots` (`tree_controller.dart:2281-2291`, the local at `:2282-2284`, so the
`if (parentKey != null)` add at `:2286-2288` is skipped and the
`out.addAll(siblings)` at `:2289` supplies the whole set),
matching M21's `_siblingRefreshSet(null)` exactly. This is why the parameter is
`TKey? parentKey` and not `List<TKey> siblings`: with only the list M21 would
be inexpressible inside the helper. Whichever lands second must also re-point
M21's two cited line numbers, since the helper collapses `:2536` and `:3010`
into one site.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Keep `_sortedIndex` as-is and subtract 1 at the call site when
  `sortedDesired > current`. Rejected: it fixes only symptom (1). Symptom (2),
  binary-searching a list the caller has already made unsorted at one slot, is
  still live and produces an arbitrary position whenever the re-insert carries
  a changed payload. The exclusion fixes both with the same code.
- Snapshot the old data, search, then `setData`. Rejected: the search would
  then sort against the STALE payload, so a payload change would land the node
  at its old sorted position, which is the opposite of what the comparator
  contract promises.
- Leave the two blocks duplicated and patch both. Rejected: they are already
  byte-identical modulo the list variable and one dropped comment
  (`:2518` present, `:2993` absent), which is exactly how the drift starts.

**Architecture fit.** Controller layer, live-space write boundary. The helper
sits with `_liveIndexToFullInsertIndex` / `_liveCountOf`, keeping "conversion
to raw sibling lists happens once at the write boundary" true for one
implementation instead of two.

**Performance.** `_sortedIndex` stays O(log n) with no allocation (the
exclusion is an index shift, not a filtered copy); the pending-deletion arm
stays a single O(n) scan. The idempotent re-insert becomes a genuine no-op:
today it costs `removeAt` + `insert` + `_liveIndexCache.bump()` +
`_markVisibleOrderDirty()` (an immediate O(N) order rebuild outside a batch,
`tree_controller.dart:4554-4560`) + a structural notification. After the fix it
costs one comparator search and one node-data notification.

**Risk.** `_sortedIndex` has 8 call sites (`tree_controller.dart:2426, 2505,
2558, 2902, 2980, 3032, 3546, 3555`), all enumerated above; only two change
behavior. Existing tests to re-run: the whole `comparator` group in
`test/sliver_tree/tree_controller_test.dart:396-648` (in particular
`:600-630` "cancel-deletion does not reposition", which takes the
pending-deletion branch at `:2413` and is untouched, and `:441-460`
"insertRoot explicit index overrides comparator"),
`test/sliver_tree/live_index_cache_test.dart:119+` (the adversarial-comparator
pin: it depends on `_sortedIndex` running AFTER the relocate unlink in
`moveNode`, which does not change),
`test/sliver_tree/live_index_oracle_fuzz_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/data_only_reinsert_notification_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/sibling_position_freshness_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/tree_reorder_controller_test.dart`.

### M5. Standalone animations spawned by expand/collapse are timed by `enterExit`

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, four audit passes, 3 and 4 consecutively
clean; pass 2 caught the one stale doc the Solution did not enumerate: the
`animationStyle` setter's dartdoc still said the standalone ticker re-reads
`effectiveEnterExit` (now rewritten for the declared-family read). Landed as
the Solution prescribes, anchors re-derived against the landed tree:
`TreeAnimationFamily` (`animation_style.dart:41`) and `specFor` (`:190`),
`AnimationState.family` required with no default (`types.dart:57`, `:73`),
both install methods take `required TreeAnimationFamily family`
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:368`, `:573`), the per-family `_runTick`
verbatim from this block (`_standalone_animator.dart:226-275`, the two
injected getters replaced by one `styleGetter`), the coordinator's five
curve reads and the synthetic entering state resolve the declared family,
the wiring is `styleGetter: () => _animationStyle`, and the enum is exported
from the barrel. The CHANGELOG gains an Unreleased section noting the
`AnimationState` public-API break, per this block's instruction. Landing
last in chain 8, the table was re-derived per this block's own rule: the
grep returns 16 lines, minus the two declarations, so 14 sites, matching the
post-M1 projection; 13 annotations in `tree_controller.dart` (3 enterExit:
insertRoot, insert, remove; 10 expandCollapse across expand, collapse,
expandAll, collapseAll, each verified against its mutator's kill-switch
gate at `:3824`, `:4080`, `:4227`, `:4472`) plus the case-1 enterExit
literal in the policy method. One new analyzer warning (the coordinator's
now-unused `Curve` import) was removed, keeping the 48-issue baseline.

`test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_m5_test.dart` is the regression test,
family-flow style: the Path-1 standalone exit must settle on the
expandCollapse clock (pre-fix red: G1 lingered at +310 ms on enterExit's
10 s spec), the zero-enterExit mirror (pre-fix red: the old ticker's
zero branch snapped G1 away in a single frame), and the insertRoot control
(passes both sides; shown red by a mutation annotating insertRoot's site
expandCollapse, under which the enter reads progress 0.03 at +310 ms,
exactly 310 ms of the 10 s clock). All 6 assertion sites were individually
shown red: the three setup sanities by test-side constructions, the two
primary pins by the pre-fix run, and the control under the misroute
mutation, with the lib restored diff-verified byte-identical after. The block's Risk suites pass together (97 tests,
including the live-re-read pin in `animation_style_flow_test.dart`), the
full suite reads 1104 passed, 4 skipped (the 1101 post-M2 baseline plus
these three), `flutter analyze` stays at the 48-issue baseline, and the
source-encoding guard is green.

**Finding.** `StandaloneAnimator._runTick` reads one duration and one curve for
the whole active set, both from the enter/exit family
(`_standalone_animator.dart:225`, `:235`, `:258`), and `AnimationState`
carries no spec (`types.dart:52-100`). Of the 15 `_startStandalone*` call
sites (`grep -rn "_startStandaloneEnterAnimation(\|_startStandaloneExitAnimation(" lib/sliver_tree/`
returns 17 lines, minus the two declarations at
`_tree_controller_animation.dart:368` and `:497`), 10 sit inside
`expandCollapse`-gated mutators. The review counts 13; it omitted the two in
the part file.

**Root cause.** The install sites never declare a family, so the family is
re-derived downstream, at the ticker, as "always enterExit". The mismatch is
visible in the source: `expand` (`tree_controller.dart:3670-3672`), `collapse`
(`:3916-3918`), `expandAll` (`:4060-4062`) and `collapseAll` (`:4305-4307`)
all compute their kill-switch flag from
`_animationStyle.expandCollapse.duration`, then install standalone states that
run on `effectiveEnterExit`. That is precisely the family-misrouting bug class
CLAUDE.md's "declare the family ONCE, at the boundary" rule exists to contain.

**Solution.** Declare the family at each install site, store it on the state,
and resolve it through the style at tick time.

1. `animation_style.dart`, add the enum and the one family-to-spec mapping:

```dart
/// The animation families a [TreeAnimationStyle] carries. Declared at the
/// site that installs an animation and never re-derived downstream.
enum TreeAnimationFamily {
  expandCollapse,
  enterExit,
  reorderSlide,
  makeRoom,
  dropSettle,
}
```

and on `TreeAnimationStyle`, beside the existing `effective*` getters
(`animation_style.dart:163-176`):

```dart
  /// Resolves [family] to its effective spec, applying the inheritance
  /// chain. The ONE mapping from a declared family to its timing.
  TreeAnimationSpec specFor(TreeAnimationFamily family) {
    switch (family) {
      case TreeAnimationFamily.expandCollapse:
        return expandCollapse;
      case TreeAnimationFamily.enterExit:
        return effectiveEnterExit;
      case TreeAnimationFamily.reorderSlide:
        return reorderSlide;
      case TreeAnimationFamily.makeRoom:
        return effectiveMakeRoom;
      case TreeAnimationFamily.dropSettle:
        return effectiveDropSettle;
    }
  }
```

Export `TreeAnimationFamily` from `sliver_tree.dart:13` (the
`animation_style.dart` show clause), since it becomes a public field of the
exported `AnimationState`.

2. `types.dart:53-60`, add `required this.family` to the constructor and
`final TreeAnimationFamily family;` to the fields. `required`, not defaulted:
a default is the mechanism that lets a new install site silently inherit the
wrong family again, and the whole point of the rule is that it cannot. There
are exactly three construction sites in `lib` and zero in `test`
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:382`, `:517`,
`_animation_coordinator.dart:755`), so the churn is three lines; note the
public-API break in the CHANGELOG.

3. `_tree_controller_animation.dart:368` and `:497`, add
`required TreeAnimationFamily family` and pass it into the `AnimationState`
at `:382` / `:517`.

4. `StandaloneAnimator`: replace the two injected getters
(`_standalone_animator.dart:48-49`, `:63-64`) with one
`TreeAnimationStyle Function() styleGetter`, wired from
`AnimationCoordinator` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:130-135`) and ultimately
from `tree_controller.dart:419-420` as `() => _animationStyle`. Rewrite
`_runTick` (`:220-271`):

```dart
  void _runTick(Duration elapsed) {
    if (_activeNids.isEmpty) {
      _ticker?.stop();
      return;
    }
    // Both families resolved ONCE per tick, never per node.
    final style = _styleGetter();
    final ee = style.effectiveEnterExit;
    final ec = style.expandCollapse;
    final dt = _lastTickElapsed == null
        ? Duration.zero
        : elapsed - _lastTickElapsed!;
    _lastTickElapsed = elapsed;
    final int dtUs = dt.inMicroseconds;
    final int eeUs = ee.duration.inMicroseconds;
    final int ecUs = ec.duration.inMicroseconds;
    // A zero family means "complete instantly", the same convention every
    // mutator applies on entry. Snapping only that family's states, and
    // routing them through the normal completion handler, keeps the other
    // family running; stop-and-abandon would strand rows at partial extent
    // and leak pending-deletion nodes (this finalize path is the only purge
    // path for standalone exits).
    final double eeDelta = eeUs == 0 ? double.infinity : dtUs / eeUs;
    final double ecDelta = ecUs == 0 ? double.infinity : dtUs / ecUs;
    _completedScratch.clear();
    for (final nid in _activeNids) {
      final state = _byNid[nid]!;
      final bool isEnterExit =
          state.family == TreeAnimationFamily.enterExit;
      final double delta = isEnterExit ? eeDelta : ecDelta;
      if (delta.isInfinite) {
        state.progress = 1.0;
      } else {
        state.progress += delta * state.speedMultiplier;
      }
      state.updateExtent(isEnterExit ? ee.curve : ec.curve);
      if (state.isComplete) {
        _completedScratch.add(_nids.keyOfUnchecked(nid));
      }
    }
    _onTick(_completedScratch);
    // The handler may have started fresh states (revert paths do), so only
    // stop when nothing is left.
    if (_activeNids.isEmpty) {
      _ticker?.stop();
    }
  }
```

5. The remaining reads of the enter/exit curve for a standalone state become
family reads through the same mapping: `_standalone_animator.dart:187`
(`visibleExtent`) and `_animation_coordinator.dart:477`, `:489`, `:494`,
`:740` (`getCurrentExtent`), `:890` (`getCurrentExtentNid`). Each has the
state in hand, so `_styleGetter().specFor(animation.family).curve`.

6. `_animation_coordinator.dart:754-759`
(`_buildSyntheticEnteringState`, returned by `getAnimationState` for op/bulk
members) takes `family: TreeAnimationFamily.expandCollapse`.

`tree_controller.dart:2580` (`insertRoot` fresh enter),
`:3074` (`insert` fresh enter),
`:3117` (`remove` animated exit),

Only the table grows, not the family column. `expandAll` and `collapseAll`

**Alternatives considered.**
- Per-state duration and curve frozen at install (the "resolve the spec at the
  boundary" reading). Rejected: it breaks a documented, tested behavior.
  `tree_controller.dart:120-121` states that "standalone/op-group families
  carry their own live-read semantics" and deliberately exempts them from the
  `purgeActive` transition, and
  `test/sliver_tree/animation_style_flow_test.dart:187-228` pins exactly that
  ("zeroing enterExit at runtime finalizes in-flight standalone animations on
  the next tick (live re-read through the style)"). A frozen spec would leave
  those states running the old duration forever. Recovering the behavior would
  need a new snap-in-flight hook in the `animationStyle` setter, more moving
  parts for a strictly worse fit.
- A per-nid side map from nid to family. Rejected on performance: the tick
  loop is per-frame over the active set, and a map lookup per node per tick is
  exactly what the brief rules out. The enum is a field on the state the loop
  already dereferences.
- A public `family` parameter on the mutators. Rejected: CLAUDE.md's
  containment rule forbids it ("a new consumer whose family differs from the
  API it rides gets an internal-use-only channel, never a public flag
  parameter").

**Architecture fit.** The family is decided at the install call, stored, and
never re-derived; the ticker resolves the DECLARED family through the style
rather than assuming one. `specFor` is the single mapping, next to the
`effective*` getters that already own the inheritance chain. The mutator
kill-switch gates (`:3670`, `:3916`, `:4060`, `:4305` on `expandCollapse`;
`:2404`, `:2858`, `:3088`, `_tree_controller_animation.dart:405` on
`effectiveEnterExit`) then agree with the timing the states actually get,
which they do not today.

**Performance.** Per tick, before: two closure calls plus two getters. After:
one closure call, two getter reads (`effectiveEnterExit` is a `??`), two
integer divisions. Per node, before: one add, one `updateExtent`. After: one
enum compare, two reference selects, one add, one `updateExtent`. No map
lookup, no `Curve` allocation, no per-node division. `AnimationState` grows by
one reference field; enum values are canonical const instances, so the states
share them. The read path `getCurrentExtentNid`
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:863-899`, the curve read at `:890`, per row per
layout) trades one closure call for one closure call plus a five-way switch,
no allocation.

```dart

final controller = TreeController<String, String>(
  vsync: tester,
```

(`enterExit: Duration.zero` while `expandCollapse` animates: G1 must NOT
