### M6. The bulk-only fast path falls off on every frame

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, chain 1 (one commit with M7, M8, H2). The counter landed first; `bulk_fast_path_stability_test.dart` failed on unfixed code exactly as derived (case 1: expected 1, actual 10, one rebuild per frame from frame 3 on; case 2 pre-flip sanity: actual 5). Fix landed as specified (product-form extent write plus the `bulkData` parameter); M8's Step 3a then carried the arithmetic verbatim into the admit callback in the same sitting, deleting `_admitBulkFastPath` as both blocks record. All six assertion sites were shown to fail individually: two via the pre-fix reds, four via temporary mutations (`bulkOnly` forced false, counter seeded to 1, signal disabled, out-of-band finder). Risk suites and the full suite green; analyze at the 48-issue baseline.

**Finding.** `_admitBulkFastPath` writes the per-row estimate as a difference
of two cumulative offsets, `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(i +
1) - offset` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:455-457`), while Pass 2 measures the
same row as a single product, `getAnimatedExtent` returning `fullExtent *
(bulk.group?.value ?? 0.0)` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2402-2405`,
`_animation_coordinator.dart:718-724`), and the two are compared with exact
`!=` at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2818-2823`. Measured (probe_m6.dart): over a
200-frame linear sweep on a 4000-row tree, 3071 of 3600 sampled rows mismatch
under exact `!=`; worst absolute difference 1.56e-13 px. At 400k rows
(probe_m6b.dart) 3583 of 3600 mismatch, worst difference 4.52e-9 px.

**Root cause.** `(S[i+1] + v*B[i+1]) - (S[i] + v*B[i])` is a subtraction of two
large prefix sums built in `_rebuildBulkCumulatives`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:333-334`); it is mathematically but not bitwise equal
to `full * v`. Every mismatch runs `_materializeBulkStaleExtents`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2323-2336`, which sets `_bulkCumulativesValid =
false` at `:2335`), then `_recomputeOffsetsFrom` at `:2853`, and the next
frame rebuilds the cumulatives again, so the documented "O(N)-per-frame Pass 1
walk into O(1)" (`render_sliver_tree.dart:249-250`) never holds for more than
one frame.

**Solution.** Identical arithmetic, no epsilon. In `_admitBulkFastPath`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:446-465`) stop deriving the extent from the
cumulative difference and compute it exactly the way the measurement does:

```dart
int _admitBulkFastPath({
  required int cacheStartIndex,
  required List<TKey> visibleNodes,
  required BulkAnimationData<TKey> bulkData,
  required double fullCacheEnd,
}) {
  int cacheEndIndex = cacheStartIndex;
  final orderNids = controller.orderNidsView;
  final value = _bulkValueCached;
  for (int i = cacheStartIndex; i < visibleNodes.length; i++) {
    final nid = orderNids[i];
    _nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(i);
    // Bitwise-identical to the Pass 2 measurement
    // (`AnimationCoordinator.getAnimatedExtent`, which returns
    // `fullExtent * bulk.group.value` for a member and `fullExtent`
    // otherwise). A cumulative DIFFERENCE is only algebraically equal,
    // and the exact `!=` at the measurement site turns the last bit of
    // that difference into an every-frame fall-off.
    final full = controller.getEstimatedExtentNid(nid);
    _nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = bulkData.containsMemberNid(nid)
        ? full * value
        : full;
    ...
  }
}
```

`bulkData` is already fetched once per frame at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:2605` and `containsMemberNid` is a `Uint8List` read
(`types.dart:479-484`); `getEstimatedExtentNid` is a `Float64List` read
(`tree_controller.dart:981-985`). `_bulkValueCached` is set from
`bulkData.value` at `:2623`, which is the same `g.value` that
`getAnimatedExtent` reads through `bulk.group` (`_bulk_animator.dart:125-137`),
so the two multiplicands are bit-identical.

Add a debug counter beside the existing ones
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:500-543`):

```dart
/// Lifetime count of `_rebuildBulkCumulatives` calls. Perf oracle for the
/// bulk-only fast path: a bulk animation whose rows do not change height
/// must build the cumulatives ONCE, not once per frame.
@visibleForTesting
int debugBulkCumulativeRebuildCount = 0;
```

Proof the estimate cannot mask a real height change. The comparison at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:2819` stays exact `!=`, and after the change it reads
`full_measured * v != full_cumulative * v` for a member (`full_measured =
child.size.height`, written by `setFullExtent` at `:2400` immediately before
`getAnimatedExtent` at `:2402`) and `full_measured != full_cumulative` for a
non-member. For a non-member the test is literally an equality on the measured
height: zero masking. For a member and any `v != 0`, IEEE-754 multiplication by
a fixed nonzero finite double maps two doubles to the same result only when
they are within one ulp of each other, so the masking window is at most 1 ulp
of the row height, about 7.1e-15 px at a 48 px row. That is fifteen orders of
magnitude below any height change a layout can produce, and six orders below
the CURRENT code's false-positive window (measured 4.52e-9 px at 400k rows).
At exactly `v == 0.0` every product is `+0.0` and a height change is masked;
this is not introduced by the fix, because today's estimate at `v == 0` is
`(S[i+1] + 0*B[i+1]) - (S[i] + 0*B[i])`, and `_rebuildBulkCumulatives` does not
advance `sStable` for a member (`render_sliver_tree.dart:325-334`), so `S[i+1]`
and `S[i]` are the same double and today's estimate is exactly `0.0` as well.
Behaviour at `v == 0` is bit-for-bit unchanged.

The extent-changed signal also drives `_sticky.dirty = true`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2837`) and the offsets recompute at `:2853`. Both
keep firing on every genuine height change; they simply stop firing on
nothing.

**Alternatives considered.**

- *Compare with `precisionErrorTolerance`* (`foundation/constants.dart:71`,
  `1e-10`). Measured to NOT fix the bug: at 400k rows 2928 of 3600 samples
  still exceed 1e-10 (probe_m6b.dart), because the error scales with the
  prefix-sum magnitude (ulp of a 2.16e7 offset is 3.7e-9). A tolerance that
  works there has to be scale-relative, which means computing the scale per
  row and accepting a masking window that grows with tree size. Identical
  arithmetic has a fixed 1-ulp window.
- *Recompute the estimate from `getCurrentExtentNid`.* That is the correct
  value but it re-enters the three-source precedence chain
  (`_animation_coordinator.dart:863-899`: bulk, then op group, then
  standalone) per row, including a `TKey` hash when any op group exists
  (`:874-876`). The fast path exists to avoid exactly that; the
  bulk-membership branch is one `Uint8List` byte.

**Architecture fit.** Stays inside the render layer's bulk fast path, which
already owns the "syncs them into the per-nid slots so downstream code reads
correct values without a branch per access" duty
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:435-438`). It reuses the same membership mirror the
cumulative rebuild uses (`render_sliver_tree.dart:325`,
`bulkData.containsMemberNid`) and the same nid-keyed extent read
(`:324`). No new layer, no new concept.

**Performance.** Before: every bulk frame runs `_materializeBulkStaleExtents`
(O(N)), `_recomputeOffsetsFrom` (O(N)) and next frame `_rebuildBulkCumulatives`
(O(N)), i.e. 3 O(N) typed-array passes per frame; the review reports 30 bulk
frames costing 62 ms at 5k rows and 349 ms at 400k rows (their measurement, not
re-run here). After: those passes run only when a row's measured height
actually changes; the steady-state bulk frame is Pass 1 O(1)
(`_offsetAtVisibleIndex(n)` at `:2624`) plus the cache-region admission loop.
Per-row cost inside `_admitBulkFastPath` goes from 2 cumulative reads + 2
multiplies + 1 subtract to 1 cumulative read pair + 1 array read + 1 multiply,
i.e. slightly cheaper. Zero new allocations.

**Risk.** `_nodeExtentsByNid` under the fast path is read by
`_findFirstVisibleIndex`'s non-bulk branch (`render_sliver_tree.dart:3310-3313`,
not reached while `_bulkCumulativesValid`), by `LayoutAdmissionPolicy.admit`'s
budget accumulator (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:119`, ulp-insensitive), by
the sticky force-create compare (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2961-2969`) and by
the paint-extent loop (`:3039-3040`, which M7 removes). None depends on the
extents summing bit-exactly to the offsets, and the current code already has
the inverse inconsistency. Existing tests to re-run:
`test/sliver_tree/bulk_sticky_recompute_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/sticky_bulk_stale_offset_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/find_row_after_bulk_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/bulk_reentry_continuation_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/concurrent_extents_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/bulk_fast_path_stability_test.dart`:
1000 uniform 48 px children under one root, `expandAll()` with a 300 ms linear
`expandCollapse` spec. Setup sanity: after the first animation frame assert
`debugBulkCumulativeRebuildCount == 1` (the fast path was entered). Then pump
10 frames of 20 ms and assert `debugBulkCumulativeRebuildCount == 1` still.
Fails today (it climbs one per frame, since every frame falls off and the next
re-enters), passes after.

Second case, the teeth: make the child at VISIBLE INDEX 5 (`c4`) change height
mid-animation (a `StatefulWidget` row that flips 48 to 96 on the 5th frame),
pump one more frame, and assert `debugBulkCumulativeRebuildCount == 2`, proving
the fix did not simply disable the signal. The row has to sit inside the
admitted band or the case tests nothing. In the standard 800x600 harness
`fullCacheEnd` is `fullStart + remainingCacheExtent + slideOverreach * 2`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2744-2752`), which at scroll offset 0 with a 600 px
viewport, the 250 px default cache extent and no slides
(`slideOverreach = controller.composedSlideAbsDeltaBound`, `:2592`, zero with
no drag and no FLIP) is 850, so the break at `:458-459` trips at visible index
18 (`48 * 18 = 864 >= 850`) and the frame admits the root plus `c0..c16`, 18
rows. A row at index 500 is never admitted, so the create loop skips it
(`:2794-2802`, gated on `_inCacheRegionByNid`), its `StatefulWidget` never
builds, `_layoutNodeChild` returns null at `:2383-2385`, and the counter never
advances: the case would fail AFTER the fix instead of proving anything.

Status of the two cases, stated plainly. Case 1 is the pre-fix repro: it fails
today because the counter climbs one per frame. Case 2 does NOT fail today; it
passes for the wrong reason, because today every frame falls off and rebuilds.
It is a post-fix guard, and its job is to still pass once case 1 does.

**Sequencing dependency.** Chain 1 in the plan's Sequencing section is M6, then
M7, then M8, then H2. M6 goes FIRST because every later block in the chain
consumes what it lands. M7 and M8 in two ways. (1) The counter:
`debugBulkCumulativeRebuildCount` is declared here, and it is the oracle M7's
second and third cases and M8's setup-sanity assertion all read. Until M6
lands it climbs once per frame on its own, which is this block's Finding, so
it can distinguish nothing for them.
(2) The fix: while every bulk frame falls off the fast path, every frame runs
`_materializeBulkStaleExtents` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2845-2851`) plus
`_recomputeOffsetsFrom` (`:2853`), and the materialize rewrites
`_nodeExtentsByNid` from `controller.getCurrentExtentNid` for every index at or
past `fromIndex` outside the cache region (`:2331-2333`). That refreshes
wholesale, every frame, exactly the off-cache slots whose staleness M7's parts
2 and 3 are about and whose per-nid-versus-range freshness M8's Step 4 rests
on. Both blocks would otherwise be tested against a tree that hides their
subject.

H2 (Chain 1's last block) DOES depend on this block directly, and an earlier
draft of this paragraph denied it by asserting that "M6 exports nothing to H2
directly". That was false; source settles it, and H2's own Sequencing paragraph
already records both halves. What follows states the same conclusion from this
side, and adds two items neither side had.

*Shared item 1, the same five lines.* This block rewrites the per-row extent
write at `render_sliver_tree.dart:457`
(`_nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(i + 1) - offset`); H2's part
(c) replaces the break one line later at `:458-459` with a paint-region floor
whose own predicate reads `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]`, the slot `:457` produces.
Both edits land inside the one loop body at `:453-463`.

*Shared item 2, the same new parameter.* The live signature takes three
parameters, `cacheStartIndex`, `visibleNodes`, `fullCacheEnd`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:446-450`, the parameters at `:447-449`), and the sole
call site passes exactly those three (`:2768-2772`; `grep -n
"_admitBulkFastPath" lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart` returns the
declaration at `:446` and that one call). Both blocks add the SAME required
`BulkAnimationData<TKey> bulkData` parameter to that signature and the same
`bulkData: bulkData` argument at that call site: this block for
`containsMemberNid` plus the value multiply, H2's part (c) for the
`!bulkData.containsMemberNid(nid)` term that keeps sub-pixel members out of the
floor. The local is already in scope at the call site (`:2605`).

ORDER: M6 FIRST, then H2. That is Chain 1's order and it is what H2's block
states. In the wrong order H2 lands the parameter and the floor first, and
then three things go wrong: this block's quoted `_admitBulkFastPath` no longer
matches the method on disk, so its replacement body has to be re-derived
against H2's version; an implementer following both texts literally threads
`bulkData` in TWICE, at the signature and at the call site, which does not
compile; and H2's floor is calibrated against an extent whose producer this
block then replaces.

What the second lander finds, since in the correct order the second lander is
H2. `bulkData` is ALREADY a parameter of `_admitBulkFastPath` and already an
argument at `:2768-2772`, so H2's part (c) adds neither; it consumes the one
this block threaded. H2's quoted signature, "today `cacheStartIndex`,
`visibleNodes`, `fullCacheEnd`, at `:447-449`", is a pre-M6 reading and goes
stale at that moment, by one added parameter and nothing else; H2's part (c) as
written is otherwise unaffected. This block's own quoted signature never goes
stale, because nothing in Chain 1 lands before it. And this composes with M8's
Step 4 as H2 already describes: if M8 unifies the bulk loop behind
`LayoutAdmissionPolicy`, the `bulkData` this block threaded is what M8's
`BulkAdmissionView` carries forward and H2's part (c) then applies to the
unified policy instead. H2's dependency on M8's Step 4 rule stands unchanged,
as that block records; it is simply not H2's only Chain 1 dependency.

Two further shared items inside the method, read this session and recorded on
neither side.

- *The membership read is duplicated.* After both land,
  `bulkData.containsMemberNid(nid)` (`types.dart:479-484`) is called TWICE per
  row in one iteration: once for this block's member branch on the extent
  write, once for H2's floor term. Hoist it to a single
  `final bool isMember = bulkData.containsMemberNid(nid);` above the extent
  write and let both read it. It is a `Uint8List` read either way, so this is
  tidiness, not a measured cost.
- *The `offset` local at `:455` is load-bearing for H2.* H2's floor predicate is
  written as `offset < paintRegionEnd && offset + _nodeExtentsByNid[nid] >
  paintRegionStart`, on H2's stated premise that both values are "already
  computed at `:455-457`", which is true of the code on disk (`:455` binds
  `final offset = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(i);`, `:456` and `:457` are its only
  readers). This block's replacement body no longer needs `offset` for the
  extent. DECISION: KEEP the local anyway, `final offset =
  _offsetAtVisibleIndex(i);` at `:455` with `_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] = offset;`
  at `:456`, which is free because `:456` still reads it, so that H2's
  predicate pastes unchanged. Dropping it would make H2's snippet reference an
  undeclared name.

One doc consequence, flagged here because it belongs to H2's commit, not this
one. H2's Doc change item 6 rewrites `_admitBulkFastPath`'s dartdoc
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:433-445`) and its replacement keeps the sentence
"Pulls per-row offset/extent from the precomputed cumulatives". After this
block that sentence is half false: the OFFSET still comes from the cumulatives
through `_offsetAtVisibleIndex` (`:455`), but the EXTENT becomes
`controller.getEstimatedExtentNid(nid)` (`tree_controller.dart:981-985`) times
the cached group value, precisely so it is bitwise equal to the Pass 2
measurement. H2's replacement should split the clause accordingly. This block
edits no dartdoc, so there is no competing edit to that range.

**Effort.** S.

### M7. Paint-extent loop reads unwritten per-nid slots on bulk frames

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, chain 1 commit. `bulk_paint_extent_test.dart` pre-fix reds: case 1 paintExtent 480.0 against 600.0 (the review's number), case 2 rebuild counter 3 against 1, case 3 mismatch counter 1 against 0 after landing `debugStickyOffsetAuthorityMismatchCount` against the old write, per the promoted flow. Two test-side corrections against the block, both measured: the pinned header at the jump frame is C9, not C10 (the block's arithmetic evaluates the probe at v = 0.5, but the pump after the jump advances v), so case 3 asserts on the actually-pinned pre-measured header; and its pre-jump sanity was rewritten to a pre-jump snapshot, because force-creation itself builds the row, so a post-jump `buildCounts` lookup could never fail in the direction its reason claimed. Every assertion shown red individually; parts 1 to 3 landed as printed (part 2's loop later gained M8/L25.6's nid-threaded `_layoutNodeChild` record form). Risk suites and the full suite green.

**Finding.** The paint-extent loop at `render_sliver_tree.dart:3035-3055` reads
`_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid]` and `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` directly for every
visible index from `startIndex` upward. Under the bulk-only fast path those
slots are documented as fresh only for cache-region nids
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:229-232`, "only slots for cache-region nids are kept
fresh"), and `_admitBulkFastPath` writes them only up to its break
(`:453-463`). Rows whose nid was never laid out read `0.0 / 0.0` from the
zero-initialised `Float64List`s (declared at `:233` and `:237`), so the break
at `:3043` (`offset >= scrollOffset + remainingPaintExtent`) never fires and
the loop runs to `visibleNodes.length`, contributing nothing.

**Root cause.** The loop bypasses `_structuralOffsetAt`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:352-356`), which is the accessor that exists
precisely because "under the bulk-only fast path the per-nid offset slots are
stale for off-cache nids" (`:346-351`). `paintExtent` therefore under-reports,
and `hitTestExtent` follows it (`SliverGeometry` defaults `hitTestExtent` to
`paintExtent`), so taps below the under-reported extent are rejected and a
following sliver paints inside the tree.

**Solution, part 1: the paint-extent loop.** Delete the loop and the
`_findFirstVisibleIndex` call that feeds it (`render_sliver_tree.dart:3033-3055`,
which also removes the `startIndex` local at `:3035`, used only at `:3037`, and
the `orderNids` local at `:3036`, used only at `:3038` -- verified with
`grep -n "startIndex" lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart`, whose only
other hits are the separate locals at `:3356`, `:4164`). Replace with the
contiguous-range form:

```dart
// Rows are contiguous by construction: every Pass 1 branch writes
// `offset(i+1) = offset(i) + extent(i)` (`:2636-2642`, `:2668-2674`,
// `:2687-2703`), and the bulk fast path's cumulatives are prefix sums by
// definition (`_rebuildBulkCumulatives`, `:333-334`). The visible portion
// of a contiguous [0, totalScrollExtent) band is therefore exactly the
// sliver-protocol intersection, with no per-row walk and no dependence
// on per-nid slot freshness.
double paintExtent = calculatePaintOffset(
  constraints,
  from: 0.0,
  to: totalScrollExtent,
);
```

`calculatePaintOffset` is `RenderSliver`'s own helper
(`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/sliver.dart:1573-1587`):
`clampDouble(clampDouble(to, a, b) - clampDouble(from, a, b), 0,
remainingPaintExtent)` with `a = constraints.scrollOffset`,
`b = a + constraints.remainingPaintExtent`. The layout's `scrollOffset` and
`remainingPaintExtent` locals ARE those two constraint fields
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2521-2522`), so for `from = 0 <= a` it reduces to
`clamp(min(total, b) - a, 0, remainingPaintExtent)`, which is bit-for-bit the
sum the loop intends. It returns 0 for an empty tree and 0 when scrolled past
the content, matching the loop's behaviour in both cases. Its
`assert(from <= to)` (`sliver.dart:1578`) holds because `totalScrollExtent` is
a sum of non-negative extents.

The sticky-inflation clamp that follows (`:3061-3072`) is unaffected in
structure and strictly better fed: it only ever RAISES `paintExtent`
(`if (stickyBottom > paintExtent) paintExtent = stickyBottom;` at `:3071`) and
sets `stickyInflationClamped` from `remainingPaintExtent`, not from
`paintExtent`; the final `clamp(0, min(remainingPaintExtent,
totalScrollExtent))` at `:3079-3082` still caps it. With a correct (larger)
base, a header that used to inflate past an under-reported base now does not,
which is the intended behaviour.

**Solution, part 2: the adjacent sticky force-create site.** Same bug class,
same change, and it is not optional -- see the freshness argument below. The
compare at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2961-2969` reads `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]`
as `priorExtent` (`:2963`) for nodes the comment at `:2998-2999` says were
"outside the cache region during Pass 1 and never had it set". That slot
holds whatever the last branch to write it left there, and on a bulk frame
that is not the current value for an ANIMATING nid: the fast path writes
extent slots only from `cacheStartIndex` to its break (`:453-463`), so an
off-cache bulk member keeps `full * v_previous` (or the zero-initialised
`0.0` when no Pass 1 branch ever wrote it) while `_layoutNodeChild` measures
`full * v_now`. Then `stickyExtentsChanged` fires spuriously and drags in
`_materializeBulkStaleExtents(fromIndex: 0, ...)` plus a full
`_recomputeOffsets` (`:2970-2984`). For a NON-member sticky ancestor the slot
and the accessor already agree, which is why the second test case below has
to pin a member; the change is still the right one, because this site must
not depend on which of the two a candidate happens to be.

DECISION: use `controller.getCurrentExtentNid(nid)`. Do NOT use
`_structuralOffsetAt(i + 1, ...) - _structuralOffsetAt(i, ...)`.

```dart
for (final nodeId in newStickyNodes) {
  final nid = _controller.nidOf(nodeId);
  // Prior estimate read through the SAME chain the measurement resolves:
  // `_layoutNodeChild` returns `getAnimatedExtent(nodeId,
  // child.size.height)` (`:2400-2405`). `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` is not
  // that value for an off-cache ANIMATING nid on a bulk frame -- these
  // nids were selected precisely because `_inCacheRegionByNid[nid] == 0`
  // (`:2931`), and `_admitBulkFastPath` writes extent slots only from
  // `cacheStartIndex` to its break (`:453-463`), so a pinned bulk member
  // holds a previous frame's product (or a never-written 0.0) and the
  // exact `!=` at `:2967` fires on nothing.
  final priorExtent = controller.getCurrentExtentNid(nid);
  final extent = _layoutNodeChild(nodeId, crossAxisExtent);
  if (extent != null) {
    _nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = extent;
    if (extent != priorExtent) stickyExtentsChanged = true;
  }
}
```

The body above is the PRE-H1 shape of these nine lines. H1's Solution step 3
adds an `aboveAnchorDelta` accumulation inside the `extent != priorExtent`
branch (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2967`) and prints the COMBINED body; H1 lands
after this block (Chain 16 below), so H1's version supersedes the one above
and nothing decided here has to be revisited.

Why the difference-of-prefix-sums form loses, two independent reasons:

1. *It re-creates the M6 bug.* The compare at `:2967` is an exact `!=` against
   `_layoutNodeChild`'s return, which is `getAnimatedExtent`'s single product
   at `:2402-2405`. A difference of two prefix sums is only algebraically equal
   to that product, so the comparison would fire on the last bit exactly as
   M6 documents for `:2818-2823`. Fixing one site while re-introducing the
   same arithmetic at the other is not a fix.
2. *It is not computable in that loop.* The loop iterates `newStickyNodes`
   (a `Set<TKey>` built at `:2928-2934`), not visible indices, so there is no
   `i` in scope; recovering one costs a `visibleIndexOfNid` per node purely
   to feed an expression that reason 1 already rejects.

`getCurrentExtentNid` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:863-899`) and
`getAnimatedExtent` (`:718-749`) run the same three-source precedence over the
same operands. The only input that changes across the `_layoutNodeChild` call
is `_fullExtentByNid[nid]`, which `setFullExtent` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2400`)
overwrites with `child.size.height`. So `priorExtent != extent` iff the
measured height differs from the stored full extent, which is exactly the
signal the block wants. The two accessors' bulk guards are not textually
identical (`bulk.isMember(key)` at `_animation_coordinator.dart:723` versus
`bulk.isMemberNid(nid) && bulk.group != null` at `:867`); they can differ only
for a member with a null group, which `BulkAnimator.snapshot` already reports
as inactive (`_bulk_animator.dart:125-129`). If they ever did diverge the
divergence is a false POSITIVE on the compare (one extra recompute), never a
missed height change, which is the safe direction.

Note the fix does NOT suppress the genuine signal the comment at `:3008-3013`
describes: a never-measured sticky candidate reads `defaultExtent` from
`getCurrentExtentNid` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:864-865`), so a real height
that differs from 48 px still trips `stickyExtentsChanged`.

**Solution, part 3: what keeps the layoutOffset write correct afterwards.**
Suppressing the spurious `stickyExtentsChanged` also removes the
`_recomputeOffsets()` at `:2984`, and that call is today the only thing making
`_nodeOffsetsByNid` fresh for the layoutOffset write at `:3004-3005`, whose
nids are by construction outside the cache region (`:2931`) and therefore
stale under the bulk fast path. Two things restore it, and the change uses
both; a third item, the counter, is what pins that it stays restored:

1. *Change the write to read the structural authority instead of the raw
   slot.* This is the load-bearing half.

   ```dart
   for (final nodeId in newStickyNodes) {
     final child = getChildForNode(nodeId);
     if (child == null) continue;
     final nid = _controller.nidOf(nodeId);
     final visIdx = _controller.visibleIndexOfNid(nid);
     if (visIdx < 0) continue; // mirrors the guard at `:3185-3189`
     final parentData = child.parentData! as SliverTreeParentData;
     parentData.layoutOffset = _structuralOffsetAt(visIdx, nid);
   }
   ```

   `_structuralOffsetAt` (`:352-356`) serves `_offsetAtVisibleIndex` while
   `_bulkCumulativesValid` and the per-nid slot otherwise, which is exactly
   the authority `_stickyFreshOffsetAt` (`:422-431`) hands the re-probe at
   `:3026`; write and probe therefore cannot disagree. `visibleIndexOfNid` is
   an O(1) `Int32List` read with no key hash (`tree_controller.dart:969-972`),
   and the loop is bounded by the sticky candidate count.

2. *Backstop.* The unconditional parentData refresh at `:3150-3250` visits
   every mounted child, skips only those with `_inCacheRegionByNid[nid] != 0`
   (`:3179-3183`) -- which excludes exactly the `newStickyNodes`, selected on
   that same flag being 0 at `:2931` -- resolves the offset per-nid through
   the bulk cumulatives (`:3199-3202`) or a fresh cumulative (`:3203-3211`),
   and writes `parentData.layoutOffset` at `:3238`. So the frame's FINAL
   parentData is correct either way. What (1) buys is that no reader between
   `:3005` and `:3238` observes the stale value. Checked: nothing in
   `_sticky_header_computer.dart` reads parentData (`grep -n "parentData"
   lib/sliver_tree/_sticky_header_computer.dart` returns no lines);
   `computeStickyHeaders` takes `nodeOffsetsByNid` and `freshOffsetAt` as
   parameters (`:3014-3027`). (1) is still the fix rather than a nicety,
   because writing a slot the frame has not written is the defect class this
   block exists to remove, and the backstop's coverage is an ordering
   accident, not a contract.

3. *The counter that pins (1).* There is no end-of-frame observable for (1):
   the backstop rewrites the SAME `parentData.layoutOffset` later in the same
   layout (`:3238`), so a test that reads the pinned row's parentData after a
   `pump` sees the correct value with or without (1). What (1) establishes is
   an in-frame ordering property, so it gets a debug counter on the render
   object, which is the house convention for exactly this
   ("Perf contracts are pinned via debug counters on the render object",
   CLAUDE.md). DECISION, named in full:

   ```dart
   /// Force-created sticky rows whose written `parentData.layoutOffset`
   /// disagreed with the frame's structural authority
   /// ([_structuralOffsetAt]) at the moment of the write. MUST be 0 on
   /// every layout: the sticky block writes that authority, and this
   /// write is the one place in `performLayout` that used to read a raw
   /// `_nodeOffsetsByNid` slot for a nid the frame never wrote. Reset at
   /// the top of `performLayout`.
   @visibleForTesting
   int debugStickyOffsetAuthorityMismatchCount = 0;
   ```

   Declared beside the existing counters (`render_sliver_tree.dart:500-543`),
   reset unconditionally beside `debugLastParentDataRefreshIterationCount` at
   `:2422`, and incremented ONLY inside an
   `assert(() { ... return true; }())`, the same guard shape `paint` already
   uses for `debugLastPaintedStickyKeys` (`:3328-3332`, `:3746-3749`), so a
   release build pays nothing and a debug build pays one compare per sticky
   candidate:

   ```dart
   final structural = _structuralOffsetAt(visIdx, nid);
   parentData.layoutOffset = structural;
   assert(() {
     if (parentData.layoutOffset != structural) {
       debugStickyOffsetAuthorityMismatchCount++;
     }
     return true;
   }());
   ```

   Be honest about what this is. Post-fix the counter is 0 by construction,
   because the write and the probe evaluate the same expression. Its teeth are
   the pre-fix run, and the promoted-repro flow makes that explicit: land the
   counter FIRST with the write still reading `_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid]`, run the
   third test case and watch it report 1, then land (1) and watch it report 0.
   What it buys permanently is that the moment anyone routes that write back
   through a raw per-nid slot, the counter trips instead of the defect hiding
   behind the backstop as it does today.

Rule for the implementer: inside `performLayout`, never read
`_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid]` for a nid the frame has not written. Go through
`_structuralOffsetAt(visibleIndex, nid)`, or through
`_offsetAtVisibleIndex`/`_stickyFreshOffsetAt` when the index is already in
hand.

**Sequencing dependency (Chain 16, M7 then H1).** H1's Solution step 3 adds an
`aboveAnchorDelta` accumulation inside the `extent != priorExtent` branch at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:2967`, i.e. inside the same nine-line loop
(`:2961-2969`) this block's Solution part 2 replaces wholesale. Required
order: M7 first, then H1, and the COMBINED body for those nine lines is
printed once, in H1's step 3, which supersedes the body printed in part 2
above. The two changes are compatible in substance (this block changes how
`priorExtent` at `:2963` is computed, H1 adds an accumulation that consumes
it), but the merge is not automatic in either direction: pasting part 2's body
over an H1-modified loop deletes the accumulation while leaving
`aboveAnchorDelta` declared and still emitted at H1's `:3029` site, so nothing
fails to compile and the scroll correction simply under-reports by every
force-created sticky row's measurement residual. The order is also what makes
H1's residual mean "measured minus what this frame's offsets assumed":
`controller.getCurrentExtentNid(nid)` IS that assumption by construction
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:867-868` against `:723-724`), while the raw
`_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` this block replaces agrees with it only for the
non-animating non-member candidates analysed above, and only because some
earlier Pass 1 branch happened to write it.

**Alternatives considered.**

- *Swap the two array reads for `_structuralOffsetAt(i, nid)` and the next
  offset.* Correct, minimal, and it keeps the O(rows in viewport) walk. It also
  keeps a redundant `_findFirstVisibleIndex` binary search and a per-row branch
  on `_bulkCumulativesValid` (`:353`) that the closed form does not need.
  Rejected because the closed form is both correct and strictly cheaper.
- *Keep the loop but seed `startIndex` from the fresh cumulative.* Does not
  help: the staleness is in the per-row reads, not the start index
  (`_findFirstVisibleIndex` already uses the cumulatives under the fast path,
  `:3272-3283`).

**Architecture fit.** Uses the sliver protocol's own helper for the job it
exists for, and removes the paint-extent loop's direct reads at `:3039-3040`.
Together with part 3 that leaves no unguarded direct `_nodeOffsetsByNid` read
inside `performLayout` on a bulk frame: `grep -n "_nodeOffsetsByNid\["
lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart` returns 21 lines, and the remaining
in-layout ones are writes (`:456`, `:2347`, `:2367`, `:2638`, `:2671`,
`:2698`), reads inside the fresh `[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)` band
(`:2828`, `:2865`), or reads guarded by `_bulkCumulativesValid` /
`offsetsAuthoritative` / `stickyMeasurementMovedOffsets` (`:355`, `:2136`,
`:3198`, `:3217`, `:3310`). The out-of-layout reads in `_findRowBoundedScan`
(`:2066`, `:2096`, `:2117`) are a separate question this block does not assess
and does not touch.

**Performance.** Before: one binary search O(log N) plus a walk that is
O(rows in viewport) on healthy frames and O(N) on bulk frames whose off-cache
slots read 0 (the review measured `paintExtent == 480` against 600 expected at
2000 children). After: O(1), three `clampDouble` calls, no allocation, no array
reads. On a 200k-row `expandAll` this removes 400k `Float64List` reads (two per
row, `:3039-3040`) plus 200k `Int32List` reads (`orderNids[i]` at `:3038`) per
layout. Part 2 removes, per bulk frame with a pinned header, one
`_materializeBulkStaleExtents(fromIndex: 0)` plus one full `_recomputeOffsets`,
both O(N_visible). Part 3 adds one `Int32List` read per sticky candidate.

**Risk.** `paintExtent` feeds `geometry.paintExtent` and `hasVisualOverflow`
(`:3084-3113`). The `scrollOffset + paintExtent < totalScrollExtent` disjunct
at `:3111` becomes false in cases where the under-reported extent used to make
it true; the `scrollOffset > 0.0` disjunct at `:3112` still forces the viewport
clip whenever the first visible row starts before `scrollOffset`, which is the
case the comment at `:3103-3108` is defending. Existing tests to re-run:
`test/sliver_tree/sticky_small_tree_max_paint_test.dart` (the
`paintExtent <= maxPaintExtent` pin), `test/sliver_tree/paint_purity_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/cache_extent_protocol_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/bounded_iteration_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/bulk_sticky_recompute_test.dart` and
`test/sliver_tree/sticky_bulk_stale_offset_test.dart` (both cover parts 2 and
3), `test/sliver_tree/offscreen_anchor_exit_ghost_test.dart` and
`test/sliver_tree/adjacent_collapsed_exit_ghost_test.dart` (both derive their
probe viewport from `render.geometry!.paintExtent`, at `:185` and `:157`
respectively).

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/bulk_paint_extent_test.dart`: 2000 children
under one root, a 600 px viewport, a trailing `SliverToBoxAdapter` footer,
`expandAll()` with a 300 ms linear spec. Pump to the frame at value 0.5, then
assert `render.geometry!.paintExtent == 600.0` and that the footer's global
top is at or below 600. Setup sanity: assert `render.debugChildCount` is well
under 2000, proving the frame really is on the fast path with most slots
unwritten. Fails today (480), passes after.

Second case, for part 2, and it needs a tree of its own. Establish first what
`_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` and `controller.getCurrentExtentNid(nid)` have to
disagree about at the force-create site, because part 2 changes `priorExtent`
from the former to the latter and changes nothing else. Three shapes that look
like they would discriminate and do not:

- A single-root `expandAll`. The pinned ROOT is a bulk non-member, so
  `getCurrentExtentNid` returns its stored full extent
  (`_animation_coordinator.dart:864-865`, `:867-868`), the pre-expand full
  walk already wrote exactly that into the slot
  (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2636-2642`), and `_layoutNodeChild` measures the
  same height again (`:2400-2405`). All three agree, and the `!=` at `:2967`
  correctly stays quiet before and after.
- The third case's tree, one level down. Its `C0..C39` are VISIBLE pre-expand
  (their parent `R` is expanded), and the full-walk branch at `:2626` (reached
  because `_structureChanged` starts true at `:614`) writes every visible
  index whether or not a child was ever mounted (`:2636-2642`). `expandAll`
  there makes only the grandchildren bulk members, so a pinned `Ci` carries
  slot 48, `getCurrentExtentNid` 48 and a measurement of 48. This corrects the
  earlier draft of this case, which asserted that a never-mounted `C30` still
  held the zero-initialised `0.0`: mounting is irrelevant, VISIBILITY drives
  the full walk, so the premise was false and the case read the same counter
  before and after the fix. M8's block states the same fact correctly ("keep
  the 48 apiece that the pre-collapse full walk wrote (`:2636-2642`)"), and
  the third case below depends on it, which is how the contradiction was
  found.
- Any variant that only makes the row measure something other than 48. Then
  `priorExtent` is 48 under BOTH readings while the measurement is not, so the
  compare fires either way and the case proves nothing.

The divergence has exactly one source, and it is worth stating as the rule.
`getCurrentExtentNid` moves every frame for an ANIMATING nid, and the bulk
fast path is the only Pass 1 branch that leaves an animating row's slot
unwritten: it writes from `cacheStartIndex` to its break (`:453-463`, the
write at `:457`), while the full walk covers the whole visible prefix
(`:2636-2642`), the active-animation branch covers everything from the first
animating index (`:2668-2674`), and the transitional branch covers everything
from the first changed row (`:2687-2703`). The one branch that writes nothing
(`:2645-2648`) runs only when no animation is active now or was last frame,
where the accessor is static too. So an op-group or standalone animation
cannot show this at all, both take a non-bulk branch, and the discriminating
candidate is a force-created sticky ancestor that is ITSELF a bulk member. No
tree whose sticky ancestors are all non-members has one.

Tree: root `R` (48 px, COLLAPSED at first layout), children `C0..C39`
(48 px), each `Ci` with 100 grandchildren (48 px); every row exactly
`TreeController.defaultExtent` (`tree_controller.dart:831`, 48.0), which
matters because `getCurrentExtentNid` falls back to that for an unmeasured nid
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:864-865`) and a row of any other height would
put the case in the third bullet above; `maxStickyDepth: 2` (depths 0 and 1
pin, `_sticky_header_computer.dart:339`); a `ScrollController`; `expandAll()`
on a 300 ms linear `expandCollapse` spec. Because `R` is collapsed, the
harvest at `tree_controller.dart:4102-4121` collects `C0..C39` AND the 4000
grandchildren, and every one of them joins the bulk group at `:4281`; `R` is
already in `_order`, so it is the lone non-member. That is the whole trick: a
depth-1 sticky ancestor that is a bulk MEMBER, whose current extent moves
every frame while the fast path never writes its slot.

Arithmetic at `v = 0.5`. `_rebuildBulkCumulatives` charges the one non-member
to `_stableCumulative` and every member to `_bulkFullCumulative`
(`:324-334`), so `_offsetAtVisibleIndex(i) = 48 + v * 48 * (i - 1)`
(`:342-343`). `Ci` sits at visible index `1 + 101*i`, i.e. at
`48 + 4848 * v * i`, which at `v = 0.5` is `48 + 2424 * i`: `C30` at 72768,
its grandchildren from 72792 to 75192, and a total scroll extent of
`48 + 4040 * 24 = 97008`.

Script. Setup sanity BEFORE `expandAll`, and this one is load-bearing:
`controller.visibleNodeCount == 1`. It pins that every pre-expand full walk
saw a one-row visible order, so no `Ci` slot was ever written by

Assertions, and none of them names an index, because `v` keeps growing and the

depth-1 header) and assert that key is NOT in the pre-jump built-key set. That

above the scroll offset and about 982 px above `cacheStart` (74000 - 250), so

`render.debugBulkCumulativeRebuildCount == 1`.

Why it FAILS today, and what it reads after. Today `priorExtent` is the raw

holds 48 and both readings return 48. The counter delta is attributable to the

Not `debugLastParentDataCumulativeBuilds`, which the first draft used and
which is 0 both before AND after the fix: it is bumped only inside

The third case needs a different tree again, and a two-level one: a sticky

**Sequencing dependency.** Chain 1 in the plan's Sequencing section is M6, then
