### M8. Bulk `collapseAll` never admits rows after the collapsing subtree

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, chain 1 commit. `bulk_collapse_admission_test.dart` pre-fix: case 1 red (B still unbuilt at 250 ms), cases 2 and 3 green, exactly as the block states. Steps 1 to 5 landed as specified: `isCollapsing`, `BulkAdmissionView`, `fullCacheEnd` deleted whole, the callback widened to `(nid, visibleIndex)` with both slot writes in the dispatch closure, the per-nid materialize skip, the sparse-track create/measure/rewrite loops with `firstChangedTrackPos`, and the collapse prefix with survivor hops plus the zero-extent linear fallback. One consequence Step 3 implies but never prints, found when the phase-2 teeth demo refused to go red: the phase-1 walk must break on the LIVE view alone on the bulk arm, because members keep the post accumulator flat, so the dual-view stop would walk the whole collapsing subtree (the naive O(N) the hop exists to avoid) and leave phase 2 dead code; landed as a bulk-only break beside the two-view stop. The returned `cacheEndIndex` then has no reader and is discarded at the call site. Demos recorded: range-keyed freshness (scrollExtent off by 190.08 px), first-survivor-only (C unbuilt), full-charge removal (frame-1 mount 2001), non-bulk arm, huge-cache sanities. Doc items 1 to 19 landed per the ownership split with H2. Full suite green.

**Finding.** `_admitBulkFastPath` breaks on
`_stableCumulative[i] + _bulkFullCumulative[i] >= fullCacheEnd`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:458-459`). Both operands are full-space prefix sums
that do not depend on the animation value, and `fullCacheEnd` is computed once
before the loop from the same full-space quantities
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2744-2752`), so the break index is constant for the
whole collapse. Rows after the collapsing subtree therefore never enter the
cache region, however far the subtree has shrunk. The op-group path solved the
same problem with a second accumulator that charges exits 0
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:41-54`, `:100-125`) and it is pinned by
`test/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:886-888` ("collapsing a subtree
pre-mounts following rows so they do not pop in at dismiss"); nothing pins the
bulk path.

**Root cause.** Two admission implementations. `_admitBulkFastPath`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:446-465`) expresses only the LIVE view, and it
expresses it as an absolute position test rather than an accumulator, which
hides that it is the same rule: `fullOffset(i) >= fullOffset(cs) +
remainingCacheExtent + 2*slideOverreach` (`:2746-2749`) is exactly
`!(liveAccum < budgetCap)` from `_layout_admission_policy.dart:78, 86`. The
post view has no bulk counterpart at all.

**Solution.** Unify the decision in `LayoutAdmissionPolicy`, and give the bulk
branch a closed form so it does not pay a walk.

*Step 1, expose the group direction.* A bulk group's direction is uniform by
construction, and `pendingRemoval` is the test for it. The three writers:

- `expandAll`'s fresh-group branch calls `createGroup` at
  `tree_controller.dart:4264` (no `initialValue`, so 0.0 by the default at
  `_bulk_animator.dart:241-245`) and adds MEMBERS only at `:4281`; `expandAll`
  contains no `_addBulkPending` call at all (`grep -n "_addBulkPending"
  lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart` returns `:516`, `:4423`, `:4485`).
- `expandAll`'s reverse-a-collapsing-group branch clears the pending set
  wholesale (`_clearBulkPending()`, `:4212`) BEFORE adding members at `:4225`.
- `collapseAll`'s fresh-group branch calls `createGroup(initialValue: 1.0)`
  (`:4467-4471`) and adds each key to BOTH sets in the same iteration
  (`_addBulkMember` then `_addBulkPending`, `:4484-4485`), skipping keys
  already flagged `_isPendingDeletion` at `:4477` so those become neither.
- `collapseAll`'s reverse-an-expanding-group branch (`:4417-4425`) adds every
  existing member to `pendingRemoval` EXCEPT keys already flagged
  `_isPendingDeletion` (`:4422`).

Correction to the earlier draft of this block: that last branch does NOT put
every member in both sets, so "collapseAll puts every member in both sets" is
false as a blanket statement. It is still not a MIXED group.
`_isPendingDeletion` is the mid-`remove` marker, not the bulk pending set:
`tree_controller.dart:522` forwards to `_animation_coordinator.dart:528-532`,
backed by `_isPendingDeletionByNid` (`:204`), written only from `remove`'s
animated path at `tree_controller.dart:3112`; the bulk set is written by
`_addBulkPending` -> `_anim.bulk.addPending` (`tree_controller.dart:516`). A
key that branch skips is already on its way out, so it is exiting either way,
and `containsMemberNid` (`types.dart:479-484`) still covers it through the
member mirror. Direction stays uniform.

So add to `BulkAnimationData` (`types.dart:369-485`):

```dart
/// Whether this group is COLLAPSING (`collapseAll`) rather than expanding
/// (`expandAll`). Direction is uniform per group by construction; see the
/// four writer sites in `tree_controller.dart` (`:4212`/`:4225`, `:4281`,
/// `:4421-4425`, `:4484-4485`).
///
/// Known degenerate case, deliberately accepted: if EVERY member of an
/// expanding group is concurrently mid-`remove` (`_isPendingDeletion`),
/// `collapseAll`'s reversal skips all of them at `:4422` and this returns
/// false for a frame while the controller reverses. The only consequence
/// is that the post view charges those rows their full extent, i.e. the
/// admission degenerates to today's under-admission. Never incorrect,
/// only unoptimised.
bool get isCollapsing => _pendingRemoval?.isNotEmpty ?? false;
```

*Step 2, move the decision.* Add a `BulkAdmissionView` value type to
`_layout_admission_policy.dart` carrying `stableCumulative`, `fullCumulative`,
`value`, `isCollapsing` and the `BulkAnimationData` snapshot, and take it as an
optional named parameter on `admit`. The per-row views become closed forms:

| quantity | non-bulk (today) | bulk |
|---|---|---|
| `liveOffset(i)` | `nodeOffsetsByNid[nid]` (`:82`) | `S[i] + v*B[i]` |
| `liveContribution(i)` | `full` if animating else live extent (`:114-122`) | `getEstimatedExtentNid(nid)` |
| `postContribution(i)` | `0` if exit else same (`:117`) | `0` if member and collapsing, else the same |
| `isExit` | `isAnimatingNid && isExitingNid` (`:100-101`) | `isCollapsing && containsMemberNid(nid)` |

with the admit rule (`:102`) and the both-views-failed break (`:92-94`)
unchanged. For an EXPAND the post contribution equals the live contribution, so
the rule degenerates to today's bulk break exactly; for a COLLAPSE the post
accumulator sums only surviving rows, which is the missing view.

Every cell in the bulk column above is a DECISION input and nothing else. In
particular `liveContribution(i) = getEstimatedExtentNid(nid)` is the row's FULL
extent because charging animating rows their full extent is what holds
admission near the pre-animation row count
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:44-47`); it is NOT the value
`_nodeExtentsByNid[nid]` has to hold, which is the ANIMATED extent the Pass 2
measurement is compared against. The two are different numbers for a bulk
member on every frame with `v != 1`. Step 3a below owns the slot values and is
the only place in this block that states them.

*Step 2a, the fate of `fullCacheEnd`.* Step 2 replaces the bulk break and never
says what becomes of the value that break tested against, so this step says it.
DECISION: `fullCacheEnd` is DELETED, the local, the parameter and the
computation alike. What it ENCODES is not dropped. The full-extent bound
survives inside `admit` as the `liveAccum < budgetCap` half of `liveBudgetOk`
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:86`), term for term; what goes is only the
absolute-position FORM of the test, which is the form this block's Root cause
already names as the thing hiding that it was the same rule.

*What it is today, and who reads it.* `fullCacheEnd` is a Pass 2 frame local
declared at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2744`. It is assigned
`fullStart + remainingCacheExtent + slideOverreach * 2.0` at `:2749`, where
`fullStart` is `_stableCumulative[cacheStartIndex] +
_bulkFullCumulative[cacheStartIndex]` (`:2746-2748`), `remainingCacheExtent` is
the constraint local from `:2523` and `slideOverreach` is
`controller.composedSlideAbsDeltaBound` from `:2592`; and it is assigned `0.0`
on the else at `:2751`. It has exactly two executable readers: the argument at
the sole call site (`:2771`) and the break `if (fullOffset >= fullCacheEnd)
break;` at `:459`. `grep -rn "fullCacheEnd" lib test`, run this session,
returns SEVEN lines, all in `lib` and none in `test`: `:439` (the dartdoc
sentence naming it), `:449` (the parameter), `:459`, `:2744`, `:2749`, `:2751`,
`:2771`.

*Why the bound survives the unification, term for term.*
`_rebuildBulkCumulatives` charges every row's
`controller.getEstimatedExtentNid(nid)` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:324`) into
exactly ONE of the two prefix sums, `sBulkFull` for a member and `sStable` for
a non-member (`:325-332`), writes both at `:333-334`, and starts both at 0
(`:314-317`). So `_stableCumulative[k] + _bulkFullCumulative[k]` is the sum of
`getEstimatedExtentNid` over rows `[0, k)`, and

    fullOffset(i) - fullStart == sum of getEstimatedExtentNid over [cacheStartIndex, i)

Step 2's bulk column makes `liveContribution(i)` exactly that per-row term, and
`admit` adds it to `liveAccum` for every ITERATED row from `cacheStartIndex`
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:79`, `:112-123`, and the comment at `:109-111`
stating the charge is unconditional), so when the loop reaches row `i`,
`liveAccum` IS `fullOffset(i) - fullStart`. The cap it is spent against,
`budgetCap = remainingCacheExtent + slideOverreach * 2.0`
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:78`), is the same expression `:2749` adds to
`fullStart`, built from the same two frame locals, which the call site already
passes (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2782-2783`). `liveAccum < budgetCap` at `:86`
and `fullOffset(i) < fullCacheEnd` at `:459` are therefore the same predicate.
That is this block's Root cause read forwards instead of backwards: it asserts
that `fullOffset(i) >= fullOffset(cs) + remainingCacheExtent + 2*slideOverreach`
is exactly `!(liveAccum < budgetCap)`, and the paragraph above is the
derivation.

*Every line that goes, and where its job lands.*

- `render_sliver_tree.dart:459`, the break. Its job splits in two, which is the
  whole Finding: the full-space cap becomes `liveAccum < budgetCap` at
  `_layout_admission_policy.dart:86`, and for a COLLAPSE the rows it used to
  refuse are recovered by Step 3's phase 2, which the cap never governed.
- `:2771`, the argument, and `:449`, the parameter: deleted with the method
  Step 3a deletes.
- `:439-441`, the dartdoc sentence "Anchors the admission band to full-space
  (`fullCacheEnd`) so a low bulk progress value doesn't admit thousands of
  sub-pixel rows on frame 1 of `expandAll`": deleted with that dartdoc, per Doc
  changes item 9. Its content is not lost; it becomes the `liveContribution`
  bullet of item 4's appended dartdoc block, which states the same cap in
  accumulator terms.
- `:2744-2752`, the whole computation, and `:2738-2743`, the comment above it:
  deleted, per Doc changes item 12.
- The else at `:2750-2752` is dead today and loses nothing by going. It is
  reached only when `!_bulkCumulativesValid`, in which case the dispatch takes
  `_admission.admit` at `:2774` and never sees the value, or when
  `cacheStartIndex >= visibleNodes.length`, in which case
  `_admitBulkFastPath`'s loop at `:453` never executes. `admit`'s loop is
  bounded the same way (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:79`) and its one other
  `cacheStartIndex < visibleNodes.length` read is already guarded at `:70-72`,
  so no guard has to be re-created.

Nothing outside those seven lines reads it, so nothing else has to be touched
and no other reader needs a full-extent bound of its own.

*Does this change which rows are admitted?* The full-space cap is unchanged, so
the answer is entirely about what Step 2's predicate ADDS to it. Three parts.

1. *Phase 2, on a COLLAPSE: strictly more rows.* That is the Finding, and it is
   the point of the block.
2. *A live-position conjunct, in both directions.* `liveBudgetOk` is a
   conjunction (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:86`), so the bulk arm gains
   `liveOffset(i) < effectiveCacheEnd` on top of the cap, where
   `liveOffset(i) = S[i] + v*B[i]` (Step 2's table,
   `render_sliver_tree.dart:342-344`) and
   `effectiveCacheEnd = cacheEnd + slideOverreach` (`:2595`). Today's bulk arm
   has no live-position test at all. The conjunct is NON-BINDING in the
   ordinary case, and the condition for that is exact rather than approximate.
   Write `seed := liveOffset(cacheStartIndex) - effectiveCacheStart`, which is
   H2 part (a)'s seed. Then:
   - `effectiveCacheStart + budgetCap == effectiveCacheEnd` identically
     (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2529`, `:2530`, `:2594`, `:2595` against
     `_layout_admission_policy.dart:78`);
   - `liveOffset(i) = liveOffset(cs) + sum over [cs, i) of the live extents`,
     and a live extent is `full * v` for a member and `full` for a non-member
     (difference the closed form at `render_sliver_tree.dart:342-344`), so with
     `v <= 1` it is at most `full` and therefore
     `liveOffset(i) <= liveOffset(cs) + liveAccum(i)`;
   - so when `seed <= 0` and `v <= 1`, `liveAccum(i) < budgetCap` already
     implies `liveOffset(i) < effectiveCacheEnd`, and the conjunct refuses
     nothing.

   `seed <= 0` holds for every `cacheStartIndex >= 1`, because
   `_findFirstVisibleIndex` returns the first index whose offset PLUS extent
   exceeds its argument and therefore only advances past an index whose offset
   does not (`render_sliver_tree.dart:3272-3283`, the branch taken under the
   bulk cumulatives). The one way to get `seed > 0` is `cacheStartIndex == 0`
   with `effectiveCacheStart < 0`, i.e. the window starting above the content
   top, which needs `slideOverreach > cacheStart` (`:2529`, `:2594`) and hence
   a FLIP slide or a held make-room offset in flight concurrently with the bulk
   animation (`slideOverreach` is `composedSlideAbsDeltaBound`, `:2592`).
   `v <= 1` holds for `Curves.linear`, the uniform default
   (`animation_style.dart:113-115`), but `AnimationGroup.value` is
   `curve.transform(controller.value)` (`types.dart:199`), so an overshoot
   curve can exceed 1. In BOTH corners the conjunct only ever refuses rows
   whose LIVE position is already past the live cache band, which is the
   discipline the non-bulk arm has always applied at
   `_layout_admission_policy.dart:86`, and in both it is transient: an
   overshoot settles, and `slideOverreach` shrinks to 0 as the slide progresses
   (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2575-2577`). ACCEPTED, not worked around. Giving
   the bulk arm a position test the non-bulk arm does not have, or exempting it
   from one the non-bulk arm does have, re-splits the rule this block exists to
   unify. H2's seed then removes the first corner outright, see the handoff
   below.
3. *Float.* `liveAccum` accumulates from `cacheStartIndex` while
   `fullOffset(i) - fullStart` is a difference of prefix sums accumulated from
   index 0, so the two are algebraically but not bitwise equal, exactly as M6
   documents for its own pair. It does not matter here, and the reason is
   structural rather than a tolerance: the comparison is `<` against a budget
   (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:86`), not the exact `!=` M6 is about, so a
   last-bit difference can move the decision only for rows whose full-space
   prefix distance from `cacheStartIndex` lands within the accumulation error
   of `budgetCap`, and it moves the admitted count by at most that row, plus
   any zero-extent run adjacent to it, in either direction. No cascade: the
   threshold is monotone in `i`, so a shifted boundary is still a boundary.

*Why `effectiveCacheEnd` alone will NOT do, stated because Step 2's formula
invites it.* Reading Step 2's bulk `liveOffset` row on its own suggests the
bulk arm could be just `S[i] + v*B[i] < effectiveCacheEnd` with the full-extent
bound gone. It cannot. On frame 1 of `expandAll` the group value is 0
(`createGroup`'s `initialValue` default, `_bulk_animator.dart:244`, and
`expandAll` passes none, `tree_controller.dart:4264`), so every entering
member's live extent is `full * 0`, the live position stops advancing across
the entire entering subtree, and the position test stays true for thousands of
rows. That is precisely the mass-mount hitch the comment at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:2738-2743` says the full-space anchor exists to
prevent. Note which pin exists and which does not:
`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:874-882` pins the ANALOGOUS NON-BULK case at
`lessThan(50)`, and only that, because its enclosing test (`:787-884`) uses
`controller.expand` (`:826`) and `controller.collapse` (`:855`) and never
`expandAll`/`collapseAll`, so `bulkOnly` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2606`,
`bulkData.isValid && !controller.hasOpGroupAnimations`) is false for its whole
animation and the dispatch takes the `_admission.admit` arm. The BULK frame-1
pin does not exist today; this block's second test case adds it.
Step 2 does not ask `effectiveCacheEnd` to carry it: `liveContribution(i) =
getEstimatedExtentNid(nid)` keeps the FULL charge in both views, so the cap is
still spent at the pre-animation rate in the live view and, on an expand, in
the post view too, where `postContribution` equals `liveContribution`. The
full-extent bound is load-bearing and is retained; only its name is not.

*Handoff to H2, Chain 1's last block.* H2 part (c) rewrites this same
computation and H2's Doc changes item 7 rewrites the comment above it. After
this step neither has a target, and item 7 is withdrawn in H2 rather than left
pointing at deleted lines. Nothing H2 wants is lost. The anchor error part (c)
repairs, the band ending short by the leading row's overhang above the window,
is the same defect part (a) repairs in the accumulator, and after this block
the bulk arm spends that accumulator, so part (a) covers both arms with one
seed. One constraint on how, the same one Step 3a imposes on H2's paint floor:
part (a)'s seed is written as `nodeOffsetsByNid[orderNids[cacheStartIndex]] -
effectiveCacheStart`, and on the bulk arm that slot is not readable for the row
the loop is deciding about, so the seed's first term must come from the bulk
view instead, as `bulkView.stableCumulative[cs] + bulkView.value *
bulkView.fullCumulative[cs]`. That is Step 2's `liveOffset(cacheStartIndex)`,
and it is the same quantity `postOffsetOrigin`
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:70-72`) needs on that arm, so one expression
serves both. With that seed in place, part 2 above's `seed > 0` corner
disappears outright rather than merely being bounded: `liveAccum` then starts
at `seed`, so `liveAccum < budgetCap` becomes
`liveOffset(cs) + fullAccum(i) < effectiveCacheEnd`, which implies the position
conjunct for every `v <= 1` with no condition on `cacheStartIndex` at all.

*Step 3, keep it O(log N)-ish.* A naive unified walk is unacceptable for a
large collapse: measured (probe_m8b.dart) 6.24 ms per frame for one root with
200k collapsing children, because the loop must reach the survivors past the
subtree. Two observations collapse it:

- For a COLLAPSE, a member's post contribution is 0, so
  `postAccum(i) == _stableCumulative[i] - _stableCumulative[cacheStartIndex]`
  exactly, and `postOffset(i)` is that plus `postOffsetOrigin`. The post view's
  admissible set is therefore a PREFIX `[cacheStartIndex, K)` whose cut `K` is
  ONE upper-bound binary search on the non-decreasing `_stableCumulative`. No
  accumulator, no walk.
- Beyond the live cut only NON-members can admit (an exit admits via the live
  view only, `_layout_admission_policy.dart:96-102`), and `_stableCumulative`
  is constant across a run of members (`render_sliver_tree.dart:325-334`), so
  enumerating the survivors inside `[cacheStartIndex, K)` is a survivor-to-
  survivor hop, each step an upper-bound binary search.

```dart
// First index k in (from, n] with stableCumulative[k] > stableCumulative[from];
// k - 1 is the next surviving (non-member) row.
int _nextSurvivor(Float64List stable, int from, int n) { ... }
```

Phase 1 (live) is today's rule, unchanged, bounded by `budgetCap /
minRowHeight`. Phase 2 (post) runs ONLY when `bulkView.isCollapsing`: for an
expand the post-animation layout IS the full-space layout, so the post test is
identical to phase 1's full-space break and phase 2 would add nothing. That
early return is what preserves the frame-1 mass-mount cap. Measured
(probe_m8c.dart) on the same 200k worst case: 4 us per frame, 35 rows touched,
against 6242 us and 199998 rows for the naive walk.

Guard for zero-extent survivors, required for correctness. `stable[k] >
stable[from]` first becomes true one past the first non-member with NON-ZERO
extent, so a non-member measured at exactly 0 px is invisible to the hop and
would never be admitted. `getEstimatedExtentNid` returns a measured height
(`tree_controller.dart:981-985`), which a row widget can make 0, so this is
reachable. Fix: `_rebuildBulkCumulatives` already computes `full` for every row
in a pass that runs once per membership change (`render_sliver_tree.dart:324`);
have it also set a `bool _bulkHasZeroExtentNonMember` when a non-member's
`full == 0.0`. Phase 2 uses the hop when that flag is false and a plain linear
scan over `[cacheStartIndex, K)` when it is true. One bool, no per-frame cost,
and the pathological case is no slower than the naive walk it replaces.

*Step 3a, the write site: who fills `_nodeOffsetsByNid` and
`_nodeExtentsByNid` for an admitted row.* Step 2 deletes the only writer those
two arrays have on a bulk frame, so this block owes a replacement, named in one
place, for both arms.

State the hole precisely, because the diff hides it. `_admitBulkFastPath`'s own
dartdoc states the split (`render_sliver_tree.dart:443-445`): "The caller owns
the outer-loop dispatch; this method performs the per-row writes and
sparse-track buffer maintenance for the admitted range." Those writes are
`:455-457` (`final offset = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(i);`,
`_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] = offset;`, `_nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = ...`).
`LayoutAdmissionPolicy.admit` performs no equivalent: it writes
`inCacheRegionByNid[nid] = 1` and fires `onCacheRegionAdmit(nid)`
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:103-107`), and that callback is
`void Function(int nid)` (`:61`), so it does not even receive the visible index
`_offsetAtVisibleIndex` needs. Pass 1 does not cover for it: the `bulkOnly`
branch touches no per-nid slot at all, it rebuilds the cumulatives and sets
`totalScrollExtent = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(n)`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2608-2625`), which is the stated point of the fast
path ("Avoid touching `_nodeOffsetsByNid` for nodes outside the cache region,
that write is what the per-frame O(N) cost was buying", `:2610-2612`). Nor does
the parentData refresh, which skips admitted rows outright (`:3179-3183`). Left
unclosed, Step 5's `final estimated = _nodeExtentsByNid[nid];` and its
`layoutOffset = _nodeOffsetsByNid[nid];` would read slots nothing wrote that
frame: the phase-2 survivors this block exists to admit would carry
pre-collapse offsets, and the exact `!=` compare would mismatch every frame,
which is M6's failure chain reinstated one step downstream of where M6 removed
it.

DECISION: widen the callback to
`void Function(int nid, int visibleIndex) onCacheRegionAdmit` and perform the
two slot writes in the render object's callback body, on the BULK arm only.
Admission then has exactly three effects and all three happen at one site: the
flag (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:104`), the sparse-track append (`:105`),
and the slots. `_inCacheRegionByNid[nid] != 0` comes to mean precisely "these
two slots were written this frame", which is the invariant Step 4's per-nid
rule then rests on, held by construction instead of by two sites staying in
step.

The dispatch site (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2766-2785`) already branches on
`_bulkCumulativesValid` to build the `BulkAdmissionView`, so the callback is
selected there, out of the loop body, per the convention the file states at
`:2754-2757`:

```dart
final void Function(int nid, int visibleIndex) onAdmit;
if (bulkView != null) {
  // Same field `bulkView.value` carries and `_offsetAtVisibleIndex` reads
  // (`:342-344`), assigned once per frame at `:2623` from `bulkData.value`,
  // so the slot and the admission decision cannot disagree about `v`.
  final double v = _bulkValueCached;
  onAdmit = (int nid, int visibleIndex) {
    // Moved verbatim from the deleted `_admitBulkFastPath` (`:455-457`),
    // carrying M6's extent arithmetic rather than the cumulative
    // difference. Bitwise-identical to the Pass 2 measurement
    // (`getAnimatedExtent`, `_animation_coordinator.dart:718-724`), which is
    // what keeps the exact `!=` in Step 5 firing only on a real height
    // change.
    _nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] = _offsetAtVisibleIndex(visibleIndex);
    final full = controller.getEstimatedExtentNid(nid);
    _nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = bulkData.containsMemberNid(nid) ? full * v : full;
    _writeCacheRegionNid(nid);
  };
} else {
  // (int nid, int _) => _writeCacheRegionNid(nid)
  onAdmit = _appendAdmittedNid;
}
```

`bulkData` is the frame local at `:2605`, already in scope at the dispatch
site.

Per arm, stated flatly.

- BULK arm: the closure above, for every admitted row, in phase 1 and phase 2
  alike. Phase 2's hop knows each survivor's visible index (it produces those
  indices by binary search on `_stableCumulative`), so it calls the same
  callback with it, which is exactly what stops a phase-2 survivor carrying a
  pre-collapse offset. Offset value: `_offsetAtVisibleIndex(visibleIndex)`,
  i.e. `S[i] + v*B[i]`, the same expression Step 2's table gives as the bulk
  `liveOffset(i)` and the same one `:455` writes today. Extent value:
  `getEstimatedExtentNid(nid) * v` for a member, `getEstimatedExtentNid(nid)`
  for a non-member (`tree_controller.dart:981-985`, `types.dart:479-484`).
- NON-BULK arm: unchanged, and the callback ignores its new second parameter.
  Pass 1 already writes the whole visible prefix on every non-bulk branch that
  can invalidate a slot (the full walk `:2636-2642`, the active-animation
  branch `:2668-2674`, the transitional branch `:2687-2703`), and the
  pure-scroll branch (`:2645-2648`) writes nothing because nothing changed, so
  the prior layout's slots stand. The file records the conclusion itself at
  `:2705-2707` ("Each non-bulk branch above writes the full visible prefix, so
  yes") and encodes it as `offsetsAuthoritative = !bulkOnly` (`:2717`). That
  is also why `admit` READS these two arrays today (`:82`, `:119`) instead of
  writing them, and it is why the write is bulk-only: overwriting a non-bulk
  row's extent slot with the bulk formula would be wrong twice over, the
  cumulatives are not even valid on that arm.

Two consequences of narrowing the written set from iterated rows to admitted
rows, both checked.

- Today `_admitBulkFastPath` writes slots for every ITERATED row, including the
  row it breaks on (`:455-457` precede the break at `:459`). The unified loop
  admits conditionally (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:102-107`) and breaks
  only when both views fail (`:92-94`), so it can iterate past a non-admitted
  row, which now gets no write. Every in-layout reader of an off-cache bulk
  slot is routed away from the raw array by the time this lands: consumer 3
  materializes those rows because their flag is 0 (Step 4), the sticky
  force-create's two raw reads at `:2963` and `:3005` are replaced by M7's
  parts 2 and 3, the paint-extent loop's reads at `:3039-3040` are deleted by
  M7's part 1, and `_findFirstVisibleIndex`'s raw-slot branch (`:3308-3319`)
  is reachable only when `!_bulkCumulativesValid && !_lastFrameUsedBulkCumulatives`,
  the case its own comment labels "Last frame was non-bulk: per-nid arrays were
  fully populated" (`:3305`).
- The write must happen at ADMIT time, not lazily inside Step 5's loop, and
  the reason is mechanical rather than stylistic. `_layoutNodeChild` calls
  `controller.setFullExtent(nodeId, child.size.height)` (`:2400`), and that is
  the input `getEstimatedExtentNid` resolves (`tree_controller.dart:981-985`).
  Computing the estimate after the measurement would compare the new
  measurement against itself, `extentsChanged` would never fire, and the
  offsets would never be recomputed.

Losers, and why.

- *(B) Keep the writes in the render object, as a second loop over
  `_writtenCacheRegionNids` run immediately after `admit` returns.* Correct,
  and it keeps the arithmetic in plainly visible render-object code. M8's
  unified-policy goal survives it intact, since the policy would still own the
  decision, and the bulk and non-bulk arms would share the write site only in
  the trivial sense that the non-bulk arm would skip it. It loses on the
  invariant before it loses on cycles: it re-splits "decided" from "written"
  into two sites that must be kept in step, which is the exact split that
  produced this hole. The cycles are the second reason: the policy holds the
  visible index for free (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:79`), and this form
  throws it away and then buys it back with a
  `controller.visibleIndexOfNid(nid)` per admitted row
  (`tree_controller.dart:969-972`) plus a second pass over the track. An index
  track appended beside the nid track would remove that lookup and is rejected
  separately, by Step 4's alternative (i) and again in the Chain 17 paragraph
  below.
- *(C) Hand the policy the offset function and let it write the slots.*
  Rejected on layering. `LayoutAdmissionPolicy` declares itself stateless
  apart from a controller back-pointer, with every per-frame input arriving as
  a parameter and nothing cached between calls
  (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:4-6`); the only render state it mutates is
  `inCacheRegionByNid`, a flag whose meaning it owns. Owning the VALUES in
  `_nodeOffsetsByNid` / `_nodeExtentsByNid` would mean importing
  `_offsetAtVisibleIndex` as a per-row closure call, `_bulkValueCached` and
  the member mirror, and relocating M6's bitwise-identity contract with
  `getAnimatedExtent` into a file that has no other tie to it. CLAUDE.md puts
  those slots in the render object, and this block's own Architecture fit
  argues the policy owns a decision.

Cost of the winner, per admitted row: zero additional calls, because
`onCacheRegionAdmit` already fires once per admitted row
(`_layout_admission_policy.dart:105`); one additional int argument; and the two
slot writes with their operands, namely `_offsetAtVisibleIndex` (two
`Float64List` reads, one multiply, one add), one `Float64List` read
(`getEstimatedExtentNid`), one `Uint8List` read (`containsMemberNid`) and one
multiply. That is the work `:455-457` does today minus the second
`_offsetAtVisibleIndex(i + 1)` call M6 already removes, so the bulk arm's
per-row slot cost does not rise, it falls slightly, and it is now paid for
admitted rows only rather than for every iterated one. Allocations: one closure
per bulk layout, beside the one `BulkAdmissionView` the Performance section
already accounts for.

`admit` is a shared declaration, so its users are enumerated before the
signature changes (`grep -rn "onCacheRegionAdmit\|\.admit(" lib test`): one
library call site (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2774`, callback argument at
`:2780`) and three test call sites in
`test/sliver_tree/layout_admission_policy_test.dart` (`:61`, `:85`, `:104`),
each passing `onCacheRegionAdmit: writtenNids.add` (`:67`, `:91`, `:110`).
`writtenNids.add` is a `void Function(int)` tear-off and does not satisfy the
widened type, so those three arguments become
`(int nid, int _) => writtenNids.add(nid)`. There is no other implementer, no
other caller, and no subclass.

*Step 4, required companion: stop treating `[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)`
as a membership test.* This is the design question the hop forces, and it has
one answer.

After the hop, `cacheEndIndex` can be 199998 in the worst case while the
admitted set inside it is 35 rows. `grep -n "cacheEndIndex\|cacheStartIndex"
lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart` gives exactly FOUR executable
consumers of the returned range (the hits at `:3117` and `:3168` are comments;
the parentData refresh itself gates on the per-nid flag at `:3179-3183`):

1. the create loop, `:2794-2803`;
2. the measurement loop, `:2812-2829`;
3. `_materializeBulkStaleExtents`'s "these slots are fresh, skip them" test,
   `:2331`, fed from `:2847-2848` and `:2979-2980`;
4. the post-recompute parentData rewrite, `:2858-2866`.

Consumer 3 is the one the earlier draft of this block silently broke: it skips
`[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)` on the premise that those slots are fresh,
which is true today only because `_admitBulkFastPath` writes every iterated
slot before its break (`:455-457` precede the break at `:459`). After the hop
the skipped members inside the inflated range keep a stale
`_nodeExtentsByNid`, so `_recomputeOffsetsFrom` (`:2853`) and `_recomputeOffsets`
(`:2984`) would produce wrong offsets and a wrong `geometry.scrollExtent`.

DECISION: make freshness a PER-NID question, answered by
`_inCacheRegionByNid`, and make enumeration a SPARSE-TRACK question, answered
by `_writtenCacheRegionNids`. Concretely:

- Consumer 3: drop the `cacheStartIndex` / `cacheEndIndex` parameters from
  `_materializeBulkStaleExtents` (`:2323-2328`) and change the skip at `:2331`
  to `if (_inCacheRegionByNid[orderNids[i]] != 0) continue;`. This is EXACTLY
  equivalent today: `_admitBulkFastPath` sets the flag at `:460` for every
  index in `[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)` and for no other index, and the
  function is only reachable while `_bulkCumulativesValid`, which only the bulk
  path establishes. Under the hop it is correct by construction, because a
  hopped-over member is not flagged and therefore gets materialized. Cost is
  unchanged (the loop already walks every index from `fromIndex`; two int
  compares become one `Uint8List` read) and no second range has to be kept in
  sync.
- Consumers 1, 2 and 4: iterate the sparse admitted track the render object
  already maintains -- `_writtenCacheRegionNids` / `_writtenCacheRegionNidsLen`
  (`:482-483`, appended by `_writeCacheRegionNid` at `:491-498`), cleared at the
  top of Pass 2 (`:2729-2735`), written inline by the bulk path at `:461` and
  by the policy through the `onCacheRegionAdmit` callback wired at `:2780` and
  fired at `_layout_admission_policy.dart:105`. It is appended in ascending
  index order by both writers, so `firstChangedIdx` ordering is preserved.
  Resolve the key with `controller.keyOfNid(nid)` (already used at
  `render_sliver_tree.dart:4001`), which also removes the `TKey` hash those
  loops pay today at `:2798` and `:2817`.

Rejected, with reasons:

- *(i) Keep a separate contiguous "synced range" alongside the sparse track.*
  Rejected on architecture. It adds a third bookkeeping notion ("iterated",
  "admitted", "synced") that every present and future admission body has to
  maintain, which is the same class of duplicated invariant this block's
  Finding blames for the bulk path never growing a post view. It also cannot
  express the hop's real shape: phase 2's synced set is genuinely sparse, so a
  contiguous range either over-claims (skipping stale members, the bug) or
  under-claims (re-materializing the whole tail, O(N), giving back the win).
- *(iii) Abandon the hop.* It does fix the Finding, but at the measured 6.24 ms
  per frame for the 200k case (probe_m8b.dart) against 4 us with the hop
  (probe_m8c.dart), on a path whose entire reason for existing is that the
  bulk-only frame must not walk N.

Rule for the implementer, and it covers every future consumer: after this
change `[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)` is an ITERATION BOUND, never a
membership test. To ask "was this row admitted / are its per-nid slots fresh
this frame", read `_inCacheRegionByNid[nid]`. To VISIT the admitted rows,
iterate `_writtenCacheRegionNids[0 .. _writtenCacheRegionNidsLen)`.

*Step 5, index recovery in the measurement loop.* The sparse track holds nids,
but the measurement loop still needs a visible INDEX for `firstChangedIdx`
(`:2823`), for `_recomputeOffsetsFrom(firstChangedIdx)` (`:2853`) and for
`updateStart` (`:2858`).

DECISION: recover it with `controller.visibleIndexOfNid(nid)`
(`tree_controller.dart:969-972`), an O(1) `Int32List` read into
`_order.indexByNid` with no `TKey` hash, and call it AT MOST ONCE PER LAYOUT.
Because the track is ascending in visible index, the first tracked entry whose
extent changes is also the lowest-index one, so:

```dart
int firstChangedIdx = visibleNodes.length;
int firstChangedTrackPos = _writtenCacheRegionNidsLen; // none yet
for (int pos = 0; pos < _writtenCacheRegionNidsLen; pos++) {
  final nid = _writtenCacheRegionNids[pos];
  final nodeId = controller.keyOfNid(nid);
  if (nodeId == null) continue;
  final actual = _layoutNodeChild(nodeId, crossAxisExtent);
  if (actual == null) continue;
  final estimated = _nodeExtentsByNid[nid];
  if (actual != estimated) {
    _nodeExtentsByNid[nid] = actual;
    totalScrollExtent += actual - estimated;
    if (!extentsChanged) {
      extentsChanged = true;
      firstChangedTrackPos = pos;
      firstChangedIdx = controller.visibleIndexOfNid(nid); // once per layout
    }
  }
  final child = getChildForNode(nodeId)!;
  (child.parentData! as SliverTreeParentData).layoutOffset =
      _nodeOffsetsByNid[nid];
}
```

and consumer 4 then drops `updateStart` entirely: it resumes the track at
`firstChangedTrackPos`, which is the sparse equivalent of
`math.max(cacheStartIndex, firstChangedIdx)` (every tracked nid is at an index
>= `cacheStartIndex` by construction). Cost of the whole recovery is one
`Int32List` read per layout.

Both slot reads in that body are covered by Step 3a, and the coverage is exact
rather than incidental. The loop's only source of nids is
`_writtenCacheRegionNids[0 .. _writtenCacheRegionNidsLen)`, and the only writer
of that buffer is `_writeCacheRegionNid` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:491-498`),
which after Step 3a is called from exactly one place: the admit callback, after
both slot writes. So `final estimated = _nodeExtentsByNid[nid];` and
`layoutOffset = _nodeOffsetsByNid[nid];` read, on the bulk arm, values the
callback wrote earlier in this same layout, and on the non-bulk arm values Pass
1 wrote or carried forward under `offsetsAuthoritative` (`:2705-2707`, `:2717`),
which is what they read today. No entry can reach the track without both slots
being current, in either arm. The rows Step 3a stops writing, iterated but not
admitted, never enter the track and are therefore never read here.

One consumer of that decision, recorded here because it is the thing most
likely to be lost in the rewrite: H1's Solution step 2 adds a two-line
`aboveAnchorDelta` accumulation to the `if (actual != estimated)` branch of
the body above, and H1 lands AFTER this block (Chain 17 below), so what is
printed here is the pre-H1 shape. Its condition is an offset compare, not an
index compare, so the sparse track does not have to expose the visible index
it deliberately does not carry.

One behavioural difference to record, and it is safe: today's loop at
`:2860-2866` also rewrites parentData for rows inside the range that were
iterated but NOT admitted. The sparse loop does not. Those rows, when mounted,
are picked up by the unconditional parentData refresh at `:3150-3250`, which
skips only `_inCacheRegionByNid[nid] != 0` (`:3179-3183`), recovers the index
itself at `:3184`, resolves the offset from the bulk cumulatives (`:3199-3202`)
or a fresh cumulative (`:3203-3211`), and writes `layoutOffset` at `:3238`.

A SECOND behavioural difference, and this one needs its replacement stated
because a comment in the file names it as a guarantee. Today's measurement loop
calls `_layoutNodeChild` on EVERY index in `[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)`,
admitted or not, and `render_sliver_tree.dart:3166-3173` leans on exactly that:
non-admitted-but-mounted children inside the range "have
`_inCacheRegionByNid[nid] == 0` here and would also have been touched by the
measurement loop via `_layoutNodeChild`, letting them through is a redundant
(but correctness-safe) re-write of the same offset. Cost is one field
assignment per such row; the case is rare (off-screen exits during a
collapse)." The sparse loop iterates admitted nids only, so it stops touching
them, and after the hop the case is no longer rare: every mounted row in the
skipped span is one. What replaces the guarantee, per the two things
`_layoutNodeChild` did for such a row:

- *The parentData writes.* All three are performed by the refresh instead:
  `layoutOffset` at `:3238`, `indent` and `visibleExtent` at `:3248-3249` from
  `controller.getIndent` and `controller.getCurrentExtentNid`, which the
  comment at `:3239-3247` already states is the same chain `_layoutNodeChild`
  consumes via `getAnimatedExtent`. The refresh reaches exactly these rows
  (it skips only `_inCacheRegionByNid[nid] != 0`, `:3179-3183`, and a
  hopped-over row is flagged 0), so nothing is lost. The comment at
  `:3166-3173` needs rewriting with this change: the re-write is no longer
  redundant, it is the only write, and the case is no longer rare.
- *The `child.layout` call.* Not replaced, and it does not need to be, because
  "mounted this frame, laid out by nobody this frame" is already the normal
  state of every retained off-cache row: edge ghosts, exit phantoms and
  slide-active rows all sit outside `[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)` and are
  already never passed to `_layoutNodeChild`, as the refresh loop's own cost
  comment records (`:3143-3146`). Paint and hit-test iterate viewport-bounded
  bands (`:3355-3356` and `:3375`, `:4162-4164` and `:4271`) and skip indices
  with no mounted child, so the population at risk of painting unlaid-out was
  always the retained-mounted one, unchanged here. The hop moves rows from
  "outside the range, unadmitted" to "inside the range, unadmitted"; the per-nid
  flag `_inCacheRegionByNid` answers both identically, which is the whole point
  of Step 4.

**Sequencing dependency (Chain 17, M8 then H1).** H1's Solution step 2 adds a
frame-local `aboveAnchorDelta` accumulation to the extent-changed branch of
the measurement loop at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2819-2824`, which is inside
the loop Step 5 above replaces wholesale (`:2812-2829`, consumer 2 of the four
this block enumerates). Required order: M8 first, then H1. Landing H1 first
puts M8 in the position of pasting a full replacement body over a loop that
already carries two lines it does not print, which deletes them without
breaking the build, since `aboveAnchorDelta` stays declared and stays emitted
at H1's `:3029` site; the correction then silently under-reports by every
measured row above the viewport top. Landing M8 first makes H1 a two-line
insert into the `if (actual != estimated)` branch of Step 5's body. This block
does NOT owe H1 a visible index. H1's condition is
`_nodeOffsetsByNid[nid] + estimated <= scrollOffset`, an offset compare on
values the loop already holds (`scrollOffset` is the constraint local at
`:2521`), which is exactly `i < _findFirstVisibleIndex(scrollOffset)` because
that search is the same comparison on the same two arrays (`:3310-3313`). Keep
it that way: appending a parallel index track beside `_writtenCacheRegionNids`
would add the third bookkeeping notion Step 4's alternative (i) rejects,
maintained in lockstep by two writers (`:461` and `:491-498`), and recovering
`visibleIndexOfNid` per changed row instead is the per-row lookup Step 5's
"AT MOST ONCE PER LAYOUT" rule exists to remove.

**Doc changes.** Steps 2 to 5 change, falsify, or leave silent on a new term,
nineteen comment sites in two files: thirteen rewrites, two DEFERRALS (items 1
and 2, whose final text H2 owns and this block pastes, see the ownership
paragraph below), two DELETIONS (items 9
and 12, both unconditional once Step 2a settles `fullCacheEnd`), and two
deliberate NON-changes (items 5 and 7,
recorded so the absence is a finding rather than an omission). All are landed
in the SAME commit as the code. Line numbers are as read this session at
`4d15c0c`. Code lines appear inside a replacement only so the comment can be
pasted in position: they are the Steps' lines, not a second specification of
them. The list was built by reading `_layout_admission_policy.dart` end to end
and every `render_sliver_tree.dart` range the Steps touch, not by following the
Steps' own cross-references, so it names sites no Step names; item 19 is a
rewrite Step 5 promises without printing.

*Ownership with H2, settled jointly so nobody carries two versions of one
comment.* Per the plan header's "Conventions used in the blocks", another
block is named by ID and section, never by line, and its words are quoted
rather than pointed at. H2's Doc changes opens by counting itself: "nine
comment sites in two files, presented below as eight items". SEVEN of those
nine sites are ones this block also changes: `_layout_admission_policy.dart:3-6`,
`:15-21` (H2's item 5 targets both), `:41-54`, `:90-102`, and
`render_sliver_tree.dart:433-445`, `:2738-2743`, `:2754-2765` (H2's item 8

```dart
  /// fires `onCacheRegionAdmit(nid, visibleIndex)` for each admitted nid,

  /// from it, so admission has exactly three effects and all three happen
  /// at one site: the flag here, the caller's sparse-track append, and
  /// those two slots. `inCacheRegionByNid[nid] != 0` therefore means
  /// precisely "admitted this layout, and its per-nid slots were written
  /// this layout", an invariant held by construction rather than by two
  /// sites staying in step.

  /// That is an ITERATION BOUND, never a membership test:

  /// past without admitting, and on a bulk collapse it contains long runs
  /// it never visited at all. To ask whether a row was admitted, or

  /// VISIT the admitted rows, iterate the caller's sparse track.
```

```dart
  ///
  /// On the BULK arm ([BulkAdmissionView] non-null) the same two views take
  /// closed forms, and nothing else about the rule changes:
  ///
  /// - the live position is `stableCumulative[i] + value *
  ///   fullCumulative[i]`, the animated offset the render object's
  ///   `_offsetAtVisibleIndex` computes, not a per-nid slot read;
  /// - both views charge the row its FULL extent
  ///   ([TreeController.getEstimatedExtentNid]), for the same reason the
  ///   non-bulk arm charges an animating row its full extent: it is what
  ///   holds admission near the pre-animation row count;
  /// - the post view charges 0 for a MEMBER of a COLLAPSING group. That is
  ///   the exit rule with `isCollapsing && containsMemberNid(nid)` standing
  ///   in for `isAnimatingNid && isExitingNid`; a bulk group's direction is
  ///   uniform by construction ([BulkAnimationData.isCollapsing]).
  ///
  /// For an EXPAND the post charge equals the live charge, so the post view
  /// adds nothing and the walk stops where the live view stops, which is
  /// what keeps frame 1 of `expandAll` from mass-mounting the entering
  /// subtree. For a COLLAPSE the post view's admissible set is a PREFIX,
  /// because `postAccum(i)` reduces to a difference of `stableCumulative`,
  /// so it is resolved by binary search and its survivors are enumerated by
  /// survivor-to-survivor hops rather than by walking the collapsing
  /// subtree. Rows that phase hops over are NOT admitted and NOT flagged,
  /// which is what routes them to the render object's per-nid freshness
  /// paths instead of leaving them silently stale.
```

```dart
        // mounted row in the hopped-over span, which is why the three
        // writes below (layoutOffset, indent, visibleExtent) resolve from
        // `controller.getIndent` and `controller.getCurrentExtentNid`, the
        // same chain [_layoutNodeChild] consumes via `getAnimatedExtent`.
        // Such a row is mounted but not laid out this frame, which is
        // already the normal state of every retained off-cache row (edge
        // ghosts, exit phantoms, slide-active rows) and is bounded by the
        // viewport-bounded paint and hit-test bands.
```

**Alternatives considered.**

- *The review's suggested `fullOffset < fullCacheEnd || stableCumulative[i] -
  stableCumulative[cacheStartIndex] < remainingCacheExtent`.* Rejected: during
  `expandAll` the entering members contribute 0 to `_stableCumulative`

  thousands of rows and re-introduces exactly the frame-1 mass-mount the
  full-space anchor was added to prevent (`:2738-2743`). The bulk form of that
  hitch has no existing pin, for the reason given under "Why
  `effectiveCacheEnd` alone will NOT do"; this block's second test case adds
  it, and `sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:874-882` pins only the non-bulk
  analogue. The
  enter/exit distinction is load-bearing and the fix must carry it; the
  `isCollapsing` gate on phase 2 is where this block carries it.
- *Give `_admitBulkFastPath` its own second accumulator, leaving two
  implementations.* Rejected on architecture: two copies of the dual-view rule
  is the root problem, and the bulk copy has already diverged once (it never
  grew a post view). The rule belongs in one place, with the bulk view as a
  data-shaped input rather than a second body.

**Architecture fit.** `LayoutAdmissionPolicy` already declares itself the owner
of the dual-view decision ("Owns the dual-accumulator (live/post) admission
decision used in the non-bulk path", `_layout_admission_policy.dart:3-4`) and
already takes every per-frame input as a parameter with nothing cached between
calls (`:5-6`). Adding a bulk view removes the qualifier "non-bulk" from that
sentence. The `if (bulkView != null)` hoist out of the loop body follows the
convention the render object states at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2754-2757`
("Dispatch the per-iteration branch out of the loop body"). The sparse-track
companion reuses the buffer the render object already maintains for its Pass 2
sparse clear (`:472-483`, `:491-498`), and the per-nid freshness test reuses the
flag the parentData refresh already trusts for the same question (`:3179-3183`).
Step 3a's callback widening keeps the per-nid slot arithmetic in the render
object, where CLAUDE.md places that state, and moves nothing into the policy
but the decision: `admit`'s dartdoc already frames admission as an event the
caller is told about ("fires [onCacheRegionAdmit] for each admitted nid in
iteration order", `_layout_admission_policy.dart:37-39`), and Step 3a only
enlarges what the event carries from "which nid" to "which nid, at which
visible index".

**Performance.** Before: `_admitBulkFastPath` is O(admitted) with a constant
break index (measured 1 us, 18 rows, probe_m8.dart) and never admits the
followers, so they mass-mount in one non-bulk settle layout. After, per bulk
frame: phase 1 O(admitted), phase 2 O(survivors admitted * log N), measured 4
us on a 200k worst case (probe_m8c.dart) against 6242 us for the naive unified
walk. Per-row arithmetic in phase 1 roughly doubles (two budget comparisons and
two accumulator adds instead of one position compare) on a loop of about 18
rows. Allocations: one `BulkAdmissionView` per layout (a const-shaped record;
can be a field reused in place if the allocation shows up), plus the one
closure per bulk layout Step 3a's write site allocates. Step 3a adds no
per-admitted-row call, because `onCacheRegionAdmit` already fires once per
admitted row (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:105`), and its two slot writes are
the ones `render_sliver_tree.dart:455-457` performs today minus the second
`_offsetAtVisibleIndex(i + 1)` call M6 removes, so the bulk arm's per-row slot
cost is slightly lower than today's and is now paid for admitted rows only, not
for every iterated one. Measured
(probe_m8d.dart): the create + measurement loops cost 7.97 ms per frame when
walked over 200k indices; the sparse-track switch removes that and is a pure
win on the op-group collapse path too, where the same O(subtree) caller walk
is invisible only because the pinned test uses 200 children
(`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:918`).

**Risk.** `admit`'s return value feeds the create loop, the measurement loop,
`_materializeBulkStaleExtents`, the post-recompute parentData rewrite, and
`isNodeRetained`'s cache-region check (`:1502-1504`, which reads the per-nid
flag and is unaffected); the sparse-track switch touches the first two and the
fourth, and the per-nid switch touches the third. The parentData refresh's
`_inCacheRegionByNid` gate (`:3179-3183`) is unchanged and becomes load-bearing
for hopped-over mounted rows. Step 3a changes `admit`'s signature, whose users
are enumerated in that step: one library call site and three in
`test/sliver_tree/layout_admission_policy_test.dart` (`:61`, `:85`, `:104`),
where `onCacheRegionAdmit: writtenNids.add` (`:67`, `:91`, `:110`) stops
type-checking and becomes `(int nid, int _) => writtenNids.add(nid)`; those
three edits are mechanical and the tests' assertions are untouched. Existing
tests to re-run:
`test/sliver_tree/layout_admission_policy_test.dart`,

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/bulk_collapse_admission_test.dart`, mirroring

Third case, the Step-4 teeth. The height-changing row must be an ADMITTED one,
not a row inside the skipped span: a skipped row is never created
(`:2794-2802` gates on `_inCacheRegionByNid`), so its `StatefulWidget` never

LAND in the skipped span. So: about 20 ms into the same collapse, where the

`StatefulWidget`.

Where phase 1 cuts, and whether the cut moves with `v`. It does not move, and
the reason is Step 2's charging rule. The budget is `remainingCacheExtent +
slideOverreach * 2` (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:78`), 850 in this harness:
at scroll offset 0 a 600 px viewport with the 250 px default cache extent
(`viewport.dart:289`) yields `cacheOrigin == 0` and
`remainingCacheExtent == 850`: `viewport.dart:1795-1806` computes
`fullCacheExtent = 600 + 2 * 250` and, at `centerOffset == 0`,
`forwardDirectionRemainingCacheExtent = 1100 - 250`, which reach the sliver
sequence beside `cacheOrigin = clampDouble(0, -250, 0)` (`:1843-1844`) and are
passed to the first sliver unchanged (`:836`). `slideOverreach` is 0 with no
FLIP slide and no held preview (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2592`). That
budget is spent by `liveAccum < budgetCap` (`_layout_admission_policy.dart:86`),
and on the bulk arm Step 2's table charges `liveAccum` the row's FULL extent,
`getEstimatedExtentNid(nid)`, for every ITERATED row: the same charge the
non-bulk arm applies to an animating row (`:115-116`), added at `:123`. That
value is `_anim.fullExtentOfNid(nid) ?? defaultExtent`
(`tree_controller.dart:981-985`, `defaultExtent` 48.0 at `:831`), with no
animation value in it at all. Every
row here is 48 px, so `liveAccum` before row `i` is `48 * i` at EVERY `v`, and
`48 * i < 850` fails first at `i = 18`. The live-position conjunct beside it in
the same `&&` is slack throughout: `liveOffset(17) = 48 + 48 * 16 * v <= 816 <
850` for `v <= 1` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:342-343` over the cumulatives at
`:322-334`), which is Step 2a's part-2 argument holding here concretely. So
phase 1 admits `A` plus `a0..a16`, 18 rows, at `v = 0.93` and at `v = 0.34`
alike.

An earlier draft of this case charged members their ANIMATED extent `48 * v`
and concluded the admitted count grew to about `802 / (48 * v)` members, all 50

left to damage". That form is the live-POSITION bound

accumulator cap the sentence named, and Step 2 says the opposite twice: its
bulk `liveContribution` cell, and the "keeps the FULL charge in both views, so
the cap is still spent at the pre-animation rate in the live view" sentence
under "Why `effectiveCacheEnd` alone will NOT do".

hopped over for the whole collapse. Nothing about the case is timed. The 20 ms

and both setup-sanity assertions hold at any `v`: `buildCounts["a0"] > 0`
(index 1, `liveAccum` 48 at its decision, admitted at every `v`) and
`buildCounts["a30"] == 0` (index 31, inside the skipped span `[18, 50]`, never
created at any `v`).

`firstChangedIdx` is then 1: `A` at index 0 measures 48 against the 48 its slot

Both endpoints, with arithmetic, and its status stated honestly, because it is
not a pre-fix repro like case 1. TODAY it PASSES. `_admitBulkFastPath` breaks
on the full-space position `fullOffset(i) >= fullCacheEnd`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:458-459`), `48 * i >= 850` at `i = 18`, so
`cacheEndIndex` is 18 and `B` and `C` never enter the cache region on any frame
of the collapse, which is this block's Finding; but `:455-457` precede that
break, so `[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)` is exactly the fresh set and the
range-keyed skip at `:2331` materializes indices 18 to 52 correctly. AFTER
Steps 2 to 4 it also passes, for the reason it is being written: phase 1 cuts
at the same index 18, phase 2 admits 51 and 52, `cacheEndIndex` is 53, the
hopped-over `a17..a49` are unflagged, and the per-nid skip materializes exactly
them, so `scrollExtent` matches `48 + 96 * v + 48 * v * 49 + 96`. The
configuration that FAILS is M8's own intermediate, the hop landed with consumer
3 still keyed on the range: `[0, 53)` then covers the 33 hopped members, whose
slots still hold the 48 apiece the pre-collapse full walk wrote (`:2636-2642`)
against a true animated extent of `48 * v`, so the recompute overstates
`scrollExtent` by `33 * 48 * (1 - v)`, about 106 px at `v = 0.93` and about
1320 px at case 1's `v = 0.17`. In one sentence: a range-keyed freshness test
believes rows the hop never visited, and because the span persists at every `v`
there are always 33 of them to believe. Land it together with Step 4 and it
guards that decision permanently.

Cases 1 and 2 were re-derived under the same charging rule and stand unchanged.
Case 1's `B` is admitted by the POST view at any `v` (`postOffset` 48,

mounted count stays the 18 the `lessThan(50)` assertion allows.

**Sequencing dependency.** Chain 1 in the plan's Sequencing section is M6, then

M6 first, for three reasons, the last of which corrects a claim an earlier
draft of this paragraph made. (1) Shared method body. M6 rewrites

and adds a `BulkAnimationData<TKey> bulkData` parameter to its signature
(`:446-450`), while this block replaces the whole method and its call site

every-frame fall-off there, one step downstream. M6's `bulkData` parameter is

`BulkAdmissionView`'s snapshot field. (2) M6 adds
`debugBulkCumulativeRebuildCount`, which this block's setup sanity assertion

has to be written against M6's landed behaviour. (3) The correction: it is NOT
true that M6's fall-off keeps the bulk ADMISSION arm from being taken.
`_materializeBulkStaleExtents` clears `_bulkCumulativesValid` at `:2335`, but it
is only called from `:2845-2850`, AFTER the admission dispatch at `:2766-2772`;
and on the next frame Pass 1's `bulkOnly` branch re-validates at `:2615-2619`
and `_rebuildBulkCumulatives` sets the flag true again at `:337` BEFORE the
dispatch reads it. `bulkOnly` itself (`:2606`) is
`bulkData.isValid && !controller.hasOpGroupAnimations` and never consults the
cumulatives flag. So `_admitBulkFastPath` runs on every bulk-only frame with or
without M6, and what the fall-off actually costs is the O(N)
`_rebuildBulkCumulatives` walk plus `_materializeBulkStaleExtents` and
`_recomputeOffsetsFrom(firstChangedIdx)` (`:2853`) every frame, i.e. the
documented O(1) offset claim, not the admission arm. That still bears on this

cannot attribute the recompute to its own flip.

H2 is sequenced after M8 and must be WRITTEN against M8's final
shape, specifically Step 4's rule: any H2 text that treats
`[cacheStartIndex, cacheEndIndex)` as a membership or freshness answer will be

Step 3a is the second thing H2 has to be written against. M6's block already

Step 2a is the third thing, and it retires two H2 items rather than

(`:2406-2416`), and all eight call sites as one-word renames (`:2711`,
`:3206`, `:3252`, `:3259`, `:3347`, `:3437`, `:3761`, `:3762`). One placement
deviation: the counter is declared beside its subject, directly above

`test/sliver_tree/sibling_refresh_batching_test.dart` is the regression test,
landed via the promoted-repro flow this block prescribes: the counter landed
first inside the old `_siblingRefreshSet` body, and the pre-fix pins read
exactly the predicted 25, 20 and 1 (the first two red, the third green),
against 2, 1, 1 after the fix. Half (a) passed on both sides, as the block
predicts. All 13 assertions were individually shown red: seven by
constructing the rejected state test-side (collapsed parent, short setup, no
runBatch, undercounted inserts, a same-position move, a double insert), two
by the pre-fix run, and four under three temporary lib mutations (parent key
dropped from the copy site; a root token recorded for every dirty parent; the
`_batchDepth` gate removed so the deferral leaks out of runBatch), with the
mutation reverted and diff-verified byte-identical after each. The block's
Risk suites pass together (198 tests), the full suite reads 1088 passed, 4

**Finding.** `_siblingRefreshSet` allocates a `Set` and copies the whole
sibling list plus the parent on every call
(`tree_controller.dart:2281-2291`), and it is called from eight sites, all
sibling-list mutators: `insertRoot` `:2586`, `insert` `:3081`, `remove`
`:3127` and `:3134`, `reorderRoots` `:3222`, `reorderChildren` `:3312`,
`moveNode` `:3636-3637` (`grep -rn "_siblingRefreshSet" lib/` returns 9 lines:
the declaration at `:2281` plus exactly these eight call sites). Inside
`runBatch` each call's set is then unioned into `_batchAffectedStructuralKeys`
with an `addAll` (`tree_controller.dart:2300`), so K appends under a parent
with S siblings do `sum(S..S+K)` set adds twice. Measured (probe_m9.dart, Dart
VM): the notification bookkeeping alone costs 223 ms at N=2000, 883 ms at
N=4000 and 3823 ms at N=8000, against 0 ms for the deferred shape, and both
shapes produce an identical 16001-key union at N=8000.

**Root cause.** The set is materialized at MUTATION time even though inside a
batch it is not consumed until batch exit (`tree_controller.dart:2214-2245`).
Every intermediate set is built, unioned and discarded.

**Solution.** Defer materialization to batch exit by recording dirty parents,
which is the same deferral `_visibleOrderDirty` already applies to the O(N)
order rebuild (`tree_controller.dart:814-828`). Two new batch fields beside the
existing ones at `:793-812`:

```dart
/// Parents whose sibling list changed inside the current [runBatch].
/// The O(siblings) refresh set is built ONCE per distinct parent at
/// batch exit instead of once per mutation: K appends under one parent
/// go from O(K*S) set work to O(K + S). Same deferral discipline as
/// [_visibleOrderDirty]. Null when nothing recorded.
Set<TKey>? _batchDirtySiblingParents;

/// Root-list counterpart of [_batchDirtySiblingParents]. A separate bool
/// rather than a null entry in the set, because [TKey] is unbounded
/// (`class TreeController<TKey, TData>`, `:63`) and may itself be
/// nullable.
bool _batchDirtyRootSiblings = false;
```

Split the existing helper so the batch-exit path can write straight into the
union without an intermediate set, and so every call site stays a one-word
substitution:

```dart
/// Adds every key whose builder output can change when the sibling list
/// under [parentKey] (or the root list, when null) changes: every
/// sibling, plus the parent itself. See [_siblingRefreshSet] for the
/// rationale.
///
/// THE single O(siblings) copy site: [_siblingRefreshSet] is reduced to
/// `final out = <TKey>{}; _addSiblingRefreshInto(parentKey, out); return
/// out;` so both the unbatched path and the batch-exit drain pass through
/// here, and one counter covers both.
void _addSiblingRefreshInto(TKey? parentKey, Set<TKey> out) {
  assert(() {
    debugSiblingRefreshSetBuilds++;
    return true;
  }());
  if (parentKey != null) {
    out.add(parentKey);
  }
  out.addAll(parentKey == null ? _roots : (_childListOf(parentKey) ?? const []));
}

/// The refresh set for [parentKey] outside a batch; inside one, records a
/// TOKEN and returns the shared empty set, because the union is not
/// consumed until [runBatch] exit and the set can be built once per
/// distinct parent there. `Set<Never>` is assignable to `Set<TKey>` by
/// covariance and the literal is const-canonical, so the in-batch path
/// allocates nothing; the same idiom as the `const []` fallback at
/// `:2284`. The returned set is never mutated by any caller: the two
/// consumers both read it (`_notifyStructural`'s `addAll` at `:2300`,
/// `_fireStructuralListeners` at `:2304`).
Set<TKey> _siblingRefreshOrToken(TKey? parentKey) {
  if (_batchDepth > 0) {
    if (parentKey == null) {
      _batchDirtyRootSiblings = true;
    } else {
      (_batchDirtySiblingParents ??= <TKey>{}).add(parentKey);
    }
    return const <Never>{};
  }
  return _siblingRefreshSet(parentKey);
}
```

The oracle, declared beside the controller's existing debug counters
(`tree_controller.dart:686-701`):

```dart
/// Cumulative count of O(siblings) sibling-refresh set builds, i.e. calls
/// to [_addSiblingRefreshInto], which both [_siblingRefreshSet] and the
/// [runBatch] exit drain route through. Perf pin for this block's
/// contract: K mutations under ONE parent inside one batch must build the
/// refresh set once, not K times. Counts builds rather than keys, so the
/// budget is exact and independent of the sibling count. The increment is
/// assert-guarded (the `assert(() { ... return true; }())` shape
/// `render_sliver_tree.dart:3328-3332` uses), so a release build pays
/// nothing on a mutation hot path. Never reset internally; tests zero it
/// directly, the same convention as [debugIndexInParentIterationCount]
/// (`tree_controller.dart:1225-1232`).
int debugSiblingRefreshSetBuilds = 0;
```

All eight call sites become a rename: `_siblingRefreshSet(x)` ->
`_siblingRefreshOrToken(x)`. Nothing else at those sites changes -- the four
that pass the result straight to `_notifyStructural` (`:2586`, `:3081`,
`:3222`, `:3312`) keep doing so, and the four that fold it into an existing
`affected` local (`:3127`, `:3134`, `:3636`, `:3637`) keep doing that; inside a
batch their `addAll` of the empty set is a no-op and the token carries the
keys. `moveNode` calls it twice (`:3636-3637`), which is where the "one token
per distinct parent" dedupe pays. In `runBatch`'s exit block
(`tree_controller.dart:2220-2228`), after reading
`_batchAffectedStructuralUnknown`:

```dart
Set<TKey>? structuralAffected;
if (_batchAffectedStructuralUnknown) {
  structuralAffected = null; // poison pill already subsumes the tokens
} else {
  structuralAffected = _batchAffectedStructuralKeys;
  if (_batchDirtyRootSiblings || _batchDirtySiblingParents != null) {
    structuralAffected ??= <TKey>{};
    if (_batchDirtyRootSiblings) {
      _addSiblingRefreshInto(null, structuralAffected);
    }
    final parents = _batchDirtySiblingParents;
    if (parents != null) {
      for (final parent in parents) {
        _addSiblingRefreshInto(parent, structuralAffected);
      }
    }
  }
}
_batchDirtySiblingParents = null;
_batchDirtyRootSiblings = false;
```

Note the tokens are read AFTER `_ensureVisibleOrder()` at `:2219`, so the
sibling lists are the post-batch ones.

Contract check against CLAUDE.md's `affectedKeys` semantics. For a batch of
pure inserts the exit-time set is `{parent} + S_original + {n_1..n_K}`, which
is exactly the union of the per-call sets, and probe_m9.dart confirms the two
unions have the same 16001 members at N=8000. For a batch containing removals
the exit-time set is a strict SUBSET: keys removed later in the batch are
absent. That is correct under the contract ("exactly these rows may differ"):
a removed row has no row to refresh, and the element GCs it
(`_scheduleGarbageCollection` fires from `_onStructuralChange` at
`sliver_tree_element.dart:234`, and `_collectGarbage` evicts every mounted key
whose `getNodeData` is null, `:365-374`). It is also strictly better than
today, where an intermediate set can carry a key that a later in-batch mutation
removes. A parent removed later in the batch yields `_childListOf` == null
(`_node_store.dart:291-294` returns null for an unregistered key) and
contributes just its own dead key, which the element's mounted-row narrowing at
`sliver_tree_element.dart:245-249` then drops or the GC reaps; today's code can
already leave the same dead key in the union.

**Alternatives considered.**

- *Switch to `affectedKeys: null` above a threshold.* Rejected on
  architecture, not on cost. It works (`TreeNodeBuilder._onStructuralChange`
  re-reads its flags on null and `setState`s only on a real change,
  `tree_node_builder.dart:102-113`; the element does
  `_dirtyKeys.addAll(_children.keys)`, `sliver_tree_element.dart:237`, bounded
  by the cache region) but it breaks the budget contract that
  `rebuild_budget_test.dart:254-260` states as "the budget guarantee that
  matters: rows outside the mutated sibling list are untouched". The deferral
  achieves the same asymptotics with the contract intact. Worth keeping in the
  back pocket only if a single mutation OUTSIDE a batch ever needs it, which
  is inherent: an unbatched notification must carry its keys now.
- *A "sibling list of X changed" token in `affectedKeys` that the element
  expands.* Rejected: it widens the public `Set<TKey>?` channel into a tagged
  union that every one of the two in-repo subscribers
  (`sliver_tree_element.dart:125`, `tree_node_builder.dart:69`) and every
  external subscriber would have to learn. The deferral keeps the channel a
  plain key set and confines the change to the controller's batch bookkeeping.

**Architecture fit.** The controller already owns exactly this deferral
pattern for its other O(N) batch cost: `_visibleOrderDirty` defers the full
`_rebuildVisibleOrder` so that "K reparents in one batch then collapse to ONE
rebuild at outermost batch exit instead of K full DFS+post-order passes"
(`tree_controller.dart:816-818`). This is the same sentence with "sibling
refresh set" substituted. The `affectedKeys` contract, the element's
mounted-row narrowing (`sliver_tree_element.dart:245-249`) and the poison-pill
rule (`tree_controller.dart:2260-2262`) are all unchanged.

**Performance.** Before, inside a batch: O(K * S) set adds for the per-call
sets plus O(K * S) for the unions, plus K `Set` allocations. Measured 3823 ms
of pure set work for K = S = 8000 (probe_m9.dart); the review reports 13.9 s
end to end for that case and 5.1 s under a collapsed parent (their numbers, not
re-run). After: O(K) token adds into a set that holds at most one entry per
distinct parent, plus O(S_final) once at exit, and ONE set allocation (the
in-batch return is a const empty set, so the call sites allocate nothing).
Measured 0 ms at K = S = 8000. `TreeSyncController.syncChildren` appending N to
N inherits this, since it batches. Outside a batch nothing changes: the set is
still built per call, which is required because the notification fires
immediately.

**Risk.** The eight call sites are all in `tree_controller.dart` and all
in-package; `_siblingRefreshSet` has no callers outside it (`grep -rn
"_siblingRefreshSet" lib/`). Existing tests to re-run:
`test/sliver_tree/rebuild_budget_test.dart` (the insert/remove/reorder budget
assertions at `:204`, `:264`, `:313`, `:351`),
`test/sliver_tree/sibling_position_freshness_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/batch_notification_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/child_count_invalidation_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/insert_after_move_in_batch_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/tree_sync_controller_test.dart`,
`test/sliver_tree/live_index_oracle_fuzz_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/sibling_refresh_batching_test.dart`, two
halves. (a) Equivalence: roots `[p, other]`, `p` with children `c0..c9`,
expanded. Capture `addStructuralListener` sets. Run `controller.runBatch(() {
for (i in 0..4) controller.insert(parentKey: "p", node: n_i); })`. Assert
exactly one structural fire, and that its set equals `{p, c0..c9, n0..n4}` and
does NOT contain `other`.

Half (a) is NOT the repro: the contract check above argues that the exit-time
set equals the union of the per-call sets, so it passes before the fix as well.
It pins that the deferral did not change WHAT is notified, which is worth
pinning, and nothing more.

(b) The regression test, on `debugSiblingRefreshSetBuilds` rather than a
wall clock. A ratio test is not usable here: the pre-fix set cost is
`2 * K * S + K^2` adds, whose (4000, 4000) to (8000, 8000) ratio is exactly
4.0 (48e6 against 192e6), so an "under 4x" assertion sits on its own boundary
value and the measured 4.33x is constant-factor noise. Counter budgets are
exact. Same tree as (a). Three exact pins:

- Zero the counter, then run ONE batch containing 20 `insert`s under `p` and 5

- Same-parent dedupe: zero it, then run one batch of 10 `moveNode` calls that

- Unbatched behaviour is unchanged: zero it, do one `insert` outside any
  batch, assert `== 1`. An immediate notification must carry its keys now, so

Expected values before and after, stated exactly. After the fix: 2, 1, 1.
Before: 25, 20, 1, because every mutation site calls `_siblingRefreshSet`
itself (`:3081` for `insert`, `:3636-3637` for `moveNode`) and unions the

**Sequencing dependency.** Chain 2 in the plan's Sequencing section is M9, then
