harness shape: an 800 px viewport (flutter_test's default surface), the tree
wrapped in `SliverPadding(padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 100))`,
50 px rows, `indentWidth: 30`, the proxy enabled, and rows built as
`TreeDelayedDragHandle(child: SizedBox(key: ValueKey("row-$key"), height: 50,
child: Text(key)))`, which is the mount
`default_indent_pointer_mapping_test.dart:26-82` and
`drag_proxy_indent_handoff_test.dart:47-101` already use.

The tree is roots `[x, p, b]` with `p` expanded over a single child `c`, so the
visible order is `x(0) 0..50`, `p(1) 50..100`, `c(2) 100..150`, `b(3) 150..200`.
Row `b` is the discriminating shape the first version of this block lacked: a
depth-0 row whose PREVIOUS visible row is depth 1, i.e. a subtree LEFT boundary.
The `above` zone builds its candidate chain by walking down from that previous
row (`_drop_zone_resolver.dart:308-333`) and only then appends the target's own
level (`:334-340`), so hovering `b` yields TWO candidates, depth 1 (`parentKey:
"p"`, `rawIndex: 1`) and depth 0 (`parentKey: null`, `rawIndex: 2`), giving
`deepest == 1`, `shallowest == 0` (`:583-584`) and a hint clamp (`:585`) that
can actually move. A `below`-zone probe cannot serve here: that chain climbs to
ANCESTORS (`:464-499`) and a root has none, so on any depth-0 row its single
candidate is depth 0 and every hint clamps to it, which is exactly why case 3
below is written on `above`.

**Case A** (`TreeAnimationStyle.disabled`, so make-room installs are refused and
painted geometry stays structural for the whole gesture).

1. Setup sanity, not a pin: `tester.getRect(find.byKey(const ValueKey("row-x")))`
   is `left == 100`, `width == 600`. Rows lay out against
   `crossAxisExtent - indent` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2387-2394`) and
   `SliverPadding` hands its child `crossAxisExtent - crossAxisPadding`
   (`rendering/sliver_padding.dart:142`), so this establishes the band the two
   pins are measured against. Passes either way.
2. Long-press `x`, pump once so the overlay entry builds, and measure the proxy
   clone with the finder `drag_proxy_indent_handoff_test.dart:114-122`
   established, `find.ancestor(of: find.text("x").last, matching:
   find.byKey(const ValueKey("row-x")))` (`.last` is the overlay copy; the
   in-place row is hidden but still mounted). Assert `left == 100`,
   `width == 600`. FAILS today at `left == 0`, `width == 800`: the band is
   `Positioned(left: viewportGlobalLeft, width: viewport.size.width)` taken off
   the SCROLLABLE's box (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:1640`, `:1651`, `:1655`,
   `:1657`), which spans the whole viewport, padding included.
3. Same gesture, `moveTo(const Offset(105, 155))`, pump. `y = 155` is 5 px into
   row `b` (150..200), so `t == 0.1` and the zone is `above` (`:269-282`); the
   grab was at the row's centre, so `probeDy` is 0 and the probe is the raw
   pointer. Setup sanity: `currentTarget!.targetKey == "b"` and
   `currentTarget!.zone == TreeDropZone.above`, which prove the left-boundary
   chain was the code path reached. THE PIN: `currentTarget!.depth == 0` and
   `currentTarget!.parentKey == null`. FAILS today because `PointerSpace.sample`
   sets `sliverX: local.dx` off the scrollable (`_drag_session.dart:87-89`), so
   the hint is `(105 / 30).floor() == 3`, `:585` clamps it to 1, and the sort at
   `:586-594` puts the depth-1 candidate first, resolving `parentKey == "p"`,
   `depth == 1`. After the fix `sliverX` is `105 - 100 == 5`, the hint is 0, and
   the depth-0 candidate wins.

**Case B**, the release handoff. Style: `expandCollapse` and `makeRoom` zero,
`reorderSlide` and `dropSettle` 200 ms linear, the `_liveCommitStyle` shape at
`drag_proxy_indent_handoff_test.dart:147-152`. Zero `makeRoom` snaps the proxy
indent (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:504-506`) so the proxy's visual x is
deterministic; a live `reorderSlide` leaves the commit FLIP in flight.

Step 4 of the solution changes NO code, so a case that reads only the staged
baseline x cannot discriminate: `DropSettler.baselineOverrides` writes
`_proxyCrossOffset()` (`_drag_session_behaviors.dart:426-433`), which is
`_proxyIndent.value` (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:725-727`), the same number
before and after. What the fix moves is the FRAME the proxy paints that number
in, so this case measures the PROXY's rendered rect and converts it into the
sliver's cross space.

Lift `x` and `moveTo(const Offset(140, 155))`. Both worlds resolve the SAME
target here, deliberately, so that the proxy frame is the only variable: after
the fix `sliverX == 40` and the hint is `(40 / 30).floor() == 1`; before the fix
`sliverX == 140`, hint 4, which `:585` clamps to the same 1. Setup sanity:
`currentTarget!.depth == 1` and `currentTarget!.parentKey == "p"`, so
`_retargetProxyIndent` snapped `_proxyIndent` to `1 * 30 == 30`
(`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:496-506`). Then, still holding the pointer:

- `crossOrigin = tester.getTopLeft(find.byKey(const ValueKey("row-b"))).dx`,
  sanity-asserted `== 100.0`. `b` is a depth-0 row, so its painted left IS the
  sliver's cross origin, and it is readable on unfixed code, which is what keeps
  the test compilable before `crossAxisGlobalOrigin` exists.
- `proxyGlobalX`, the proxy clone's global left, via the case-2 finder.
- THE PIN: `expect(proxyGlobalX - crossOrigin, moreOrLessEquals(30.0))`. FAILS
  today at `0 + 30 - 100 == -70`.

Then `up()`, one `pump()`, and the continuity pin, which is the user-visible
symptom the block's Finding describes: `tester.getTopLeft(find.byKey(const
ValueKey("row-x"))).dx` must equal `proxyGlobalX`. The committed depth (1)
matches the indent the proxy tracked (30), so the FLIP's x delta is exactly 0
and the row paints at `parentData.indent + slideDeltaX == 30` sliver-local
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:4389-4412`), i.e. global 130, on every frame of the
glide: no tolerance, no timing dependence. FAILS today because the card sat at
global 30 while the row appears at global 130, the 100 px jump at release. (The
overlay entry is gone by this frame, `_onDragEnd` removing it, so the row key is
unique again.)

**Effort.** M.

### M19. `Opacity(1.0)` around every reorderable row

**Finding.** Every reorderable row is wrapped unconditionally in
`IgnorePointer(ignoring: hidden, child: Opacity(opacity: hidden ? 0.0 : 1.0, ...))`
(`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:1127-1130`, `hidden` computed at `:1032`).
`RenderOpacity.isRepaintBoundary => alwaysNeedsCompositing => child != null && _alpha > 0`
(`proxy_box.dart:884`, `:887`), so every VISIBLE row is a composited repaint
boundary with its own `OpacityLayer`, on top of the package's own
`RepaintBoundary` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:538-541`). Nothing in the wrap
touches focus, so a focused `TextField` in the dragged row keeps primary focus
while invisible.

**Root cause.** `Opacity` is being used as a visibility switch. Its render
object is a compositing boundary at alpha > 0 by construction
(`proxy_box.dart:884-887`), which is exactly the state 100% of rows are in
100% of the time, and `addRepaintBoundaries: false` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:539`)
therefore cannot remove the boundary it exists to remove. Focus exclusion was
never part of the wrap: `RenderOpacity` has no focus behavior, and there is no
`ExcludeFocus` anywhere in `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart` (grep: the only
`Opacity` hits are `:1129` and the proxy's `:1597`).

**Solution.** Replace both wrappers at `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:1127-1130`
with the framework's `Visibility`, configured to keep everything the current
wrap keeps:

```dart
content = Visibility(
  visible: !hidden,
  maintainSize: true,
  maintainState: true,
  maintainAnimation: true,
  child: content,
);
```

Why this is a drop-in and not a behavior change, item by item, against
`visibility.dart:265-290`:

- Layout: `maintainSize: true` routes through `_Visibility`
  (`visibility.dart:269-273`), whose render object is a plain
  `RenderProxyBox` (`visibility.dart:591-593`) that only skips `paint`
  (`:621-627`). Size is untouched, so `controller.setFullExtent(nodeId, child.size.height)`
  (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2400`) keeps measuring the real row height.
- Layers: `_RenderVisibility` overrides neither `alwaysNeedsCompositing` nor
  `isRepaintBoundary` (`visibility.dart:591-628` contains only `visible`,
  `maintainSemantics`, `visitChildrenForSemantics` and `paint`), so the
  per-row `OpacityLayer` disappears and `addRepaintBoundaries: false` becomes
  meaningful again. The file states this as the widget's whole purpose
  (`visibility.dart:566-571`).
- Pointer: `Visibility` emits the same `IgnorePointer(ignoring: !visible && !maintainInteractivity)`
  the package hand-rolls today (`visibility.dart:272`), so
  `hidden_row_hit_test.dart`'s "invisible content must not be tappable" pin
  (`test/sliver_tree/hidden_row_hit_test.dart:219-223`) is preserved by the
  same mechanism.
- Semantics: `maintainSemantics` defaults to false, so `_RenderVisibility.visitChildrenForSemantics`
  drops the hidden subtree (`visibility.dart:614-619`). That is EXACTLY what
  `RenderOpacity.visitChildrenForSemantics` already does at alpha 0
  (`proxy_box.dart:955-960`), so the semantics outcome is unchanged. The row's
  reorder `Semantics` stays OUTSIDE this wrapper (added at `:1166`, after
  `:1130`), which is what `hidden_row_hit_test.dart:229-243` pins.
- Focus: `Visibility` always emits `ExcludeFocus(excluding: !visible && !maintainFocusability)`
  (`visibility.dart:267`), which builds `Focus(canRequestFocus: false, skipTraversal: true, includeSemantics: false, descendantsAreFocusable: !excluding)`
  (`focus_scope.dart:947-955`). `FocusNode.descendantsAreFocusable=false`
  unfocuses a focused descendant (`focus_manager.dart:583-593`). That is the
  focus half of the finding, fixed for free.
- Shape stability: the widget SHAPE is identical in both states. `maintainSize`
  is a compile-time constant here, so the same chain
  (`_VisibilityScope > _Visibility > IgnorePointer > ExcludeFocus > content`,
  `visibility.dart:267-289`) is emitted whether hidden or not; only flags
  change. Element identity and every row `State` survive the hidden flip,
  which is the house convention this file already states twice, at
  `:1113-1114` ("`ignoring` tracks `hidden`, so the widget shape is stable
  across the drag") and at `:1158-1165` ("The WRAPPER is unconditional; only
  its payload varies ... re-inflating the whole row subtree and disposing the
  app's `State` under it").

The existing comment block at `:1088-1126` must be rewritten: its "Nesting is
load-bearing in both directions" (`:1099`) and "IgnorePointer, not Opacity
alone" (`:1107`) paragraphs describe wrappers that no longer exist. Keep the
two facts that still matter (the `Semantics` must stay outside the wrapper;
the drag surface may sit inside) and add why `Visibility` and not `Opacity`
(the compositing boundary) and not `Offstage` (below). One test comment goes
stale with them and must be updated in the same change:
`hidden_row_hit_test.dart:232-238` explains its ordering pin in terms of
`RenderOpacity.visitChildrenForSemantics`; the mechanism becomes
`_RenderVisibility.visitChildrenForSemantics` with `maintainSemantics: false`
(`visibility.dart:614-619`) and the pin itself is unchanged.

Eight test files introspect `Opacity` for the hidden-state probe (grep
`test/sliver_tree` for `byType(Opacity)|widget<Opacity>|widgetList<Opacity>`:
16 hits across exactly these 8 files):

| file | probe today | should assert instead |
|------|-------------|-----------------------|
| `can_reorder_flip_mid_drag_test.dart:28-39` | `_opacityOf` returns 1.0/0.0 | `tester.widget<Visibility>(ancestor of row).visible` |
| `drag_handle_hidden_test.dart:82-90` | `_effectiveOpacity` = min over ancestor `Opacity`s | `_isVisible`: every ancestor `Visibility.visible` true |
| `drag_subtree_hide_test.dart:99-108` | `_inPlaceOpacityOf` scoped under `CustomScrollView` | same finder, read `Visibility.visible`; KEEP the scoping, see the note below |
| `external_cancel_drag_test.dart:25-33` | `_opacityOf` | `Visibility.visible`; KEEP the proxy disabled, and rewrite the note at `:21-24`, see below |
| `reorder_controller_disposed_swap_test.dart:63-73` | `_rowOpacity(...).first` | `Visibility.visible` |
| `reorder_controller_swap_mid_drag_test.dart:95-105` | `_rowOpacity(...).first` | `Visibility.visible` |
| `reorder_enabled_toggle_test.dart:27-38` | `_opacityOf(...).first` | `Visibility.visible` |
| `sliver_reorderable_tree_widget_test.dart:85-93` | `_opacityOf` | `Visibility.visible` |

Mechanical migration: one helper per file, `double 1.0/0.0` becomes
`bool true/false`. No assertion SEMANTICS change.

**Correction to an earlier draft of this block (proxy stack).** An earlier
version of this block asserted that the drag proxy's descendant clones carry
the reorderable-row wrapper, citing `:1579-1587` and `:1560-1590`. That is
FALSE, and every conclusion drawn from it is withdrawn. `_DragProxy.nodeBuilder`
is wired at `:656-657` to `SliverReorderableTree.nodeBuilder`, the caller's RAW
builder, not to the `_ReorderableRow`-wrapping closure the sliver itself gets
at `:757-761`. The field's own doc says so: "a handle inside a clone finds no
[TreeRowDragScope] and is inert" (`:1530-1532`). The overlay therefore contains
NO row wrapper at all, neither `Opacity` today nor `Visibility` after the
change; the only `Opacity` the proxy emits is its own default 90% at `:1597`.
Two consequences for the table above:

- `drag_subtree_hide_test.dart` must KEEP its `CustomScrollView` scoping, but
  for the reason its own doc gives (`:96-98`), not the withdrawn one: the proxy
  mounts the dragged row's captured child (`:1550`, `:1560`) and rebuilds one
  clone per frozen descendant (`:1579-1586`), and both reproduce the row's
  `ValueKey("row-$k")`, so `find.byKey` is ambiguous mid-drag through
  DUPLICATED KEYS, independent of what type the wrapper is.
- `external_cancel_drag_test.dart` must KEEP `showDragProxy: false` for the
  same reason. Its note at `:21-24` states the ambiguity comes from the
  proxy's own `Opacity`, and that half stops being true once the wrapper is a
  `Visibility`; rewrite the note to name key duplication instead of deleting
  it. Deleting it would licence re-enabling the proxy in those mounts, and the
  finder would then be ambiguous again for a different reason.

**Sequencing dependency (chain 4, H5 with M19).** H5 ("A `GlobalKey` inside a
row breaks dragging") decides whether the row's captured widget instance may be
mounted twice: it replaces the in-place copies of the dragged subtree with
sized `SizedBox` placeholders whenever the proxy is enabled, so the row content
is inflated exactly once. That decision reaches into M19 in three places, and
M19 must not land first:
1. If H5 lands, the hidden row's payload is a `SizedBox`, so the wrapper is
   hiding nothing that paints and the layer argument (minus one composited
   layer per MOUNTED row) is the only remaining reason for M19. That reason
   survives intact, because it is about the 100% of rows that are VISIBLE.
2. H5's placeholder keeps the wrapper unconditional and byte-identical
   (`:1127-1130` is explicitly listed as untouched in H5's block), so the two
   changes compose; but H5 also notes the `Opacity(0)` "is now redundant over
   a `SizedBox` but stays" for shape stability, and that sentence has to be
   rewritten to name `Visibility` if M19 lands after it.
3. The two blocks name overlapping test sets (`drag_subtree_hide_test.dart`,
   `drag_handle_hidden_test.dart`, `external_cancel_drag_test.dart`,
   `can_reorder_flip_mid_drag_test.dart`, `reorder_controller_*_swap*`,
   `reorder_enabled_toggle_test.dart`,
   `sliver_reorderable_tree_widget_test.dart`). H5 BREAKS several of them (the
   in-place `ValueKey` stops existing mid-drag); M19 only rewrites their
   helper's return type. Migrating them twice is wasted work. Land H5 first,
   then port the surviving probes to `Visibility.visible`.
Decide them together; if H5 is dropped, M19 stands unchanged on its own.

**Alternatives considered.**
- `Offstage(offstage: hidden)`: rejected, it changes layout.
  `RenderOffstage.computeDryLayout` returns `constraints.smallest` and
  `performLayout` lays the child out without adopting its size
  (`proxy_box.dart:3903-3910`, `:3918-3925`), so the hidden row would measure
  0 and poison `setFullExtent` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2400`), the offset
  prefix sum, and the make-room lift. `Visibility(maintainSize: false, maintainState: true)`
  builds exactly that `Offstage` (`visibility.dart:278-282`), which is why
  `maintainSize: true` is not optional here.
- Opacity only when hidden (`hidden ? Opacity(0, child) : child`): removes the
  layer for visible rows but changes the widget SHAPE at the flip, so the row
  subtree is re-inflated and every row `State` is lost, which is exactly the
  hazard the file's own comment at `:1158-1165` records. It also still leaves
  the focus half unfixed.
- A package-private `_HiddenRow` `SingleChildRenderObjectWidget` over a
  paint-skipping `RenderProxyBox`: this is a byte-for-byte re-implementation
  of `visibility.dart:566-628` and would still need a hand-written
  `IgnorePointer` and `ExcludeFocus` beside it. Rejected on maintenance: no
  behavior the framework widget does not already provide, and it would need
  its own semantics test coverage.

**Architecture fit.** Widget layer only; `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart` already
owns row presentation and already emits `IgnorePointer` here. Reuses the house
convention stated in the code at `:1113-1114` and `:1158-1165` (flags track
`hidden`, the widget shape never changes across the drag) and in
`TreeDragHandle.build`. `ReorderRenderPort`, the render object and the
controller are untouched.

**Performance.** Per mounted row, before: one `RenderOpacity` that is a
compositing boundary plus one `OpacityLayer` in the layer tree, ALWAYS (alpha
1.0 rows included). After: one `_RenderVisibility` (`RenderProxyBox`, no
layer), one `_VisibilityScope` `InheritedWidget` element
(`visibility.dart:289`), and one `Focus` element, which itself carries a
`FocusNode` (`focus_scope.dart:552-553`, created lazily by `_createNode` at
`:592`) and emits one `_FocusInheritedScope` (`:731`; no `Semantics`, since
`includeSemantics` is false). Net: minus one composited layer per mounted row,
plus one `FocusNode` and two `InheritedWidget` elements per mounted row.
Mounted rows are bounded by the viewport plus cache region, not by tree size,
so the `FocusNode` count is tens, not thousands; the layer saving is the same
magnitude and lands on every frame of every paint. Layout cost unchanged (one
more proxy `performLayout` hop, no measurement change). No per-frame
allocations either way.

**Risk.** Reads of this path: `hidden_row_hit_test.dart` (pointer and
semantics contracts, does NOT introspect `Opacity`, expected to keep passing;
only its explanatory comment at `:232-238` goes stale) and the drag-proxy
stack builder (`:1550`, `:1560`, `:1579-1586`), which does NOT re-emit this
wrapper, see the correction above, so the overlay is unaffected by the change.
`repaint_boundary_test.dart` is RESOLVED, not deferred: it is provably
unaffected. Its harness builds a plain `SliverTree` with no
`SliverReorderableTree` anywhere (`:20-42`), the only finder is
`find.byType(RepaintBoundary)` (`:49-53`), and the word `Opacity` does not
occur in the file. Neither of its two cases can observe this change. Tests to
update: the eight named above. Also re-run `caller_placed_handle_test.dart`
and `drag_handle_audit_test.dart` (their comments at `:241` and `:455`
reference the old `Opacity(0)` reasoning but they do not introspect the
widget; update the wording) and `policy_flip_preserves_row_state_test.dart`
(row `State` preservation is exactly what the shape-stability argument rests
on).

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/reorder_row_layer_and_focus_test.dart`,
three cases:
1. `addRepaintBoundaries: false`, three reorderable rows, no drag: assert
   `find.descendant(of: find.byType(CustomScrollView), matching: find.byType(Opacity))`
   is `findsNothing`, and that no row-ancestor `RenderObject` between the row
   and the sliver reports `isRepaintBoundary == true`. Fails today (two
   `RenderOpacity` boundaries with `addRepaintBoundaries` both true and false,
   as the review measured).
2. Focus: a `TextField` in row "a", `focusNode.requestFocus()`, pump, assert
   `hasFocus` true (setup sanity), then start a drag on "a", pump, assert
   `focusNode.hasFocus == false`. Fails today.
3. Shape stability, mounted with `showDragProxy: false`. A `StatefulWidget` in
   the row records every `initState` into a list and publishes its `State`
   instance. Assert across drag start, drag move and drop that the recorded
   count for row "a" is exactly 1 AND that the `State` instance is `identical`
   to the one captured before the lift. Passes today and must keep passing (it
   is the guard against the "conditional wrapper" alternative, which
   re-inflates the subtree at the hidden flip and would report 2).
   `showDragProxy: false` is load-bearing and not incidental: under the
   default `showDragProxy: true` (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:122`) the
   proxy mounts the dragged row's CAPTURED child in the root overlay
   (`:1550`, `:1560`, reached because the early-out at `:635` does not fire),
   which inflates a second element for the same widget and fires a second
   `initState` at lift. That is H5's subject, not M19's, and counting it here
   would make the case fail for a reason M19 does not control. If the case is
   ever wanted under the default, scope the counter by having the row publish
   its `BuildContext` and record only inits whose context has a
   `CustomScrollView` ancestor.

**Effort.** M (one-line production change plus a comment rewrite, plus eight
mechanical test-helper migrations).

### M20. `animateScrollToKey` ignores the sticky band

**Finding.** The three target computations in the orchestrator
(`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:261-264`, `:377-380`, `:459-462`) are
`sliverBaseOffset + offset - (viewportExtent - rowExtent) * alignment` with no
sticky term; grep for "sticky" over `_scroll_orchestrator.dart` returns zero
hits. Meanwhile sticky headers pin at `stackTop`, starting at
`math.max(0.0, overlap)` (`_sticky_header_computer.dart:336`), with
`pinnedY = math.min(stackTop, pushUpY)` (`:444`) and `stackTop = pinnedY + extent`
per level (`:451`), and Pass B paints them over the rows
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:3719-3725`). At `alignment: 0.0` the target lands at
painted y 0, exactly under its own pinned ancestor.

**Root cause.** Layer split: `maxStickyDepth` is a widget/render property
(`sliver_tree_widget.dart:65`, `:93`, `:113`, `:124`;
`render_sliver_tree.dart:194-200`), while `animateScrollToKey` lives on the
controller (`tree_controller.dart:2000-2018`) and delegates to
`ScrollOrchestrator` (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:186`). The controller has no
route to `maxStickyDepth`: the only render back-channel is
`Set<TreeRenderHost> _renderHosts` (`tree_controller.dart:587`), and
`TreeRenderHost` is a bare function typedef
(`bool Function({required Duration duration, required Curve curve})`,
`tree_controller.dart:42-43`) that can carry only the baseline-staging call.

**Solution.** Two additive pieces plus one internal widening. No silent
behavior change: the default stays exactly what it is today.

1. Widen the render-host contract instead of adding a second back-channel.
   Replace the typedef at `tree_controller.dart:42-43` with an interface:

   ```dart
   abstract interface class TreeRenderHost {
     bool stageSlideBaseline({required Duration duration, required Curve curve});
     int get maxStickyDepth;
   }
   ```

   `RenderSliverTree` already has `maxStickyDepth` as a public getter
   (`render_sliver_tree.dart:195`), so it gains `TreeRenderHost` on its
   `implements` clause (`:84-85`, currently `implements ReorderRenderPort<TKey>`)
   and a `stageSlideBaseline` method carrying the body of the current
   `_hostCallback` closure (`:751-762`). Registration then passes `this`
   instead of the closure at `:132`, `:2184` and `:2189` (`:130` for the
   unregister on controller swap); the `late final` closure at `:751-762`
   goes away, and identity in the `Set` is the render object itself, which is
   what `attach`/`detach` symmetry wants anyway.
   `_stageSlideBaselineOnHosts` (`tree_controller.dart:670-680`) calls
   `host.stageSlideBaseline(...)` at `:677`. `TreeRenderHost` is not exported
   from the barrel (`sliver_tree.dart:23` exports only `TreeController` from
   that file) and has exactly one implementer and zero test implementers (grep
   over `test/`: only `animated_move_to_test.dart:385`, a comment), so this is
   a closed change.

2. Add to `TreeController`:

   ```dart
   /// Largest `maxStickyDepth` among attached render hosts, 0 when none
   /// pins headers. Config only: valid before the first layout.
   int get maxStickyDepthAcrossHosts { ... }   // O(hosts), hosts is 1 in practice
   ```

3. Compute the inset in the orchestrator, from controller data only. TWO
   shapes, ONE walk: a private core that selects its extent source, and a
   public settled-extent delegator. This is the decision the earlier draft
   left open, see "Decision: which extent source" below.

   ```dart
   // PRIVATE core. `animated` selects the extent source and never reaches
   // public API.
   double _stickyInsetCore(
     TKey key, {
     required bool animated,
     double Function(TKey key)? extentEstimator,
   }) {
     final limit = _controller.maxStickyDepthAcrossHosts;
     if (limit <= 0) return 0.0;
     double inset = 0.0;
     TKey? current = _controller.getParent(key);   // STRICT ancestors only
     while (current != null) {
       if (_controller.getDepth(current) < limit) {
         inset += animated
             ? _controller.getCurrentExtent(current)
             : extentOf(current, extentEstimator: extentEstimator);
       }
       current = _controller.getParent(current);
     }
     return inset;
   }

   /// Height of the sticky band that will sit above [key] after a scroll
   /// that brings it to the top. Settled (non-animated) extents, matching
   /// [scrollOffsetOf] and [extentOf].
   double stickyInsetOf(TKey key, {double Function(TKey key)? extentEstimator}) =>
       _stickyInsetCore(key, animated: false, extentEstimator: extentEstimator);
   ```

   No layout dependency: `maxStickyDepth` is widget config and `extentOf` is
   the same measured-or-estimated chain `scrollOffsetOf` already uses
   (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:161-166`; controller delegators at
   `tree_controller.dart:1939-1949`).

   **Decision: which extent source, and where the flag may appear.** The
   follower at `:377-380` must re-derive the inset per tick, because a
   concurrent expand is changing the ancestors' extents while the scroll runs.
   `extentOf` CANNOT serve it: it returns `getMeasuredExtent` first and falls
   back to the estimator only when that is null (`:161-166`), so an animating
   ancestor that has ever been laid out never reaches the estimator and the
   inset would be frozen at the settled height for the whole animation. The
   fix is the private `animated` flag above, not a second public entry point
   and not a parameter on `stickyInsetOf`.
   RULE for any future call site: pick `animated` by one question, does this
   same site read `getCurrentExtent` for the TARGET's own row extent? The
   follower does (`:375`), so it passes `animated: true`. The two one-shot
   sites read `extentOf` (`:260`, `:458`), so they pass `animated: false`.
   `animated` never appears in a public signature; a future public consumer
   that needs animated extents gets its own internal delegator, the way
   `animateDropSettleGlide` is an internal-use-only channel beside the public
   slide API (CLAUDE.md, "Declare an animation's family ONCE").
   Rejected here, with the reason each lost:
   - Put `animated` (or an `extentReader` callback) on the PUBLIC
     `stickyInsetOf`: publishes an internal timing concept on a surface whose
     documented meaning is "the band that will exist after the scroll
     settles", and invites callers to ask a question whose answer is only
     meaningful mid-animation. Same containment rule as above.
   - Make `extentOf` fall back to `getCurrentExtent`: it is documented as the
     best-known FULL (non-animated) extent (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:159-160`,
     `tree_controller.dart:1944-1947`) and `scrollOffsetOf`'s prefix sum is
     built on that meaning (`:150-155`). Changing it would make every settled
     offset query animation-dependent.
   - Have the follower pass an `extentEstimator` closure that returns animated
     extents: silently ineffective. `extentOf` prefers `getMeasuredExtent`
     (`:162-163`), so the closure is skipped on exactly the animating nodes
     that motivated it. This is the trap the audit caught; do not re-derive it.

   **Why the inset equals the band the scroll will produce.** Let
   `A_0 .. A_{k-1}` be [key]'s strict ancestors at depth < limit, root-first,
   and `inset = sum(extent(A_j))`. After the scroll,
   `scrollOffset = targetOffset - inset`. Induction over levels with
   `stackTop_d = sum_{j<d} extent(A_j)`:
   - The candidate at level `d` IS `A_d`. The probe sits at
     `scrollOffset + stackTop_d = targetOffset - sum_{j>=d} extent(A_j)`, and
     `targetOffset >= offset(A_d) + sum_{j>=d} extent(A_j)` because every one
     of those ancestor rows precedes the target inside `A_d`'s subtree.
     So the probe lands in `[offset(A_d), subtreeBottom(A_d))` and
     `_ancestorAtDepth` returns `A_d` (`_sticky_header_computer.dart:298-308`,
     called at `:345`); the parent-chain guard at `:348-350` passes.
   - `A_d` pins FLUSH. `subtreeBottom(A_d) >= targetOffset + rowExtent`
     because the target is inside its subtree, so
     `pushUpY_d = subtreeBottom(A_d) - scrollOffset - extent(A_d) >= inset + rowExtent - extent(A_d) = stackTop_d + rowExtent + sum_{j>d} extent(A_j) > stackTop_d`
     (`:443`). Hence `pinnedY_d = stackTop_d` (`:444`), the
     `pinnedY + extent <= stackTop` drop at `:446` cannot fire (extents are
     positive), and `stackTop_{d+1} = stackTop_d + extent(A_d)` (`:451`).
   The band therefore ends exactly at `inset`, which is where the target's top
   now sits. STRICT ancestors only, and that is not an approximation: a target
   whose own depth is inside the limit becomes the level-`D` candidate by the
   same argument and pins at `stackTop_D = inset`, i.e. precisely where
   alignment 0 plus the inset already placed it.
   An earlier draft justified this with "after an `alignment: 0.0` scroll the
   row at the probe IS the target". That is FALSE once the inset is applied:
   the probe at `stackTop_d` lands on a row that PRECEDES the target, and for
   a target that is not a first child that row can belong to an earlier
   sibling's subtree. The result survives because every probe still lands
   inside the correct ancestor's subtree, which is all `_ancestorAtDepth`
   needs.
   LIMITATION, stated on the parameter's doc: the walk predicts the tree's own
   band measured from the sliver's paint origin, while
   `_forEachStickyCandidate` starts the band at `math.max(0.0, overlap)`
   (`:336`). Under a preceding pinned sliver that overlaps the tree by `h`,
   the real band ends `h` px lower and the target is covered by `h`. The
   controller cannot read `constraints.overlap` before layout, and publishing
   it would recreate the layout dependency the second rejected alternative
   below rules out. Unverified against a running app: no test in
   `test/sliver_tree` mounts the tree under an overlapping pinned sliver (grep
   for `SliverAppBar|SliverPersistentHeader|pinned: true` over `test/` returns
   nothing).

4. Public API, additive, default preserves today's behavior. On
   `TreeController.animateScrollToKey` (`tree_controller.dart:2000-2018`) and
   its orchestrator twin (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:186-195`):

   ```dart
   bool avoidStickyHeaders = false,
   ```

   plus a public `TreeController.stickyInsetOf(key, {extentEstimator})`
   delegator, so callers composing their own scrolls (or combining with a
   pinned app bar via `sliverBaseOffset`) can read the same number. Target
   math at all THREE sites becomes:

   ```dart
   final inset = avoidStickyHeaders ? <the right inset call> : 0.0;
   final usable = viewportExtent - inset;
   final rawTarget = sliverBaseOffset + sliverOffset - inset - (usable - rowExtent) * alignment;
   ```

   with `<the right inset call>` = `stickyInsetOf(key, extentEstimator: extentEstimator)`
   at `:261-264` and `:459-462`, and `_stickyInsetCore(key, animated: true)`
   at `:377-380`, per the rule above.
   This is exact at both ends: at `alignment: 0` the row lands `inset` px below
   the viewport top (just under the band); at `alignment: 1` the expression
   collapses to `-(viewportExtent - rowExtent)`, i.e. bottom alignment is
   untouched, because the band does not cover the bottom.

5. Threading into the private concurrent path. `_animatedConcurrentScroll`
   (`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:283-292`) takes only `required` named
   parameters, so it gains `required bool avoidStickyHeaders,` beside
   `required double sliverBaseOffset,` (`:291`), and the single call site at
   `:219-228` forwards it (`avoidStickyHeaders: avoidStickyHeaders,` beside
   `sliverBaseOffset: sliverBaseOffset,` at `:227`). No default: the method is
   private with one caller, and a defaulted bool there would let a future
   caller silently opt out. The follower's per-tick inset then sits beside the
   existing correction loop, which already reads `getCurrentExtent` for the
   same reason (`correct` at `:363-368`, driven at `:371-373`), and the final
   snap at `:459-462` re-derives it from settled extents like the rest of that
   block (`:454-458`).

**Sequencing dependency (chain 5, H1 then H3 then M20).** All three edit the
same three target computations, `_scroll_orchestrator.dart:261-264`, `:377-380`
and `:459-462`. H1 changes what a scroll offset MEANS for never-measured rows,
which changes the `sliverOffset`/`currentOffset`/`finalOffset` operands this
block adds a term to; H3 changes WHEN the orchestrator may read the position,
which changes the guards around those same lines (H3's block already records
its side of this). M20's test asserts an exact painted top (48.0 for a 48 px
header), so it is unstable on top of an unfixed H1: an estimator/measurement
disagreement moves the same number the sticky inset is being blamed for.
Land H1, then H3, then M20, and rebase this block's three anchors on whatever
H1 and H3 leave behind rather than reusing the line numbers above.

**Alternatives considered.**
- A caller-supplied `topInset` alone: rejected. The caller cannot compute it,
  which is the finding: the pinned extent depends on which ancestors fall
  within `maxStickyDepth` and on their MEASURED heights, both of which live
  inside the package (`_sticky_header_computer.dart:339-345`, extents in the
  controller). Exposing `stickyInsetOf` gives the escape hatch without making
  the common case the caller's problem.
- Having the render object publish the measured band height (e.g. via
  `ReorderRenderPort` or a new callback): rejected. The band that matters is
  the one that will exist AFTER the scroll, not the one on screen now, so a
  measured value from the current layout is the wrong number and creates a
  layout dependency for an API that is called before layout. The render side
  only needs to publish the CONFIG scalar, which is what widening
  `TreeRenderHost` does without adding a back-channel.

**Architecture fit.** Render publishes config through the existing host
registry (`tree_controller.dart:587`, `:648-662`); the controller owns the
scroll API and the extent data and does the geometry, matching how
`scrollOffsetOf`/`extentOf` already work (`tree_controller.dart:1939-1949`).
`ScrollOrchestrator` keeps sole ownership of the four scroll methods
(`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:3-8`). No new registry, no new interface beyond
promoting a typedef that was already documented as internal
(`tree_controller.dart:40-41`).

**Performance.** The inset walk is O(depth of key), with `depth` typically
under 5, and its per-level read is an O(1) map lookup plus fallback in both
modes. Called once per plain scroll and once per animation tick in the
concurrent path (the tick already runs an O(A) correction loop at `:371-373`,
so this is strictly smaller). `maxStickyDepthAcrossHosts` is O(hosts), one in
practice. Zero allocations: `animated` is a bool parameter, not a closure, so
the per-tick path allocates nothing. `maxStickyDepth == 0` (the default)
short-circuits to 0.0 before any walk, so trees without sticky headers pay one
int compare.

**Risk.** The typedef-to-interface change touches
`render_sliver_tree.dart:130`, `:132`, `:751-762`, `:2184`, `:2189` and
`tree_controller.dart:42-43`, `:587`, `:648-662`, `:670-680`, `:4660`.
`render_host_registry_test.dart` verifies registry membership INDIRECTLY
through `moveNode(animate: true)` (its own header, `:1-6`), so it exercises
the new path without source changes; re-run it first. `animated_move_to_test.dart:385`
covers unregister-after-dispose. The behavior addition is opt-in, so the nine
`sticky_*_test.dart` / `scroll_orchestrator_*_test.dart` files should be
unaffected; unverified whether any of them asserts the default target math in
a way that a new named parameter would perturb (it should not, parameters are
named with defaults).

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/scroll_sticky_inset_test.dart`: six sections
of twenty children, 48 px rows, `maxStickyDepth: 1`.
- Setup sanity: `animateScrollToKey("r3c10", duration: Duration.zero)` (default
  `avoidStickyHeaders: false`) leaves the target painted at top 0.0 and
  `render.debugStickyHeaders` holding `r3` at `pinnedY 0.0, extent 48`
  (`StickyHeaderInfo` fields at `types.dart:499-507`), which is the defect and
  must keep reproducing under the default.
- The pin: the same call with `avoidStickyHeaders: true` paints the target at
  top 48.0 with the same sticky set. Fails before (lands at 0.0), passes after.
- `alignment: 1.0` with `avoidStickyHeaders: true` lands the row's bottom at
  the viewport bottom, identical to `avoidStickyHeaders: false` (the
  no-double-count guard).
- The animated-extent case, which is what the `animated` flag exists for:
  collapsed `r3`, `ancestorExpansion: AncestorExpansionMode.animated`,
  `expandCollapse` set to a long spec, `avoidStickyHeaders: true`. Pump to
  roughly half the expansion and assert the target's painted top is at the
  CURRENT band height, not the settled 48.0; then `pumpAndSettle` and assert
  48.0. A `stickyInsetOf`-based follower (settled extents) fails the mid-flight
  half.

**Effort.** M.

### M21. Same-parent relocation notifies only the moved key

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24, three audit passes, 2 and 3 consecutively
clean; pass 1 found two defects in newly written text, both fixed: the helper
doc and the rewritten test header claimed the set carries "every sibling plus
the parent", false as literally read for the roots case (a null parent adds
nothing), and the rewritten header bullet had re-typed the file's pre-existing
arrow and em-dash characters, now plain ASCII. Landed in the post-M9, post-M4
shape both sequencing notes prescribe: ONE line inside
`_relocateOrUpdateExistingSibling`,
`_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: _siblingRefreshOrToken(parentKey))`
(`tree_controller.dart:2808`), serving both `insertRoot` and `insert`;
`_siblingRefreshOrToken` now has nine call sites (measured; this block's
"nine and ten" collapsed into one when M4 folded the twin arms). The helper's
doc (`:2758-2770`) states the sibling-refresh-set payload, discharging this
block's "update those two comments" instruction (M4 had already collapsed the
two cited comments into that doc), and the stale `affectedKeys: {key}`
contract in `data_only_reinsert_notification_test.dart`'s header is
rewritten. That file's assertions are counts-only, exactly as this block
records, and all its tests pass unchanged.

`test/sliver_tree/insert_relocation_sibling_refresh_test.dart` is the
regression test: the block's three prescribed cases (roots set equality,
child mirror with the parent in the set, and the widget half pinning that
displaced rows re-render their index labels), plus a fourth case for the M9
interaction this block says must be known: batched relocations must join the
deferred token path, pinned as `debugSiblingRefreshSetBuilds == 1` for two
same-parent in-batch relocations. Pre-fix reds: the captured sets read `{c}`
and `{z}`, the displaced row kept its stale "a:0" label, and the counter read
0. All 18 assertions were individually shown red: eleven by test-side
constructions, four by the pre-fix run, and three more under four temporary
lib mutations (the index-arm relocation suppressed; the notify reverted to
the one-element set, reaching the stale-label and batch-set assertions; the
parent dropped from the copy site, additionally pinning the child case's
parent claim; the token path bypassed with a direct `_siblingRefreshSet`
call, additionally pinning the counter in the over-counting direction,
builds == 2), with the lib restored and diff-verified byte-identical after
each. The block's re-run list plus the M9 and M4 regressions and the oracle
fuzz pass together (35 tests), the full suite reads 1097 passed, 4 skipped
(the 1093 post-M4 baseline plus these four), `flutter analyze` stays at the
48-issue baseline, and the source-encoding guard is green.

**Finding.** The relocation branches of `insertRoot` and `insert` fire
`_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: <TKey>{node.key})`
(`tree_controller.dart:2536`, `:3010`) right after mutating the raw sibling
list (`:2525-2531` and `:2999-3005`: `removeAt` then `insert` then
`_liveIndexCache.bump()`). Every other sibling-list mutator uses
`_siblingRefreshSet` (`tree_controller.dart:2281-2291`), whose own doc at
`:2266-2280` states the rule these two sites break: "sibling mutations cannot
narrow their notification to the parent alone".

**Root cause.** Two literal one-element sets. The displaced siblings' rendered
inputs (`getIndexInParent`, first/last, sibling count) changed but no
notification names them, so mounted sibling rows are never added to the
element's dirty set (`sliver_tree_element.dart:245-249` narrows `affectedKeys`
to mounted rows).

**Solution.** At `tree_controller.dart:2536`:

```dart
_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: _siblingRefreshSet(null));
```

and at `tree_controller.dart:3010`:

```dart
_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: _siblingRefreshSet(parentKey));
```

Both calls already sit AFTER the `siblings.insert(...)` write (`:2529`,
`:3003`) and after `_liveIndexCache.bump()` (`:2531`, `:3005`), so the set is
built from the post-relocation list and includes `node.key`
(`_siblingRefreshSet` does `out.addAll(siblings)`, `:2289`). The "structural
subsumes data" contract is unaffected: still exactly one `_notifyStructural`
and no `_notifyNodeDataChanged` on this branch, which is what the comment at
`:2533-2535` / `:3007-3009` promises. Update those two comments to say the set
is the sibling refresh set, and update the header of
`data_only_reinsert_notification_test.dart:6` which currently documents
`affectedKeys: {key}` as the contract.

Interaction with M9, explicitly: this ADDS two more O(S) set builds to the
exact call sites M9 measures. M9's list, re-derived here from
`grep -rn "_siblingRefreshSet" lib/` (nine hits, one of which is the
declaration at `:2281`), is the eight call sites `tree_controller.dart:2586`,
`:3081`, `:3127`, `:3134`, `:3222`, `:3312`, `:3636` and `:3637`; `:2536` and
`:3010` join it, making ten. (An earlier draft of this block listed `:2594`,
`:3080`, `:3137`, `:3222`, `:3314`, `:3636-3637`, which disagreed with M9's own
block; `:2594` and `:3314` are blank lines, `:3080` is a comment and `:3137` a
closing brace. Use the eight above.)
Inside `runBatch` the union `addAll` at `:2300` repeats the O(S) work per call,
so K comparator-driven re-inserts under one parent with S siblings go from
O(K) notification work to O(K*S), the same shape M9 reports. These two lines
must therefore be landed as part of, or after, M9's batching redesign, and
whatever mechanism M9 chooses (record "the sibling list of X changed" and
materialize once at batch exit, or fall back to `affectedKeys: null` above a
threshold) must cover these two sites. Landing M21 alone is correct but makes
M9's measured 8000-into-8000 case worse; landing M9 first makes M21 free.

**Sequencing dependency (chain 2, M9 before M21).** Chain 2 in the plan's
Sequencing section is M9, then M21, and M9's block records the matching note.
The shared surface is `_siblingRefreshSet` (`tree_controller.dart:2281`) and
the eight call sites enumerated above. M9 renames every one of them to
`_siblingRefreshOrToken(...)`, which inside a `runBatch` records a per-parent
TOKEN and returns a shared empty set instead of building the O(S) set, and
moves the union assembly to `runBatch`'s exit block (`:2220-2228`, read after
`_ensureVisibleOrder()` at `:2219`), where one build per DISTINCT parent
replaces one per mutation. This block adds call sites nine and ten, at `:2536`
and `:3010`.

M9 first, because the two lines this block writes are either the post-M9 shape
or not. Written against the pre-M9 API they read `_siblingRefreshSet(null)` and
`_siblingRefreshSet(parentKey)`, and M9 then has to rewrite both, re-derive its
eight-site rename list (which its design states as an enumeration, not as a
grep run at implementation time), and re-verify that a relocation inside a
batch records a token rather than materializing a set. Landing this block first
is correct in behavior but not free: inside `runBatch` the union `addAll` at
`:2300` repeats the O(S) copy per call, so K comparator-driven re-inserts under
one parent with S siblings cost O(K*S) instead of O(K+S), which is the exact
shape M9 measures and, on its 8000-into-8000 case, the exact regression it
exists to remove. The other direction costs nothing: after M9 these two sites
are a one-word substitution to `_siblingRefreshOrToken`, and the batching
covers them automatically, M9's `debugSiblingRefreshSetBuilds` oracle included,
because that increment lives in `_addSiblingRefreshInto`, which both the
unbatched helper and the batch-exit drain route through. No new oracle is
needed for these two sites; what does need saying is that M9's budget for a
batch of K relocations under one parent must be written knowing they exist.

**Sequencing dependency (chain 13, M4 with M21).** M4 folds the two relocation
blocks this item edits into a single helper,
`_relocateOrUpdateExistingSibling(...)`: `insertRoot:2501-2544` becomes one
call and `insert:2975-3016` becomes another. The line M4's helper inherits from
those two blocks is exactly the `_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: <TKey>{node.key})`
this item replaces (`:2536` and `:3010`, the same two anchors named above). As
drafted, that helper takes only the RAW sibling list, the node
and the index, so it holds no parent key and cannot call `_siblingRefreshSet`,
whose whole signature is the parent (`tree_controller.dart:2281-2288`: null
means the root list, non-null adds the parent to the set). Consequences:
- Land M4 first and M21 becomes a ONE-LINE change inside the helper, with the
  helper taking an added `TKey? parentKey` (null at the `insertRoot` call site,
  `parentKey` at the `insert` one) purely so it can pass it through. M4's block
  carries the matching note and the parameter.
- Land M21 first and M4 must carry the corrected notification INTO the helper
  when it folds the blocks, or the fold silently reinstates this defect at both
  sites.
Either order works and neither is expensive; M4 first is cheaper, one edit
instead of two. Under either order the anchors above (`:2536`, `:3010`) and the
two comments at `:2533-2535` / `:3007-3009` collapse to one site: rebase on
whatever the helper leaves behind rather than reusing these line numbers. The
Test to add is unaffected either way, since it drives the public `insertRoot`
and `insert` surfaces and never names the internal shape.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Notify `null` (full refresh) from these two branches: rejected, it discards
  the targeting the whole channel exists for and would refresh every mounted
  row on an idempotent comparator re-insert.
- Compute a narrowed range (only siblings between the old and new index):
  rejected. `_siblingRefreshSet` is the single existing shape for this
  question and a second, subtly different one invites divergence; the parent
  itself must be in the set regardless (its child-list order changed), and the
  element narrows to mounted rows anyway (`sliver_tree_element.dart:245-249`).

**Architecture fit.** Controller layer, reusing the existing
`_siblingRefreshSet` helper and its documented rationale
(`tree_controller.dart:2266-2291`). Makes the two outliers match the eight
sibling-mutator call sites that already comply.

**Performance.** Before: O(1) set of one, two allocations per relocation
(`Set` plus its entry). After: O(S) build with S+1 hash insertions, one `Set`
allocation. Fires only on the relocation branch (`wantsRelocate == true`,
`:2524-2529` / `:2998-3003`), not on the data-only branch (`:2537-2542` /
`:3011-3016`). Per-frame cost unchanged; the element still rebuilds only
mounted rows.

**Risk.** Readers of this path: `addStructuralListener` consumers
(`sliver_tree_element.dart:245-249`, `TreeNodeBuilder`,
`_scroll_orchestrator`'s prefix invalidation). Existing tests that touch it:
`data_only_reinsert_notification_test.dart` asserts only listener COUNTS
(`(_) => structuralFires++` at `:96`, `expect(structuralFires, greaterThan(0))`
at `:53-57` and `:117`) and never inspects the set, so no assertion breaks;
only its header comment at `:6` goes stale.
`sibling_position_freshness_test.dart` is the closest behavioral neighbor and
should gain the new case rather than change. Also re-run
`batch_notification_test.dart` and `tree_node_builder_targeted_rebuild_test.dart`
(rebuild-count pins could tighten or loosen; unverified whether either
exercises the relocation branch).

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/insert_relocation_sibling_refresh_test.dart`:
roots `[a, b, c]`, a structural listener capturing the set. Setup sanity:
`controller.getIndexInParent("a") == 0` before. Then
`insertRoot(const TreeNode(key: "c", data: "C"), index: 0)`; assert the
captured `affectedKeys` equals `{a, b, c}` (today it is `{c}`), and a widget
half asserting that rows "a" and "b" re-render their index labels after the
call. Mirror case for `insert(parentKey: "p", node: c1, index: 0)` hitting
`:3010`, where the expected set additionally contains the parent `"p"`
(`_siblingRefreshSet` adds it at `:2286-2288`).

**Effort.** S.

### M22. `expand` Path 1 leaves the animating mirror stale

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23, six audit passes, 5 and 6 consecutively clean. The three lib edits were unchanged after landing; every later correction was to the test setup or to this paragraph. Three edits, exactly as the Solution prescribes: `_operation_group_registry.dart` gains a required `onMembershipVisibilityChanged` callback stored beside `_onTick` and `_onStatusChanged` and fired in `runWithGroupDetached`'s `finally`; `_animation_coordinator.dart` wires it as `onMembershipVisibilityChanged: bumpAnimGen` in the `opGroups` field initializer (`:149-163`), adjacent to the `bulk` one (`:165-176`) carrying the identical `onGroupDisposed: bumpBulkGen` precedent; and the now-redundant `_bumpAnimGen()` after collapse Path 1's detach was deleted from `tree_controller.dart`. The conditional bump inside `if (existingGroup.pendingRemoval.isNotEmpty)` was left alone, as the Solution directs, because it records a different fact.

`test/sliver_tree/expand_reversal_animating_mirror_test.dart` is the regression test. Verified by reverting exactly these three files to HEAD with H6 and M14 left in place: it fails on assertion 1 (`isAnimating("a1")`), after the setup sanity and the control both pass. Full suite 1076 passed, 4 skipped; the five Risk suites run green together (31 tests); `flutter analyze` unchanged at 48.

TWO DEVIATIONS from the block's Test-to-add, both deliberate. First, the CONTROL (`hasActiveAnimations`) is asserted BEFORE the two failing assertions rather than between them. The block lists it second but states its job is to prove the group is genuinely alive, and that only rules anything out if it runs before what it explains. Second, the test ends with `pumpAndSettle` plus a `hasActiveAnimations` false check. Without it the FIXED code fails teardown with `A Ticker was active at the end of the test` (`widget_tester.dart:1042-1059`), so the test could never go green; a fixed 400ms pump is genuinely not enough, verified. An earlier draft of this line justified it by saying the ticker check MASKS the real assertions on unfixed code. That is FALSE and was written without running it: `flutter_test` skips the end-of-test invariants when the body already failed (`binding.dart:1955-1958`), so on unfixed code the assertion failure is reported normally.

A THIRD correction, found in review and worth recording because it changed what the test actually exercises: as first written it reversed a collapse that had made ZERO progress. A ticker started outside a frame leaves `_startTime` null (`scheduler/ticker.dart:202-204`) and the first tick sets `_startTime ??= timeStamp` (`:276`), so a timed pump issued without a preceding bare pump advances the animation by nothing. The comment claimed the collapse was halfway; it was parked at the start, so the test was reversing a fresh expand rather than an in-flight collapse. The setup now pumps bare before each timed pump and ASSERTS the collapse is partway. The bound must be the row's own extent: `computeExtent` ignores its `fullExtent` argument whenever `targetExtent != -1.0` (`types.dart:251-257`), and an unmeasured row targets `TreeController.defaultExtent`, which is 48.0 (named, not cited by line: M23's later insert moved it from `:831` to `:873`), so a first attempt that passed 100.0 as the upper bound could not fail for the parked-at-start case this guard exists to catch. It is not unfailable in general: once the group is torn down `getAnimatedExtent` returns its `fullExtent` argument verbatim (`_animation_coordinator.dart:746`). Verified both directions: with the bound at the measured extent the assertion fails at 48.0 when the collapse's bare pump is removed, and the test still fails on assertion 1 against the three files at HEAD.

The block predicts assertions 1 and 3 both fail today, and BOTH DO. Only 1 fails in the test as written, because it aborts before 3 runs; 3 was checked separately by deleting 1 and re-running against the three files at HEAD, where it fails with `Expected: a value less than <3> / Actual: <3>` and passes once the fix is restored. Recorded because an earlier draft of this line claimed the block had OVERSTATED its prediction. It had not. That claim was written without running the check, which is the failure mode this plan's Verified claims rule exists to prevent, and it was aimed at the plan rather than at my own unverified assumption.

**Finding.** In expand Path 1 the only `_bumpAnimGen()` runs BEFORE the detach
window, and only conditionally (`tree_controller.dart:3765-3768`, inside
`if (existingGroup.pendingRemoval.isNotEmpty)`); `runWithGroupDetached` at
`:3779-3781` sets `group.controller.value = 0.0`, and nothing bumps afterwards
(`:3782` is `existingGroup.controller.forward()`, and the path ends at
`:3803-3805` with only `_structureGeneration++` and `_notifyStructural`).
Collapse Path 1 does bump after (`_anim.opGroups.runWithGroupDetached` at
`:3996-3998`, `_bumpAnimGen()` at `:3999`).

**Root cause.** `runWithGroupDetached` removes the group from `_groups`, runs
the body, and re-inserts it in a `finally`
(`_operation_group_registry.dart:207-218`). Assigning `controller.value`
notifies synchronously, the registry forwards ticks through
`onTick: notifyListeners` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:154`,
`_operation_group_registry.dart:173`), and a synchronous listener that reads
`currentlyAnimatingKeys` rebuilds the union mirror by iterating
`opGroups.groups` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:810`, the getter at
`_operation_group_registry.dart:133`), which does not contain the detached
group, then caches it against the CURRENT `_animationGeneration`
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:239`, written at `:850-851`). Nothing
invalidates that cache after reattach, so `isAnimating`
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:652`, `contains` on that cache) and
`computeFirstAnimatingVisibleIndex` (`tree_controller.dart:1450-1457`, which
keys its own cache on the same generation) stay wrong until the group
completes.

Precision the earlier draft lacked, and it decides the test's shape: the
listener dispatch is synchronous ONLY outside the transient-callbacks phase.
`AnimationCoordinator.notifyListeners` defers to a microtask when
`schedulerPhase == SchedulerPhase.transientCallbacks` and dispatches inline
otherwise (`_animation_coordinator.dart:298-313`). A user- or test-driven
`expand()` runs in the idle or post-frame phase, so the poisoning happens
synchronously inside the detach window; an `expand()` issued from an animation
callback defers past the window and does not poison. The test below must
therefore call `expand` from the test body, not from a ticker callback.

**Root cause, restated as the pattern.** The bump is a CALL-SITE obligation of
a primitive whose whole purpose is to make membership temporarily invisible.
One of the two call sites forgot it; a third will.

**Solution.** Move the obligation into the primitive, wired at the
construction boundary, using the pattern the file already uses for the bulk
animator. In `_animation_coordinator.dart:149-156`, add a callback to the
`OperationGroupRegistry` constructor exactly as `BulkAnimator` gets
`onGroupDisposed: bumpBulkGen` at `:158-169` (whose comment at `:163-168`
states the reasoning: "Wired at the construction boundary so no disposal path
can forget the pairing; the extra bumps ... are free, since bumpBulkGen only
increments counters"):

```dart
opGroups = OperationGroupRegistry<TKey>(
  ...
  onMembershipVisibilityChanged: bumpAnimGen,
);
```

In `_operation_group_registry.dart`, store it beside the existing injected
callbacks (`:32-48`) and call it in the `finally` of `runWithGroupDetached`
(`:213-217`):

```dart
void runWithGroupDetached(TKey opKey, void Function(OperationGroup<TKey> group) body) {
  final group = _groups.remove(opKey);
  if (group == null) return;
  try {
    body(group);
  } finally {
    _groups[opKey] = group;
    // The detach window hides this group from `groups`, so any mirror
    // rebuilt by a synchronous listener inside `body` is missing it and
    // was cached against the pre-detach generation. Invalidate here so
    // no caller can forget to.
    _onMembershipVisibilityChanged();
  }
}
```

Then delete the now-redundant `_bumpAnimGen()` at `tree_controller.dart:3999`
(collapse Path 1) and leave `:3767` alone: it guards a real membership change
(`pendingRemoval.clear()` at `:3766`) that happens before the detach window
and is a different fact.

Only the `finally` bump matters. A pre-detach bump cannot help: the poisoned
mirror is created DURING the window and cached at whatever generation is
current then, so only a post-window increment invalidates it.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Add `_bumpAnimGen()` after `:3781` at the call site and leave the primitive
  alone: rejected on architecture. It restores symmetry with collapse Path 1
  but leaves the same trap for the next caller, and this item exists precisely
  because the symmetric pair diverged once already. Single owner beats two
  disciplined call sites.
- Have `ensureAnimatingKeys` refuse to cache while any group is detached (a
  "detached depth" counter on the registry): rejected. It adds a second piece
  of state describing the same fact the generation counter already describes,
  and it would silently disable the cache if the counter ever leaked.

**Architecture fit.** The generation and the union mirrors are
`AnimationCoordinator`-owned (`_animation_coordinator.dart:236-252`,
`:216-230`); the registry gets a callback, not a reference, matching how it
already receives `onTick` and `onStatusChanged`
(`_operation_group_registry.dart:32-48`). The wiring site is the same
constructor block that already carries the identical precedent for
`BulkAnimator` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:158-169`).

**Performance.** One extra `int` increment per `runWithGroupDetached` call,
i.e. per Path-1 expand or collapse reversal, which is a user-driven event, not
a per-frame one. The invalidation cost is the next `ensureAnimatingKeys`
rebuild, which is O(members) with a sparse clear over
`_writtenAnimatingNids` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:225-230`, drained at
`:774-786`), and that rebuild was going to happen anyway because the reversal
genuinely changed what is animating. One closure allocation at coordinator
construction. Net cost of the fix on the collapse path is zero (one bump
moves, none is added).

**Risk.** Everything gated on `_animationGeneration`: `currentlyAnimatingKeys`
(`tree_controller.dart:1002`), `isAnimating`/`isAnimatingNid`
(`tree_controller.dart:1495`), `isExiting`,
`computeFirstAnimatingVisibleIndex` (`tree_controller.dart:1450-1457`) and the
render object's active-animation branch. Existing tests to re-run:
`op_group_iteration_snapshot_test.dart`, `independent_timelines_test.dart`,
`animation_transitions_test.dart`, `bulk_dispose_generation_test.dart`,
`animation_notify_coalescing_test.dart`. Perf pins that count generation
churn, if any, could move; unverified which of these assert exact counters.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/expand_reversal_animating_mirror_test.dart`:
`A > [a1, a2]` expanded, `expandCollapse: 300ms`. `collapse(key: "A")`, pump
100 ms (setup sanity: `controller.isAnimating("a1")` is true here, proving the
group exists and the reversal branch will be taken). Register
`controller.addAnimationListener(() { controller.currentlyAnimatingKeys; })`
(the scroll orchestrator's follower is exactly such a listener,
`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:330-389`, installed at `:391`). Call
`expand(key: "A")` FROM THE TEST BODY, so the dispatch is synchronous
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:299-312`). Assert immediately after it returns:
1. `controller.isAnimating("a1") == true`: FAILS today. The poisoned mirror
   omits the detached group's members, and `isAnimating` is a `contains` on
   that cache (`_animation_coordinator.dart:652`).
2. `controller.hasActiveAnimations == true`: PASSES today, kept as a CONTROL.
   It is `standalone.hasAny || opGroups.isNotEmpty || !bulk.isEmpty`
   (`_animation_coordinator.dart:922-923`), and `runWithGroupDetached` re-inserts
   the group in its `finally` (`_operation_group_registry.dart:216`) before

   job is to prove the group is genuinely alive, which is what makes assertion
   1's failure a MIRROR bug rather than a missing group.
3. `controller.computeFirstAnimatingVisibleIndex() < controller.visibleNodeCount`

   visible index and returns `_order.length`.
So: 1 and 3 fail today, 2 is the control. (An earlier draft claimed all three
fail.)

**Effort.** S.

### M23. Empty operation-group shells keep `hasActiveAnimations` true

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-23, nine audit passes, 8 and 9 consecutively clean. Both sub-fixes landed as prescribed. Sub-fix A adds `_abandonEmptyOperationGroup` beside the existing `_disposeOperationGroupIfEmpty` forwarder in `tree_controller.dart` and guards both Path-2 starts with it; the two `opGroups.install` call sites are the only two in `lib/` (measured), so coverage is complete. Sub-fix B adds the missing `_disposeOperationGroupIfEmpty` to `_purgeNodeData` (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:325-329`), making it the fourth of four op-group member-removal paths to ask the question: measured, `group.members.remove(` has exactly four op-group sites (`_animation_coordinator.dart:585`, `:629`, `_tree_controller_animation.dart:170`, `_tree_controller_helpers.dart:325`); the fifth hit, `_bulk_animator.dart:167`, is the bulk group and not in the set.

In this file, cite `opGroups.install` and the member loops by name, not by line.

The third was not prescribed: it collapses a parent whose descendant is NOT pending-deletion and asserts the group is still started and still consumes its `pendingRemoval`, which is what makes the emptiness condition load-bearing rather than decorative. Verified by neutering that condition: C stays visible past `pumpAndSettle` and `visibleNodeCount` reads 2 instead of 1. With both sub-fixes reverted, cases 1 and 2 fail while case 3 correctly passes.

Every one of the twelve assertions was individually shown to fail against a state it claims to reject, not merely shown to fail as a group. Two candidate assertions were DROPPED for failing that bar: `getNodeData("C")` and `visibleNodeCount` at the end of case 1 both still passed with the collapse commented out, because C's own exit purges it either way and P alone is then the whole tree. The perf pin needed restructuring to earn its wording: `tester.pump(d)` produces ONE frame however large `d` is, so the original single 300ms pump measured 1 layout and could not distinguish a one-off from a per-frame cost. **Finding.** `hasActiveAnimations` is
`standalone.hasAny || opGroups.isNotEmpty || !bulk.isEmpty`
(`_animation_coordinator.dart:922-923`), so a group with zero members and zero
`pendingRemoval` holds it true for its full duration. Two producers.
(a) Collapse Path 2 installs and `reverse()`s the group unconditionally
(`tree_controller.dart:4017-4022` install plus bump, `:4024-4036` member loop
that `continue`s on `_isPendingDeletion`, `:4039` reverse), and the entry guard
only rejects `descendants.isEmpty` (`:3943-3946`), not "every descendant is
pending-deletion"; expand Path 2 is the same shape (`:3812-3816` install plus
bump, `:3819-3827` counts that both come out 0, `:3900` forward).
(b) `_purgeNodeData` removes a member from its group without
`disposeIfEmpty` (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:320-331`), unlike
`AnimationCoordinator.removeFromAllSources` (`:613-636`, `disposeIfEmpty` at
`:627`), unlike `captureAndRemoveFromGroups` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:582`)
and unlike the preserve-entering branch
(`_tree_controller_animation.dart:166-176`, which calls the controller's
`_disposeOperationGroupIfEmpty` forwarder at `tree_controller.dart:510-511`
from `:172`).

**Root cause.** Group LIFETIME is not tied to group CONTENT. The registry's
`disposeIfEmpty` (`_operation_group_registry.dart:187-196`) exists exactly for
this and three of the four member-removal paths call it; the install paths
never ask the question at all.

**Solution, sub-fix A (install paths).** After each Path-2 member loop, if the
group ended up empty, dispose it instead of running it. Add one controller
helper next to the existing forwarder at `tree_controller.dart:510-511`:

```dart
/// True when [group] took no members: an empty shell would still hold
/// `hasActiveAnimations` true for a full duration (render cache off,
/// per-frame extent walk, eviction deferred, one forced layout per frame).
bool _abandonEmptyOperationGroup(TKey opKey, OperationGroup<TKey> group) {
  if (group.members.isNotEmpty || group.pendingRemoval.isNotEmpty) return false;
  _anim.opGroups.disposeIfEmpty(opKey);
  _bumpAnimGen();
  return true;
}
```

Collapse Path 2, at `tree_controller.dart:4038-4039`:

```dart
_structureGeneration++;                      // currently :4038
if (!_abandonEmptyOperationGroup(key, group)) {
  group.controller.reverse();                // currently :4039
}
```

Expand Path 2, at `:3899-3900` (`_structureGeneration++` then
`group.controller.forward()`): identical guard around the `forward()` call.
Nothing downstream is lost: `disposeIfEmpty` disposes the
`AnimationController` (`types.dart:293-295`) before it is ever started, so no
status event is owed, and the `dismissed`/`completed` handlers had nothing to
do for zero members. The standalone-ticker gates that follow (`:4041-4043` /
`:3904-3906`) are independent of the group and stay. `_structureGeneration++`
and the closing `_notifyStructural(affectedKeys: <TKey>{key})` (`:4044` /
`:3907`) stay where they are, so the expansion flag flip is still published.
(An earlier draft anchored `reverse()` at `:4038`, `forward()` at `:3898`, the
expand edit at `:3896-3898` and both notifies at `:4039` / `:3901-3904`; every
one of those was off. Use the numbers above.)

**Solution, sub-fix B (`_purgeNodeData`).** In
`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:320-331`, add the missing call so the block
matches `removeFromAllSources` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:621-628`):

```dart
final removedMember = group.members.remove(key) != null;   // :325
final removedPending = group.pendingRemoval.remove(key);   // :326
if (removedMember || removedPending) {
  _bumpAnimGen();                                          // :328
}
_disposeOperationGroupIfEmpty(opGroupKey, group);           // new
```

Ordering is safe: the following block (`:337-339`) handles the
`key`-IS-the-opKey case via `removeGroup`, which is a different slot and
tolerates an already-removed group (`_operation_group_registry.dart:228-230`
returns false).

**What is saved.** While the shell is up, every one of these is on, per frame,
for the shell's full duration:
- `SliverTreeElement._onAnimationTick` calls `renderObject.markNeedsLayout()`
  on every tick because `active` is true (`sliver_tree_element.dart:283-292`,
  the read at `:285` and the call at `:292`). The shell's `AnimationController`
  ticks through `controller.addListener(_onTick)`
  (`_operation_group_registry.dart:173`) and `onTick: notifyListeners`
  (`_animation_coordinator.dart:154`), so this is a FULL LAYOUT PASS PER FRAME
  for an animation with nothing in it: about 60 forced layouts for the
  review's 1000 ms case.
- Stale eviction is deferred at both gates
  (`sliver_tree_element.dart:463`, `:476`), so mounted rows accumulate for the
  whole duration.
- The `_findFirstVisibleIndex` cumulative scratch cannot cache
  (`canCache = !hasActiveAnimations`, `render_sliver_tree.dart:373`), so every
  call re-materializes an O(N) `Float64List`.
- Pass 1 takes the animated branch (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2601`) and the
  sticky precompute is invalidated every frame instead of being reused
  (`:2879-2887`), and `_sticky_header_computer.dart:407` takes its
  animating branch.
- `computeFirstAnimatingVisibleIndex` loses its O(1) early-out
  (`tree_controller.dart:1451`) and forces a mirror rebuild per call.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Make `hasActiveAnimations` ask `opGroups` whether any group has members
  rather than whether any group exists: rejected. It turns an O(1) `isNotEmpty`
  into an O(groups) scan on the hottest boolean in the render path
  (`render_sliver_tree.dart:373`, `:2601`, `sliver_tree_element.dart:285`), and
  it leaves the shell's `AnimationController` ticking and its `onTick`
  dispatching, so the per-frame notify storm survives. Fixing lifetime is
  strictly better than fixing the predicate.
- Pre-filter `descendants` / `nodesToShow` for pending-deletion before
  `install` and early-return: equivalent outcome but duplicates the
  `_isPendingDeletion` filter that the member loops already run (`:4025`,
  `:3822`, `:3839`, `:3852`, `:3871`), and would need the same guard added
  again at the next install site. The post-loop "did anything join?" check is
  one condition per path and cannot drift from the loop's own filter.

**Architecture fit.** Both sub-fixes use `OperationGroupRegistry.disposeIfEmpty`
(`_operation_group_registry.dart:187-196`) through the controller's existing
`_disposeOperationGroupIfEmpty` forwarder (`tree_controller.dart:510-511`),
making `_purgeNodeData` the fourth of four member-removal paths to comply
rather than the one outlier. Sub-fix A stays in the controller's
expand/collapse mutators, which already own group installation.

**Performance.** Cost of the fix: one `isNotEmpty` pair per Path-2
expand/collapse, one map lookup plus two `isEmpty` checks per `_purgeNodeData`
call. Saving, per empty shell, over its full duration at 60 fps: N forced
layouts (N = duration in frames), N deferred-eviction skips, N O(N)-row
scratch rebuilds and N sticky precompute invalidations, all reduced to zero.
For the review's measured case (1000 ms `expandCollapse`) that is roughly 60
whole-sliver layout passes removed. Allocations: none added.
