### M25. Scroll subscription bound to the `ScrollPosition` captured at `startDrag`

**Finding.** `startDrag` subscribes the session to the position captured at
that instant: `session.subscribeScroll(scrollable.position, _onScrollPositionChanged)`
(`tree_reorder_controller.dart:375`), stored on the session at
`_drag_session.dart:299-303` by `subscribeScroll` (`:311-320`) and detached in
`detachAll` (`:360-365`). `ScrollableState` replaces its `ScrollPosition`
whenever the physics `runtimeType` changes (`scrollable.dart:686-694`, the
comparison at `:690`, inside `_shouldUpdatePosition`, applied by
`_updatePosition` at `:617-636`), which the textbook
`physics: isDragging ? const NeverScrollableScrollPhysics() : ...` pattern does
on the first drag notification. After the swap the listener sits on the dead
position and no re-resolution ever fires. This is also the only
`scrollable.position` read outside `PointerSpace` (grep over
`tree_reorder_controller.dart`: one hit, `:375`), contradicting
`_drag_session.dart:6-11` ("[PointerSpace] is the ONLY component that touches
the scrollable").

**Root cause.** The subscription is a one-shot capture with no identity
re-validation. Note the coordinate half is already correct:
`PointerSpace.sample` reads `_scrollable.position.pixels` live
(`_drag_session.dart:79-97`, the read at `:91`), so only the notification path
is broken, which is why the target freezes rather than jumping.

An earlier draft of this block added a second clause: that "`ScrollableState`
publishes no swap notification" and "the only position handling is
`_updatePosition` at `:617`". That is WRONG and is withdrawn.
`ScrollableState.build` wraps its whole subtree in
`_ScrollableScope(scrollable: this, position: position, ...)`
(`scrollable.dart:1023-1025`; the class at `:538-548`), whose
`updateShouldNotify` is exactly `position != old.position` (`:544-547`, and
`ScrollPosition` does not override `==`, so it is identity). `ScrollableState.build`
always rebuilds that scope (its own comment, `:536-537`), so on a swap
`InheritedElement.updated` -> `notifyClients` -> `notifyDependent` ->
`dependent.didChangeDependencies()` runs SYNCHRONOUSLY during that build
(`framework.dart:6396-6400`, `:6414-6429`, `:6372-6374`). Every widget that
resolved the scrollable through `Scrollable.of`/`maybeOf` is such a dependent,
because `maybeOf` calls `originalContext.dependOnInheritedElement(element)`
(`scrollable.dart:387`), and dependencies registered outside `build` persist
(they are cleared only on `activate`, `framework.dart:4762`, and on unmount).
`SliverReorderableTree` already makes three such calls
(`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:1351` in the dragged row's `_startDrag`, `:424`,
`:660`). So a widget-level re-bind is available, and the block below adopts it.

**Solution.** Two mechanisms with ONE implementation, chosen deliberately
(alternatives (i) and (ii) alone are rejected under "Decision" below):

**(1) Ownership and re-validation live in `PointerSpace`.** In
`_drag_session.dart`, `PointerSpace` gains, reusing its existing nullable
`position` getter (`:68-74`) rather than re-implementing the `mounted` check:

```dart
VoidCallback? _scrollListener;
ScrollPosition? _subscribedPosition;

/// Subscribes [listener] to the scrollable's CURRENT position and keeps
/// the subscription glued to it. `ScrollableState` swaps its
/// `ScrollPosition` whenever the physics runtimeType changes
/// (`scrollable.dart:686-694`, applied at `:617-636`), so identity is
/// re-checked from [sample] and from [syncScrollSubscription].
void bindScroll(VoidCallback listener) {
  _scrollListener = listener;
  syncScrollSubscription();
}

/// Re-points the subscription at the live position when it has been
/// swapped. Idempotent, allocation-free, and a no-op in the steady state.
void syncScrollSubscription() {
  final listener = _scrollListener;
  if (listener == null) return;
  final live = position;                 // null when unmounted (:68-74)
  if (identical(live, _subscribedPosition)) return;
  _subscribedPosition?.removeListener(listener);
  _subscribedPosition = live;
  live?.addListener(listener);
}

void unbindScroll() {
  final listener = _scrollListener;
  if (listener != null) {
    _subscribedPosition?.removeListener(listener);
  }
  _scrollListener = null;
  _subscribedPosition = null;
}
```

and `sample()` (`_drag_session.dart:79-97`) begins with
`syncScrollSubscription();`.

`DragSession` keeps the single-entry / single-teardown shape: delete
`_subscribedPosition`, `_scrollListener` and `subscribeScroll`
(`_drag_session.dart:299-320`), replace with
`void bindScroll(VoidCallback listener) => pointerSpace.bindScroll(listener);`
and `void resyncScroll() => pointerSpace.syncScrollSubscription();`, and in
`detachAll` (`:358-370`) replace the manual remove-listener block (`:360-365`)
with `pointerSpace.unbindScroll();`.

`tree_reorder_controller.dart:375` becomes
`session.bindScroll(_onScrollPositionChanged);`, which removes the last direct
`scrollable.position` read from the controller (the remaining `scrollable`
uses are the parameter at `:274` and the `PointerSpace` construction at
`:298-301`).

**(2) A widget-level edge trigger, so no swap waits for a pointer event.**
`TreeReorderController` gains one public method:

```dart
/// Re-points the live drag session's scroll subscription at the
/// scrollable's current `ScrollPosition`.
///
/// `ScrollableState` swaps its position when the physics runtimeType
/// changes and publishes the swap through `_ScrollableScope`
/// (`scrollable.dart:544-547`, :1023-1025). Call this from
/// `didChangeDependencies` in any widget that resolved the scrollable
/// with `Scrollable.of`/`maybeOf`. Optional for correctness (the session
/// also re-validates on every pointer sample); it is what removes the
/// latency between the swap and the next pointer event.
void notifyScrollableChanged() => _session?.resyncScroll();
```

The call site is `_ReorderableRowState.didChangeDependencies`
(`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:886-918`), which already exists and already
carries an `_isDraggingThisRow`-guarded backstop for the controller-swap case
(`:907-910`). Add, after the existing block and before the cache refresh at
`:911`:

```dart
if (_isDraggingThisRow) {
  _reorder.notifyScrollableChanged();
}
```

The dependency this rides on is registered by `Scrollable.maybeOf(context)` in
`_startDrag` (`:1351`), through `dependOnInheritedElement`
(`scrollable.dart:387`). That coupling is currently incidental, so annotate
`:1351` to say the lookup is load-bearing for the swap notification and pin it
with the test's swap case, rather than leaving a future refactor free to cache
the `ScrollableState` and silently kill the trigger.

DELETE the `addPostFrameCallback` re-check an earlier draft put inside
`bindScroll`. It existed only to paper over the drag-start window, which
mechanism (2) now closes deterministically, in the same build phase as the
swap, without a per-session closure or a `SchedulerBinding` dependency.

Where re-validation actually runs, after both mechanisms: `sample()` is called
from `DragSession.resolve` (`:328`, one sample per event), from
`resolveTargetOnly` (`:343-348`, the commit script, sample at `:345`), from
`startDrag`'s liveness gate (`tree_reorder_controller.dart:302`), and from
`AutoScroller._onTick` (`_drag_session_behaviors.dart:112`) BEFORE it reads
`_space.position` (`:113`) and calls `jumpTo` (`:141`), so the autoscroll
ticker re-subscribes before it drives the new position. On top of that,
`notifyScrollableChanged` fires synchronously inside the frame that performs
the swap. There is no residual window left in the widget-driven configuration.

**Decision: which mechanism, and why not just one.** The auditor's three
candidates, judged on architecture (CLAUDE.md: `PointerSpace` is the only
component touching the scrollable) and per-event cost:
- (i) `sample()` re-validation ALONE. Rejected as the sole mechanism. It
  leaves a real, observable window: after the swap, any scroll that is not
  driven by our own autoscroll ticker (a wheel, a second finger, a
  programmatic `jumpTo`/`animateTo`, a keyboard scroll) moves content under a
  stationary pointer while our listener sits on the dead position, and the
  target stays stale until the next pointer event, with no bound on how long
  that is. Polling is not an option: the controller explicitly refuses it
  ("Edge-triggered, not polled: an idle drag with no movement and no
  scrolling costs nothing", `tree_reorder_controller.dart:413-414`).
- (ii) `didChangeDependencies` re-bind ALONE. Rejected as the sole mechanism.
  `TreeReorderController.startDrag` is public and takes an explicit
  `ScrollableState` (`:271-280`), so a caller can drive a session with no
  `SliverReorderableTree` above it and no `didChangeDependencies` anywhere;
  `drag_session_unit_test.dart` already constructs `PointerSpace`/`DragSession`
  headlessly. A mechanism that exists only in one widget cannot be the
  correctness floor for a controller-level contract.
- (iii) BOTH. ADOPTED. Division of labor, and this is the rule an implementer
  follows without further thought:
  `PointerSpace.syncScrollSubscription()` is the ONE implementation and the
  ONLY code that reads `_scrollable.position` for subscription purposes, which
  keeps the CLAUDE.md invariant intact. `sample()` calls it as the correctness
  floor (every path that resolves a target re-validates first, widget layer or
  not). The widget calls it through `notifyScrollableChanged()` as the latency
  floor. Neither the widget nor the controller ever touches a `ScrollPosition`:
  the widget supplies an EDGE, `PointerSpace` does the read.
Also rejected, on cost: making the dependency explicit by calling
`Scrollable.maybeOf(context)` inside `_ReorderableRowState.build`. That is one
inherited lookup per row per build, for every mounted row, to serve state that
exists only for the ONE row being dragged. The `_startDrag` lookup already
registers it; annotate it instead.

Cost per event: one `ScrollableState.mounted` read, one `position` getter, one
`identical`. On the common path (no swap) it returns before touching either
notifier. `sample()` already reads `_scrollable.position` at
`_drag_session.dart:91`, so the getter can be hoisted into one local and the
added work is a single identity compare. Cost per `didChangeDependencies` on a
dragging row: one null check plus the same identity compare.

What happens to state captured against the old position: nothing is
invalidated. `_updatePosition` builds the replacement with
`createScrollPosition(physics, this, oldPosition)` (`scrollable.dart:633`) and
`ScrollPosition.absorb` copies `minScrollExtent`/`maxScrollExtent`, `pixels`,
`viewportDimension` and the live activity from the old position
(`scroll_position.dart:322-345`), so `pixels` is continuous across the swap.
The drag's own captures are position-independent: `DragProbe.captureGrab`
stores `grabDy`/`grabRowExtent` in ROW-relative space
(`_drag_session.dart:125-133`), the FLIP commit baseline is staged against the
render object, and `DropSettler` reads the live position through
`PointerSpace` already. Detaching from a position that has since been disposed
is safe: `ChangeNotifier.removeListener` is explicitly documented to return
immediately on disposed instances (`change_notifier.dart:330`, `:339-344`).
Removing a listener during that notifier's own dispatch is likewise supported
by `ChangeNotifier`, which matters because `_onScrollPositionChanged`
(`tree_reorder_controller.dart:389-395`) runs inside `notifyListeners`.

**Alternatives considered.**
- Subscribe to `ScrollableState.widget.controller` instead of the position,
  since `ScrollController` survives the swap (`_effectiveScrollController.attach(position)`,
  `scrollable.dart:635`): rejected. `Scrollable.controller` is nullable (a
  `Scrollable` with no controller uses an internal fallback created in
  `initState`, `scrollable.dart:660-665`), the app can swap the controller
  itself (`_shouldUpdatePosition` also fires on `controller.runtimeType`
  change, `scrollable.dart:697`), and it would move the subscription off the
  object whose notifications actually define "content moved", trading one
  identity problem for another.
- Re-validate from `TreeReorderController.updateDrag` / `_resolveAndNotify`
  instead of `PointerSpace.sample`: rejected. It re-introduces scrollable
  knowledge into the controller, which is the second half of this finding, and
  it misses the autoscroll ticker, which does not go through `updateDrag`
  (`_drag_session_behaviors.dart:109-143`).

**Architecture fit.** Restores `PointerSpace` as the single component touching
the scrollable, which its own library doc asserts (`_drag_session.dart:6-11`,
`:275-278`), while `DragSession` keeps the one teardown site (`detachAll`,
`:358-370`) and the one choreography site (`resolve`, `:327-336`). The widget
hook adds no scrollable knowledge to the widget beyond the
`Scrollable.maybeOf` calls it already makes (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:424`,
`:660`, `:1351`), and it reuses the `didChangeDependencies` site that already
owns the row's mid-drag backstop (`:886-918`). No new component, no
`ReorderRenderPort` change.

**Performance.** Per pointer event and per autoscroll tick: one extra getter
read plus one `identical` compare, zero allocations, no branch taken in the
steady state. Per drag session: zero closures (the post-frame callback is gone).
Per `didChangeDependencies` on the dragged row: one null check plus one
identity compare; that method already runs on every inherited-scope change for
this row. Per actual swap: one `removeListener` (O(listeners) on the dead
notifier) plus one `addListener` (O(1)); swaps are user-triggered and rare.

**Risk.** Readers of this path: `DragSession.detachAll`
(`_drag_session.dart:358-370`, which currently owns the unsubscribe),
`AutoScroller._onTick`'s `jumpTo` notify contract
(`_drag_session_behaviors.dart:138-141`), and every consumer of
`_resolveAndNotify` (`tree_reorder_controller.dart:389-395`). The widget half
additionally touches `_ReorderableRowState.didChangeDependencies`, whose
existing controller-swap backstop is ordering-sensitive by its own comment
(`:894-906`, "the ordering is load-bearing because the helper reads
[_reorder]"): the new call must go AFTER that block and read the same
`_reorder`, never before it. Existing tests to re-run:
`scroll_reresolve_test.dart` (the direct owner of this behavior),
`drag_session_unit_test.dart` (constructs `PointerSpace`/`DragSession`
headlessly, so a constructor or method rename lands here first, and it is the
proof that mechanism (i) must exist),
`scroll_orchestrator_position_swap_test.dart` (the orchestrator's own,
independent position-swap handling at `_scroll_orchestrator.dart:293-299`),
`policy_flip_offscreen_autoscroll_test.dart`,
`reorder_controller_swap_mid_drag_test.dart`,
`reorder_controller_disposed_swap_test.dart`, `external_cancel_drag_test.dart`
and `tree_reorder_controller_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/drag_position_swap_test.dart`: 40 rows of
50 px in a 600 px viewport, harness state flipping
`physics: dragging ? const NeverScrollableScrollPhysics() : const ClampingScrollPhysics()`
from the reorder controller's own listener. Long-press r0, move the pointer to
y = 275 (mid-viewport, outside the autoscroll edge zone), pump. Setup sanity,
which is what makes the test honest: capture `scrollable.position` before the
drag and assert `identical(before, Scrollable.of(ctx).position) == false` after
the physics flip, and assert `reorder.currentTarget!.targetKey == "r5"`. Then
`controller.jumpTo(500)` and pump: expect `currentTarget!.targetKey == "r15"`;
then `jumpTo(1000)`: expect `"r25"`. Assert `targetKey`, `zone` and
`parentKey`, never `indexInFinalList` alone (it is 0 for every `into` target,
which is the false-negative the audit recorded). Today the target stays at
`"r5"` for both jumps. Two more cases pin the two mechanisms separately:
- Mechanism (2) alone, no pointer event between swap and scroll: exactly the
  `jumpTo` sequence above, which never calls `updateDrag`. It passes only if
  the widget-level re-bind fired, because nothing sampled in between.
- Mechanism (i) alone, headless: extend `drag_session_unit_test.dart` with a
  `DragSession` whose `PointerSpace` wraps a `ScrollableState` that swaps its
  position, then call `sample()` and assert the listener moved. This is the
  path with no widget layer at all.
Add the no-swap control (stable physics) in the same file so a future
regression cannot be blamed on the harness.

**Effort.** M.

### M26. Hot reload does not refresh rows when the `SliverTree` instance is hoisted

**Status.** NEWLY FILED 2026-08-22, during the implementation review of H6. It has NOT been through this plan's three-pass readiness audit, unlike the other 57 items, and the Solution below still carries an open decision. Treat it as a recorded finding, not as ready-to-implement.

**Finding.** After a hot reload that changes a `nodeBuilder` body, mounted rows keep rendering the OLD closure output whenever the ancestor hands `SliverTree` down as a hoisted child. Measured this session with a probe driving `buildOwner.reassemble(rootElement)` on a 20-root tree, 18 rows mounted:

- Hoisted ancestor (`build` returns `widget.child`): `identical(before, after) == true`, rows rebuilt on the reassemble frame = **0**.
- Ancestor constructing a fresh `CustomScrollView` + `SliverTree` each build: `identical(before, after) == false`, rows rebuilt = **18**.

The hoisted shape is not exotic. It is what `AnimatedBuilder`, `ValueListenableBuilder` and `AnimatedTheme` produce through their `child` pass-through, and it is the shape `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_h6_test.dart` itself relies on.

**Root cause.** `Element.reassemble` (`framework.dart:3754-3759`) calls `markNeedsBuild()` and recurses, so `SliverTreeElement` is dirty and `SliverTreeElement.reassemble` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:144-147`) sets `_didReassemble`. The only consumer of that flag is `update` (`:177-184`), which calls `_invalidateAllChildren()` (`:248`) and `markStructureChanged()`. But when the ancestor rebuild yields the IDENTICAL `SliverTree` instance, `Element.updateChild` short-circuits at `framework.dart:4014` (`if (hasSameSuperclass && child.widget == newWidget)`), so `update` never runs that frame. The element is still dirty, so the build phase reaches `performRebuild` (`:213`), which deliberately queues nothing. `_didReassemble` stays set until some later `update` that may never come, and because no key entered `_dirtyKeys`, `createChild` early-returns for every existing key (`:567-570`). Net effect: zero rows rebuild.

This is pre-existing, and H6 did not introduce it: before H6, `performRebuild` queued nothing either. H6 made it visible by forcing the two dirty causes to be enumerated.

**Solution.** Handle the reassemble cause at its own call site, per the RULE recorded in `performRebuild`. Two candidates, and the choice is the open decision this item still owes:

1. Queue in `reassemble`, mirroring `_onNodeDataChanged` (`:381-382`):

```dart
@override
void reassemble() {
  super.reassemble();
  _didReassemble = true;
  if (_children.isEmpty) {
    return;
  }
  _dirtyKeys.addAll(_children.keys);
  renderObject.markNeedsLayout();
}
```

   Cheap and phase-safe (it only writes a set and sets a flag), and it rebuilds each admitted row through `updateChild`. It is WEAKER than `_invalidateAllChildren`: rows are updated in place rather than deactivated and recreated, so a hot reload that changes a row widget's TYPE relies on `updateChild`'s own type check rather than on forced recreation.

2. Call `_invalidateAllChildren()` from `reassemble` directly, matching what `update` does. Strictly stronger, but it deactivates child elements, and `BuildOwner.reassemble` runs outside the build phase that `update` is called from. Whether deactivating there is legal must be verified against `BuildOwner.reassemble` and `Element.deactivateChild` before this option is chosen; I have NOT verified it, and that is precisely the open question.

Candidate 1 is the presumption because it is provably phase-safe and matches the existing producers; candidate 2 needs the phase check to be admissible at all.

**Alternatives considered.**

- Queue in `performRebuild` instead. This WOULD close the gap, because the element is dirty on the reassemble path (measured: the probe's zero is a consequence of `performRebuild` queueing nothing, not of it never running). Rejected on architecture, not on effect: `performRebuild` is a shared sink for both dirty causes, and routing reassemble through it re-creates the attribution ambiguity that H6 exists to remove. It would also re-queue redundantly on every dependency notification, which already queued in `didChangeDependencies`.
- Do nothing and document it. Rejected: hot reload silently showing stale rows is the single worst failure mode for a widget whose entire API surface is a builder callback, and the cost of candidate 1 is a set insert on a debug-only path.

**Architecture fit.** Element layer. Adds a fourth `_dirtyKeys` producer next to the existing four, at the call site that owns the cause, which is exactly the rule `performRebuild`'s comment states. No new state: `_didReassemble` already exists.

**Performance.** Debug and hot-reload only; `Element.reassemble` is not called in profile or release. Cost per reassemble is `O(|_children|)` set inserts plus one `markNeedsLayout`, measured at 18 mounted rows for a 20-root tree. Zero cost in every non-reassemble frame.

**Risk.** `reassemble` currently only sets a flag, so this is the first side effect it acquires. If candidate 2 is chosen instead, the deactivation phase-safety question above is the whole risk. Re-run the suites H6 names, since both touch the same refresh path: `test/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_widget_test.dart` (the four build-count regressions at `:535`, `:610`, `:685`, `:787`), `test/sliver_tree/controller_swap_test.dart`.

**Sequencing dependency.** Lands AFTER H6, and when it lands it must update the `performRebuild` comment in `sliver_tree_element.dart`, which currently records this gap as open and cites M26 by number. Leaving that comment stale would reintroduce exactly the kind of false claim L26 (g)2 exists to fix.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/audit_repro_m26_test.dart`. Drive `tester.binding.buildOwner!.reassemble(tester.binding.rootElement!)` followed by `await tester.pump()`. Note the harness constraint found this session: `tester.binding.reassembleApplication()` does NOT work here, it awaits a frame that the test never pumps and the run hangs until timeout. Two cases, both asserting `identical(before, after)` on the `SliverTree` instance so the hoist is proven load-bearing rather than assumed: (a) hoisted ancestor, assert rows rebuild, which fails on unfixed code with 0 rebuilds; (b) fresh-instance ancestor as the control, which passes today at 18 rebuilds and proves the harness sound.

**Effort.** S.

## Low

### L1. Skip order compaction when the removed batch held no visible slot

**Finding.** `_purgeAndRemoveFromOrder`'s pre-purge capture computes
`visibleCount` but discards it (`lib/sliver_tree/_tree_controller_helpers.dart:403-421`).
With every key hidden the batch is classified as not contiguous, and BOTH
conjuncts say so: the capture loop increments `keyCount` for every key in
`keysSet` (:405, :408) while `visibleCount` stays 0, so `visibleCount ==
keyCount` fails at :418 and `maxIdx >= 0` fails at :419. The point is not
which conjunct fires; it is that the Step 3 gate at :467 asks only
`compactOrder` and never asks whether there is anything to sweep. So Step 3
calls `_removeFromVisibleOrder(keysSet)` (:481-483), whose `allKeysPresent`
gate (:169) is also false, routing to `_order.purgeCompact` (:178): an O(N)
`removeWhereKeyIn` sweep (`lib/sliver_tree/_visible_order_buffer.dart:549-567`)
plus `rebuildIndex()` (:218-223) whose `resetIndexAll()` is an O(nidCapacity)
memset counted by `debugResetIndexAllCount` (:184-190).

**Root cause.** The classifier at
`lib/sliver_tree/_tree_controller_helpers.dart:417-420` answers exactly one
question, "are the visible slots a contiguous run", and Step 3 (:467) branches
on nothing else. "There are no visible slots" is therefore funnelled into the
branch that exists for "the visible slots are scattered", and only the second
of those needs a sweep.

**Solution.**
1. Hoist `visibleCount` out of the `if (compactOrder)` block: declare
   `int visibleCount = 0;` beside `minIdx`/`maxIdx`/`contiguous` at
   `_tree_controller_helpers.dart:400-402`, and assign it in the existing
   capture loop (:404-416) instead of declaring it locally at :404.
2. Change Step 3's gate at :467 from `if (compactOrder)` to
   `if (compactOrder && visibleCount > 0)`. Nothing else changes; both existing
   branches keep their bodies.

Zombie safety, verified: the only zombie source inside this call is Step 2's
`_purgeNodeData` (:459, body at :312-352), which clears the reverse-index slot
at :350 and releases the nid at :351 while leaving the `_orderNids` entry
behind. It can only strand an entry for a key that HELD a slot, and
`visibleCount == 0` says none did. Pre-existing zombies from an earlier call
are already assumed absent by this method: the contiguous branch at :468-476
removes only `[minIdx, maxIdx + 1)` and never sweeps. The two zombie-producing
callers both pass `compactOrder: false` and batch their own compaction
(`lib/sliver_tree/_tree_controller_animation.dart:321` then `:337`, and `:674`
whose `return true` feeds the caller's batch at :230 / :337).

**Alternatives considered.** Early-returning inside `_removeFromVisibleOrder`
on `visibleCount == 0` would also work, but that method is the batched
zombie-sweep entry point for the animation paths
(`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:151-168`), so the guard belongs at the capture
site that already knows the answer.

**Architecture fit.** Keeps `VisibleOrderBuffer` as the sole owner of the bulk
removal protocols and the capture block as the sole classifier of a batch.

**Performance.** Removes one O(N + nidCapacity) pass per removal of a node
that is hidden under a collapsed ancestor (`remove(animate: false)`, and the
animated arm's finalize). Costs one `int`.

**Risk.** `_removeNodesImmediate` (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:490-492`) is
the only `compactOrder: true` caller, reached only from
`TreeController.remove` (`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:3129`).
`test/sliver_tree/remove_contiguous_fast_path_test.dart:86-112` exercises the
MIXED shape (visible root "p" plus hidden children c0/c1, so
`visibleCount == 1`), which stays on the sweep; note it asserts the resulting
order, data and cache consistency (:108-110), NOT the reset counter, so it
constrains this change only through those. No existing test pins the
`visibleCount == 0` shape.

**Test to add.** A fourth case in
`test/sliver_tree/remove_contiguous_fast_path_test.dart`: 50 roots,
`setChildren("r10", [c0, c1])` with r10 collapsed, capture
`debugOrderResetIndexAllCount`, `remove(key: "c0", animate: false)`, assert the
counter is unchanged, `visibleNodes.length == 50`,
`getNodeData("c0") == null`, and `debugAssertVisibleSubtreeSizeConsistency()`.

**Effort.** S.

### L2. Delete the dead `remaining.insert` on the `syncChildren` path

**Finding.** `lib/sliver_tree/tree_sync_controller.dart:266-269` builds
`remaining`, :271-274 reads it once to seed `remainingBit`, and :319 then pays
an O(N) `remaining.insert(targetIndex, node.key)` per inserted key; the twin is
at :697. `grep -n "remaining" lib/sliver_tree/tree_sync_controller.dart` gives
16 hits, which split as: the LIST at 266, 271, 319 (roots) and 632, 637, 697
(children); the FENWICK `remainingBit` at 270, 273, 285, 320 and 636, 639, 650,
698; and one prose mention at :383 plus the doc reference at :513. So as of
`4d15c0c` neither function reads the list after its seeding loop, and only
`remainingBit` is read for positions (:285, :650). See "Sequencing dependency":
M12 changes that for the roots copy.

**Root cause.** The Fenwick tree replaced the list-scan index computation (its
rationale is the comment at :259-262 and :625-628) but the list mutation it
made redundant was left behind.

**Sequencing dependency.** M12 reintroduces reads of `remaining.length` and
`remaining[survivorIndex]` INSIDE the very insert loop this item empties, in
the `_syncRootsImpl` copy: that makes `tree_sync_controller.dart:319`
load-bearing again. So this item is NARROWED to the `_syncChildrenImpl` copy
and must land AFTER M12 (or in the same change as it), never before:

- Delete only `:697` (and fold `remaining` away only in `_syncChildrenImpl`,
  :632-640).
- LEAVE `:319` and the `_syncRootsImpl` `remaining` list (:266-269) exactly as
  they are; M12 owns them, and M12's block carries the matching note.
- If M12 is dropped, this item widens back to both copies; that is the only
  condition under which `:319` may be deleted.

**Solution.** Delete `tree_sync_controller.dart:697`. In `_syncChildrenImpl`
`remaining` then exists only to seed the Fenwick, so fold it away:

```dart
final remainingBit = _Fenwick(desiredKeys.length);
for (final k in currentKeys) {
  if (toRemove.contains(k)) {
    continue;
  }
  final p = desiredPos[k];
  if (p != null) {
    remainingBit.update(p, 1);
  }
}
```

Drop "the post-removal list plus" from the comment at :625-628 only; :259-262
keeps its wording because the roots copy keeps its list. Leave :510-513 alone
for the same reason: its "internal `remaining` tracker" justification for the
duplicate-key check still describes the roots path (the more precise reason,
worth adding rather than replacing, is that duplicates produce wrong Fenwick
offsets, which is true of both paths).

**Alternatives considered.** Deleting both copies now and letting M12 re-add
the list it needs: rejected, it churns the same six lines twice and leaves a
window where M12's own citations point at deleted code.

**Architecture fit.** Restores the O(K log N) insert loop the Fenwick comment
already claims for `_syncChildrenImpl`; the list mutation was the last
O(K * N) term in it. The roots path keeps its list for M12's survivor lookup.

**Performance.** Removes K list inserts of O(N) each per `syncChildren` /
`syncMultipleChildren` / recursive-walk parent (K new keys against N
retained), plus one list allocation and its copy per such call. `syncRoots`
is unchanged by this item.

**Risk.** Nothing reads the `remaining` LIST in `_syncChildrenImpl` (grep
above: 632 declares it, 637 seeds the Fenwick from it, 697 is the write being
deleted). Insert positioning is covered by
`test/sliver_tree/tree_sync_controller_test.dart` and
`test/sliver_tree/tree_sync_deep_tree_test.dart`; both must stay green
unchanged.

**Test to add.** None: cleanup with no observable behavior change.

**Effort.** S.

### L3. Route `setChildren` through the buffer's removal owners and flush first

**Finding.** `setChildren` reads `_order.indexOf` at
`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:2759` and `_order.indexOf(parentKey)` at
:2825 without calling `_ensureVisibleOrder()`, unlike `insert` (:2871) and
`remove` (:3101). It also hand-rolls both removal protocols: :2789-2790
(`_order.removeRange` plus `_updateIndicesAfterRemove`) and :2793-2794
(`_order.removeWhereKeyIn` plus `_rebuildVisibleIndex`), which
`lib/sliver_tree/_visible_order_buffer.dart:145-150` reserves for
`removeContiguousRange` (:514-524) and `purgeCompact` (:532-538).

**Root cause.** Two duplicated copies of protocols the buffer documents as
its own, in the one mutator that never learned the batch-deferral flush rule
(`tree_controller.dart:4562-4571`).

**Scope: this whole item is hygiene.** Step 1 is NOT a bug fix, and the
implementer should not go looking for a red test. Traced end to end: a stale
order inside a batch means `_visibleOrderDirty` was set by a prior mutator
(:4554-4560). `grep -n "_markVisibleOrderDirty()"` gives ten call sites:
`insertRoot` :2460/:2476/:2532, `insert` :2937/:2951/:3006, `reorderRoots`
:3216, `reorderChildren` :3308, `moveNode` :3571, and `expandAll` :4167 (which
flushes on its own two lines later at :4178, so it never leaves the flag set
past its own body). Whatever those leave behind, every order-derived decision
`setChildren` then makes is repaired at batch exit by `_order.rebuild(...)`,
which clears, re-derives the DFS order, calls `rebuildIndex()` and
`_rebuildSubtreeSizes()` (`_visible_order_buffer.dart:372-379`): a wrong
`removeRange` range, a skipped or misplaced `insertAllKeys`, a wrong
`bumpFromSelf` delta, all of it. Nor is there a RangeError analogue of the
crash `insert`'s comment describes (:2862-2870), because `insertIdx =
parentIdx + 1` and `minIdx`/`maxIdx` all come from the buffer's own reverse
index, which the four sites I read (`reorderRoots` :3210-3216, `reorderChildren`
:3290-3308, `moveNode` :3540-3571, `insertRoot`'s relocation branch
:2525-2532) leave untouched alongside the structural write. Unverified: I did
not read the other five bodies for that property, and it is worth a second
look if this item is ever upgraded from hygiene to a fix. The value of step 1
is that this whole paragraph stops being load-bearing.

**Solution.**
1. Add `_ensureVisibleOrder();` immediately after the `_hasKey` assert at
   `tree_controller.dart:2691` (before the pending-deletion throw at :2696).
   Do NOT copy `insert`'s rationale comment at :2862-2870 verbatim: it claims
   a RangeError this site cannot hit. Write the uniformity reason instead
   ("every mutator flushes on entry so no mutator has to reason about a stale
   order; nothing here is currently observable through the batch-exit
   rebuild").
2. Replace :2789-2790 with
   `_order.removeContiguousRange(minIdx, maxIdx + 1);` followed by
   `_assertIndexConsistency(fromIndex: minIdx);`. The extra reverse-index
   clears the method performs (`_visible_order_buffer.dart:516-521`) are
   harmless re-writes: `_purgeNodeData` already cleared each slot
   (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:350-351`) and no nid is re-adopted between
   the purge loop (`tree_controller.dart:2781-2783`) and this block, because
   `_adoptKey` for the new children runs later at :2808.
3. Replace :2793-2794 with `_order.purgeCompact(oldKeySet);` followed by
   `_assertIndexConsistency();`. `purgeCompact`'s leading `clearIndexOf` loop
   no-ops on released keys (`_visible_order_buffer.dart:153-159`).
4. Leave the contiguity test at :2787 as it is. Unlike
   `_removeFromVisibleOrder`'s `allKeysPresent` gate
   (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:169`), `visibleCount < allOldKeys.length` is
   the NORMAL shape here (collapsed descendants), and
   `maxIdx - minIdx + 1 == visibleCount` already proves the range holds exactly
   the visible old keys.
5. Leave the single bulk `bumpFromSelf(parentNid, -visibleCount)` at
   :2773-2778: that shortcut is the documented reason this site bypasses
   `_purgeAndRemoveFromOrder` (`_tree_controller_helpers.dart:358-363`).
6. With :2789 and :2793 rerouted, `VisibleOrderBuffer.removeRange` (:493-507)
   and `removeWhereKeyIn` (:549-567) each have exactly one caller left, both
   inside the buffer (:522 and :536). Rename them `_removeRange` and
   `_removeWhereKeyIn`, fold their docs into `removeContiguousRange` and
   `purgeCompact`, and retarget the two references to `removeWhereKeyIn`'s
   zombie protocol in `_tree_controller_helpers.dart:166` and :478-480 at
   `purgeCompact`. Grep confirms no `test/` file calls either directly (only
   comments in `purge_visible_subtree_size_test.dart:8`,
   `remove_contiguous_fast_path_test.dart:8`,
   `remove_from_order_zombie_leak_test.dart:23`).

**Alternatives considered.** Routing `setChildren` through
`_purgeAndRemoveFromOrder` entirely would lose the single bulk cache decrement
and re-introduce the per-key first-surviving-ancestor walk; rejected. Dropping
step 1 (since nothing observable changes) was weighed and rejected: the
`_ensureVisibleOrder()` addition costs one bool check on the common path and
one rebuild that a later mutator in the same batch would have paid anyway,
against an invariant ("mutators flush on entry") that is otherwise true of
every mutator but this one, and whose absence forces the Scope paragraph's
case analysis onto every future edit of `setChildren`. Uniformity wins.

**Architecture fit.** Restores "there is deliberately no raw per-slot index
write" (`_visible_order_buffer.dart:145-150`) and CLAUDE.md's "mutators flush
via `_ensureVisibleOrder` on entry".

**Performance.** Neutral. `removeContiguousRange` adds one pass over the
removed range writing slots that already hold `kNotVisible`.

**Risk.** `setChildren` is a public mutator and is also the sectioned module's
workhorse. Covered by `test/sliver_tree/set_children_no_op_test.dart`,

`_ensureVisibleOrder()` addition bumps `_structureGeneration` earlier inside a

### L4. Make the four key-existence guards throw in release too

**Finding.** `updateNode` (`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:3148`),
`insert` (:2861), `setChildren` (:2691) and `moveNode` (:3368-3372) validate
key existence with `assert` only. In release, `updateNode` on an unknown key
runs `_adoptKey` then `setData` (:3149-3150) and registers an orphan nid that
is in no child list, no `_roots` and no `_order`, so nothing will ever purge
it. `insert` with an unknown `parentKey` reaches
`_setParentKey(node.key, parentKey)` (:3023) after `_adoptKey(node.key)`
(:3021) and null-derefs `nids[parent]!` at
`lib/sliver_tree/_node_store.dart:278`, leaving the child registered. `insert`
of an EXISTING key under an unknown parent overwrites data at :2961 before
delegating to `moveNode` (:2972), which asserts only.

**Root cause.** The module already throws in all build modes for every
neighbouring failure class (`setChildren`'s pending-deletion `StateError` at
:2696-2702 and its `ArgumentError`s at :2706-2726; `moveNode`'s cycle and
pending-deletion `StateError`s at :3375-3409; `reorderRoots`'s `ArgumentError`
at :3190-3194), but not for "the key does not exist", which is the one that
leaves a registered zombie.

**Solution.** Replace each assert with a runtime `ArgumentError`, placed before
any adopt or data write. `ArgumentError` (not `StateError`) matches
`reorderChildren`'s unknown-parent policy: an unknown key is a bad argument,
while cycles and pending deletion are bad state.

- `setChildren` :2691:
  `if (!_hasKey(parentKey)) { throw ArgumentError.value(parentKey, "parentKey", "not found"); }`
- `insert` :2861: the same for `parentKey`, before `_ensureVisibleOrder()`.
- `moveNode` :3368-3372: the same for `key`, and for `newParentKey` when
  non-null, before the cycle walk at :3383-3393.
- `updateNode` :3148: the same for `node.key`, before `_adoptKey` at :3149.

Keep `remove()`'s silent no-op (`tree_controller.dart:3091-3093`): removing a
node that is not there is idempotent, not a programming error. Add a one-line
comment there so the asymmetry reads as deliberate. Document the new throws on
each method's doc comment, mirroring `moveNode`'s wording at :3353-3359.

**Alternatives considered.** Null-guarding `NodeStore.setParent` would silence
the crash but keep the registered zombie, which is half the damage; rejected.

**Architecture fit.** One policy for "unknown key" across the mutator surface,
matching the existing one for cycles and pending-deletion parents.

**Performance.** One map probe per call, on paths that already probe through
`_adoptKey` or `_depthOfKey`.

**Risk.** Any caller relying on a silent release no-op now throws. Callers
enumerated this session with
`grep -rn "\.setChildren(\|\.updateNode(\|\.moveNode(\|\.insert(" lib test examples/lib examples/test`.
Every `lib/` caller already proves existence before the call, but NOT all for
the same reason:

- `TreeSyncController.syncChildren` returns early on
  `_controller.getNodeData(parentKey) == null`
  (`lib/sliver_tree/tree_sync_controller.dart:502-504`) and is the ONLY caller
  of `_syncChildrenImpl` (:506), so the two `insert(parentKey:)` sites (:659,
  :682) and the `moveNode(node.key, parentKey, ...)` at :672 all run under a
  proven parent. `syncMultipleChildren` (:834) and `_syncChildrenRecursive`
  (:1113) reach the impl only through that same public guard, never directly.
- The four `updateNode` sites sit inside proven-existence branches: :306 and
  :671 under `getNodeData(node.key) != null` (:287, :652); :338 and :720 under
  `current != null` (:337, :719). The `moveNode(node.key, null, ...)` at :307
  passes a null parent, so only the `key` guard applies and :287 supplies it.
- `SectionedListController` does NOT route through `TreeSyncController` for
  these four. It calls the tree controller directly:
  `lib/sectioned_sliver_list/sectioned_list_controller.dart:331`
  (`setChildren`), :353 and :428 (`updateNode`), :406 (`insert`), :491
  (`moveNode`). It is still clean, for two reasons neither of which is the sync
  layer. `_requireSection` (:908-912) and `_requireItem` (:914-918) pre-check
  `_tree.getNodeData(...) == null` and reach `_throwMissing` (:920-924) before
  the mutator: :352 guards :353, :397 guards :406, :427 guards :428, :473 and
  :481 guard :491. And :331 needs no guard at all, because it runs in the same
  `runBatch` immediately after `_tree.insertRoot` (:314) created that very
  section key.
- `TreeReorderController` (`lib/sliver_tree/tree_reorder_controller.dart:718`)
  is the gesture-driven drag commit, the caller
  `tree_controller.dart:3357-3359` names by name. Treated on its merits below.

`getNodeData(k) != null` is STRICTER than the `_hasKey(k)` these guards stand
in for: `_hasKey` is `_store.has` (`tree_controller.dart:284`,
`lib/sliver_tree/_node_store.dart:219`, a bare `nids.contains`), while `dataOf`
(`_node_store.dart:226-229`) needs the same nid AND a non-null data slot. So
every guard listed above refuses at least as much as the new throw, and none of
them can leak an unknown key past it.

**The reorder path, on its merits.** L4's new `ArgumentError` cannot fire on a
drag commit that previously succeeded. `endDrag`
(`tree_reorder_controller.dart:481`) is synchronous and re-resolves before it
validates: `session.resolveTargetOnly()` (:495), then
`_canCommit(dragged, target.parentKey)` (:502), whose body (:650-665) refuses on
`treeController.getNodeData(key) == null` (:654) and, for a non-null parent,
requires `getNodeData(newParent) != null` (:661). Only then does :604-609 call
`_applyMove`, whose cross-parent branch is the `moveNode` at :718. Those are
exactly the two existence reads the new guard would perform, taken AFTER the
async gap rather than before it, which is what the doc note at
`tree_controller.dart:3357-3359` asks for. The one re-entrancy window is
`canReorder`, which runs inside `_canCommit` itself (:651) and is caught by the
`identical(_session, session)` check at :510-512; nothing between :502 and :718
calls back into app code. `moveTo` (`_canCommit` at :755, `_applyMove` at :782)
and the four semantics moves (`_moveBySiblingDelta` :819, `moveOut` :832,
`moveIntoPrevious` :851, all via `moveTo`) share that same `_canCommit`. So the
reorder path needs no change and this block prescribes none for it; recording
that is the point, since an unexamined gesture caller is what the doc note
warns about.

The two internal self-calls are covered too: `insert`'s delegation
(`tree_controller.dart:2972`) sits inside `if (_hasKey(node.key))` (:2959) and
passes the `parentKey` that insert's own new :2861 guard has already validated,
and `insertRoot`'s (:2498) passes a null parent.

`examples/` calls these four at `animated_reparent_example.dart:89` and `:140`,
`concurrent_ops_example.dart:257`, `:346` and `:454`,
`drag_and_drop_example.dart:76`, `:81`, `:85`, `:90` and `:124`, and
`macro_playground_example.dart:283`, `:541`, `:582`, `:626` and `:654`;
`examples/test/` calls none of them. Each derives its key from a live controller
read, a literal seeded in the same method, or a mounted row's own key, all
inside one synchronous handler (`_liveVisible()` at
`concurrent_ops_example.dart:329`; `rootKeys` at
`macro_playground_example.dart:537`, `:564` and `:644`; `_resolveTarget`'s
pool re-check at :497-510; `getParent` at `animated_reparent_example.dart:126`;
`setRoots` at `drag_and_drop_example.dart:71-75`; the nodeBuilder's `key` at
`:195-196`), so none can pass an unknown key. Worth knowing anyway: three of
them wrap `moveNode` in `on StateError` ONLY
(`concurrent_ops_example.dart:455`, `macro_playground_example.dart:595` and
`:664`), which would not catch an `ArgumentError`; a future example that caches
keys across a frame must widen that catch.

`test/` cannot be relying on the release no-op: `flutter test` runs with asserts
enabled, so all four guards already throw today for an unknown key, which is why
none of the 57 `insert(parentKey:)` sites across 23 files, nor the
`setChildren` / `moveNode` / `updateNode` sites, can be passing one. The only
tests this can reclassify are ones pinning `AssertionError` from these four, and
there are none:
`grep -rn "throwsAssertionError\|isAssertionError\|AssertionError" test/`
returns 23 lines in 7 files, all on other guards
(`sectioned_list_controller_test.dart:155-203` and
`controller_uniqueness_test.dart:131`/`:136` fire in the sectioned controller's
own `_throwMissing`; `move_into_pending_parent_test.dart:49` and
`audit_repro_f3_test.dart:71` are pending-deletion;
`animation_style_test.dart:164`/`:172` is a negative duration;
`axis_unsupported_test.dart:52` is the axis assert). One to re-run
deliberately: `visible_subtree_size_invariant_fuzz_test.dart:130` swallows
`on AssertionError` around a loop calling `insert` (:59), `moveNode` (:103) and
`setChildren` (:114). Its keys come from `debugAllKeys` (:46, :94; definition at
`tree_controller.dart:386-391`), which yields every registered nid's key, so
`_hasKey` holds for all of them and the new `ArgumentError` cannot reach that
handler; but the handler is now narrower than the guard it was written against.

**Test to add.** New `test/sliver_tree/mutator_unknown_key_guard_test.dart`:
each of the four throws `ArgumentError`; afterwards `getNodeData(<the new
key>) == null` (proving no zombie was registered) and
`debugAssertVisibleSubtreeSizeConsistency()` passes.

**Effort.** S.

### L5. `animateSlideFromOffsets` null-check on an unregistered key

**Finding.** The install branch calls `_setSlide(key, slide)` at
`lib/sliver_tree/_slide_animation_engine.dart:307`, and `_setSlide` (:596-601)
does `_nids[key]!`, which throws for a key the controller never registered; the
nid is only resolved defensively three lines later at :309-310.
`TreeController.animateSlideFromOffsets` (`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:1553-1570`)
is public and takes caller-supplied maps, so a key present in both maps but
unknown to the controller crashes.

**Root cause.** The install branch writes before resolving the nid, unlike
`_slideAt` (:590-594) and `_clearSlide` (:603-612), which both tolerate a null
nid and an out-of-range nid. `_setSlide` also indexes `_slideByNid[nid]`
without the bounds check its two siblings carry.

**Solution.**
1. Resolve once at the top of the per-entry loop, after the `prior == null`
   skip at `_slide_animation_engine.dart:277-278`:

```dart
final nid = _nids[key];
if (nid == null || nid >= _slideByNid.length) {
  continue;
}
```

2. Change `_setSlide(TKey key, SlideAnimation<TKey> slide)` (:596-601) to
   `_setSlideNid(int nid, SlideAnimation<TKey> slide)`, dropping its
   `_nids[key]!` line, and call it with the resolved nid at :307.
3. Delete the now-duplicate lookup at :309-310 and use `touched.add(nid)`.

`_clearSlide(key)` at :291 and :317 already tolerates the null nid, so it stays
as is. The disabled-mode branch (:207-251) iterates `_activeSlideNids` and
cannot see an unregistered key. Extend the doc at
`tree_controller.dart:1529-1534` ("a node only in one map is ignored") with
"and so is a key the controller does not know".

**Alternatives considered.** Throwing `ArgumentError` would match L4's policy,
but this API is fed by render-layer snapshots that legitimately race a purge
(the `nid < 0` skips at `lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart:3496-3500` and
:3625-3629 exist for exactly that), so skipping is the consistent choice.

**Architecture fit.** Matches the engine's existing tolerate-a-freed-nid
posture in `_slideAt` and `_clearSlide`.

**Performance.** One map probe moved earlier; the duplicate probe at :309 goes
away.

**Risk.** Internal callers are `lib/sliver_tree/_ghost_registry.dart:489` and
`lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart:1310`, both passing snapshot keys.
Install-path coverage: `test/sliver_tree/animation_style_flow_test.dart:321-345`,
`slide_distance_gate_test.dart`, `slide_engine_preserve_progress_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** Roots `[a, b]`; call
`animateSlideFromOffsets({"a": (y: 0, x: 0), "ghost": (y: 0, x: 0)}, {"a": (y: 50, x: 0), "ghost": (y: 50, x: 0)})`;
expect no throw, `getSlideDelta("a") != 0.0`, and `getSlideDelta("ghost") == 0.0`.

**Effort.** S.

### L6. `applyPaintTransform` has no branch for anchor-based exit ghosts

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24. Repro appended to `phantom_exit_reparent_test.dart`: pre-fix the transform reported the stale slot plus the composed delta (24.0) against the painted 72.0, differing by exactly the 48 px slot offset. The branch landed as printed, mirroring M10's FLIP-only Pass A.5 gate symbol for symbol (ghost and anchor `getFlipSlideDeltaNid` reads) and translating by the shared base plus the composed delta with no `yAdjust`; the hoisted cast sits beside the branch, before the edge-ghost section, an equivalent placement both ghost branches read. One compile fix: `typedNodeId != null` joins the guard so the key promotes into `ghostKey:`. The inventory recipe re-run returns 21 non-comment lines minus 3 declarations = eighteen reads, category (c) six, fifteen FLIP-only; the AGENTS.md bullet carries those figures. Sanity demos shown red individually (oracle emptiness past settle; distinguishability at t = 0.005, 0.24 against the 0.5 tolerance). `childMainAxisPosition` carries no ghost term and stays a recorded follow-up as the block states. Risk suites 19 green; full suite 1132 passed, 4 skipped; analyze at the 48-issue baseline.

**Finding.** Pass A.5 paints a phantom exit ghost at
`_exitGhostPaintedBaseScrollSpace(...)` plus the ghost's own slide delta
(`lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart:3531-3538`, painted at :3566 and
:3594-3603; base derivation at :1668-1711), while `applyPaintTransform`
(:4349-4417) branches only for sticky (:4358-4364), the animating y-adjust
(:4372-4377) and composer EDGE ghosts (:4402-4410), then translates from
`parentData.layoutOffset` (:4410) and `parentData.indent` (:4412). A row
sliding into a collapsed parent therefore reports its old slot to
`localToGlobal`, semantics and focus traversal for the slide's duration.

**Root cause.** `_phantomExitGhosts` is a second ghost model
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:3481`) that the transform never learned about; only
`_composer.ghosts` did. Records are built at exactly four sites, two per
exit-phantom loop: :1141-1146 (controller-staged, anchor ON screen, `clipped:
true`) and :1161-1162 (controller-staged, anchor off screen, `edge`) in the
first loop; :1235-1236 (render-side fallback, anchor on screen, `clipped`) and
:1246-1247 (fallback, `edge`) in the second. :1141-1146 is the one this item
is really about: reparent into a collapsed, ON-SCREEN parent is precisely the
anchor-based case, and it was missing from the earlier draft's list.

**Sequencing dependency.** M10 rewrites Pass A.5's liveness gate at
:3512-3521 to be FLIP-only (today both the ghost read at :3501 and the anchor
read at :3514 use the COMPOSED `getSlideDeltaNid`). This item therefore lands
AFTER M10 and mirrors WHATEVER gate M10 leaves, symbol for symbol, rather than
the composed form written below. Reason: CLAUDE.md's PAIR rule. The transform
gate decides "does this row report its ghost position", the paint gate at
:3516-3521 decides "does it paint there", and the Step 0a prune decides
"does the record survive"; a transform reading a different delta than the paint
it mirrors reintroduces the bug this item exists to close, in the opposite
direction (`localToGlobal` pointing at a ghost position nothing paints). If
M10 lands first, copy its condition. If for any reason this item lands first,
it MUST be revisited when M10 does, and M10's block carries that note.

For the record, all three phantom-exit-ghost gates read the SAME deltas today,
which is the property to preserve: the Pass A.5 paint gate (:3501, :3514), the
Step 0a prune criterion (`_pruneSettledPhantomExitGhosts`, ghost at :3871,
anchor at :3880-3882), and, after this item, the transform. Whatever M10 does,
the three must still agree afterwards.

This item also CREATES read locations, so it owns a DELTA of plus TWO in
category (c), EXIT-ghost LIFECYCLE, of the carve-out inventory M10 establishes
in CLAUDE.md. Two, not one, because mirroring M10's gate symbol for symbol
means reading `getFlipSlideDeltaNid` for the ghost AND for its anchor, the
same pair the prune criterion and the Pass A.5 gate read. Category (c), not
(a): (a) is edge-ghost lifecycle, and this site is an exit-ghost liveness
gate. If this item somehow lands BEFORE M10, it mirrors the composed gate
instead and contributes zero, then is revisited when M10 lands. Write no
absolute total here: M10 and L7 also change that inventory and the landing
order among the three is not fixed. Re-run M10's canonical recipe after this
change and write the number it returns.

**Sequencing dependency (L7).** Same file, same question, different ghost
model. L7 changes Pass A's edge-ghost skip at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:3417-3421` from the COMPOSED delta
(`getSlideDeltaNid`, read at :3402) to the FLIP-only one, so that skip and Pass
A.6's paint gate (:3658-3661) become exact complements. That is the
`_composer.ghosts` model, not the `_phantomExitGhosts` model this item is
about, so neither block touches the other's predicate and they can land in
either order. What they share is the METHOD this item opens up.
`applyPaintTransform` already carries an edge-ghost branch whose `useGhost`
predicate reads the same COMPOSED delta Pass A reads today (:4406-4407, with
`slideDelta` from `getSlideDeltaNid` at :4386-4388). Once L7 lands, a
FLIP-settled edge-ghost row carrying a held preview falls THROUGH Pass A's skip
and paints at structural plus composed via `_paintRow` (:3785-3790), while
`useGhost` stays true and the transform still substitutes `baseForEdge`
(:4408-4409); paint and transform then disagree by exactly
`baseForEdge - layoutOffset`, which is the defining offset of an edge ghost.
That is the same PAIR-rule failure this item exists to close, one branch higher
in the same method, and this item is the natural owner because it is already
rewriting that method. Traced, not tested: no existing test asserts
`localToGlobal` on a FLIP-settled edge ghost under a held preview. Land L7
first and this item reconciles :4406-4407 with whatever question Pass A's skip
ends up asking; land this item first and L7 carries the reconciliation. L7's
block records the same, and the two inventory deltas stay distinct: plus TWO in
category (c) here, plus ONE in category (a) there.

**Sequencing dependency (L24).** Same map, disjoint halves. L24 adds
`_computeA7Anchors`, a second new consumer of `_phantomExitGhosts`, keyed on
the ANCHOR where this item's branch is keyed on the GHOST, and its first
filter is `if (ghost.clipped) continue;`.
An `_ExitGhost` is edge-painted XOR clipped by construction (:65-69), so the
two blocks take opposite halves of one map: L24 keeps Pass A.7 only for the
EDGE records (:1161-1162), while the record this item targets is the CLIPPED
one with an on-screen anchor (:1141-1146). Neither changes the other's
predicate and there is no conflict in either order. The order-dependence is in

`_exitGhostPaintedBaseScrollSpace` reads the anchor's LAYOUT values (:1696-1698
for y, :1709 for x) and never its painted placement; but the four suites named
under Risk below are the same four L24 names, and a painted-rect assertion
written around a reparent-into-collapsed animation before L24 lands is
calibrated on anchor geometry L24 changes. Land L24 first and this item's test
is calibrated once; land this item first and re-run those four suites when L24
lands.

**Solution.** In `applyPaintTransform`, hoist the `typedNodeId` cast that
currently sits at :4402 to just after the sticky branch, then add before the
edge-ghost `base` resolution:

```dart
final exitGhost = (_phantomExitGhosts == null || typedNodeId == null)
    ? null
    : _phantomExitGhosts![typedNodeId];
```

When `exitGhost != null` and Pass A.5's liveness gate holds, resolve the base.
The gate to mirror is the one at :3512-3521, read at implementation time, NOT
the form quoted here: today that is `slideDelta != 0.0 || slideDeltaX != 0.0 ||
anchorSlide != 0.0` with all three read through the COMPOSED
`getSlideDeltaNid` (ghost at :3501, anchor at :3514 via
`controller.nidOf(exitGhost.anchor)`), and M10 is expected to make the two Y
reads FLIP-only. Take whichever is in the file, with the same reads:

```dart
final ghostBase = _exitGhostPaintedBaseScrollSpace(
  ghostKey: typedNodeId,
  ghost: exitGhost,
);
```

and, when it is non-null, translate by
`(ghostBase.x + slideDeltaX, ghostBase.y - scrollOffset + slideDelta)` with NO
`yAdjust`, matching :3537-3538 and :3566. Note the x term: Pass A.5 uses
`base.x`, not `parentData.indent`. Fall through to the existing code when the
gate fails or the base is null, so a settled ghost reports its structural slot,

Verified and deliberately out of scope: `childMainAxisPosition`
(:4428-4436) carries no slide, edge-ghost or exit-ghost term at all. Record it
as a separate follow-up rather than widening this item.

**Alternatives considered.** None: the transform must mirror paint or
`localToGlobal` lies, and the painted base is already factored into one helper
for exactly this reason (:1651-1655).

**Architecture fit.** Reuses `_exitGhostPaintedBaseScrollSpace`, the documented
single source of truth for the exit-ghost painted base, so the transform cannot
drift from paint.

**Performance.** One null check plus one map probe per
`applyPaintTransform` call, and only when `_phantomExitGhosts` is non-null
(guard first, as Pass A.5 at :3485 and Pass A.7 at :3689-3691 do).

**Risk.** `applyPaintTransform` feeds `localToGlobal`, semantics, focus

`test/sliver_tree/phantom_exit_reparent_test.dart`,
`adjacent_collapsed_exit_ghost_test.dart`,
`offscreen_anchor_exit_ghost_test.dart`, `tall_card_occlusion_zorder_test.dart`.
