**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24. New `ghost_flip_only_pass_a_skip_test.dart` builds exactly the block's geometry (leading-edge ghost from the n12 move, the 3 s n55 FLIP keeping frames paint-only, n20's 200 px held lift); pre-fix red at the main assert with the n17 control advancing, pinning the row painted by neither pass on a paint-only frame. The skip landed as printed; the break comment gained the composed-overreach clause; and, L6 having landed first, this block carried the recorded reconciliation: `applyPaintTransform`'s edge-ghost `useGhost` gate is now FLIP-only with the same PAIR rationale. Inventory recipe re-run at landing: 23 non-comment lines minus 3 declarations = twenty reads, category (a) eight, seventeen FLIP-only; the AGENTS.md bullet carries those figures (the block's recipe-tightening note is satisfied by the recipe wording M10 landed). Twelve demo states shown red individually; the control's reject-state is a skipped frame, because a pumped no-op frame still paints under this harness (measured). Risk suites 18 green; full suite 1133 passed, 4 skipped; analyze at the 48-issue baseline.

**Finding.** Pass A skips a row that has a registry ghost entry when the
COMPOSED delta is non-zero (`lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart:3417-3421`,
`slideDelta` from `controller.getSlideDeltaNid` at :3402), while Pass A.6
declines to paint it when the FLIP-only delta is zero (:3658-3661). With a held
make-room preview on a FLIP-settled ghost, composed is non-zero and FLIP is
zero, so Pass A skips at :3420 and Pass A.6 skips at :3660: the row is painted
by neither.

**How long the hole lasts, precisely.** Not "until the next layout" in
general, and ZERO frames in the simplest case, which is why the earlier
draft's test could not have failed. When the settling FLIP is the LAST one,
`hasActiveFlipSlides` goes false, `SliverTreeElement._onAnimationTick` takes
the settle-transition branch (`sliver_tree_element.dart:293-294`) and marks
layout, and that same frame's Step 0b calls `_composer.ghosts.clearAll()`
(`render_sliver_tree.dart:2500-2506`), so `hasEdgeGhosts` is false at :3417
and the row paints normally through Pass A. The hole is real only while
ANOTHER FLIP slide is still in flight: then `hasActiveFlipSlides` stays true,
no settle-transition layout is scheduled, ticks route to `markNeedsPaint`
(:314-328 in the element, unless the composed bound exceeds
`admittedSlideBound`), Step 0b's `pruneSettled` branch never runs, and the
retired ghost's row goes unpainted on every one of those paint-only frames,
until whatever eventually forces a layout (a scroll, a structural change, or
the last FLIP settling).

**And the qualifier that decides whether "unpainted" means "invisible".** Only
when the row's COMPOSED painted position falls inside the paint region. Fixing
Pass A restores a `_paintRow` call, and `_paintRow` culls at
`render_sliver_tree.dart:3780-3782`
(`if (nodeOffset + slideDelta >= scrollOffset + remainingPaintExtent) return;`)
before any painter runs. So for a TRAILING-edge ghost, whose structural
destination is off the BOTTOM by construction (that is what made
`priorOn && !targetOn` true at `_ghost_registry.dart:367-378`), the row would
be culled anyway and the skip costs nothing visible. The loss is real for a
LEADING-edge ghost: its structural destination is above the viewport top,
`_paintRow` carries NO top-edge cull, and a held make-room preview offset can
shift it back down into view, which is precisely the state the test below
builds. Stated without the qualifier, "invisible on every frame" is wrong for
half the ghosts.

**Root cause.** The same question ("does this row still paint as a ghost") is
asked with two different deltas. `getFlipSlideDeltaNid` is the documented
ghost-lifecycle read (`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:1043-1061`) and
`getSlideDeltaXNid` is already FLIP-only (:1059-1060, :1067), so only the Y
term at :3417-3419 is wrong.

**Solution.** Change the skip at `render_sliver_tree.dart:3417-3421` to:

```dart
if (hasEdgeGhosts &&
    _composer.ghosts.entryFor(nodeId) != null &&
    (controller.getFlipSlideDeltaNid(nid) != 0.0 || slideDeltaX != 0.0)) {
  continue;
}
```

so the two gates become exact complements. Leave the following
`if (slideDelta != 0.0 || slideDeltaX != 0.0)` at :3423 on the COMPOSED read: a
ghost row that falls through must still paint at structural plus FLIP plus
preview. Rewrite the comment at :3405-3416 to say the skip mirrors Pass A.6's
criterion and `GhostRegistry.pruneSettled`. The break comment at :3372-3374
needs one clause too: it justifies the `paintBound` early exit with "Pass A
already skips them", which after this change holds only for FLIP-live ghosts.
The exit itself stays correct and must not be widened: `paintBound` already
carries the composed overreach (:3355, :3375), so a row past it cannot paint
inside the paint region at any composed offset. Add this site to CLAUDE.md's
FLIP-only read inventory, in group (a), edge-ghost LIFECYCLE, as a DELTA of
plus one. Do not write an absolute total here: M10 lands first and rewrites the
inventory into four categories with its own recipe, and L6 adds two to category
(c), so any absolute number written in this block is wrong as soon as either of
those lands. Re-run M10's canonical recipe after this change and
write the number it returns. Note while editing that CLAUDE.md's
stated recipe is already loose and should be tightened rather than copied:
`grep -rn "hasActiveFlipSlides\|getFlipSlideDeltaNid" lib` currently returns 14
lines, and "minus the two declarations" (`tree_controller.dart:1061`, `:1332`)
leaves 12, not nine, because three of the remainder are prose mentions
(`tree_controller.dart:1321`, `_ghost_registry.dart:136`, `:173`). The nine are
CODE reads: `_ghost_registry.dart:154` (pruneSettled) and `:319` (install-side
predicate), `render_sliver_tree.dart:1366` (Step 9 clearAll), `:2501` (Step 0b
clearAll), `:3658` (ghost paint skip), `:1529` (`isNodeRetained`),
`sliver_tree_element.dart:287` (settle transition), `:464` and `:477` (the two
eviction gates). This change makes `render_sliver_tree.dart:3417-3421` the
tenth.

**Sequencing dependency (chain 3: M10 first, then L6, L7 and L24).** Chain 3 in
the plan's Sequencing section is the exit-ghost pipeline, M10 first and then
L6, L7 and L24 in an order that is not fixed. All four decide which delta a
ghost pass reads and who paints the anchor.

M10. This block does not own its own vocabulary. M10 establishes the
`getHeldPreviewDeltaNid` accessor and the identity
`getSlideDeltaNid == getFlipSlideDeltaNid + getHeldPreviewDeltaNid`, and it
rewrites CLAUDE.md's carve-out inventory from nine reads across two categories
into sixteen across four, together with the grep recipe that becomes the single
source of truth for the count. That is why the Solution above writes a DELTA
(plus one in category (a)) and no absolute total. Land M10 first: landing this
block first means the inventory sentence it edits is still the two-category
one, so the delta lands against a total M10 immediately replaces and has to be
re-derived anyway. M10's block records the same rule and owns the recipe.

L6. Same file, same question, different ghost model, and the coupling is one
site. L6 gives `applyPaintTransform` its missing branch for anchor-based EXIT
ghosts (`_phantomExitGhosts`) while this block changes the skip for EDGE ghosts
(`_composer.ghosts`), so neither touches the other's predicate. But
`applyPaintTransform` already carries an EDGE-ghost branch whose `useGhost`
predicate reads the COMPOSED delta (`render_sliver_tree.dart:4406-4407`, with
`slideDelta` from `getSlideDeltaNid` at :4386-4388), which is the same
composed-versus-FLIP question this block fixes in Pass A. After this block
lands, a FLIP-settled edge ghost carrying a held preview falls through Pass A's
skip and paints at structural plus composed through `_paintRow` (:3785-3790),
while `useGhost` stays true and the transform still substitutes `baseForEdge`
(:4408-4409), so `localToGlobal` reports the row `baseForEdge - layoutOffset`
away from where it now paints. That is this block's own PAIR rule, violated at
the transform instead of at the paint pass. Traced, not tested. L6 is the
natural owner, since it is already rewriting that method, and its block records
the same note: land L6 second and it reconciles :4406-4407 with the question
this block leaves in Pass A; land it first and this block carries the
reconciliation. Either way the two gates end up asking the same question. The
two inventory deltas stay distinct and must not be conflated: plus ONE in
category (a) here, plus TWO in category (c) for L6, per L6's block and M10's.

L24. Both blocks edit the Pass A loop's skip block, and both are governed by
one invariant: the set Pass A skips must be exactly the set some other pass
paints. This block makes the edge-ghost skip at :3417-3421 the exact complement
of Pass A.6's gate at :3658-3661; L24 adds a THIRD skip to the same loop, for
the anchors its `_computeA7Anchors` selects, and states the same constraint in
its own words ("the skip set and the paint set must be one set, by
construction"). The two skips are independent in content, `_composer.ghosts`
against `_phantomExitGhosts`, but they are adjacent edits to one loop between
:3384 and :3421, so whichever lands second re-derives its anchors and must
confirm the two compose for a row that is BOTH an edge-ghost row and an
exit-ghost anchor: with this block landed, such a row falls through the
edge-ghost skip whenever its FLIP delta is zero, so L24's anchor skip has to be
what catches it, which means that skip must sit ABOVE the sliding-bucket branch
at :3423-3426 or the row is bucketed as sliding AND repainted by A.7. Land L24
second and that is one reading of one loop; land it first and this block makes
the same check from the other side. Not covered today: no existing test builds
a row that is both.

**Alternatives considered.** Making Pass A.6 paint on the composed delta
instead would re-couple ghost lifecycle to the held preview, which is exactly
the regression `test/sliver_tree/ghost_prune_flip_only_test.dart` pins;
rejected.

**Architecture fit.** Extends CLAUDE.md's rule that the prune criterion and the
paint skip are a PAIR reading the same delta, to the third gate that decides
the same question.

**Performance.** One extra `_slide.deltaForNid` per edge-ghost row per frame,
only while `hasEdgeGhosts`. What it buys back is not one frame: it is every
paint-only frame between the ghost's FLIP settling and the next layout, which
is unbounded while another FLIP keeps ticking (see "How long the hole lasts").

**Risk.** Edge-ghost paint and prune are covered by
`test/sliver_tree/ghost_prune_flip_only_test.dart`,
`ghost_revisible_double_paint_test.dart`, `slide_viewport_clamp_test.dart` and
`preview_eviction_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** Three things are mandatory, and the earlier draft of this
block had only the second of them, which is why its case could not have failed.
(a) A LEADING-edge ghost. A trailing-edge ghost's structural destination is off
the BOTTOM by construction, so once Pass A stops skipping it the row reaches
`_paintRow` and is culled at :3780-3782 before any painter runs; the counter
would not advance in either build. `_paintRow` has no top-edge cull, so only
the leading edge discriminates. (b) A SECOND FLIP still in flight, or the
settle-transition layout at `sliver_tree_element.dart:293-294` clears the
registry in the same frame and nothing fails. (c) A held preview offset large
enough to put the row's composed painted position back INSIDE the paint region,
so the skipped row is one the user can actually see.

New file `test/sliver_tree/ghost_flip_only_pass_a_skip_test.dart`, modelled on
`ghost_prune_flip_only_test.dart`'s harness but with its own geometry, stated
in full because every assertion below is arithmetic on it:

- Viewport 550 px (`SizedBox(height: 550) > CustomScrollView` with a
  `ScrollController`), a single `SliverTree(addRepaintBoundaries: false, ...)`.
- 60 roots `n0..n59`. Every row is 40 px EXCEPT `n20`, which is 200 px. So
  `y(n_i) = 40 * i` for `i <= 20` (`n20` spans `[800, 1000)`), and
  `y(n_i) = 1000 + 40 * (i - 21)` above it.
- Each row is a `CustomPaint` whose painter increments `counts[key]`.
- `reorderSlide` 300 ms linear, `makeRoom` 200 ms linear.

1. Pump and settle at scroll 0, THEN `scrollController.jumpTo(400.0)` and pump.
   Settling at 0 first is load-bearing: it measures the leading rows, so their
   extents are the real 40 px rather than the estimate, and the structural
   offsets below are exact. After the jump the tree sliver's
   `constraints.scrollOffset` is 400 and its paint region is `[400, 950)` in
   sliver scroll space. `n20` is inside the cache region at that offset, so
   this layout measures it. Setup assertion:
   `controller.getCurrentExtent("n20") == 200.0`
   (`tree_controller.dart:1513`), because the preview lift IS that extent
   (`tree_controller.dart:1713-1716`) and an unmeasured row would contribute
   the estimate instead.
2. `moveNode("n12", null, index: 9, animate: true, slideDuration: 300ms,
   slideCurve: Curves.linear)`, then `pump()` to consume the baseline. `n12`
   goes from `y = 480` (fully visible) to `y = 360`, a row spanning
   `[360, 400)` that overlaps the viewport by 0 px, so `meaningfullyVisible`
   is false (`_viewport_snapshot.dart:115-126`) and
   `applyClampAndInstallNewGhosts` takes the `priorOn && !targetOn` arm at
   `_ghost_registry.dart:367-378`: a TOP edge ghost. Setup assertion
   `sliver.debugComposerGhostCount == 1`, which also pins WHICH row it is, by
   elimination: `n9` goes 360 to 400, the slide-IN arm (:345-366); `n10` and
   `n11` are on screen on both sides, the "animate real delta" arm (:335);
   every other row's offset is unchanged, so no other row installs an entry:
   the unchanged rows that are ON screen take the `priorOn && targetOn` arm
   (`:335`), and the unchanged rows with both ends off screen take the
   `!priorOn && !targetOn` arm (`:336-344`). Neither arm installs, which is
   what makes `debugComposerGhostCount == 1` exact.
3. Second FLIP, long and far away, installed WITHOUT a baseline consume so the
   engine cannot re-base `n12`:
   `animateSlideFromOffsets({"n55": (y: 600.0, x: 0.0)}, {"n55": (y: 0.0, x:
   0.0)}, duration: Duration(seconds: 3), curve: Curves.linear)`, then
   `pump()`. It reaches the engine directly and names only `n55`, so `n12` is
   untouched, and the default `maxSlideDistance` is `double.infinity`
   (`tree_controller.dart:1558`) so the 600 px delta is not gated. Do NOT use a
   second `moveNode`: a baseline consume re-bases every row whose painted
   position changed, `n12` included, which restarts its slide and destroys the
   staggered-end state.
4. `setReorderPreviewAtIndex(draggedKey: "n20", gapVisibleIndex: 5)`, `pump()`,
   then `pump(200ms)` so the gap finishes opening and the offsets HOLD. Lift is
   `n20`'s 200 px; `n12` sits at visible index 9, inside
   `[gapIndex, draggedEnd) = [5, 21)`, so its held shift is `+200`
   (`tree_controller.dart:1769-1774`).
5. `pump(150ms)`. `n12`'s slide is now 350 ms in, past its 300 ms; `n55` is
   350 ms into 3 s.

The painted arithmetic that makes the assertion mean something: `n12`'s
structural offset is 360, `constraints.scrollOffset` is 400, its composed delta
is +200, so its painted top is `360 - 400 + 200 = 160` and its bottom is 200,
both well inside the paint region `[0, 550)`.

Setup assertions, all required before the paint assertion is meaningful:
- `controller.hasActiveFlipSlides` true (that is `n55`).
- `controller.getFlipSlideDeltaNid(controller.nidOf("n12")) == 0.0`.
- `controller.getSlideDelta("n12")` is `closeTo(200.0, 0.001)`.
- `360.0 - 400.0 + controller.getSlideDelta("n12")` is `closeTo(160.0, 0.5)`
  and that value plus 40 is `lessThan(550.0)`: the composed painted position is
  inside the paint region, so this row's absence is visible.
- `sliver.debugComposerGhostCount == 1`: the entry survived, because no layout
  ran to prune it.
- `sliver.debugPerformLayoutCount` unchanged across step 5's pump. Relayouts
  are expected EARLIER and are harmless: `composedSlideAbsDeltaBound` SUMS the
  two engines (`tree_controller.dart:1387-1388`), so the preview install pushes
  it past the `admittedSlideBound` latched at :2593 and the element re-admits
  once (`sliver_tree_element.dart:315`). That layout runs while `n12`'s FLIP is
  still live, so `pruneSettled` keeps the ghost, and the bound only shrinks
  afterwards, so nothing re-triggers it.

Assertion: record `counts["n12"]` and `counts["n17"]`, then
`await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 16))` and assert
`debugPerformLayoutCount` is STILL unchanged (the frame was paint-only),
`counts["n17"]` advanced, and `counts["n12"]` advanced. `n17` is the control:
it carries the same `+200` held offset and paints at
`680 - 400 + 200 = 480`, it has no registry entry, and its counter advancing
proves the frame painted at all, so a stalled `n12` counter is attributable to
the skip and not to a frame that never painted.

Why it FAILS today, in one sentence: on that frame `n12` has a surviving
registry entry and a non-zero COMPOSED delta, so Pass A `continue`s at
:3420 while Pass A.6 `continue`s at :3658-3660 on the zero FLIP delta, and the
row is painted by NEITHER pass, so its counter does not advance. After the fix
Pass A's skip reads the FLIP delta, sees 0.0, falls through to the composed
test at :3423, and `_paintRow` draws the row at painted y 160 (the cull at
:3780-3782 compares `360 + 200 = 560` against `400 + 550 = 950` and does not
fire).

`addRepaintBoundaries: false` is load-bearing (`sliver_tree_widget.dart:66`,
:103): with the default `RepaintBoundary` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:539`)
`context.paintChild` replays a cached layer and the painter would not run even
when the row IS painted, so the counter would not discriminate.
`tester.getRect` cannot substitute either: it reads the transform, not whether
paint ran.

**Effort.** S.

### L8. Make `snapshotSettledVisibleOffsets` lazy at the consume site

**Finding.** `lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart:1063` computes
`snapshotSettledVisibleOffsets()` on every baseline consume. The method is an
O(N_visible) walk that allocates a map of records (:1737-1753). Its only reads
are `settled[anchorKey]` at :1115 (used again at :1127 and :1134) and
`settled[cursor]` at :1218 (again at :1225 and :1232), both inside
`if (anchorOnScreen)` branches of the two exit-phantom loops (:1065-1165 and
:1181-1249).

**Root cause.** An eagerly-initialized local whose two consumers are both
conditional and both uncommon.

**Solution.** Change :1063 to a lazily-initialized local:

```dart
late final Map<TKey, ({double y, double x})> settled =
    snapshotSettledVisibleOffsets();
```

Dart evaluates a `late` local's initializer on first read, so :1115 and :1218
stay byte-identical and the walk runs only when an exit-phantom branch with an
on-screen anchor is actually taken. Move the "Computed once and shared" comment
at :1058-1062 onto the declaration and say it is computed on first use. The
`assert(geometry != null)` at :1738-1741 then fires only on the paths that read
it, which is strictly weaker and still correct: both readers run inside
`performLayout`.

**Alternatives considered.** A nullable field plus a `??=` accessor closure is
the same thing with more code; `late final` is the idiomatic form.

**Architecture fit.** No contract change. The method's own doc claim that "its
only consumer is the exit-phantom destination injection" (:1720-1722) becomes
true of the computation as well as the value.

**Performance.** Removes one O(N_visible) walk and one map allocation per
animated reorder consume on every path with no on-screen-anchored exit phantom,
which is the common case: plain reorders, entry phantoms, and edge-anchored
exits (:1237-1247 does not read `settled`).

**Risk.** No behavior change. The walk reads only settled extents via
`getEstimatedExtentNid` (:1750), so its timing within `performLayout` is
immaterial. Coverage: `test/sliver_tree/phantom_exit_reparent_test.dart`,
`adjacent_collapsed_exit_ghost_test.dart`, `unmeasured_exit_extent_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** None: cleanup with no observable behavior change.

**Effort.** S.

### L9. O(1) preview overreach bound via a maintained high-water mark

**Finding.** `ReorderPreviewEngine.maxAbsDelta`
(`lib/sliver_tree/_reorder_preview_engine.dart:122-133`) walks every entry.
`TreeController.composedSlideAbsDeltaBound`
(`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:1387-1388`) calls it and is read at
`lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart:2052` (bounded drop-target scan),
:2592 (layout), :3355 (paint) and :4162 (hit test), plus
`lib/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_element.dart:315` (eviction gate): several times
per frame for the whole drag, over an entry set spanning every shifted row.

**Root cause.** A derived aggregate recomputed on read, in an engine whose
every mutation already funnels through two write sites (`setTargetsForNids`
:151-249 and `_onPreviewTick` :304-349).

**Solution.** Maintain `double _maxAbsDelta = 0.0;` and fold into it at every
write:

- Snap branch (:157-176): set to `0.0` alongside `_entries.clear()` at :158,
  then fold `entry.value.abs()` per installed entry.
- Install and retarget (:188-215): fold `target.abs()`, and on retarget also
  `existing.current.abs()` (the new `start`).
- Release loop (:219-237): fold `e.current.abs()` before the target flips to 0.
- `_onPreviewTick` (:312-333): fold `e.current.abs()` inside the loop that is
  already running. This is the only way an overshooting `Curve` can exceed
  `max(abs(start), abs(target))`, and `Curves.elasticOut` / `easeOutBack` do
  overshoot through `e.curve.transform` at :329.
- Reset to `0.0` in `snapClearAll` (:266-273), `clearAll` (:282-287), and at
  the tail of `_onPreviewTick` when `_entries.isEmpty` (:343).
- `clearForNid` (:277-279): reset to `0.0` only when `_entries` becomes empty;
  otherwise leave it (conservative).
- Getter: `double get maxAbsDelta => _entries.isEmpty ? 0.0 : _maxAbsDelta;`

**The documented property changes, and the docs must change with it.** This is
not a pure refactor and must not be described as one. Today the value is
`max(|current|, |target|)` per entry, maxed across entries, and three doc sites
say so in as many words: `_reorder_preview_engine.dart:114-121` ("`max(|current|,
|target|)` per entry, not `|current|`" ... "`current` stays in the max for a
release"), `tree_controller.dart:1380-1386` ("The preview's contribution is its
TERMINAL magnitude (`max(|current|, |target|)` per row)"), and
`tree_controller.dart:1356-1357` ("the preview half of this is the TERMINAL
magnitude of each held offset, not its instantaneous one"). A maintained mark
is NOT that: folds never lower it, so during a release it holds the session
PEAK while every entry decays toward zero, and it returns to `0.0` only when
the last entry leaves. Rewrite all three to the new property:

> Session HIGH-WATER MARK: the largest magnitude any entry in the current
> preview session has held or been targeted at. Monotone non-decreasing while
> any entry exists, and reset to `0.0` when the last one leaves. It is an
> UPPER BOUND on every offset the engine will produce from now on, never an
> exact maximum: during a release it over-reports, holding the pre-release
> peak while the offsets decay. Consumers must treat it as a bound only.

That is sound for every consumer because all five want a window guaranteed to
contain the composed painted positions, and a too-wide window costs extra scan
or admission iterations, never a wrong answer: `render_sliver_tree.dart:2052`
(bounded drop-target scan), :2592 (layout admission), :3355 (paint iteration
start), :4162 (hit-test start), and `sliver_tree_element.dart:315` (the
re-layout trigger, which fires LESS often under a monotone bound). The mark is
also EQUAL to the old value at every install and retarget instant, which is
where `_admittedSlideBound` latches it (:2593). Rule for the implementer: if a
future consumer needs the exact current maximum, it does not get it from this
getter; it gets its own walk, and the doc above says why.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) Leave it: the walk is a linear map iteration
bounded by the visible row count, which is why the review lists it "for
completeness". Take the change only when this file is open anyway. (b) Keep the
exact per-entry max by recomputing the walk whenever any entry is releasing:
rejected, that restores O(entries) reads for the whole release glide, which is
several frames of every single drag, exactly the window this item is about.
(c) Recompute the mark when an entry is removed so it decays: rejected, that is
the same walk paid per arriving entry, which is worse than paying it per read
in the common case. (d) Keep a multiset or max-heap of magnitudes for an exact
O(log n) max: rejected, an allocation and a rebalance per write to keep a value
exact that no consumer needs to be exact.

**Architecture fit.** Mirrors `SlideAnimationEngine`'s existing habit of
maintaining cheap aggregates at the write sites (`hasActiveX` /
`_xActiveCount`, `_slide_animation_engine.dart:119-122`).

**Performance.** Turns five-plus O(entries) walks per frame into O(1) reads for
the length of a drag; costs one `double` and a handful of `max` folds. Also
makes the bound monotone within a preview session, so
`sliver_tree_element.dart:315`'s re-layout trigger fires strictly less often.

**Risk.** `test/sliver_tree/make_room_preview_test.dart:77-81` asserts
`maxActiveSlideAbsDelta == ext` immediately after `setReorderPreview`, an
install instant where the mark equals the old value.
`findrow_bounded_scan_oracle_test.dart:245-250` uses `maxActiveSlideAbsDelta` as
a setup gate mid-open, where the old getter already returns `abs(target)`;
unchanged. `make_room_offcache_build_test.dart`, `preview_eviction_test.dart`
and `reorder_preview_capacity_scan_test.dart` cover the bound's consumers.
`mid_slide_eviction_test.dart` reads the FLIP engine's maxAbsDelta, which this
change does not touch. The behavior change is confined to the release glide,
where the value is now larger than before; no existing test asserts it there
(grep: `maxActiveSlideAbsDelta` appears in `test/` at
`make_room_preview_test.dart:78` and `findrow_bounded_scan_oracle_test.dart:247`
only, plus a comment at `mid_slide_eviction_test.dart:25`).

**Test to add.** New `test/sliver_tree/reorder_preview_max_delta_test.dart`
pinning the REWRITTEN property, not the old one:
`maxActiveSlideAbsDelta` equals the lift at install, still equals it after a
mid-open pump, still equals it partway through a release glide once the
offsets have measurably decayed (assert both: the bound still equals the lift
AND `getSlideDelta(<a shifted row>).abs()` is now strictly less than it, which
is what makes it a bound rather than a maximum), and is `0.0` once the last
entry leaves and after `clearReorderPreview(animate: false)`. Name the decay
assertion for what it is: over-reporting is the contract, so a later change
that "fixes" it to track the decay must fail here.

**Effort.** M.

### L11. Drop the two internal exports from the barrel

**Finding.** `lib/sliver_tree/sliver_tree.dart:19` exports `SliverTreeElement`
and `TreeChildManager`. Inside `lib/`, the only uses are
`lib/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_widget.dart:106-107` (`createElement`'s return
type) and `lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart:204`
(`TreeChildManager<TKey>? childManager`, assigned from
`lib/sliver_tree/sliver_tree_element.dart:124`). Nothing in
`lib/sectioned_sliver_list/` references either, and `test/` mentions them only
in comments (`preview_eviction_test.dart:4`,
`controller_swap_children_retained_test.dart:11`,
`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart:1768`, `tree_controller_test.dart:61`).
`RenderSliverTree.admittedSlideBound` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:742-749`) is
documented "**Internal contract**" while reachable through the exported
`RenderSliverTree`.

**Root cause.** The element and its manager interface are layer plumbing that
never needed a consumer-facing name; the barrel's own doc at
`sliver_tree.dart:9-10` states that what it exports IS the public surface.

**Solution.**
1. Delete `lib/sliver_tree/sliver_tree.dart:19`.
   `SliverTree.createElement()` keeps its narrowed
   `SliverTreeElement<TKey, TData>` return type, which is legal for a
   non-exported type; `analysis_options.yaml` includes only
   `package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml`, which has no rule against it. Confirm
   with `flutter analyze`.
2. Keep `RenderSliverTree.childManager` public (it must be: the element
   assigns it from a different library at `sliver_tree_element.dart:124`) and
   keep `admittedSlideBound` public (:749), and do NOT annotate either
   `@internal`. Mark them internal in prose instead, which is what the package
   already does everywhere else: `admittedSlideBound` already carries it
   (":742-748, **Internal contract**: read by [SliverTreeElement] ... external
   callers should not depend on it"), so only `childManager` needs the
   addition, its doc at :203 currently says nothing beyond "Child manager (the
   element) that creates/removes children". Copy the `admittedSlideBound`
   wording. No `pubspec.yaml` change, no new dependency.

   This replaces an earlier draft that prescribed `@internal` plus a `meta`
   dependency. Both halves of that were wrong. First, the dependency is
   unnecessary: `package:flutter/foundation.dart` re-exports `internal` (its
   `export 'package:meta/meta.dart' show ...` list at lines 12-25 names
   `internal` on line 16) and `render_sliver_tree.dart:7` already imports
   foundation, so nothing would be imported that `depend_on_referenced_packages`
   (enabled through `package:lints/core.yaml:19`, included by
   `flutter_lints/flutter.yaml`) could complain about. Second, and fatally, the
   annotation itself does not compile clean here: the analyzer's
   `invalid_internal_annotation` says "Only public elements in a package's
   private API can be annotated as being internal", and a package's private
   API is `lib/src/`. `lib/sliver_tree/render_sliver_tree.dart` is a public API
   file, so annotating a public member of it is a diagnostic, and step 1's own
   `flutter analyze` confirmation would fail on the change that added it. The
   repo
   already knows this: `tree_controller.dart:987-995` heads its
   INTERNAL ACCESSORS section with exactly that reasoning ("The package layout
   (`lib/sliver_tree/...`) doesn't qualify for the `@internal` annotation,
   which expects elements in `lib/src/`").

   The rejected alternative is moving the declarations under `lib/src/` so the
   annotation becomes legal. Rejected on cost against zero benefit for these
   two members: `RenderSliverTree` is and stays exported (it is the
   `ReorderRenderPort` implementer and tests resolve it via
   `tester.renderObject<RenderSliverTree<...>>`), so its members stay reachable
   from a consumer either way; the annotation would only add a consumer-side
   lint. Against that, `lib/sliver_tree/` holds 41 files and `lib/sectioned_sliver_list/`
   7, and `test/` carries 179 direct `package:widgets_extended/sliver_tree/<file>.dart`
   imports across 141 files that a move would break. The barrel already
   declares the enforcement mechanism this package uses
   (`sliver_tree.dart:9-10`, "anything not exported here is internal
   regardless of its name"), and step 1 is what applies it here.

   Rule for the implementer: in this package `@internal` is unusable outside
   `lib/src/`, and there is no `lib/src/`. Express internal-ness by keeping the
   symbol out of the barrel and saying so in the doc comment. Never add the
   annotation to a file under `lib/sliver_tree/` or `lib/sectioned_sliver_list/`.
3. Breaking-change cost: real but small. The package is 0.0.34, pre-1.0, and
   the only way a consumer could have used these is to subclass the element or
   drive the child manager by hand, which the barrel doc already disclaims.
   Land a single CHANGELOG "Breaking" bullet naming both symbols and pointing
   at `ReorderRenderPort` as the supported render-layer contract.

**Alternatives considered.** Keep the exports and document them as internal;
that leaves the API surface committed, which is the cost this item is about.

**Architecture fit.** `ReorderRenderPort` (`lib/sliver_tree/reorder_render_port.dart`)
is the deliberate narrow render-layer contract; these two exports bypass it and
commit the element's shape instead.

**Performance.** None.

**Risk.** An external subclass of `SliverTreeElement` or implementer of
`TreeChildManager` breaks at compile time, which is loud rather than silent. No
in-repo breakage: verified by grep across `lib/`, `test/` and `examples/`
sources.

**Test to add.** None: cleanup with no observable behavior change. Optionally
add a barrel-surface guard test in the style of
`test/source_encoding_guard_test.dart` that asserts the exported symbol list,
so a future accidental re-export is caught.

**Effort.** S.

### L12. `insertRoot`/`insert` must not gate `moveNode` on the `enterExit` kill switch

**Finding.** `insertRoot` clamps `animate` to false when
`effectiveEnterExit.duration == Duration.zero`
(`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:2404-2406`) and forwards that clamped
flag to `moveNode` at :2498; `insert` does the same at :2858-2860 and :2972.
`moveNode` resolves its own timing from `reorderSlide` (:3479-3480) and applies
no enterExit gate, so with `enterExit: zero` and `reorderSlide: 300ms` a
relocating `insert`/`insertRoot` produces no slide while an equivalent direct
`moveNode` does.

**Root cause.** One `animate` variable carries two families' kill switches. The
comments justifying the delegation at :2490-2493 and :2964-2967 are also stale:
they claim `moveNode`'s `affectedKeys` omits the moved key, but :3636-3637
unions `_siblingRefreshSet(oldParent)` and `_siblingRefreshSet(newParentKey)`,
and `_siblingRefreshSet` (:2281-2291) adds the parent plus its entire child
list (or `_roots` when the parent is null), which contains the moved key after
the move.

**Solution.**
1. Capture the caller's flag before the enterExit clamp:
   `final bool callerAnimate = animate;` immediately above
   `tree_controller.dart:2404` and above :2858, then pass
   `animate: callerAnimate` at :2498 and :2972. `moveNode`'s own reorderSlide
   resolution (:3473-3481) then owns the decision, which is the boundary rule.
2. Replace the stale comments at :2490-2493 and :2964-2967. The real reason the
   data channel fires first is that the payload was overwritten one line
   earlier and `moveNode`'s structural notification is a targeted set;
   reword against :3636-3637 rather than repeating the omission claim.

**Alternatives considered.** Gating the delegation on `effectiveReorderSlide`
inside `insert`/`insertRoot` would duplicate the family decision at a second
site, which the same rule forbids.

**Architecture fit.** CLAUDE.md's "declare an animation's family ONCE, at the
boundary": a relocation is a reorderSlide event and must not inherit the
enterExit decision made for the enter path.

**Performance.** None.

**Risk.** With `enterExit: zero` and a non-zero `reorderSlide`, a relocating
`insert` now slides where it previously did not. Family-flow coverage lives in
`test/sliver_tree/animation_style_flow_test.dart`;
`test/sliver_tree/tree_controller_test.dart:1377-1419` and
`data_only_reinsert_notification_test.dart` cover the relocation paths.

**Test to add.** In `animation_style_flow_test.dart`, a case with
`TreeAnimationStyle(enterExit: Duration.zero, reorderSlide: 300ms)`:
`insert(parentKey: "P2", node: <an existing child of P1>)` must install a slide
(`hasActiveSlides` true, non-zero `getSlideDelta`), matching the equivalent
direct `moveNode`, and the converse case (`reorderSlide: zero`,
`enterExit: 300ms`) must install none.

**Effort.** S.

### L13. Make every scroll the orchestrator starts single-flight, both directions

**Finding.** The plain path
(`lib/sliver_tree/_scroll_orchestrator.dart:236-276`) never reads
`_activeScroll` (:54); only `_animatedConcurrentScroll` (:397-401) and
`dispose` (:480-487) cancel. The follower installed at :391 calls
`position.jumpTo` every animation tick (:386-388), and
`ScrollPositionWithSingleContext.jumpTo` calls `goIdle()`
(`C:/flutter_sdk/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/scroll_position_with_single_context.dart:197-198`),
which disposes the plain path's `DrivenScrollActivity`;
`DrivenScrollActivity.dispose`
(`C:/flutter_sdk/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/scroll_activity.dart:800-804`)
completes its completer at :801, and `animateTo`
(`scroll_position_with_single_context.dart:177-193`) returns exactly that
completer's future (`return activity.done;` at :193, `done` declared at
`scroll_activity.dart:748`). So the `await` at `_scroll_orchestrator.dart:273`
returns early and :275 returns `true` regardless of where the viewport ended
up.

**Root cause.** There is no stated policy for a plain-vs-animated race, and no
mechanism for one. The doc at :47-53 is accurate about what it covers, and
should not be read as a broken promise: it scopes single-flight to ANIMATED
scrolls ("Animated scrolls are SINGLE-FLIGHT: starting a new one cancels the
in-flight one"), which is exactly what :392-403 implements. The gap is that the
plain path (:236-276) sits outside that slot in both directions: it neither
cancels an in-flight animated scroll nor registers itself where a later one
would find it.

**Solution.**
1. Extract the cancel from :397-401 into a helper:

```dart
void _cancelActiveScroll() {
  final session = _activeScroll;
  if (session == null) {
    return;
  }
  session.cancelled = true;
  _teardownScroll(session);
  _activeScroll = null;
}
```

   Call it at :397 (the new session is installed right after at :402-403, which
   overwrites the slot anyway) and from `dispose` in place of :482-487.
2. Make the fix SYMMETRIC, which is a decision, not a detail. Cancelling from
   the plain path alone leaves the mirror defect alive: a plain `animateTo`
   started first is still killed by a later animated scroll's follower
   `jumpTo` (:386-388) while its own `await` at :273 resolves and :275 reports
   `true`, which is the same false success this item exists to remove. So the
   plain path both cancels AND registers:
   - Give `_ActiveScroll` a resource-less form (nullable `progress` and
     `follower`, plus a `plain` constructor) and null-guard the two lines in
     `_teardownScroll` (:65-66). `cancelled` and `tornDown` are unchanged, and
     both remain the same tokens `dispose` and a superseding scroll set.
     Retitle its class doc (:493-499), which currently reads "Per-invocation
     session record for [ScrollOrchestrator]'s animated concurrent scroll": it
     now records EITHER path, and only the animated one carries resources.
   - In the plain path, immediately after the `AncestorExpansionMode.none`
     early-return at :231-234, call `_cancelActiveScroll()` and then install
     `_activeScroll = _ActiveScroll.plain()`. That placement is BEFORE the
     one-frame wait at :236-253 and before `position.maxScrollExtent` is read
     at :265-268, so the follower stops jumping before anything is measured,
     and the whole plain path (including its awaits) is covered by the slot.
   - Wrap the rest of the method in `try { ... } finally { ... }` clearing the
     slot only when it still holds this session, copying the identity check at
     :445-447 verbatim (an unconditional null-out strands a successor).
   - Return `!session.cancelled` at :275 instead of `true`. The
     `duration == Duration.zero` branch at :271 keeps returning true: `jumpTo`
     is synchronous, so nothing can cancel between it and the return.
   The cancelled animated scroll hits its own `session.cancelled` check at
   :420-423 and resolves `false` without its final snap; a cancelled plain
   scroll now reports `false` the same way.
3. Widen the two existing docs rather than writing new ones. Both already say
   the right thing about the wrong scope: `TreeController.animateScrollToKey`
   at `tree_controller.dart:1992-1994` ("Animated-mode scrolls are
   single-flight: starting one while another is still in flight cancels the
   earlier scroll (its future resolves false), the newer target wins") and the
   `_activeScroll` field at `_scroll_orchestrator.dart:47-53` ("Animated
   scrolls are SINGLE-FLIGHT ..."). Drop "Animated-mode" / "Animated" from
   both so the rule reads across modes. The return-value doc at
   `tree_controller.dart:1996-1999` already lists "the scroll was cancelled
   (superseded, or the controller was disposed)" as a `false` case and needs
   no edit; step 2 is what finally makes it true of the plain path. Without
   step 2 the sentence would have to grow a carve-out ("unless the loser was a
   plain scroll that started first"), which is the second reason step 2 is not
   optional.
4. Leave one comment at :270-275 recording the residual: a plain `animateTo`
   interrupted by anything OUTSIDE the orchestrator (a user drag, an app-level
   `jumpTo`) still returns `true`. Closing that needs an explicit landed-check
   and is out of scope here.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) Awaiting the in-flight scroll instead of
cancelling changes the contract from latest-wins to queued; the animated path
already chose latest-wins at :392-396, so cancelling is the consistent choice.
(b) Cancel from the plain path but do not register it, and document the
asymmetry instead: rejected. It leaves a `Future<bool>` that reports success
for a scroll the orchestrator itself overrode, which is the exact defect
class; it makes step 3's doc a two-clause rule ("cancels the other, unless the
other is plain and started first") that a caller cannot reason about; and the
extra code it saves is a nullable pair plus one `try/finally`.

**Sequencing dependency (H3).** H3 restructures the SAME method and adds a
resolve guard that returns false for an unresolvable key before either of its
routing decisions. That guard must PRECEDE the session install specified here.
With the install first, an unresolvable key would register a plain session,
cancel an in-flight animated scroll through the single-flight slot, and only
then return false, reintroducing exactly the defect H3's guard exists to
prevent. Whichever of the two lands second is responsible for the final
ordering; H3's block records the matching note.

Also add a cancelled check after the one-frame `await scheduler.endOfFrame` at
`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:246-251`. Step 2's claim that the
`duration == Duration.zero` branch "keeps returning true, jumpTo is
synchronous, so nothing can cancel between it and the return" does not hold
once the session is installed BEFORE that await: a zero-duration call with a
collapsed-ancestor expansion can be superseded during the await, and would
still `jumpTo` and report true. Check `session.cancelled` after the await and
return false when it is set, matching the animated path's own post-await
check.

**Architecture fit.** Makes `_activeScroll` the single-flight slot for every
scroll the orchestrator starts, and widens the doc at :47-53 from "animated
scrolls" to "scrolls". Rule for anything added to this file later: a code path
that moves `position` registers a session in `_activeScroll` before it starts
and resolves `!session.cancelled`; `_teardownScroll` tolerates a session with
no resources.

**Performance.** None.

**Risk.** `test/sliver_tree/scroll_orchestrator_dispose_test.dart` and
`scroll_orchestrator_position_swap_test.dart` exercise teardown, and both must
be re-run specifically against the resource-less session: `dispose` now tears
down a session whose `progress` and `follower` may be null, and the
null-guarded `_teardownScroll` is the only thing standing between that and a
null dereference on the disposal path. The follower is the per-tick callback installed
at `_scroll_orchestrator.dart:391`, reachable only through
`_animatedConcurrentScroll`, so its coverage is whatever passes
`AncestorExpansionMode.animated`. Measured this session,
`grep -rn "AncestorExpansionMode.animated" test/sliver_tree/`: five uses in
`scroll_orchestrator_dispose_test.dart`, three in
`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart`, two in
`scroll_orchestrator_position_swap_test.dart`, and none anywhere else. Note
that `scroll_reresolve_test.dart` and `slide_scroll_concurrency_test.dart` do
NOT cover it despite their names: each contains zero `animateScrollToKey` and
zero orchestrator references, and moves the position with a direct test-side
`position.jumpTo`. Any test that
starts two scrolls in either order and expects both futures to be `true` needs
updating. Several tests assert a plain-path `true` today, not one. Do not trust a count
written here; re-derive the set, because the two spellings need two searches:
`grep -rn "expect(ok, true)" test/sliver_tree/` finds the direct form, and a
test may instead capture the future into a flag, which is why
`audit_repro_f24_test.dart` (`:84-103`, asserting via a `completed` flag set
at `:92`) is invisible to that grep. Measured this session, the set is
`audit_repro_f24_test.dart:84-103` plus four in `sliver_tree_widget_test.dart`,
each with `duration: Duration.zero`: `:1308-1314`, `:1341-1348`, `:1371-1377`
and `:1411-1421`. The last of these is the one that matters most and is the
easiest to miss: it takes the default `ancestorExpansion`
(`tree_controller.dart:2006` = `AncestorExpansionMode.immediate`, and
`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:215-218` routes only `animated` away from the plain
path). It is not alone in reaching the one-frame wait at
`_scroll_orchestrator.dart:246-251` that step 2 adds a `session.cancelled`
check to: that wait runs only when the immediate path actually expanded
collapsed ancestors, and `audit_repro_f24_test.dart` does too, since it asserts
its target starts hidden behind a collapsed ancestor (`:65-69`), calls with the
default `ancestorExpansion` (`:84-89`), and asserts the ancestor expanded
afterwards (`:112`). Do not state which tests reach that wait as a count or as
an exclusive: derive it by looking for a collapsed ancestor plus the default
`AncestorExpansionMode.immediate`, which is the condition the branch tests.
`sliver_tree_widget_test.dart` holds 13 of the 29 `animateScrollToKey` uses in
`test/`, the largest concentration anywhere, so it is the file to check first
rather than one this Risk section can omit. All four run a single uncontended scroll, so no session
is ever cancelled and `!session.cancelled` still returns `true`; all four must
stay green unchanged, which is the point of replacing a bare `return true`
with a cancellation-aware one rather than with `false`. `grep -rn "animateScrollToKey" --include=*.dart examples/`
returns one real call site, `examples/lib/main.dart:485` in
`_scrollToSelected` (`:480-492`), plus four prose mentions (`:76`, `:156`,
`:207`, `:819`). That caller `await`s the future and DISCARDS the bool, so no
example depends on the returned value and none needs updating; the point is
that the reader set is one caller, not zero.

**Test to add.** Both directions, since step 2 fixes both.

1. Promote the review's L13 probe: start
   `animateScrollToKey(deepKey, ancestorExpansion: AncestorExpansionMode.animated, duration: 300ms)`
   without awaiting; `pump(100ms)`; then `await animateScrollToKey("k1")` whose
   target is 50. Expect the first future to resolve `false`, the second
   `true`, and `position.pixels` to end at the second target.
2. The mirror: start a plain
   `animateScrollToKey("k1", duration: 300ms)` without awaiting; `pump(100ms)`;
   then start an animated concurrent scroll to a deep key and await it. Expect
   the PLAIN future to resolve `false` (it fails today: the follower's `jumpTo`
   completes its `DrivenScrollActivity` and :275 returns `true`), the animated
   one `true`, and `position.pixels` at the animated target.

**Effort.** S.

### L14. Expansion memory on the direct `syncChildren` path is never consumed or pruned

**Finding.** `_pruneExpansionMemory`
(`lib/sliver_tree/tree_sync_controller.dart:1174-1200`) is called from exactly
one place, `_syncRootsImpl` step 8 (:461-464). In `_syncChildrenImpl` step 3,
only the brand-new-node branch consumes its entry via `_restoreExpansion`
(:693-695); the pending/live re-add branch (`insert` with
`preservePendingSubtreeState: true`, :654-665) and the cross-parent `moveNode`
branch (:666-680) do not, while step 1 recorded an entry for every removed key
at :621. A stale `true` then re-expands a user-collapsed node through the
exact-match early-out at :545-551 or the step-6 parent retry at :765-769
(`_restoreExpansion` only ever expands, :1209-1222).

**Root cause.** `_syncRootsImpl` funnels all three step-3 branches into
`addedRoots` (:321) and restores them together at :457-459; the children path
restores only one of its three branches, and prunes on neither entry point.

**Solution.**
1. Hoist the restore in `_syncChildrenImpl` step 3 so all three placements
   consume their entry: delete the call at :693-695 and add the block below
   after the OUTER if/else closes at **:696**, immediately before
   `remaining.insert(...)` at :697 (or before `remainingBit.update` at :698 if
   L2 has already removed :697). Anchoring it at :680 instead, as an earlier
   draft said, is wrong and silently breaks the case that works today: :680
   closes only the INNER `oldParent == parentKey` if/else, so a block placed
   there is inside the `getNodeData(node.key) != null` arm and never runs for
   a brand-new node, which is precisely the branch whose restore is being
   deleted at :693-695. Verify while editing that the insertion point is
   inside the `for (final node in desired)` loop at :646 and outside the
   `if (...) { } else { }` pair, i.e. at the same indentation as :697:

```dart
if (!_deferExpansionRestore) {
  _restoreExpansion(node.key, animate: animate);
}
```

   Safe on the re-add branches: `_restoreExpansion` only expands, and only when
   the remembered value is `true` and the node already has children
   (:1211-1221). `insert(preservePendingSubtreeState: true)` and `moveNode`
   both preserve subtree state, so the call is a no-op that consumes the entry.
2. Prune on the direct entry points too, ONCE per public call. The guard has
   to cover two different nestings, and `_deferExpansionRestore` alone covers
   only one of them:
   - `_syncChildrenRecursive` calls the PUBLIC `syncChildren` per node (:1113)
     and defers every restore to the bottom-up loop at :1126-1128, so pruning
     mid-walk would drop pending restores. `_deferExpansionRestore` is true
     throughout (set at :359, cleared at :366), so it catches this one.
   - `syncMultipleChildren` ALSO calls the public `syncChildren`, once per
     parent at :834, and `_deferExpansionRestore` is false there. A guard on
     that flag alone would therefore prune once per parent plus once at the
     tail: N+1 `removeWhere` passes over expansion memory for an N-parent
     call, which is the per-parent cost this item's own Alternatives rejects.

   So gate the per-call prune on BOTH, using `_globallyDesiredChildren` as the
   "inside a larger multi-parent sync" signal. It is non-null in exactly the
   two nesting contexts and nowhere else (`grep -n "_globallyDesiredChildren"`:
   declared :99, assigned :360 and cleared :367 for `_syncRootsImpl` step 5,
   assigned :793 and cleared :856 for `syncMultipleChildren`; every other hit
   is a read or a comment). Add one private helper and call it from
   `syncChildren` (:505-507), after `_syncChildrenImpl` inside the same
   `runBatch`:

```dart
/// Prunes expansion memory unless this call is nested inside a larger
/// sync that owns the prune itself: `_syncChildrenRecursive` (whose
/// restores are deferred to its bottom-up loop) and `syncMultipleChildren`
/// (which prunes once at its tail, not once per parent).
void _pruneExpansionMemoryIfOutermost() {
  if (!_memoryEnabled ||
      _deferExpansionRestore ||
      _globallyDesiredChildren != null) {
    return;
  }
  _pruneExpansionMemory();
}
```

   Then at the tail of `syncMultipleChildren`'s batch (after the
   deferred-removal loop at :841-854, inside the `try` that ends at :855) call
   `_pruneExpansionMemory()` DIRECTLY, guarded only by `_memoryEnabled`: at
   that point `_globallyDesiredChildren` is still non-null (it is cleared at
   :856 in the `finally`), so routing the tail call through the helper would
   suppress the one prune the whole guard exists to preserve. Net cost: exactly
   one prune per public `syncChildren` / `syncMultipleChildren` call, matching
   `_syncRootsImpl`'s single prune at :461-464, which still runs after step 5
   with the field already nulled.
3. No change needed in `_pruneExpansionMemory`: it already keeps
   pending-deletion and exiting keys (:1186-1188) and keeps an unsatisfiable
   `true` (:1193-1197), so a prune at the end of a children sync cannot drop a
   legitimately pending restore.

**Alternatives considered.** (a) Pruning inside `_syncChildrenImpl` rather than
at the public entry points would run once per parent inside
`syncMultipleChildren`, paying an O(memory) `removeWhere` per parent;
rejected. (b) Pruning at the public entry point guarded only on
`_deferExpansionRestore`: same per-parent cost by a different route (:834
calls the public method), rejected for the same reason, which is why step 2
adds the `_globallyDesiredChildren` clause. (c) Accepting N+1 prunes and
restating the cost honestly: rejected, `expansionMemory` defaults to 1024
entries (:61), so this is up to N+1 sweeps of a 1024-entry map per call, on a
public API whose whole purpose is to batch many parents at once, bought for
nothing when one clause removes it. (`syncMultipleChildren` has no in-`lib`
caller: `grep -rn "syncMultipleChildren" lib/` finds only its declaration at
:788 and doc mentions, and the sectioned module uses `syncRoots` (:238) and
`syncChildren` (:280) instead, so the N here is a direct consumer's parent
count, in the "manual sync" usage pattern.) (d) A dedicated depth counter
instead of
reusing `_globallyDesiredChildren`: rejected, it is a second piece of state
tracking exactly what an existing field already tracks, and the two would drift.

**Architecture fit.** Makes the children path's memory lifecycle identical to
the roots path's, the same convergence the 0.0.34 work did for the removal
deferral.

**Performance.** Exactly one `removeWhere` over at most `expansionMemory`
entries (default 1024, :61) per direct `syncChildren` / `syncMultipleChildren`
call, never one per parent (see step 2's guard), and skipped entirely when the
map is empty (:1175). Nested calls from `_syncChildrenRecursive` and from
`syncMultipleChildren`'s per-parent loop add nothing.

**Risk.** `test/sliver_tree/sync_expansion_memory_regression_test.dart`,
`synced_expansion_memory_size_test.dart`,
`sync_multiple_children_subtree_test.dart`, `tree_sync_deep_tree_test.dart` and
`synced_initial_node_expansion_test.dart` all read this machinery.
`snapshotRememberedKeys()` (:954) is what `SyncedSliverTree` captures pre-sync
(`lib/sliver_tree/synced_sliver_tree.dart:855-857`); the new prune runs AFTER
the sync while that capture happens BEFORE it, so the auto-expand pass's input
is unaffected.

**Test to add.** Four calls, in order: (1) `syncChildren(P, [C])` with C
expanded over grandchildren; (2) `syncChildren(P, [])`, which records
`C: true` at :621; (3) `syncChildren(P, [C])` while C is still mid-exit,
hitting the :659 re-add branch, which is the branch solution step 1 gives a
restore to; (4) `controller.collapse(key: "C")`, then
`syncChildren("C", <the same children>)`, which takes the exact-match
early-out at :545-551 and is where the stale `true` used to re-expand C.
Assert immediately after call (3) that `snapshotRememberedKeys()` no longer
contains C (that is the entry-consumption half, and it FAILS on unfixed code),
and after call (4) that `isExpanded("C") == false` (the user-visible half).
Add a setup assertion after call (2) that the memory DOES contain C, otherwise
a change to the recording path would make the whole test vacuous.

**Effort.** M.

### L15. Gained-children heuristic can override a collapse made during the last child's exit

**Finding.** `_emptiedWhileCollapsed` is written at exactly one instant,
`lib/sliver_tree/tree_sync_controller.dart:567-578`, and only when the emptying
sync sees `desiredKeys.isEmpty && currentKeys.isNotEmpty` (:568) AND
`!_controller.isExpanded(parentKey)` (:569). `currentKeys` comes from
`getLiveChildren` (:559), which excludes pending-deletion children, and
`snapshotChildPresence` skips them too (:926-928), so a parent whose last child
is animating out reports "no live children" to the pre-sync snapshot at
`lib/sliver_tree/synced_sliver_tree.dart:846-848`. A collapse performed AFTER
the emptying sync, while the child exits, is recorded nowhere; when children
return, `expandParentsThatGainedChildren` sees `hadChildrenBefore == false`
(`lib/sliver_tree/_sync_helpers.dart:55-58`), the key absent from
`rememberedBeforeSync` (:60-62) and an unexpanded parent (:68-69), and expands
it (:70).

**Root cause.** The deliberate-collapse signal is SAMPLED at one sync instant
instead of being OBSERVED when the collapse happens.
`test/sliver_tree/auto_expand_respects_collapse_test.dart:1-10` documents only
the "collapsed before the emptying sync" ordering.

**Solution.** Observe the collapse directly.
`TreeController.addExpansionListener` / `removeExpansionListener`
(`lib/sliver_tree/tree_controller.dart:2111-2120`) fire per key after the
mutation settles and are deduped across `runBatch` (:2106-2110).

1. In `TreeSyncController`'s constructor (:53-56), when `_memoryEnabled`,
   register a bound listener; remove it in `dispose()` (:960-963). Two
   mechanics to get right: the constructor currently has no body (it is
   `: _controller = treeController;`), so one has to be added, and both the
   add and the remove must name the same instance method,
   `_handleExpansionChanged`, because `removeExpansionListener` removes by
   `==` from a `List` (`tree_controller.dart:778`, :2119) and tear-off
   identity holds only for the same method on the same receiver. Do not wrap
   it in a closure at either site. `synced_sliver_tree.dart:540`/:926 is the
   in-repo precedent for exactly that pairing. Both in-repo wrappers already call `dispose()`
   (`synced_sliver_tree.dart:773` and `:932`;
   `lib/sectioned_sliver_list/sectioned_list_controller.dart:155` and `:863`),
   and the public doc at :958-959 already instructs direct users to. Note
   `sectioned_list_controller.dart:150-161` (the `preserveExpansion` setter)
   disposes the old sync controller before building a new one, so the
   subscription follows the swap with no extra work; with `preserveExpansion`
   false the new controller gets `expansionMemory: 0` (:158) and so registers
   nothing.
2. The listener:

```dart
void _handleExpansionChanged(TKey key, bool isExpanded) {
  if (!_memoryEnabled) {
    return;
  }
  if (isExpanded) {
    _emptiedWhileCollapsed.remove(key);
    return;
  }
  _emptiedWhileCollapsed.add(key);
  while (_emptiedWhileCollapsed.length > expansionMemory) {
    _emptiedWhileCollapsed.remove(_emptiedWhileCollapsed.first);
  }
}
```

   A collapse fires only on an actual expanded-to-collapsed flip, so a node
   that was never expanded records nothing and the heuristic keeps working for
   genuinely new parents. The existing consume at :575-577 (a sync that brings
   children back clears the entry) stays and remains the lifecycle end; it runs
   after `snapshotRememberedKeys()` is captured pre-sync
   (`synced_sliver_tree.dart:855-857`), so suppression still applies to exactly
   the sync that returns the children.
3. Rename the field and its doc (:83-94) from "emptied while collapsed" to
   "deliberately collapsed", since the sync-time write at :570 becomes one of
   two writers, and update `snapshotRememberedKeys`'s doc at :943-950.
4. Keep the sync-time write at :567-578: it still catches a collapse made
   before this sync controller was attached.
5. Update the SECOND reader of the widened set, which the earlier draft never
   enumerated. `_emptiedWhileCollapsed` reaches consumers through
   `snapshotRememberedKeys` (:954-956, which unions it with
   `_rememberedExpansion`), and that has TWO callers, not one:
   `synced_sliver_tree.dart:856` (the `rememberedBeforeSync` capture this item
   already discusses) and
   `lib/sectioned_sliver_list/sectioned_list_controller.dart:197`, inside the
   public `rememberedSectionKeys()` (:194-203), which the sectioned widget
   reads at `sectioned_sliver_list_widget.dart:481` and feeds to
   `_applyInitialExpansion` (:486-492). Its doc at :181-193 currently promises
   "Section keys whose expansion state is currently REMEMBERED, meaning the
   section is not in the tree right now but its expanded/collapsed state is
   being held for a re-add", and after this change that is false: a section
   still IN the tree, collapsed by the user or by `collapseSection`, will
   appear. Rewrite it to the union it actually returns ("sections whose
   expansion the widget must not overwrite: removed-and-remembered sections,
   plus sections deliberately collapsed while present"), and keep the
   "snapshot BEFORE the sync" instruction at :192-193 unchanged. The behavior
   it drives is unchanged in practice, since `_applyInitialExpansion` already
   skips sections that are not new (`knownSections`, :468-470), but a public
   doc that lies about its own key set is how the next bug gets written.

**Alternatives considered.** Counting pending-deletion children as present in
`snapshotChildPresence` closes only the narrow mid-exit window, not the
"collapse after the exit settles" ordering, and it changes the map's documented
key-set contract (:905-908) that `_applyInitialExpansionToNewNodes` reads as
"which nodes existed before" (`synced_sliver_tree.dart:705-707`).

**Architecture fit.** Keeps CLAUDE.md's stated invariant that the auto-expand
heuristic never overrides a user's deliberate collapse, and sources it from the
controller's own expansion channel instead of inferring it from sync shapes.

**Performance.** One set write per collapse flip. The second-order cost is
real but lands on fewer setups than the earlier draft claimed. Subscribing
flips `_expansionListeners.isEmpty` to false, which switches on two things
that no-op while nothing is subscribed: prior-state recording in every
expansion mutator (`_recordExpansionChange`, `tree_controller.dart:2124-2127`,
a small map write per flip) and `collapseAll`'s flipped-key collection
(`collectFlipped: _expansionListeners.isNotEmpty` at :333, which allocates and
fills a `List<TKey>` of every key it clears instead of taking the branch-free
bulk path).

**Risk.** Two behavior widenings to weigh, plus one correction to the earlier
draft.

First, WHO starts paying the recording cost. Not `SyncedSliverTree`: it
already calls `addExpansionListener` unconditionally in `initState`
(`synced_sliver_tree.dart:540`, removed at :926), so
`_expansionListeners.isEmpty` is already false for the common declarative
setup and nothing changes there. `grep -rn "addExpansionListener" lib/` finds
that one CALL and nothing else (the other hits are doc references:
`tree_controller.dart:777`, its declaration at :2111, and
`synced_sliver_tree.dart:425`). So the setups that newly pay are (a) a bare
`TreeSyncController` over a caller-owned `TreeController` (the "manual sync"
usage pattern) and (b) the ENTIRE `sectioned_sliver_list` module, which builds
a `TreeSyncController` internally (`sectioned_list_controller.dart:71-76` in
the constructor, :156-159 on a `preserveExpansion` flip) and registers no
expansion listener anywhere. Check
`test/sliver_tree/tree_expansion_listener_test.dart` and any counter-based
perf test around expansion or `collapseAll` in `test/sectioned_sliver_list/`.

Second, a PROGRAMMATIC collapse (including `collapseAll`, which records in bulk
via `_recordExpansionChanges`, :2138-2140) now suppresses auto-expand for those
keys until children return, which is policy-correct but broader than today.

Third, the set that `snapshotRememberedKeys` returns widens, and so does
`rememberedSectionKeys` on top of it, so every assertion about either has to be
re-read. `grep -rn "snapshotRememberedKeys\|rememberedSectionKeys" test/` gives
seven assertion sites plus one comment (`preserve_expansion_declarative_test.dart:162`).
Four are positive containment after a REMOVAL and only widen:
`sync_expansion_memory_regression_test.dart:79`, :119, :123 and
`preserve_expansion_declarative_test.dart:81`, :211 (five, counting both
sectioned ones). The three that could actually break are the NEGATIVE ones,
and each survives only because its setup never collapses anything:
`tree_sync_controller_test.dart:1491` asserts `isEmpty` after three `expand`
calls (:1478-1480), and an expand REMOVES from the set rather than adding;
:1534-1543 asserts `contains("taskA")` and `contains("grand1")` are FALSE
across a reparenting `syncRoots`, where taskA is expanded and grand1 was never
expanded, so neither records a collapse flip. Re-read those three by hand
rather than trusting this paragraph if the tests have moved. Also affected:
`auto_expand_respects_collapse_test.dart`,
`synced_initial_node_expansion_test.dart`,
`snapshot_child_presence_test.dart`. A direct `TreeSyncController` user who
never calls `dispose()` now leaks a listener.

**Test to add.** Extend `test/sliver_tree/auto_expand_respects_collapse_test.dart`
with the reversed ordering: sync P with one child, expand P, sync P to empty
with `animate: true` so the child is mid-exit, collapse P during the exit,
settle the exit, then sync the children back. Expect
`isExpanded("P") == false`.

**Effort.** M.

### L16. syncMultipleChildren rejects duplicate keys only under `assert`, so release builds mutate before they refuse

**Finding.** The duplicate check at `tree_sync_controller.dart:798-814` lives inside `assert(() { ... }())`, and its `seenKeys` set is declared at `:799` OUTSIDE the per-parent loop at `:800`. So with asserts enabled it catches BOTH input shapes, a key repeated under two parents and a key repeated inside ONE parent's list: either way `seenKeys.add(c.key)` fails at `:802` and `FlutterError` is thrown at `:803-809`. It runs before the union loop at `:815-819` and before the first `syncChildren` call at `:834`, so in debug NOTHING has been mutated when it throws.

The partial-mutation hazard is therefore RELEASE-ONLY, where the assert is stripped, and it has two distinct shapes:

- Duplicate INSIDE one parent's list. `syncChildren` at `:834` calls `_assertNoDuplicateKeys` at `:497`, which is a plain static method and not an assert, and throws `ArgumentError` at `:526`. A bad k-th list throws after parents 1..k-1 have already been synced.
- Duplicate ACROSS two parents. Nothing throws at all: the second `syncChildren` reparents the key and the call completes. The doc at `:781-785` states this as intended release behaviour ("release builds silently apply last-write-wins").

The debug message is also wrong for the first shape: `{"B": [x, x]}` reports that `x` "appears under more than one parent" (`:804-805`) when it appears under exactly one.

**Root cause.** `syncMultipleChildren` is the only sync entry point that validates piecewise from inside its own batch. `syncRoots` validates the whole desired list at `:171`, BEFORE `runBatch` at `:172`; `syncChildren` does the same at `:497` before `:505`. `syncMultipleChildren`'s only unconditional per-list check is the one inside the mutation loop at `:834`, and `runBatch` commits in its `finally` (`tree_controller.dart:2208-2247`: `_batchDepth--` at `:2213`, order flush at `:2219`, notifications at `:2233-2244`), so completed parents survive the throw. The deferred-removal drain at `tree_sync_controller.dart:841-854` is skipped as well, leaving deferred movers parked under their old parents.

**Solution. Option (c): fold the check into the union pass, so partial mutation is impossible by construction and no new data structure exists.**

`_globallyDesiredChildren` is already a GLOBAL union of every desired child key (`:99`, allocated at `:793`, filled at `:815-819`), so `add` returning false is exactly the "key already claimed" predicate the assert re-derives with a second set. Delete `:798-814` outright and test the union's own `add`. Iterate `.entries` rather than `.values` so the message can name the parent:

```dart
// Build the union of all desired keys AND reject duplicates in ALL
// build modes. The union set IS the duplicate detector: `add` returning
// false means the key was already claimed, by this parent's list or by
// another's. This runs before the first syncChildren call below, so a
// rejected map mutates nothing in any build mode.
final union = _globallyDesiredChildren!;
for (final entry in desiredByParent.entries) {
  for (final c in entry.value) {
    if (!union.add(c.key)) {
      throw ArgumentError(_duplicateChildKeyMessage(desiredByParent, c.key));
    }
  }
}
```

`_duplicateChildKeyMessage` is a static helper reached ONLY on the throw path, so it can afford an O(input) rescan to name parents precisely: when every occurrence of the key sits under one parent `p` it returns `"Duplicate key <key> in syncMultipleChildren(p)"`, matching `_assertNoDuplicateKeys`'s wording at `:526` for the identical caller mistake; otherwise it returns the existing cross-parent text from `:804-808` with the offending parents named.

`ArgumentError`, not `FlutterError`. This is caller-argument validation, and this file already answers that class of input the same way twice: `_assertNoDuplicateKeys` throws `ArgumentError` at `:526`, and `_collectDesiredDescendants` throws `ArgumentError` at `:1036-1039` for its DAG case, which its doc names "same key under two parents" at `:1022`, inside the DAG clause that runs `:1021-1023` (`:1019-1020` is the CYCLE half of the same paragraph, `a` yielding `b` yielding `a`). That is the very input shape at issue here. `FlutterError` is a framework-diagnostics type (`flutter/lib/src/foundation/assertions.dart:752`); keeping it would leave `syncChildren([x, x])` and `syncMultipleChildren({"p": [x, x]})` throwing different types for one user error.

Validating into the PUBLISHED field is safe here, despite the warning at `:1011-1016` that `_collectDesiredDescendants` must never validate through `_globallyDesiredChildren`. That warning is about the `syncRoots` path, where collection happens outside the publication window at `:360-367`, so a throw there would strand the field. Here the field is assigned at `:793` before the `try` at `:794`, and the `finally` at `:855-859` nulls it on any throw, so a rejected map cannot strand it.

`_assertNoDuplicateKeys` at `:497` stays unchanged: it still guards the direct `syncChildren` and `syncRoots` entry points. On this path it becomes unable to fire, since the union already rejected any repeat, but it still runs.

**Alternatives considered.**

- **(a) Promote the assert block to an unconditional check, unchanged in shape.** Correct but strictly worse on both axes. It keeps a second `seenKeys` set and a second full traversal that the union loop at `:815-819` then immediately repeats, so release pays one extra set plus one extra hash `add` per child forever. It also forces the exception question without offering a good answer: keeping BOTH the `FlutterError` type and the `:803-809` message makes debug behaviour bit-identical to today, so no `flutter test` case could tell fixed from unfixed code and rubric 9 would have to be answered "none". Changing the type to `ArgumentError` while keeping the extra set is (c) minus the performance win.
- **(b) Keep the check assert-only and fix only its message and scope.** Rejected, and the release path is not a cosmetic gap. Shape 1 leaves the tree half-synced with the sync controller's scratch fields drained by `:855-859`; shape 2 silently reparents a node out of a subtree the caller asked to keep. Validation that runs only where a developer is watching is not validation, and this file already applies that exact reasoning to the unknown-parent guard at `:498-501`, which is deliberately unconditional because the release build is where the corruption lands.
- **Routing `:833-835` at `_syncChildrenImpl` (`:533`)** to skip the now-unfireable `_assertNoDuplicateKeys` and the nested batch. Behaviour-preserving (`runBatch` is depth-refcounted, `tree_controller.dart:2208-2213`), but it widens a validation fix into a control-flow change on the bulk entry point and drops the unknown-parent guard at `:502-503` unless that is inlined. Land separately if `:523`'s per-parent set ever shows up in a profile.
- **A rollback or undo wrapper around the loop.** There is no rollback primitive on `TreeController`, and a partial undo is strictly worse than never starting.

**Architecture fit.** Restores the file's own boundary-validation pattern (`:171-175`, `:497-507`) to the third entry point, and reuses the exact idiom `_collectDesiredDescendants` already uses at `:1035-1039`: the set being built anyway IS the duplicate detector. The diff loop at `:833-835` goes back to being mutation-only.

**Performance.** Cheaper than today in debug, near-free in release. Debug LOSES a whole traversal and a whole `Set<TKey>`, because `:798-814` and its `:799` set are deleted and the union loop absorbs the check. Release GAINS one branch per child, on an `add` it already performs at `:817`, with no allocation. The precise message costs an O(input) rescan only on the throw path. `syncChildren` at `:834` still allocates its own `Set<TKey>` at `:523` for every parent with two or more children; this change neither adds to nor removes that.

**Risk.** Two behaviour changes, stated per build mode and per input shape.

- Exception TYPE, debug, BOTH shapes: `FlutterError` (`:803`) becomes `ArgumentError`. `FlutterError extends Error with DiagnosticableTreeMixin implements AssertionError` (`flutter/lib/src/foundation/assertions.dart:752`) and `ArgumentError extends Error` (dart-sdk `lib/core/errors.dart:163`) are unrelated types, so `isA<FlutterError>()` stops matching. Exactly one in-repo test pins it and MUST be updated in the same commit: `tier1_partials_test.dart:115-122`, where `throwsA(isA<FlutterError>())` at `:120` becomes `throwsArgumentError`. `sync_duplicate_keys_test.dart:32,55` already use `throwsArgumentError` with no message pattern and are unaffected.
- Exception MESSAGE: unchanged text for a genuine cross-parent duplicate; corrected text for a within-one-list duplicate, which today misreports itself as cross-parent (`:804-805`).
- Release, shape 1: the same `ArgumentError` is thrown earlier, before any parent is synced, instead of after parents 1..k-1.
- Release, shape 2: a NEW throw where the call previously completed with last-write-wins. This is the intended fix, and the doc at `:781-785` must be rewritten to drop "Debug builds assert against this; release builds silently apply last-write-wins". No in-lib caller exists (`grep -rn syncMultipleChildren lib/` hits only `tree_sync_controller.dart`, at `:109`, `:347`, `:478`, `:481`, `:788`, `:804`), so this reaches app code only, for input the same doc already calls illegal.
- In-repo callers, measured (`grep -rn "\.syncMultipleChildren(" test/` = 10 call sites across 4 files): `batch_notification_test.dart:478`, `sync_multiple_children_subtree_test.dart:45,83,113`, `tree_sync_controller_test.dart:317,349,393,1016`, and `tier1_partials_test.dart:116,147`. Only `:116` passes a duplicate map, deliberately; `:147` is that group's negative control, distinct keys per parent asserted `returnsNormally` (`:146-152`), and it stays green because the union's `add` never rejects a key it has not already seen.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/sync_duplicate_keys_test.dart`, two legs, both of which FAIL on today's code.

Leg 1, duplicate within ONE list: with roots "A" and "B" already synced, `sync.syncMultipleChildren({"A": [TreeNode(key: "c1", data: "1")], "B": [TreeNode(key: "x", data: "1"), TreeNode(key: "x", data: "2")]})` expects `throwsA(isA<ArgumentError>().having((e) => e.message.toString(), "message", contains("syncMultipleChildren(B)")))`. It fails today because the global `seenKeys` at `:799` catches the repeat first and throws `FlutterError` at `:803`, which is not an `ArgumentError` and whose text says "appears under more than one parent" instead.

Leg 2, duplicate ACROSS parents: `{"p1": [TreeNode(key: "x", data: "X")], "p2": [TreeNode(key: "x", data: "X")]}` expects `throwsArgumentError`. It fails today for the same reason `tier1_partials_test.dart:120` passes today: the throw is a `FlutterError`.

Supplementary, and explicitly NOT a discriminator: after leg 1, assert `controller.getLiveChildren("A")` (`tree_controller.dart:1156`) is unchanged, with a setup sanity assertion that A's live children differ from the desired list so the check is not vacuous. This assertion holds BEFORE and AFTER the fix, because under `flutter test` asserts are enabled and `:798-814` already throws ahead of `:834`. It is kept as the debug-expressible statement of the release-mode property this block exists to fix; the release path itself is not reachable from `flutter test`, so no test here pins it directly, and the type and message legs above are what pin the code actually changing.

**Effort.** S.

### L17. startDrag does not re-check _session after cancelDrag

**Finding.** `tree_reorder_controller.dart:295-297` calls `cancelDrag()` and never re-reads `_session`; `cancelDrag` nulls `_session` at `:866` and fires `notifyListeners()` at `:867`, so a listener can start a nested session that `:368` then overwrites.

**Root cause.** `_session = session` at `:368` is an unconditional assignment. A nested `startDrag` that ran during the `:867` notification has already executed `renderPort.pinNode` (`:374`), `session.subscribeScroll` (`:375`, subscribing at `_drag_session.dart:316-320`) and `session.resolve()` (`:380`, which can start the `AutoScroller` ticker via `evaluate` at `_drag_session_behaviors.dart:87-91`). The overwrite drops that session without `detachAll`, and `detachAll` (`_drag_session.dart:358-370`) is the sole owner of ticker disposal (`:359` into behaviors `:147-150`), scroll unsubscription (`:360-365`) and `unpinNode` (`:369`).

The notification is UNBOUNDED, which is what kills the obvious fix. `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners` has no once-per-call gate; it explicitly SUPPORTS recursive dispatch, tracking depth in `_notificationCallStackDepth` (`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/foundation/change_notifier.dart:424-430`, incremented at `:430`, decremented at `:455`). So every `cancelDrag()` re-runs every listener, and a listener that starts a session on each `isDragging` false transition starts another one inside each cancel.

**Solution.** Make `startDrag` NON-REENTRANT with an explicit guard. Add the field beside `_session` (`:162`):

```dart
/// Re-entrancy guard for [startDrag]. See the refusal branch there.
bool _startingDrag = false;
```

and wrap the whole body, with the refusal as the first statement, before the `drivesController` check at `:281`:

```dart
if (_startingDrag) {
  // Re-entered from a listener that ran inside THIS call's own
  // `cancelDrag()` notification. `ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners`
  // supports recursive dispatch (change_notifier.dart:424-430), so
```
