```dart
  // cancelling again just re-runs the same listener; there is no
  // terminating "cancel until quiet" form. Meanwhile the unconditional
  // `_session = session` below would strand each nested session's pin,
  // scroll subscription and autoscroll ticker, none of which has an
  // owner other than `DragSession.detachAll`. The outer,
  // user-initiated drag wins.
  return false;
}
_startingDrag = true;
try {
  // ... the existing body, unchanged ...
} finally {
  _startingDrag = false;
}
```

The guard covers the WHOLE body, not just the `:295-297` cancel window. `notifyListeners()` at `:382` is a second re-entry point: a nested start there would `cancelDrag` the session this call assigned one line earlier and install its own, so the outer call would return `true` about a session that no longer exists. Refusing re-entry outright is the only form that leaves no such window.

**Rule for the implementer.** `startDrag` starts at most one session per call and refuses re-entry with `false`. Any future public mutator on this controller that both notifies and assigns `_session` needs the same treatment.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **A second `cancelDrag()` after `:297`** (the earlier draft, and the audit is right to reject it). Not terminating: the second call's `notifyListeners()` at `:867` runs the same listener a third time, which starts a third session, which `:368` strands exactly as before. The block's own test still fails after that "fix".
- **`while (_session != null) { cancelDrag(); }`.** Same defect for the same reason, expressed as a spin instead of a recursion. Bounding the loop iteration count would refuse the nested session anyway, at which point the guard is the honest way to say so.
- **Deferring `cancelDrag`'s `notifyListeners()` to a microtask.** Fixes this and breaks the widget layer's synchronous teardown contract: `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:1430-1436` documents that end/cancel deliberately drive `_onControllerChanged` through that notify rather than calling the owner's teardown directly.

**Architecture fit.** Preserves the invariant the session architecture is built on: `detachAll` is reached exactly once per constructed session (`_drag_session.dart:350-370`). With the guard, no second session is ever constructed, so there is nothing extra to tear down. `endDrag`'s post-app-code identity re-check at `:510-512` is the existing precedent for defending the commit script against listener re-entry; this is the same defence at the other end.

**Performance.** One bool test and one `try`/`finally` on the drag-start path.

**Risk.** Behaviour changes only for a re-entrant `startDrag`, which no in-repo caller performs (22 test files call `startDrag`; none from a controller listener). `endDrag`'s guard at `:510-512` is untouched. Candidate tests to re-run: `external_cancel_drag_test.dart`, `reorder_controller_swap_mid_drag_test.dart`, `drag_backstop_deactivate_test.dart`, `tree_reorder_controller_test.dart`.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/external_cancel_drag_test.dart`: start a drag on "a"; add a controller listener that calls `reorder.startDrag(key: "b", ...)` and bumps a counter whenever `isDragging` goes false; then call `startDrag(key: "c", ...)`. Assert (1) the outer call returned `true`, (2) `reorder.draggedKey == "c"` (public getter, `tree_reorder_controller.dart:194`), and (3) the scripted port's log contains no unbalanced `pin:b` (`reorder_render_port_test.dart`'s `_FakePort` already records `pin:$key` / `unpin:$key` into a `log` list at `:85-92`; reuse that shape). Setup sanity: assert the listener counter is non-zero, so a pass cannot come from the listener never running.

**Effort.** S.

### L18. startDrag accepts a pending-deletion or unknown key

**Finding.** `startDrag`'s gate chain is `drivesController` (`tree_reorder_controller.dart:281-288`), `isLaidOut` (`:289-291`), `canReorder` (`:292-294`) and a non-null pointer sample (`:302-307`). Existence and pending-deletion are checked only at commit, in `_canCommit` (`:654-657`).

**Root cause.** `startDrag` reimplements a subset of the policy `_canCommit` owns, instead of reusing it. `moveTo` calls `_canCommit` up front at `:755-757`; `startDrag` does not.

**Solution.** Replace the standalone `canReorder` check at `:292-294` with the shared predicate, parameterised on the key's CURRENT parent so the destination half of `_canCommit` is a tautology at start:

```dart
if (!_canCommit(key, treeController.getParent(key))) {
  return false;
}
```

`_canCommit` runs `canReorder` (`:651-653`), then existence and pending-deletion on `key` (`:654-657`); with `newParent` equal to the key's current parent the remaining clauses (`:661-664`) hold by construction for any live tree. Spelled out, because "by construction" is doing real work here: `getNodeData(newParent) != null` holds because a live key's parent is live; `!isPendingDeletion(newParent)` holds because `remove` marks `[key, ...descendants]` pending deletion together (`tree_controller.dart:3103`, `:3111-3113`), so a pending-deletion parent implies a pending-deletion child and `:655` has already refused; `newParent != key` and `!isStrictDescendantOf(newParent, key)` hold because a node is neither its own parent nor a descendant of itself. So this is a strict widening of the current gate with no new refusals for valid keys.

Update `startDrag`'s doc at `:240-244`. The two new false cases are UNKNOWN and PENDING DELETION, not "animating out": only pending deletion refuses. A row exiting because an ancestor collapsed is animating out and is NOT pending deletion (`tree_controller.dart:4004` skips pending-deletion nodes, and `:4007` starts a standalone exit for the rest), so `_canCommit` accepts it and the drag starts. Exact replacement for that paragraph:

> Returns `true` when the session started. Returns `false`, starting
> nothing, when [canReorder] refuses [key], when [key] is unknown to
> [treeController] or is pending deletion (mid-remove; a row merely
> animating out under a collapsing ancestor is NOT pending deletion and
> still drags), or when [renderPort] has not been laid out yet (no
> painted rows to resolve against). A policy refusal is a normal runtime
> answer, not misuse, so it is a return value rather than an exception.

**Alternatives considered.** Adding two inline checks rather than reusing `_canCommit` duplicates policy that `:641-649` explicitly exists to keep single-sourced.

**Architecture fit.** Restores the documented "shared by the drag commit script and `moveTo` so the two cannot drift" contract at `:641-644` to the third entry point.

**Performance.** One extra `getParent` plus one `_canCommit` body per drag start. That body is NOT "three O(1) reads", as an earlier draft claimed. For a key with a null parent it is `getNodeData(key)` + `isPendingDeletion(key)` and an early `return true` at `:658-659`. For a key with a non-null parent it additionally runs `getNodeData(newParent)`, `isPendingDeletion(newParent)`, `newParent != key` and `_resolver.isStrictDescendantOf(newParent, key)` (`_drop_zone_resolver.dart:757-766`), the last being an allocation-free O(depth) ancestor walk. Once per drag start, against a walk the resolver already runs up to three times per POINTER MOVE (`_drop_zone_resolver.dart:750-753`), so it is not a hot-path cost. If it ever mattered, the cheaper equivalent is `_canCommit(key, null)`, a strict subset of these checks that still covers both new refusals; the current-parent form is preferred because it keeps the call site honest about the question it is asking.

**Risk.** `canReorder` is already invoked at this point today, so app code sees no new callback. Pointer-path drags cannot reach the new refusals (hit-testing skips exiting rows, `render_sliver_tree.dart:4182`), so only programmatic callers can observe the change. Tests calling `startDrag`: 22 files (`grep -rln startDrag test/sliver_tree` = audit_repro_f42/f43/f44, auto_expand_dwell, below_zone_expanded_parent, can_reorder_flip_mid_drag, can_reorder_no_detector, drag_backstop_deactivate, drag_handle_audit, drag_handle_probe_and_multitouch, drag_proxy, external_cancel_drag, refused_gutter_is_inert, reorder_commit_path, reorder_controller_swap_mid_drag, reorder_render_port, reorder_tuning_liveness, sliver_reorderable_tree_widget, synced_reorder, sync_deferral_during_drag, touch_probe, tree_reorder_controller). All start drags on live keys.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/tree_reorder_controller_test.dart`, in the existing `"startDrag validation"` group (`:97`): `remove(key: "b", animate: true)`, sanity-assert `isPendingDeletion("b")` is true and `visibleNodes` still contains "b", then `expect(reorder.startDrag(key: "b", ...), false)` and `expect(reorder.isDragging, false)`. Second leg for an unknown key. Third leg, the negative control that pins the doc's distinction: with a nested subtree expanded, `collapse("p")` with animation live, sanity-assert a descendant of "p" is exiting but NOT pending deletion, and assert `startDrag` on that descendant returns `true`.

**Effort.** S.

### L19. _applyMove returns the unclamped index on the cross-parent path

**Finding.** `_applyMove`'s contract at `tree_reorder_controller.dart:667-670` says the returned index is "RESOLVED ... so an out-of-range request cannot be published as though it were a real position". The same-parent branch clamps at `:703` and returns `insertAt` (`:714`); the cross-parent branch at `:716-719` returns the caller's raw `index`.

**Root cause.** `moveNode` clamps internally and silently: `_liveIndexToFullInsertIndex` clamps at `tree_controller.dart:2619` (and returns `fullList.length` at `:2634` on the pending-deletion path), and the insert falls through to `.add` at `:3550`/`:3559` when the resolved position is past the end. So the node lands at the append position while `onReorder` reports the request.

**Solution.** Mirror `moveTo`'s clamp (`:762-769`) inside `_applyMove`'s cross-parent branch:

```dart
// Cross-parent: moveNode's `index` is already the position in the new
// parent's final child list, and moveNode clamps it silently, so clamp
// here too and report where the node actually landed.
final destinationLength = newParent == null
    ? treeController.liveRootCount
    : treeController.liveChildCount(newParent);
final insertAt = index.clamp(0, destinationLength);
treeController.moveNode(key, newParent, index: insertAt, animate: animate);
return (key: key, newParent: newParent, index: insertAt);
```

`destinationLength` is the FINAL list bound (the moved key is not yet a member), matching `moveTo`'s `sameParent ? destinationLength - 1 : destinationLength` at `:768`. `liveRootCount` (`tree_controller.dart:1192`) and `liveChildCount` (`:1208`) are the same accessors `moveTo` uses.

**Alternatives considered.** Having `moveNode` return the resolved index: that changes a public void-returning mutator's signature and every call site, for a contract only this method advertises.

**Architecture fit.** Live-space index contract; `_applyMove` becomes the single clamp site that `moveTo`'s pre-clamp and `endDrag`'s no-op guard (`:528-541`) both agree with, which is what `:524-527` already asks for in prose.

**Performance.** One live-count read per cross-parent commit, O(1) on the dominant path: `liveRootCount` short-circuits on `_anim.pendingDeletionCount == 0` (`tree_controller.dart:1193-1195`) and `liveChildCount` likewise (`:1213-1215`); each falls back to an O(list) scan (`:1196-1202`, `:1216-1222`) only while pending deletions exist anywhere.

**Risk.** Only `onReorder`'s reported index changes, and only for an out-of-range request. `moveTo` (`:781-783`) already clamps upstream so its report is unchanged. Existing tests asserting the reported index: `reorder_commit_path_test.dart`, `synced_reorder_test.dart`, `tree_reorder_controller_test.dart`; all commit in-range targets today.

**Test to add.** Decided: writable, no test-only shim, and here is the exact shape. It goes in `test/sliver_tree/reorder_commit_path_test.dart`, whose `_FakePort` (`:25`) already scripts `findRowAtPaintedY`.

The reachable window is `endDrag`'s own script. It re-resolves at `:495`, capturing `target.indexInFinalList`; then `_canCommit` calls `canReorder`, which is APP CODE, at `:651`; and only then commits at `:604-609` with the index captured BEFORE that call. The file's own comment at `:503-509` already names "canReorder is app code" as the hazard it defends against, and the guard installed for it (`:510-512`) covers session teardown, not a structural change. `DropZoneResolver` itself cannot emit an out-of-range index at resolution time (`_buildTarget` refuses `rawIndex < 0` at `_drop_zone_resolver.dart:656-658` and derives the rest from live sibling positions), which is exactly why the window has to be opened at commit time.

So: drive a cross-parent drop whose destination parent has N live children; install a `canReorder` that, on its commit-time invocation, calls `treeController.remove(key: <a destination child>, animate: false)` and returns `true`; assert (a) `onReorder` reports the CLAMPED index rather than the stale resolved one, and (b) `treeController.getIndexInParent(movedKey)` equals the reported index. Setup sanity: assert the destination's live child count strictly dropped between resolve and commit, and that the captured `indexInFinalList` exceeded the post-removal live count, so neither assertion is vacuous.

Rejected: (1) a `@visibleForTesting` shim on `_applyMove`, which adds test-only public surface to THE mutation site for a case the commit script can already construct; (2) injecting a scripted `DropZoneResolver`, because `_resolver` is a `late final` private field with no injection point (`tree_reorder_controller.dart:154-157`), so this would mean a new public constructor parameter existing only for tests; (3) `moveTo(key, otherParent, index: 999)`, because `moveTo` pre-clamps at `:766-769` and can never deliver an out-of-range index to `_applyMove`, and the four semantics moves all route through it.

**Effort.** S.

### L20. Autoscroll ticker keeps scheduling frames while parked at an extent

**Finding.** `AutoScroller._onTick` (`_drag_session_behaviors.dart:109-143`) stops only when `velocity == 0` (`:125-128`). With the finger in the edge zone and `position.pixels` already at `maxScrollExtent`, velocity is non-zero, `newPixels` clamps to the same value at `:135-136`, `:137` skips the `jumpTo`, and the ticker keeps requesting a frame every vsync for the rest of the drag.

**Root cause.** The stop condition tests the velocity ramp, not whether the scroll can move. Flutter's `EdgeDraggingAutoScroller` tests both: its two direction branches each require `pixels > minScrollExtent` / `pixels < maxScrollExtent` (`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/scrollable_helpers.dart:262-296`), and `_scroll` sets `_scrolling = false` and returns when `newOffset` is null or moves less than 1 px (`:299-303`).

**Solution. The stop test goes in `_onTick` ONLY, and it takes one grace tick.**

Decision stated first, because the obvious form of this fix is a regression: **`evaluate` (`:79-95`) is not touched.** It keeps arming on edge-zone membership alone. A `canScroll` gate there reads `position.maxScrollExtent` from outside a tick, where it is one layout stale, and converts a behaviour that works today into a permanent stall; the trace is under Alternatives.

Add one field beside `_lastTick` (`:51`):

```dart
/// The extent the previous tick was travelling toward
/// (`minScrollExtent` when scrolling up, `maxScrollExtent` when
/// scrolling down), or null when this is the first tick since the
/// ticker was armed. See the parked branch in [_onTick]: a tick is a
/// TRANSIENT frame callback, so it reads the extents the PREVIOUS
/// frame's layout produced, and one grace tick is what makes "the
/// arm's own mutation has been laid out" true.
double? _lastLimit;
```

Clear it wherever `_lastTick` is cleared, so a re-arm always gets its grace tick: `_stop()` (`:99-104`, beside `_lastTick = null` at `:103`) and the arm in `evaluate` (`:89`).

Replace `_onTick`'s tail (`:130-142`) with:

```dart
final limit = velocity < 0
    ? position.minScrollExtent
    : position.maxScrollExtent;
final previousLimit = _lastLimit;
_lastLimit = limit;

final dt = _lastTick == null
    ? const Duration(milliseconds: 16)
    : elapsed - _lastTick!;
_lastTick = elapsed;

final newPixels = (position.pixels + velocity * dt.inMicroseconds / 1e6)
    .clamp(position.minScrollExtent, position.maxScrollExtent);
if (newPixels != position.pixels) {
  // jumpTo synchronously notifies the session's scroll-position
  // listener, which re-resolves the target and coalesces the
  // notification: one re-resolution path for every scroll source.
  position.jumpTo(newPixels);
  return;
}
// PARKED: the clamp ate the whole step, so nothing moved. Stop
// rather than request a frame per vsync for the rest of the drag,
// but only once the SAME limit has been seen on two consecutive
// ticks. A ticker callback is a transient frame callback, so it
// reads the extents the PREVIOUS frame's layout produced: a tick
// that fires in the same frame as a content mutation still sees the
// pre-mutation limit. The two-tick rule is what keeps the dwell
// auto-expand working. [DwellExpander] expands and calls
// `_requestResolve()` synchronously inside its timer callback
// (`:227-231`), re-arming this ticker before any layout has run, so
// tick 1 necessarily reads the stale limit and tick 2 is the first
// that can read the grown one. Content that keeps growing (an
// animated expand) keeps changing the limit, so the ticker keeps
// running for the whole animation instead of for a fixed count.
if (previousLimit == limit) {
  _stop();
}
```

**Re-arm coverage, traced rather than asserted.** `evaluate` is unchanged, so every path that re-arms today still re-arms: it starts an idle ticker whenever the sample is in an edge zone. It is called only from `DragSession.resolve()` (`_drag_session.dart:335`), reached from `startDrag` (`tree_reorder_controller.dart:380`), `updateDrag` (`:464`), `_onScrollPositionChanged` (`:389-395`) and `DwellExpander`'s post-expand `_requestResolve` (`_drag_session_behaviors.dart:231`).

The dwell case, step by step, because it is the one that breaks the obvious fix:

1. The dwell timer fires between frames. It calls `_treeController.expand` (`:227`), which schedules a frame, then `_requestResolve()` (`:231`).
2. `resolve()` reaches `evaluate`; the sample is still in the edge zone; the ticker is idle (it parked earlier); it starts, clearing `_lastTick` and `_lastLimit`.
3. Frame N, TRANSIENT phase: tick 1. `position.maxScrollExtent` is still the pre-expand value, because `applyContentDimensions` runs during layout, a PERSISTENT callback later in the same frame. Nothing moves; `previousLimit` is null, so the tick does not stop.
4. Frame N, persistent phase: layout runs and `applyContentDimensions` raises `maxScrollExtent`.
5. Frame N+1: tick 2 reads the grown limit, `newPixels > pixels`, `jumpTo`. Autoscroll resumes.

**The residual, and it is real.** An EXTERNAL content growth (a sync adding rows) while the finger is completely stationary and the ticker has already parked does not re-arm. A pure extent change dispatches a `ScrollMetricsNotification` via `scheduleMicrotask(didUpdateScrollMetrics)` (`flutter/.../scroll_position.dart:670-680`, dispatched at `:1081-1091`) and never calls `notifyListeners()`, which is what the session subscribes to (`_drag_session.dart:316-320`). Any pointer move re-arms it, and the grace tick then observes the grown extent. `EdgeDraggingAutoScroller` has the identical exposure: it clears `_scrolling` when a step moves less than 1 px (`scrollable_helpers.dart:299-303`) and re-arms only from `startAutoScrollIfNecessary` (`:212-221`), which the drag update calls. Accept it and say so in `evaluate`'s doc.

**Alternatives considered.**

- **Gating the ARM on `canScroll` inside `evaluate`** (the earlier draft of this block: start only when `velocity < 0 && pixels > minScrollExtent || velocity > 0 && pixels < maxScrollExtent`). Rejected: it turns a behaviour that works today into a permanent stall. At step 2 above the predicate reads the pre-expand `maxScrollExtent` with `pixels` already sitting on it, so it refuses to start; the grown extent then arrives through `applyContentDimensions`, which only schedules the metrics notification above and never notifies the session's listener, so nothing re-evaluates and the drag never autoscrolls again. Today the ticker is simply still running and step 5 happens anyway.
- **Stopping on the FIRST immobile tick** (no grace tick). Same stall, one frame later: tick 1 at step 3 is immobile against the stale limit and would stop before step 4's layout ever raised it.
- **Re-evaluating from the structural or animation notification channel.** Neither can observe the answer. `expand` fires its structural notification synchronously inside step 1, before any layout; the animation channel is driven by ticker callbacks, which are transient and therefore also pre-layout. A post-frame callback could see it, but that puts frame scheduling inside `DwellExpander` for a case the grace tick already covers, and it would leave the same hole for every non-dwell growth.
- **Keeping today's always-ticking behaviour and narrowing the fix to the frame-scheduling cost.** There is nothing to narrow: the ticker IS the frame request, so "keep ticking, schedule fewer frames" is not a reachable state. That option is "withdraw L20", which is a legitimate outcome and is the one to take if the two-frame idle latency ever proves unacceptable.
- **Counting N consecutive immobile ticks instead of comparing the limit.** Same two-frame cost with a magic constant and no reason attached. The limit comparison states exactly what it is waiting for (the previous frame's layout produced the same bound) and, unlike a fixed count, keeps ticking for the whole of a progressively growing expand.

**Rule for the implementer.** The ARM asks only "is the finger in an edge zone". The STOP asks "did this tick move the position, and was the bound it hit the same bound the previous tick hit". Never put a scroll-extent test in `evaluate`: an extent read outside a tick is one layout stale.

**Architecture fit.** `AutoScroller` still owns "when does the ticker run", and the new state is one nullable double next to `_lastTick`, cleared by the same `_stop`. `PointerSpace.position` stays the only scrollable access (`_drag_session.dart:69-74`).

**Performance.** Removes one scheduled frame per vsync for the whole time a finger is parked in an edge zone at an extent, which is a common end-of-drag state, at a cost of two frames of latency before the ticker idles. Per tick: one branch, one double compare, one double store. `evaluate` is unchanged, so it costs nothing.

**Risk.** `AutoScroller.velocityAt` is `static` and separately tested; the change is confined to `_onTick`, which `drag_session_unit_test.dart` and `policy_flip_offscreen_autoscroll_test.dart` drive. `policy_flip_offscreen_autoscroll_test.dart` depends on autoscroll running while a row is off-cache: if any of its cases park at an extent, the ticker now idles after two ticks, so re-check its pump counts. `reorder_tuning_liveness_test.dart` covers `autoScrollEdgeZone`/`autoScrollMaxVelocity` liveness and is unaffected, since the arm predicate is untouched.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/drag_session_unit_test.dart`, a new `AutoScroller ticker lifecycle` group beside the existing `AutoScroller.velocityAt` group (`:383`). Both legs build a real `ScrollableState` the way the `PointerSpace` group does (`:419-431`), so `PointerSpace` runs over a live position, and both need `@visibleForTesting bool get debugTicking => _ticker.isActive;` on `AutoScroller`.

Leg 1, the discriminator. 30 rows of 50 px in a 600 px viewport (`maxScrollExtent` 900), `position.jumpTo(900)`, construct the `AutoScroller` with `tester` as the `TickerProvider`, and `evaluate` a sample inside the trailing edge zone. Setup sanity, which must hold both before and after the fix because the arm predicate is unchanged: `debugTicking` is true immediately after the `evaluate`, and `position.pixels == position.maxScrollExtent`. Then `await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 16))` twice and assert `debugTicking` is false with `position.pixels` still 900. FAILS today, because `_onTick` returns at `:137` without stopping whenever the clamp ate the step, so the ticker stays active on every subsequent vsync and `debugTicking` is still true.

Leg 2, the dwell control, in the exact frame ordering a dwell produces. Straight after leg 1 has parked and stopped: call `evaluate` again with the SAME edge-zone sample, which is what `_requestResolve` does; sanity-assert `debugTicking` is true; then `await tester.pumpWidget(sameAppWith60Rows, duration: const Duration(milliseconds: 16))`, one frame whose transient phase carries tick 1 against the stale 900 and whose persistent phase raises `maxScrollExtent` to 2400; then `await tester.pump(const Duration(milliseconds: 16))` for tick 2. Assert `position.pixels > 900`. The same `ListView` in the same position keeps the same `ScrollableState`, so the `PointerSpace` stays valid across the rebuild. This leg PASSES on today's code, since the ticker never stopped, and that is exactly why it is worth keeping: it FAILS on the rejected `canScroll`-in-`evaluate` design and on the no-grace-tick design, so it is the assertion that pins the decision above.

**Effort.** S.

### L21. A drag started on a sticky-pinned header probes the content beneath the strip

**Finding.** `DragProbe.captureGrab` asks `_renderPort.paintedRowBounds(_draggedKey)` (`_drag_session.dart:171`), which substitutes the pinned band (`render_sliver_tree.dart:1945-1954` delegating to `_anchorPaintedBounds`, whose sticky branch returns `info.pinnedY`/`info.extent` at `:3969-3974`). `DragProbe.resolveTarget` asks `_renderPort.findRowAtPaintedY(probeY)` (`_drag_session.dart:219`), which has no sticky awareness (`render_sliver_tree.dart:1871-1925`). The port's own doc says the two are "NOT interchangeable at a sticky header" (`reorder_render_port.dart:62-73`).

**Root cause.** The "derived invariant" at `_drag_session.dart:144-146` ("at drag start the probe is the dragged row's OWN midpoint, because the grab position cancels out") is only true when `paintedRowBounds` and `findRowAtPaintedY` agree. For a pinned header, `grabDy = start.sliverY - pinnedBounds.paintedOffset` (`:177`) and `probeDy = pinnedBounds.extent / 2 - grabDy` (`:180`), so `probeY = pinnedBounds.paintedOffset + extent / 2`, a sliver-local y that `findRowAtPaintedY` resolves against STRUCTURAL offsets and answers with whatever row is scrolled beneath the strip. Verified arithmetically against `sticky_grab_geometry_test.dart`'s setup (header 40 px, rows 50 px, scrolled to 300): grabbing the header 12 px down probes at 312 (or 320 with the midpoint probe), which lands on item `i5`.

**Solution.** Give the port a sticky-band lookup and let the probe consult it first, exactly as `hitTestChildren` Phase 1 already does (`render_sliver_tree.dart:4120-4153`).

1. Add to `ReorderRenderPort` (`reorder_render_port.dart`), documented as sliver-local like its neighbours:

```dart
/// The sticky-pinned row whose PAINTED band contains [scrollY], or null
/// when [scrollY] is not inside any pinned band. Mirrors the priority
/// `RenderSliverTree.hitTestChildren` already gives pinned headers: the
/// band is on top, so a pointer inside it is on the header, not on the
/// content scrolled underneath.
///
/// Filters pending-deletion rows and NOTHING ELSE. In particular it does
/// NOT apply the make-room lifted-range skip that [findRowAtPaintedY]
/// applies; see the decision recorded in this block.
({TKey key, double paintedOffset, double extent})? findPinnedRowAtPaintedY(
  double scrollY,
);
```

2. Implement in `RenderSliverTree` next to `paintedRowBounds` (`:1945`), scanning `_sticky.headers` (bounded by `maxStickyDepth`) shallowest-first and converting paint space to sliver-local by adding `constraints.scrollOffset`, the same conversion `paintedRowBounds` performs at `:1951`:

```dart
@override
({TKey key, double paintedOffset, double extent})? findPinnedRowAtPaintedY(
  double scrollY,
) {
  if (_sticky.headers.isEmpty) return null;
  final paintY = scrollY - constraints.scrollOffset;
  for (final sticky in _sticky.headers) {
    if (paintY < sticky.pinnedY) continue;
    if (paintY >= sticky.pinnedY + sticky.extent) continue;
    if (controller.isPendingDeletion(sticky.nodeId)) continue;
    return (
      key: sticky.nodeId,
      paintedOffset: sticky.pinnedY + constraints.scrollOffset,
      extent: sticky.extent,
    );
  }
  return null;
}
```

3. In `DragProbe.resolveTarget` (`_drag_session.dart:210-247`), try it before `findRowAtPaintedY` at `:219`:

```dart
final hovered =
    _renderPort.findPinnedRowAtPaintedY(probeY) ??
    _renderPort.findRowAtPaintedY(probeY);
```

The make-room gap branch at `:232-237` stays below it and is unaffected: a pinned hit never satisfies `probeY < hovered.paintedOffset`.

4. Correct the invariant prose at `:144-146` to state what is now true ("the pinned-band lookup is what makes this hold when the grabbed row is a pinned header") and update `reorder_render_port.dart:62-73` so it stops describing the divergence as the contract.

Consequence to state in the doc rather than hide: while the pointer is inside a pinned band, the resolved slot is the header's, so `gapVisibleIndex` points at the header's STRUCTURAL visible index, which may be scrolled off-screen and the make-room gap therefore opens where the user cannot see it. That is the same trade `hitTestChildren` already takes, and it is strictly better than resolving against an unrelated row.

**Decision: `findPinnedRowAtPaintedY` does NOT get M11's lifted skip.** M11's block hands L21 a requirement it recorded as unverified: "whoever lands L21 must confirm the pinned scan reaches the lifted row and apply the same skip if it does." Both halves, answered here, so the implementer inherits a decision and not a question.

*It does reach it.* `computeStickyHeaders` runs inside `performLayout` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2913`, `:3014`) off structure and layout offsets. The make-room preview is paint-only and changes neither (`setReorderPreviewAtIndex`'s own doc, `tree_controller.dart:1680-1682`: "Structure never changes ... layout is untouched"), and `StickyHeaderComputer` reads no slide or preview state at all (`grep -c "getSlideDelta\|slideDelta\|Slide\|preview\|Preview" lib/sliver_tree/_sticky_header_computer.dart` = 0, measured this session). So a pinned header that is itself the dragged row stays in `_sticky.headers` for the whole drag, and the new member would hand it back.

*It does not get the skip.* Three reasons.

1. **Applying it destroys the fix.** The one case L21 exists to serve is a drag STARTED on a pinned header, where the dragged row IS the lifted row. A skip there returns null on every resolve after the preview installs, the `??` falls through to `findRowAtPaintedY`, which M11 has just taught to skip that same range, and the probe lands on the content scrolled beneath the strip: the original L21 bug with one extra hop, plus a make-room gap opened under the strip at a row the user never pointed at.
2. **The own-slot answer is the correct state.** It is what `DragProbe`'s derived invariant already promises (`_drag_session.dart:144-146`) and what this block's own test asserts on the first resolve.
3. **The case the skip would have guarded is already inert.** A pinned header that is a strict DESCENDANT of the dragged row is reachable at `maxStickyDepth >= 2` (drag a parent whose own expanded child is pinned). Resolving against it goes through `DropZoneResolver`, which refuses `into` on self or a strict descendant (`_drop_zone_resolver.dart:776-781`, and the same cycle filter at `:661-668`), leaving `above`/`below`, whose `gapVisibleIndex` necessarily lands in `[draggedIndex, draggedEnd]`. Every index in that range produces an ALL-ZERO target map at `tree_controller.dart:1764-1778`: rows before `draggedIndex` match neither clause, rows in `[draggedIndex, draggedEnd)` are skipped outright at `:1765-1767`, and rows at or after `draggedEnd` take `-lift` at `:1770` and `+lift` at `:1773`. No row moves, so the state is indistinguishable from an own-slot hover.

M11's own justification is the cleanest way to see why it does not transfer: M11 skips lifted rows because they are laid out but not painted WHERE they are laid out. A pinned header is not painted where it is laid out either way, drag or no drag, which is the entire reason this member exists. The pinned lookup answers "which header owns this band", not "which live row is painted at this y".

**Rule for the implementer.** The M11 lifted skip belongs to lookups that walk the VISIBLE ORDER: `findRowAtPaintedY` and its two scans. It does not belong to `findPinnedRowAtPaintedY`, which walks `_sticky.headers`. A future `ReorderRenderPort` member takes the skip if and only if it iterates the visible order.

**Alternatives considered.** Shifting the probe by `structural - pinned` for the dragged row only: the shift is a session constant while pinning is dynamic (the header unpins the moment it scrolls back), so it would be wrong for most of the drag. Applying M11's skip and compensating in `DragProbe` by re-trying the pinned lookup with the dragged key allowed: that reintroduces the dragged key into a port-level predicate the port deliberately does not know about, and it is a longer way of writing "no skip".

**Architecture fit.** Puts the sticky substitution behind the render port, where every other coordinate question already lives, and makes drop resolution agree with hit testing instead of contradicting it.

**Performance.** One loop over `_sticky.headers` (length bounded by `maxStickyDepth`, typically 1 to 2) per resolve, executed only when the set is non-empty; a `headers.isEmpty` early-out keeps the `maxStickyDepth: 0` default at one field read. No lifted-range read, since the skip is not applied.

**Sequencing dependency.** This plan's Sequencing section, Chain 6: M11 lands BEFORE L21. Both change what `findRowAtPaintedY` answers during a drag. M11 adds the lifted-range skip; L21 makes the probe consult a pinned-band lookup ahead of it. Landing L21 first means writing the `DragProbe.resolveTarget` edit against a function M11 then re-shapes, and re-deriving the sticky test's expected answer twice. M11's block records the same dependency from its side, with the pinned-scan question marked unverified; the Decision above closes it, and M11's paragraph should be amended to point at it when M11 lands.

**Risk.** `ReorderRenderPort` has EIGHT implementers in-repo, measured this session with `grep -rn "implements ReorderRenderPort" lib/ test/`: `RenderSliverTree` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:84-85`) plus SEVEN scripted test fakes. None of them uses `noSuchMethod` (`grep -rln noSuchMethod test/sliver_tree/` returns nothing), so all seven stop compiling the moment the new member lands and every one must gain it:

- `test/sliver_tree/auto_expand_dwell_test.dart:18`
- `test/sliver_tree/drag_proxy_test.dart:27`
- `test/sliver_tree/drag_session_unit_test.dart:29`
- `test/sliver_tree/reorder_commit_path_test.dart:25`
- `test/sliver_tree/reorder_render_port_test.dart:28`
- `test/sliver_tree/reorder_tuning_liveness_test.dart:22`
- `test/sliver_tree/touch_probe_test.dart:553`

Six of the seven script no sticky state and can return `null` unconditionally; only a fake driven by a sticky test needs a real answer. The interface's doc already says external implementation is unsupported (`reorder_render_port.dart:21-24`), so the out-of-repo blast radius is bounded by that statement. Behaviour changes for any drag whose pointer enters a pinned band, so `sticky_grab_geometry_test.dart`, `sticky_root_diff_repro_test.dart` and the sectioned reorder tests are the ones to re-run.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/sticky_grab_geometry_test.dart`, third case: same pinned-header setup, drag the pinned header, and assert `reorder.currentTarget!.targetKey == "s1"` on the first resolve. Setup sanity: assert `scroll.position.pixels > _kHeader` and that the structurally-underlying row is `i5`, so a passing assertion proves the pinned lookup and not a coincidence.

Second leg, which pins the Decision above rather than the lookup: pump one more pointer move that keeps the probe inside the pinned band, so the first resolve has already installed the make-room preview and set the lifted nid, and assert `reorder.currentTarget!.targetKey` is STILL `"s1"` and that `controller.previewLiftedStartIndex` is the header's visible index (proving the lifted range really does cover the row the lookup just answered with). Under the rejected "apply the skip" variant this leg answers `i5` instead. It is written against post-M11 code, so it belongs in the same commit as L21 and not earlier.

**Effort.** M.

### L22. DropSettler's cancel/fallback glide double-counts an in-flight FLIP

**Finding.** `_installReleaseGlide` builds `current[row.key] = (y: structuralY, x: structuralX)` at `_drag_session_behaviors.dart:490-499`, where `structuralY` is `TreeController.scrollOffsetOf` (a pure full-extent prefix sum, `_scroll_orchestrator.dart:128-136`) carrying no slide delta. The engine composes `composedY = existing.currentDelta + (prior.y - current.y)` at `_slide_animation_engine.dart:288`.

**Root cause.** The engine's contract is that BOTH maps are PAINTED positions: `TreeController.animateSlideFromOffsets`'s doc names `RenderSliverTree.snapshotVisibleOffsets` as the producer of both (`tree_controller.dart:1521-1527`), and that method adds `getSlideDeltaNid` into every entry (`render_sliver_tree.dart:1582`, `:1601`). Feeding a delta-free `current` makes the row paint at `structuralY + D + (releaseY - structuralY) = releaseY + D` at t=0 instead of `releaseY`, an offset of exactly the in-flight delta D.

**Solution.** Make `current` a painted position by adding the row's live slide deltas at `:490-499`:

```dart
for (final row in _stack) {
  final structuralY = _treeController.scrollOffsetOf(row.key);
  if (structuralY == null) {
    continue;
  }
  final structuralX = _treeController.getIndent(row.key);
  // PAINTED, not structural: the engine composes against
  // `existing.currentDelta`, so a delta-free `current` double-counts an
  // in-flight FLIP at t = 0 (see animateSlideFromOffsets' contract).
  // The composed read is safe here even mid-drag: the make-room preview
  // never assigns an offset to the dragged block
  // (TreeController.setReorderPreviewAtIndex skips
  // `[draggedIndex, draggedEnd)`), and `_stack` IS the dragged block.
  final paintedY = structuralY + _treeController.getSlideDelta(row.key);
  final paintedX = structuralX + _treeController.getSlideDeltaX(row.key);
  final releaseX = crossOffset == null
      ? paintedX
      : crossOffset + row.relativeIndent;
  prior[row.key] = (y: baseY + row.relativeY, x: releaseX);
  current[row.key] = (y: paintedY, x: paintedX);
}
```

The composed accessors are the right ones and need no new FLIP-only carve-out: `TreeController.setReorderPreviewAtIndex` skips the dragged block outright at `tree_controller.dart:1765-1767`, so for exactly the keys in `_stack` the composed delta (`getSlideDelta`, `:1394-1400`) equals the FLIP delta. On the dead-commit path the preview has already been snapped to nothing by `snapForCommit` (`tree_reorder_controller.dart:593`), so the two are equal there for a second reason.

Note the `releaseX` fallback also becomes painted rather than structural, which is the same correction on the X axis (`getSlideDeltaX`, `tree_controller.dart:1071`, is already FLIP-only per `:1059-1060`).

**Alternatives considered.** Adding a key-keyed `getFlipSlideDelta`: it would be a tenth FLIP-only read site and CLAUDE.md's count would need updating, for no behavioural difference on these keys.

**Architecture fit.** Restores the "both maps are painted positions" invariant that every other `animateSlideFromOffsets` caller obeys, without touching the FLIP-only carve-out list.

**Performance.** Two O(1) delta reads per stack row per glide install (once per cancel or dead-commit), guarded internally by `_preview.hasActive`.

**Risk.** Reachable whenever a stack row carries a live FLIP at teardown: a re-grab during a previous drag's settle glide, or an external animated `moveNode` mid-drag. Existing tests over this path: `drag_proxy_settle_test.dart`, `drag_subtree_handoff_test.dart`, `drag_proxy_indent_handoff_test.dart`, `external_cancel_drag_test.dart`. None of them starts a second drag mid-glide today, so the change should be a no-op for all of them (`getSlideDelta` returns 0 when idle).

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/drag_proxy_settle_test.dart`: drag row "b", cancel (glide installs), pump ~half the settle duration, sanity-assert `controller.getSlideDelta("b") != 0`, re-grab "b", cancel again, and assert the row's painted top on the next frame equals `pointer.dy - grabDy` within a pixel (today it is off by the surviving delta).

**Effort.** S.

### L23. Sticky-classified rows never show a FLIP slide

**Finding.** Pass A skips sticky rows at `render_sliver_tree.dart:3384-3386`, before the slide reads at `:3402-3403`. Pass B paints the header at `sticky.pinnedY` with no delta (`:3751-3759`). `hitTestChildren` Phase 1 tests at `pinnedY` with no delta (`:4127-4136`), and `applyPaintTransform` returns `pinnedY` and returns early before the delta reads (`:4358-4364`). `StickyHeaderComputer` contains no slide reference at all (`grep -c "getSlideDelta\|slideDelta\|Slide" lib/sliver_tree/_sticky_header_computer.dart` = 0).

**Root cause.** The sticky set is a LAYOUT product (`computeStickyHeaders` runs late in `performLayout`, `:2913`, `:3014`), while FLIP deltas are a PAINT product that ticks without layout: a pure slide tick takes the `markNeedsPaint` branch at `sliver_tree_element.dart:327` (its layout siblings in the same method are `:292`, `:313` and `:324`; `:464` is `_scheduleStaleEviction`'s FLIP gate, not a paint-routing site). Nothing bridges the two, and the four consumers above are internally consistent about it.

**Solution.** DOCUMENT, and do not exclude. ONE reason, and it is sufficient. An earlier draft gave two; the first was wrong and is withdrawn below.

**The reason: excluding a sliding candidate empties its band.** `pinnedY` is derived from the candidate's SUBTREE BOTTOM (`_sticky_header_computer.dart:430-444`: `pushUpY = (subtreeBottom - scrollOffset) - extent`, then `pinnedY = math.min(stackTop, pushUpY)`). Drop the candidate for the frames it slides and nothing paints in that band: Pass B iterates `_sticky.headers` (`:3722-3760`) and no longer finds it, while Pass A paints it at `structural + delta`, which by definition is not the band. The rows beneath then scroll under transparent space until the slide settles and the header pops back in. A header that vanishes from its own band for the length of a reorder is a louder artifact than a header that snaps to its new band, and it is precisely the artifact the sticky feature exists to prevent.

**Withdrawn: the "read a frame apart" argument.** The earlier draft claimed the exclusion was architecturally unavailable because the sticky set is a layout product while deltas tick paint-only, so the predicate and the delta would be read a frame apart. That is not a barrier and the audit is right to reject it. All four consumers are paint- or gesture-time readers: Pass A reads `_sticky.isSticky(nid)` at `:3384` and `getSlideDeltaNid(nid)` at `:3402` in the SAME loop iteration, and Pass B (`:3722-3760`), `hitTestChildren` Phase 1 (`:4120-4153`) and `applyPaintTransform` (`:4358-4364`) all run outside layout. A paint-time predicate ("sticky AND zero delta") would be read consistently within one frame by all four, so the split the codebase documents for the ghost prune/paint pair (`:3641-3654`) does not arise here. The decision rests on the band, not on timing.

Concretely, add:

1. At the Pass A skip (`render_sliver_tree.dart:3384-3386`), a comment stating the decision and naming the other three sites so the four cannot drift:

```dart
// A sticky-classified row shows NO FLIP slide: Pass B paints it at
// `pinnedY`, hit-testing tests it at `pinnedY` (`hitTestChildren`
// Phase 1), and `applyPaintTransform` reports `pinnedY`. Deliberate.
// Excluding a sliding candidate from the sticky set is mechanically
// possible (a paint-time "sticky AND zero delta" predicate would be
// read consistently by all four sites), and is rejected because
// `pinnedY` comes from the candidate's SUBTREE BOTTOM: dropping the
// candidate empties its band, so the rows beneath scroll under
// transparent space and the header pops back in when the slide
// settles. A reordered header snaps into its new pinned band instead.
if (_sticky.isSticky(nid)) {
  continue;
}
```

2. A sentence on `StickyHeaderComputer`'s class doc and on `SliverTree.maxStickyDepth`'s doc: "A row that is currently pinned does not animate its reorder slide; it snaps to its new band. Slides resume once the row is no longer pinned."

**Alternatives considered.** Excluding a sliding candidate from the sticky set for the frame, either at layout time or via a paint-time predicate: possible, rejected because it empties the pinned band mid-slide (above). Painting the header twice (Pass A slid plus Pass B pinned): with `RepaintBoundary` rows the second `paintChild` MOVES the single `OffsetLayer` rather than drawing a second copy (`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/object.dart:289-291`, `:304-308`), which is exactly L24's defect.

**Architecture fit.** Names an existing four-site consistency as a contract rather than leaving it as four independent omissions.

**Performance.** None.

**Risk.** Comments only.

**Test to add.** None: cleanup with no observable behavior change. If a pin is wanted, `test/sliver_tree/slide_indent_test.dart` is the right home for a "pinned header does not slide" assertion that locks the decision in.

**Effort.** S.

### L24. Pass A.7 repaints an exit-ghost anchor a second time per frame

**Status.** IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-24. Test-first as a rewrite: the helper became `_expectAnchorPaintedOnceAndBandGhostFree` (band painted exactly once; sticky-ownership sanities; clip-excludes-band control), red pre-fix in case 1 at 2 paints, exactly the measured A.7 double paint; case 2 renamed with its measured-false premise corrected and green both sides (Pass B owns the anchor); the new leg red pre-fix at 2 paints for an EDGE-ghost anchor scrolled into view mid-slide. Steps 1 to 4 landed as printed: `_computeA7Anchors` shared by paint and hit test with the composed `hasSlides` per M10's item 9, the Pass A skip above the sliding-bucket branch per the L7 composition rule, A.7 painting through `_paintRow`, and the `a7Idx` bucket drained first. Doc items 1 to 9 landed; the not-falsified list re-checked. Leg 2 skipped as the block allows (no X slide constructible on this anchor); leg 4's construct found that removing the anchor also frees its ghost, so the widget leg pins the Pass A half and the fall-out-of-both state is constructed lib-side in its demo. The tap control cannot detect bucket reordering in this geometry (uniformly shifted bands never overlap the anchor's), recorded as a smoke check. Sixteen demo states shown red individually. Contributes zero to the carve-out inventory, re-verified by the recipe (23 non-comment lines, twenty reads, unchanged). Risk suites 32 green; full suite 1135 passed, 4 skipped; analyze at the 48-issue baseline.

**Finding.** Pass A paints every non-sticky in-flow row (`render_sliver_tree.dart:3378-3438` plus the sliding sub-pass), and Pass A.7 then calls `context.paintChild(anchorChild, off)` on the same row again at `:3710-3715`. With rows wrapped in `RepaintBoundary` (`sliver_tree_element.dart:539-541`, default true), `PaintingContext.paintChild` routes through `_compositeChild`, which sets `childOffsetLayer.offset = offset` and `appendLayer(childOffsetLayer)`; `appendLayer` calls `layer.remove()` first (`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/object.dart:289-291`, `:304-308`).

**Root cause.** A repaint-boundary child owns ONE `OffsetLayer`. The second `paintChild` MOVES that single layer instead of drawing a second copy, so Pass A's placement is destroyed and the surviving placement is A.7's. Three things are lost with it: A.7's offset uses `anchorParentData.indent` with no `slideDeltaX` (`:3709`) while Pass A uses `parentData.indent + slideDeltaX` (`:3787`); A.7's clip is the full `band.height` while `_paintRow` bottom-anchors an extent-animating child under a `nodeExtent` clip (`:3808-3822`); and `hitTestChildren`'s slide-active z-order buckets by `|delta|` (`:4293-4320`), so a zero-delta A.7 anchor is tested LAST while paint now puts it on top.

**Solution.** Three steps, the first of which removes the double paint for the dominant case on its own.

**1. Restrict A.7 to EDGE-painted ghosts.** A `_ExitGhost` is either edge-painted or clipped, enforced by `assert((edge != null) ^ clipped)` at `:65-69`, and a CLIPPED ghost is already excluded from the anchor's band by the EXIT clip (`_resolvePhantomAnchorBounds`: `slidUp` yields visible `[bandBottom, remainingPaintExtent]`, otherwise `[0, bandTop]`, `:4044-4056`). So the header repaint buys nothing for those. `if (ghost.clipped) continue;` joins the selection below.

**2. Compute the A.7 selection ONCE, before Pass A, and make Pass A's skip set exactly the set A.7 paints.** This is the correctness constraint the earlier draft got wrong: it built `a7Anchors` from every non-clipped ghost's anchor with no filter, while A.7 additionally skips anchors that are freed (`:3697`), sticky (`:3698`), EXITING (`:3699`), unmounted (`:3701`), without parent data (`:3703`), without a band (`:3705`) or fully outside the paint region (`:3707-3708`). Pass A paints exiting in-flow rows (it has no exiting skip), so an exiting anchor of an edge-painted ghost would have been skipped by Pass A and skipped by A.7, and painted by NO pass at all. The skip set and the paint set must be one set, by construction. Same rule the ghost prune/paint pair states for itself at `:3641-3654`.

Factor the selection into one private method so paint and hit-test cannot drift:

```dart
/// The rows Pass A.7 will repaint this frame, and therefore exactly the
/// rows Pass A must skip. ONE definition, called from both `paint` and
/// `hitTestChildren`: a predicate applied on one side only produces a
/// row that no pass paints (an EXITING anchor is painted by Pass A but
/// skipped by A.7's `:3699`).
List<({TKey key, int nid, RenderBox child})>? _computeA7Anchors({
  required double remainingPaintExtent,
  required bool hasSlides,
}) {
  if (_phantomExitGhosts == null ||
      _phantomExitGhosts!.isEmpty ||
      !hasSlides) {
    return null;
  }
  List<({TKey key, int nid, RenderBox child})>? out;
  final seenAnchors = <TKey>{};
  for (final ghost in _phantomExitGhosts!.values) {
    // Clipped ghosts are already excluded from the anchor's band by the
    // EXIT clip (_resolvePhantomAnchorBounds, role: exit), so the header
    // needs no repaint on top of them. Only an EDGE-painted ghost (which
    // takes the unclipped tail of Pass A.5) can overlap the band.
    if (ghost.clipped) continue;
    final anchorKey = ghost.anchor;
    if (!seenAnchors.add(anchorKey)) continue; // dedupe shared anchors
    final anchorNid = controller.nidOf(anchorKey);
    if (anchorNid < 0) continue; // freed key
    if (_sticky.isSticky(anchorNid)) continue; // Pass B owns it
    if (controller.isExitingNid(anchorNid)) continue; // animating out
    final anchorChild = _children[anchorKey];
    if (anchorChild == null) continue; // not mounted in-flow
    if (anchorChild.parentData is! SliverTreeParentData) continue;
    final band = _anchorPaintedBounds(anchorKey);
    if (band == null) continue;
    if (band.top >= remainingPaintExtent) continue;
    if (band.top + band.height <= 0) continue;
    (out ??= []).add((key: anchorKey, nid: anchorNid, child: anchorChild));
  }
  return out;
}
```

`band` stays local: it is a culling input only, because step 3 drops the bespoke clip. `isExitingNid` replaces `isExiting(anchorKey)` at `:3699` to save the key hash; it is the same predicate (`:4182` already uses the nid form).

In `paint`, before the Pass A loop:

```dart
final a7Paints = _computeA7Anchors(
  remainingPaintExtent: remainingPaintExtent,
  hasSlides: hasSlides,
);
Set<int>? a7AnchorNids;
if (a7Paints != null) {
  a7AnchorNids = <int>{for (final a in a7Paints) a.nid};
}
```

and skip them in Pass A immediately after the sticky skip at `:3384-3386` (nid-keyed, so no `nodeId` resolution is needed there):

```dart
if (a7AnchorNids?.contains(nid) ?? false) {
  continue; // painted by Pass A.7, exactly once
}
```

**3. Make the surviving repaint a single faithful paint rather than a layer move.** A.7's body becomes a walk of `a7Paints` with no filtering, painting through `_paintRow`:

```dart
if (a7Paints != null) {
  for (final a in a7Paints) {
    _paintRow(
      context: context,
      offset: offset,
      nid: a.nid,
      child: a.child,
      slideDelta: hasSlides ? controller.getSlideDeltaNid(a.nid) : 0.0,
      slideDeltaX: hasXSlides ? controller.getSlideDeltaXNid(a.nid) : 0.0,
      scrollOffset: scrollOffset,
      remainingPaintExtent: remainingPaintExtent,
    );
  }
}
```

The anchor is then painted exactly once, with its X slide, its extent-animation clip (`:3808-3822`) and A.7's z-order. Routing through `_paintRow` also applies the entry-phantom clip at `:3797-3806` for an anchor that happens to be an entry-phantom target as well; that is a change from A.7's bespoke `pushClipRect`, and it is the correct direction: it makes A.7 paint the anchor the same way Pass A would have.

**4. Mirror the z-order in hit testing.** In the slide-active path, collect A.7 anchors into a third bucket and test it before `slidingIdx`. In the bucketing loop at `:4295-4307`, right after the sticky skip at `:4299`:

```dart
final a7Idx = <int>[];
// ... in the bucketing loop, after `if (_sticky.isSticky(nid)) continue;`:
if (a7AnchorNids?.contains(nid) ?? false) { a7Idx.add(i); continue; }
// ... then, before the `slidingIdx` pass at :4315:
for (final i in a7Idx) { if (testRow(i)) return true; }
```

`hitTestChildren` calls `_computeA7Anchors` itself (paint state is not carried across), which is why it is one method rather than three inlined lines in two places.

**Sequencing dependency (chain 3: M10 first, then L6, L7 and L24).** Chain 3 in the plan's Sequencing section is the exit-ghost pipeline. All four blocks decide which delta a ghost pass reads and who paints the anchor; this one is the block that decides who paints the ANCHOR.

M10. Two shared artifacts, and the order is fixed. (a) The outer `hasSlides` gate. `_computeA7Anchors` lifts A.7's own gate at `render_sliver_tree.dart:3689-3691` into a parameter, and `hitTestChildren` becomes a SECOND caller that must pass the same thing (it already computes `final hasSlides = controller.hasActiveSlides;` at `:4167`, as `paint` does at `:3345`). M10's per-site table settles what that thing is: its item 9 rules the outer `hasSlides` pre-filters at `:3485` and `:3689-3691` COMPOSED and unchanged, because they only skip work while the per-entry gate is authoritative, the edge-ghost precedent being the composed `_composer.hasGhosts && hasSlides` at `:3618` sitting above a FLIP-only per-entry gate at `:3658-3661`. So pass `controller.hasActiveSlides` at both call sites, never `hasActiveFlipSlides`. Landing this block first and guessing FLIP-only there would drop A.7 for a row whose FLIP has settled while a held preview still displaces the anchor, and because this block makes Pass A's skip set the SAME set, that anchor would then be painted by no pass at all, which is exactly the failure Step 2 exists to prevent. (b) The population of `_phantomExitGhosts`, the map `_computeA7Anchors` walks. M10's per-site items 1 and 2 make the Step 0a prune criterion FLIP-only, so a ghost whose FLIP has settled retires instead of surviving a whole drag; before M10 a held preview keeps the anchor's composed delta non-zero for the length of the drag, so today's A.7 loop, and after this block the new Pass A skip with it, stays live that whole time. This block's Performance claim ("the registry it walks is small by construction") and its test's `debugPhantomExitGhostCount` sanity are both calibrated on the post-M10 population. One count correction, stated because it is easy to assume otherwise: this block adds NO carve-out read. `_computeA7Anchors` reads `nidOf`, `_sticky.isSticky` and `isExitingNid` (`tree_controller.dart:869`, the nid form already used at `render_sliver_tree.dart:4182`), and Step 3 paints through `_paintRow`, which takes the COMPOSED `getSlideDeltaNid` / `getSlideDeltaXNid` and applies them at `:3787-3788`. So this block contributes ZERO to M10's `hasActiveFlipSlides` / `getFlipSlideDeltaNid` / `getHeldPreviewDeltaNid` inventory and must write no count into CLAUDE.md. M10's own counting rule says the same thing: it names the blocks that DO change the inventory, and this block is not among them. Do not quote that list by number here, because it has grown since this block was drafted and will go stale again; M10 owns the list, and M10's sequencing paragraph states explicitly that this block contributes zero, so the two agree.

L6. Same map, disjoint halves, and the split is structural rather than conventional: `_ExitGhost` asserts `(edge != null) ^ clipped` at `render_sliver_tree.dart:65-69`, so every record is edge-painted XOR clipped. Step 1 above keeps A.7 for the EDGE records only (built at `:1161-1162`), while L6's new `applyPaintTransform` branch is for the CLIPPED, on-screen-anchor record (`:1141-1146`). Neither block touches the other's predicate and either order compiles. The order-dependence is in the TEST. Step 3 routes the surviving A.7 repaint through `_paintRow`, which moves the anchor's painted x from `anchorParentData.indent` (A.7's bespoke offset at `:3709`) to `parentData.indent + slideDeltaX` (`:3787`) and replaces A.7's `Rect.fromLTWH(0, 0, anchorChild.size.width, band.height)` clip (`:3713`) with `_paintRow`'s extent-animation clip (`:3808-3822`). L6's ghost base is unaffected, since it reads the anchor's LAYOUT values rather than its painted placement, but the suites L6 names under Risk are the four this block names, so a painted-rect assertion written around a reparent-into-collapsed animation before this block lands is calibrated on anchor geometry this block changes. Land this block first and L6's test is calibrated once; land L6 first and re-run those suites when this one lands. L6's block records the same from its side.

L7. Adjacent edits to ONE loop, and they must compose. The Pass A skip block runs from the sticky skip at `render_sliver_tree.dart:3384-3386` through the composed delta read at `:3402` to the edge-ghost skip at `:3417-3421`, immediately above the sliding-bucket branch at `:3423-3426`. L7 changes the edge-ghost skip's delta from the composed `slideDelta` to the FLIP-only one so that skip becomes the exact complement of Pass A.6's gate at `:3658-3661`; this block inserts a THIRD skip, for the `_computeA7Anchors` anchors, right after the sticky skip. The contents are disjoint (`_composer.ghosts` against `_phantomExitGhosts`), so either order compiles, but whichever lands second must confirm the two compose for a row that is BOTH an edge-ghost row and an exit-ghost anchor. With L7 landed, such a row falls THROUGH the edge-ghost skip whenever its FLIP delta is zero, so this block's anchor skip is what has to catch it, which is why that skip must sit ABOVE `:3423-3426`. Put it below and the row is bucketed into `slidingIndices` AND repainted by A.7, i.e. the double paint this block exists to remove, reintroduced for precisely the row both blocks touch. The same constraint holds in the hit test, where the new `a7Idx` bucket must be filled in the loop at `:4295-4307` right after the sticky skip at `:4299` and drained before the `slidingIdx` pass at `:4315`. L7's block records the same. Not covered today: no existing test builds a row that is both.

**Alternatives considered.** Painting the ghost passes BEFORE Pass A so in-flow rows land on top naturally: that also puts every sliding row on top of every ghost, which is the opposite of what Pass A.5's convergence needs. Building the skip set from ghost anchors without A.7's filters (the earlier draft): rejected above, it leaves an exiting anchor unpainted by any pass.

**Architecture fit.** Restores "each mounted row is painted by exactly ONE pass per frame", which the codebase already states for headers at `:3683-3684` and enforces for sticky rows via the Pass A skip, and gives that guarantee a single owner instead of two predicates that must be kept in step by hand.

Two questions, and they are separate: whether the new call is SAFE, and whether the stated contract survives it. A safe change can still falsify a stated contract, and the fix for that is to restate the contract, not to omit it.

**The new call is SAFE.** Four reasons, all read this session.

1. Same phase, same state, same method. `hitTestChildren` Phase 1 ALREADY reads `_sticky.headers` at gesture time and gives the pinned band hit priority (`:4122-4128`); `_anchorPaintedBounds`' sticky branch reads that same `_sticky` through `infoForNid` (`:3969-3974`). Step 4 introduces no new dependency, it reuses one the method it is being added to already has.
2. The precedent is in this file and it is the SAME method. `paintedRowBounds` calls `_anchorPaintedBounds` at `:1946` from GESTURE time and records why at `:1936-1943`: `_sticky` then holds the last PAINTED frame's values, "precisely the geometry the user was looking at when they pressed". That reasoning transfers, and it strengthens. For grab capture, painted-frame geometry is the right answer; for a HIT TEST it is the requirement, because hit testing exists to agree with what was painted.
3. Every other input is already read at gesture time by one of the two. `constraints.scrollOffset` (`hitTestChildren:4116`), `anchorParentData.layoutOffset` (`:4196`), `getSlideDeltaNid` (`:4204`, and again in the bucketing loop at `:4300`); `anchorChild.size.height` (`:3982`) is reached at gesture time today through `paintedRowBounds` at `:1946`.
4. The one input that could go stale cannot change a hit answer. In `_computeA7Anchors` the band is a CULLING input only (Step 2's note above: Step 3 drops the bespoke clip), and the cull condition is "band fully outside the paint region" (`:3707-3708`). A row in that state fails `testRow`'s own bounds checks (`:4208-4209`) in whichever bucket it lands in, so a band that differed between paint and the following hit test could only move a NON-hittable row between `a7Idx` and `slidingIdx`/`staticIdx`. It cannot change which row is hit.

What does NOT relax is the LAYOUT half of the rule, and item 7's replacement keeps that half in substance: `_consumeSlideBaselineIfAny` runs at `:2564`, near the start of `performLayout`, while `computeStickyHeaders` runs at `:2913` and `:3014`, so `_sticky` there is the prior frame's value or null. Step 4 gives that no cover.

One call-site consequence to carry into the code and not only the doc: `hitTestChildren` does not read `constraints.remainingPaintExtent` today, and `_computeA7Anchors` takes it as a parameter, so the hit-test call site must pass `constraints.remainingPaintExtent`, the same expression `paint` reads at `:3336`. Passing anything else makes the two call sites ask different questions, which is the failure item 5 already forbids for `hasSlides`.
