**Alternatives considered.**

- Disposing and recreating the group on reversal: precisely the snap `bulk_reentry_continuation_test.dart` was written to prevent.
- Keeping `?? _unknownExtent` and capturing the pre-reversal painted extent into `startExtent` explicitly: architecturally unavailable, not merely undesirable. `computeExtent` ignores `startExtent` entirely under the sentinel (`types.dart:252-254`), so nothing written there is read. Making it read would mean changing the sentinel's semantics, which the standalone animator's parallel handling (`_animation_coordinator.dart:893-897`, `_standalone_animator.dart:181`) and both of `setFullExtent`'s repair branches (`:456-464`) also depend on.
- Anchoring to `defaultExtent` "for the reversal window only" and restoring the sentinel afterwards: there is no "afterwards" to hook. The group runs to completion asynchronously, and a member restored to the sentinel mid-flight would jump again the moment `curvedValue` next changed. Edit 3's flag clear buys the same repair with no window to manage.
- Leaving Path 1 alone entirely: taken for the sentinel question, which is edit 3's withdrawal above. Not taken for the flag, because a one-line clear is what stops the four sites from diverging again on exactly the case that produced this item.
- Relying on `setFullExtent`'s re-target to repair a wrong terminus later without the flag clear: the repair is conditional on `!targetIsCaptured` AND `oldExtent != extent` (`_animation_coordinator.dart:462-464`), and the captured-flag case is precisely the one that cannot repair.

**Architecture fit.** Makes the four reversal sites (expand Path 1, collapse Path 1, expandAll bulk, collapseAll bulk) share ONE rebase recipe, with no unmeasured special case, instead of four variants; and makes the two bulk joiner branches agree on policy.

**Performance.** One extra `computeExtent` per group member per reversal (already paid by Path 1) and one controller reset. Removes the mis-timed frames.

**Risk.** Reachable only when a bulk call reverses a per-node op group mid-flight. Why 200 works, and what bounds it. Under edit 1 the envelope is `extent(cv) = lerp(18, 48, cv) = 18 + 30 * cv`, so exceeding 28 needs `cv > 1/3`, that is elapsed above 133.3 ms; and the read must land before the group retires at 400 ms, or it degrades into the vacuous `fullExtentOf` fallback cited above. 200 ms sits in the middle of `(133.3, 400)` and reads `lerp(18, 48, 0.5)` = 33.0. The threshold KEEPS its meaning, which is the reason this repair beats the others: a regression that rebases `startExtent` but forgets to restore `targetExtent` leaves the captured 24 in place, so its envelope is `lerp(18, 24, cv)`, bounded above by 24 for every cv in `[0, 1]`. `greaterThan(28)` therefore still states exactly what the test's name and `reason` state, and at 200 ms it separates 33.0 from 21.0 by 12 px instead of the 3 px available at 50 ms.

It also makes the `reason` string false: 21.75 is BELOW the captured 24 that the reason says the row must not be capped at. That is a pin on arithmetic replacing a pin on behaviour.
- **Threshold only, same read point.** Strictly the previous option with a looser matcher: same 0.75 px separation from the original bug, and the same dead `reason`.

The settled value is ALREADY asserted at `:1767` and reads 48 whether or not `targetExtent` was ever restored, because the group is gone by then (`_animation_coordinator.dart:739`). A monotone-increase assertion passes under the capped regression too, since `lerp(18, 24, cv)` also increases. The property is "exceeds the captured cap", which `greaterThan(28)` already says.

Nothing in this block's own list covers what `:1711` covers.

The test's NAME needs no edit: edit 1 still restores `targetExtent` to full (`member.value.targetExtent = full`). What changes is `startExtent` and the controller's timeline, neither of which the name mentions.

### L28. Direction flip under a same-frame pending baseline drops the edge-to-edge composition

**Finding.** With a baseline staged, `performLayout` calls `normalizeForViewport(installStandaloneSlides: false)` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:2558-2563`). Its direction-flip branch then updates `exits[key].edge` to the new side (`_ghost_registry.dart:476-480`) and installs nothing, because both the baseline and current maps it would have built are inside `if (installStandaloneSlides)` at `:462-475`.

**Root cause.** The consume that was supposed to carry the motion cannot see the old edge any more. `_consumeSlideBaselineIfAny` rewrites every ghost's baseline entry to `_composer.baseFor(ghostKey, currentViewport)` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:955-969`), which reads the ALREADY-FLIPPED `entry.edge`, and `current = snapshotVisibleOffsets()` (`:907`) reads the same flipped edge at `:1590-1599`. So `rawDeltaY = newBaseY - newBaseY = 0` and the ghost pops from one viewport edge to the other in a single frame. The comment at `:952-954` ("Direction-flip and re-promotion still produce non-zero deltas because they explicitly write DIFFERENT edge bases for prior vs current") is true only on the `installStandaloneSlides: true` path.

**Solution.** Have the no-install normalization record the prior base so the consume can use it, which keeps the "one animation batch per layout" rule the ordering comment at `:2532-2548` exists to enforce.

1. In `GhostRegistry`, add a one-shot per-layout record and a taker:

```dart
/// Prior EDGE BASES for ghosts whose side flipped during a
/// `normalizeForViewport(installStandaloneSlides: false)` pass, i.e.
/// under a same-frame pending baseline. The flip installs no slide of
/// its own there, so the consume owns the motion and needs the base the
/// ghost was painting at BEFORE the flip. Drained by the consume; a
/// stale entry cannot survive a layout.
Map<TKey, double>? _pendingFlipPriorBaseY;

Map<TKey, double>? takePendingFlipPriorBases() {
  final out = _pendingFlipPriorBaseY;
  _pendingFlipPriorBaseY = null;
  return out;
}
```

and populate it in the flip branch, in the `else` of the existing install gate (`_ghost_registry.dart:461-482`):

```dart
if (newEdge != entry.edge) {
  final oldBaseY = viewport.baseForEdge(entry.edge);
  if (installStandaloneSlides) {
    // ... unchanged: build the baseline/current pair ...
  } else {
    (_pendingFlipPriorBaseY ??= <TKey, double>{})[key] = oldBaseY;
  }
  exits[key] = (edge: newEdge, duration: entry.duration, curve: entry.curve);
  continue;
}
```

2. In `_consumeSlideBaselineIfAny`, prefer the recorded prior in the rewrite at `render_sliver_tree.dart:955-969`:

```dart
final flipPriors = _composer.ghosts.takePendingFlipPriorBases();
if (_composer.hasGhosts) {
  for (final ghostKey in _composer.ghosts.activeKeys.toList()) {
    if (!baseline.containsKey(ghostKey)) continue;
    // A side flip in THIS layout's normalize pass installed no slide
    // (a pending baseline was staged), so the consume owns the
    // edge-to-edge motion: use the PRE-flip base as the prior.
    // Without it prior and current both read the flipped edge and the
    // ghost jumps across the viewport in one frame.
    final ghostBase =
        flipPriors?[ghostKey] ?? _composer.baseFor(ghostKey, currentViewport);
    if (ghostBase == null) continue;
    // ... unchanged tail: add ghostSlideY / ghostSlideX and write back ...
  }
}
```

`takePendingFlipPriorBases` must also be drained (or cleared) when no baseline is consumed, so `_consumeSlideBaselineIfAny`'s early return at `:902` leaves nothing behind; call it before that return, or clear the map from `GhostRegistry.reset` and at the top of `normalizeForViewport`. Clearing at the top of `normalizeForViewport` is the simplest: the map is only ever meaningful for the consume that runs immediately after in the same `performLayout`.

3. Fix the stale comment at `:952-954` to say that flips under a pending baseline are carried by the recorded prior above, not by re-derivation.

**Alternatives considered.** Letting `normalizeForViewport` install the flip slide even under a pending baseline: that reintroduces two independent `animateSlideFromOffsets` calls in one frame, which the pipeline ordering at `:2536-2543` was written to eliminate.

**Architecture fit.** Keeps the single-batch rule and the "consume composes against fresh state" property, adding only the one datum the consume cannot recompute.

**Performance.** One small map allocated only on a flip under a pending baseline; nothing on any other path.

**Risk.** Reachable only when an animated mutation and a viewport-sized scroll jump land in the same frame with an edge ghost alive. Existing coverage: `offscreen_anchor_exit_ghost_test.dart`, `slide_scroll_concurrency_test.dart`, `slide_scroll_concurrency_fixes_test.dart`, `slide_viewport_clamp_test.dart`, `ghost_prune_flip_only_test.dart`, `ghost_remove_in_flight_test.dart`, `ghost_revisible_double_paint_test.dart`. The `preserveProgressOnRebatch` re-set at `_ghost_registry.dart:495-501` runs only in the install branch and is not affected; the consume's own composition path is what marks these.

**Test to add.** `test/sliver_tree/slide_scroll_concurrency_fixes_test.dart`. Two debug forwarders on `RenderSliverTree` come first, alongside `debugComposerGhostCount` (`render_sliver_tree.dart:551-556`), because the state this test has to prove is otherwise unreachable from outside: `@visibleForTesting bool get debugIsBaselineStaged => _composer.isBaselineStaged;` (`_slide_composer.dart:79`) and `@visibleForTesting Object? debugGhostEdgeFor(TKey key) => _composer.ghosts.entryFor(key)?.edge;` (`_ghost_registry.dart:118`). The edge accessor returns `Object?` deliberately, so the test compares it against the previous frame's value and never has to name `ViewportEdge`.

Setup: create an edge ghost anchored at the LEADING edge and carrying a live FLIP slide, then in ONE frame issue an animated `moveNode` (staging a baseline) and jump the scroll position past the ghost's structural offset so `viewport.edgeFor` answers trailing.

Setup sanity, captured on the frame BEFORE the flip and asserted before anything else: `sliver.debugComposerGhostCount > 0`; `controller.getSlideDelta(ghostKey) != 0.0`, which is what guarantees `pruneSettled` (`_ghost_registry.dart:148-158`) will not reap the entry at `render_sliver_tree.dart:943` and that the engine takes its `existing != null` branch; `sliver.debugIsBaselineStaged` true after the `moveNode` and before the pump, which is what selects `installStandaloneSlides: false` at `render_sliver_tree.dart:2561`; and record `beforeTop = tester.getRect(find.byKey(ghostRowKey)).top` and `beforeDelta = controller.getSlideDelta(ghostKey)`. On the flip frame, assert `sliver.debugGhostEdgeFor(ghostKey)` differs from its pre-flip value, proving the flip branch at `_ghost_registry.dart:460-482` actually ran.

Assertion (a), continuity, the user-visible property: `tester.getRect(find.byKey(ghostRowKey)).top` on the flip frame is within a pixel of `beforeTop`, and stays within a pixel of the new expected position on the frame after it. `applyPaintTransform` substitutes the live edge base for a ghost carrying a non-zero delta (`render_sliver_tree.dart:4402-4416`), so this reads the ghost's PAINTED position, and an edge ghost's global painted position is stable under scroll because its base IS a viewport edge. Today it differs by roughly the viewport's main-axis extent: the ghost teleports from the leading band to the trailing one in one frame.

Assertion (b), the mechanical pin, which is the MAGNITUDE the audit asked for: `(controller.getSlideDelta(ghostKey) - beforeDelta).abs()` is at least half the viewport's main-axis extent. After the fix the consume composes `rawDeltaY = oldBaseY - newBaseY` into the existing slide, so the delta moves by the edge-to-edge distance in a single frame; today the only change is one frame of the original slide's decay. Setup sanity that keeps the bound honest: assert `beforeDelta.abs() * 0.2` is below that half-viewport bound, so a 16 ms frame of a 300 ms slide cannot reach it by decay alone.

Both assertions fail today. The earlier draft's discriminator ("assert `controller.getSlideDelta(ghostKey)` is non-zero on the next frame; today it is 0") is WITHDRAWN because it is false, and the reason is worth recording so it is not reintroduced: a live registry entry IMPLIES a live FLIP delta, since `pruneSettled` reaps zero-delta entries (`_ghost_registry.dart:151-156`) immediately before the rewrite at `render_sliver_tree.dart:943`; the flipped edge then makes `prior.y` and `current.y` identical, so `rawDeltaY == 0` and the engine's no-op-composition branch preserves the existing entry untouched (`_slide_animation_engine.dart:320-341`, the `continue` at `:339-341`). The delta on the next frame is therefore non-zero today, and the old assertion passed on unfixed code.

**Effort.** M.

### L29. Optional: capture InheritedTheme for the drag proxy

**Finding.** The proxy is built inside a root-`Overlay` `OverlayEntry` (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:641-664`), so `_DragProxy.build`'s `context` (`:1538`) and the per-descendant `nodeBuilder(context, row.key, row.depth)` clones (`:1584`) resolve `Theme`/`DefaultTextStyle`/`IconTheme` against the overlay, not against the row. This is DOCUMENTED: `showDragProxy`'s doc at `:203-209` states the proxy "renders in the root [Overlay], OUTSIDE the row's original ancestry, the same contract as `Draggable.feedback`" and directs users to `dragProxyBuilder`.

**Root cause.** Nothing captures the row's inherited themes at drag start; the overlay entry is created from the OWNER state's context (`_ensureProxy(context)` at `:685`), which is the `SliverReorderableTree`'s, not the dragged row's.

**Solution, and the doc change it forces.**

1. Widen the scope callback so the row hands over its own context. `_ReorderableScope.onDragStart` is `void Function(TKey key, Widget rowChild)` (`:336`); change it to `void Function(TKey key, Widget rowChild, BuildContext rowContext)`. Sites to update, all in this one file: the field (`:336`), the constructor parameter (`:300`), the wiring (`:745`), the cached forwarder's type and assignment (`:881`, `:915`), the invocation (`:1381`, passing the row state's `context`), and the handler signature (`:670`).

2. Capture once per session in `_onDragStart`, before `_ensureProxy` at `:685`:

```dart
final overlay = Overlay.maybeOf(context, rootOverlay: true);
_capturedThemes = overlay == null
    ? null
    : InheritedTheme.capture(from: rowContext, to: overlay.context);
```

`InheritedTheme.capture(from:, to:)` returns a `CapturedThemes` whose `wrap(child)` re-provides them (`flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/inherited_theme.dart:87-126`, `:133-141`). The same-null guard matters: `_ensureProxy` already returns early when `Overlay.maybeOf` is null (`:641-644`), so there is no proxy to theme in that case. `capture` asserts that `to` is an ancestor of `from` (`:121-124`); that holds here, because `Overlay.maybeOf(context, rootOverlay: true)` resolves from the OWNER state's context and `rowContext` is a descendant of that state, hence a descendant of the overlay it found. Clear `_capturedThemes` in `_removeProxy` alongside `_draggedRowChild` and `_dragStack` (`:624-629`).

3. Apply it in `_DragProxy.build`, wrapping the whole `content` before the opacity (`:1596-1598`) and the indent padding so both the captured row widget and the descendant clones build under it. Pass the `CapturedThemes?` into `_DragProxy` as a new field set in `_ensureProxy`'s builder (`:645-663`), and in `build` insert after the stack assembly ends at `:1592`:

```dart
final captured = capturedThemes;
if (captured != null) {
  content = captured.wrap(content);
}
```

**Doc change this implies (mandatory, not optional).** `showDragProxy`'s doc at `:203-209` currently promises the `Draggable.feedback` contract. After the capture, `InheritedTheme` subclasses (`Theme`, `DefaultTextStyle`, `IconTheme`, `TooltipTheme` and friends) ARE inherited from the row, while non-`InheritedTheme` ancestors, `Material` above all, still are not, because `Material` is not an `InheritedTheme` and cannot be captured. Replacement text:

> The preview renders in the root [Overlay], OUTSIDE the row's original ancestry, but the row's [InheritedTheme] ancestors (`Theme`, `DefaultTextStyle`, `IconTheme` and any other `InheritedTheme` subclass) are captured at drag start and re-provided around it, so a locally themed row looks the same in the proxy. Non-theme ancestors are NOT captured: rows using inherited-ancestor-dependent widgets (e.g. Material ink widgets, which assert on a `Material` ancestor) still need a [dragProxyBuilder] that re-provides them (e.g. wrap in `Material(type: MaterialType.transparency)`); this package is widgets-layer-only and cannot supply Material itself.
>
> The capture applies to the widgets the proxy MOUNTS, not to the builder callbacks themselves. [dragProxyBuilder] and [nodeBuilder] are invoked with the overlay's `BuildContext`, so a builder that calls `Theme.of(context)` in its own body still reads the overlay's theme; only the widgets it RETURNS build under the captured themes.

Also add the freeze note, which `InheritedTheme.capture` documents at `inherited_theme.dart:77-81`: the captured themes are frozen for the session, so a mid-drag theme change is not reflected in the proxy. That matches the doc's existing "invoked ONCE PER DRAG SESSION" statement at `:237-240`.

**Decision on the API shape: ship it unconditionally, no flag.** It is a visible behaviour change and it goes in the changelog under "Changed", naming `showDragProxy` and `dragProxyBuilder`. There is no `captureRowThemes` parameter. Four reasons:

- `dragProxyBuilder` IS the escape hatch and it already exists (`sliver_reorderable_tree.dart:212-245`). An app that genuinely wants the overlay's theme in the proxy re-provides it there in one wrap. Adding `captureRowThemes` gives the same problem a second, narrower knob and turns `{showDragProxy, dragProxyBuilder, captureRowThemes}` into a matrix the doc has to enumerate and the tests have to cover in both states.
- A flag defaulting to `false` ships the wrong default forever. The rendering it would disable is the one every reader expects (a lifted row looks like the row it lifted from); making that opt-in means every user of a locally themed row meets the bug first and the flag second.
- A public `bool` field on `SliverReorderableTree` is permanent surface. Removing it later is itself breaking, so a flag does not avoid a breaking change, it schedules one.
- The package is at `0.0.34` (`pubspec.yaml:4`). Under pub's own semver rules a `0.0.x` bump may break; there is no stability promise here to trade against.

Rejected: gating behind `captureRowThemes: false` (reasons above); gating behind `captureRowThemes: true` (same permanent surface, plus the "off" path must keep working and be tested for a behaviour nobody asked for).

Who is affected, stated plainly so the changelog entry can say it: a row inside a local `Theme` currently renders in the proxy with the overlay's theme; after the change it renders with the row's. Apps that compensated with a `dragProxyBuilder` re-applying the row's theme keep working (the capture is a no-op for a theme they re-provide themselves). An app that deliberately relied on the overlay theme for the proxy sees a visual change with no API signal, which is what the changelog entry is for.

**Alternatives considered.** `InheritedTheme.captureAll(rowContext, child, to: overlay.context)` at build time: it needs the row's context to still be mounted at every proxy rebuild, which a drag that autoscrolls the row out of the cache region cannot guarantee, so the capture must happen once at drag start.

**Architecture fit.** Keeps the presentation decision in the widget layer; the reorder controller and the session architecture are untouched.

**Performance.** One ancestor walk at drag start (`InheritedTheme.capture` uses `visitAncestorElements`, `inherited_theme.dart:100`) and one extra `_CaptureAll` element in the proxy subtree.

**Risk.** The capture wraps the SAME `rowChild` widget instance the proxy already mounts, so it neither fixes nor worsens H5 (the `GlobalKey` double-mount). Tests over proxy content: `drag_proxy_test.dart`, `drag_proxy_move_rebuild_test.dart`, `drag_subtree_proxy_test.dart`, `drag_proxy_indent_tracking_test.dart`, `drag_proxy_indent_handoff_test.dart`, `drag_proxy_settle_test.dart`; `drag_proxy_move_rebuild_test.dart` in particular pins that pointer moves do not re-invoke `proxyBuilder`, and the wrap sits outside the pointer `ValueListenableBuilder` (`:1622-1665`), so that pin holds. The scope signature change touches `sliver_reorderable_tree.dart` only; `_ReorderableScope` is private and cannot be constructed from tests.

**Test to add.** Follows directly from the decision, and is written unconditionally because there is no flag to set: `test/sliver_tree/drag_proxy_test.dart` wraps the tree in a `MaterialApp` whose ambient `DefaultTextStyle` differs from a per-row `DefaultTextStyle`, drags a row, and asserts the proxy's `Text` resolves the ROW's style (read `DefaultTextStyle.of` at the proxy's `Text` element). Setup sanity: assert the two styles differ, and assert the resolved style is NOT the ambient one, so the test cannot pass by the two happening to coincide. The refuted M18 probe named in the audit section is the negative control and becomes this positive assertion.

**Effort.** M.
